title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
皇上御極之四十有三年乃歲甲
子天下例復當大比士於鄉
廣東試事巡按御史陳聯芳
實監臨之夙夜兢惕思祗承
聖天子寤寐求賢至意章程防範
視昔倍虔焉維時提督兩廣
===
兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史
吳桂芳文武為憲海嶠肅清
提督南贛都察院右僉都御
史吳百朋威德宣揚疆境底
定總兵官恭順侯吳繼爵敬
共武服雅尚章縫十郡之士
咸得專志鼓篋抱藝待試乃
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

皇上御極之四十有三年，乃歲甲子，天下例復當大比士於鄉。廣東試事，巡按御史陳聯芳實監臨之，夙夜兢惕，思祗承聖天子寤寐求賢至意，章程防範，視昔倍虔焉。維時，提督兩廣兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史吳桂芳，文武為憲，海嶠肅清；提督南贛都察院右僉都御史吳百朋，威德宣揚，疆境底定；總兵官恭順侯吳繼爵，敬共武服，雅尚章縫。十郡之士，咸得專志鼓篋，抱藝待試，乃
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the forty-third year of His Majesty’s reign, the jiazi year, it was once again time, according to established practice throughout the realm, for the triennial examination of scholars in the provinces. Chen Lianfang, Regional Inspecting Censor, served as Supervising Official for the examination in Guangdong. Vigilant and apprehensive day and night, he sought reverently to fulfill the sage Son of Heaven’s deepest wish to find worthy men, a concern that occupied him waking and sleeping. In administering regulations and safeguards, Chen exercised twice the care of former times.

At this time, Wu Guifang, Supreme Commander of Liangguang, Right Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, set an example in both civil and military affairs, bringing peace and order to the coastal regions. Wu Baipeng, Supreme Commander of Nan-Gan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, spread his authority and beneficence, securing the frontier territories. Wu Jijue, Regional Commander and Marquis of Gongshun, respectfully discharged his military duties and held the scholarly calling in high esteem. The scholars of the ten prefectures were thus all able to devote themselves wholly to their studies, opening their book boxes and awaiting the examination with their literary accomplishments ready. Then …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上兔罝野人亦知爭自濯磨
以階嚮用諸士今舉於鄉者
吾知其決不甘於兔罝野人
之不若也乾知又何懼哉是
舉也巡按御史姜儆以奉
命至振揚風教刑部郎中余良翰
以平讞至嘉尚文士至若飭
===
武于省則總兵俞大猷綜翊
于外則左叅政郭應聘右叅
政陳惟舉左叅議陳紀許公
高右叅議曹天祐副使方逢
時戴一俊僉事周時中徐甫
宰劉穩署都指揮僉事亦孔
昭治兵于疆則叅將門崇文
punctuated: 上《兔罝》野人亦知爭自濯磨，以階嚮用。諸士今舉於鄉者，吾知其決不甘於《兔罝》野人之不若也。乾知又何懼哉？是舉也，巡按御史姜儆以奉命至，振揚風教；刑部郎中余良翰以平讞至，嘉尚文士。至若飭武于省，則總兵俞大猷；綜翊于外，則左叅政郭應聘、右叅政陳惟舉、左叅議陳紀、許公高、右叅議曹天祐、副使方逢時、戴一俊、僉事周時中、徐甫宰、劉穩、署都指揮僉事亦孔昭；治兵于疆，則叅將門崇文、
translation_en:
…[The opening character 上 is unclear here.] Even the rustic men of “The Rabbit Net” (Tu ju) knew to strive to cleanse and refine themselves, thereby advancing toward employment in service. As for the scholars now recommended through the Provincial Examination, I know that they would never willingly fall short of those rustic men of “The Rabbit Net.” What, then, need I, Qianzhi, fear?

For this examination, Regional Inspector Jiang Jing arrived under imperial orders and promoted moral instruction. Yu Lianghan, Director in the Ministry of Justice, arrived to review judicial cases and showed esteem for men of letters. As for strengthening military preparedness in the provincial capital, there was Regional Commander Yu Dayou. Those coordinating affairs and providing support outside it were Guo Yingpin, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Chen Weiju, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right; Chen Ji and Xu Gonggao, Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners of the Left; Cao Tianyou, Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right; Fang Fengshi and Dai Yijun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Zhou Shizhong, Xu Fuzai, and Liu Wen, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Yi Kongzhao [?], Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. Those organizing troops along the frontier included Regional Vice Commander Men Chongwen…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王詔入
賀于
朝則右布政使今陞廣西左布
政使林懋舉僉事勞堪署都
指揮僉事于一芳咸先後服
勤而試典攸賴者於法得書
直隸廣德州儒學學正楊乾
===
知謹序
punctuated:
王詔；入賀于朝，則右布政使今陞廣西左布政使林懋舉、僉事勞堪、署都指揮僉事于一芳，咸先後服勤，而試典攸賴者，於法得書。
直隸廣德州儒學學正楊乾知謹序。
translation_en:
…and Wang Zhao. Those who went to court to offer congratulations were Lin Maoju, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, now promoted to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guangxi; Lao Kan, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Yu Yifang, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. All served diligently in succession, and those upon whom the conduct of the examination depended may, according to the rules, be recorded here.
This preface was respectfully composed by Yang Qianzhi, Instructor of the Confucian School of Guangde Department, Zhili.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以前巡按御史陳道基先期
禮聘乾知及教諭劉崇禮爲
考試官教授饒應禎教諭周
德崇樂浹姚英林琛韓詩劉
汝昭爲同考試官簾以內翼
如也左布政使杜拯右布政
使陳暹司提調按察使李逢
===
時副使莫抑司監試其百執
事咸慎選以充簾以外肅如
也遂晉提學僉事樊倣所簡
士一千八百有奇鎖院三試
之遵
制拔其雋七十有五人竝錄其文
之優者以
punctuated: 以前巡按御史陳道基先期禮聘乾知及教諭劉崇禮爲考試官，教授饒應禎、教諭周德崇、樂浹、姚英、林琛、韓詩、劉汝昭爲同考試官，簾以內翼如也。左布政使杜拯、右布政使陳暹司提調，按察使李逢時、副使莫抑司監試，其百執事咸慎選以充，簾以外肅如也。遂晉提學僉事樊倣所簡士一千八百有奇，鎖院三試之，遵制拔其雋七十有五人，竝錄其文之優者以
translation_en:
…the former Regional Inspector, Chen Daoji, had in advance formally invited Qianzhi and Instructor Liu Chongli to serve as Examiners, and Professor Rao Yingzhen and Instructors Zhou Dechong, Yue Jia, Yao Ying, Lin Chen, Han Shi, and Liu Ruzhao to serve as Associate Examiners. Within the curtain, all was orderly. Left Administration Commissioner Du Zheng and Right Administration Commissioner Chen Xian managed the work of the Proctors; Surveillance Commissioner Li Fengshi and Vice Commissioner Mo Yi supervised the examination. All the subordinate functionaries were carefully selected for their duties. Outside the curtain, all was solemn and disciplined.

They then admitted the more than eighteen hundred candidates selected by Fan Fang, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner serving as Education Intendant. The examination compound was locked, and the candidates were examined in three sessions. In accordance with the imperial regulations, seventy-five outstanding candidates were selected, and the best of their examination essays were also transcribed in order to …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
獻乾知猥以職事宜序諸簡端謹
稽首颺言曰猗與休哉我
國家車書
一統之盛
皇上久道化成之效觀之粵可知
也乾知嘗讀世紀考輿圖粵
之有土在南大海之隅豈非
===
古所稱方外之區哉堯宅周
疆之迹遐逖難稽秦漢以來
置郡列藩漸稱率服然史言
其貢酎之奉不輸大內則亦
羈縻云耳延及唐宋人物浸
盛張崔諸賢德業文章蔚然
著矣然誌敘陽山猶言其晝
punctuated: 獻。乾知猥以職事，宜序諸簡端，謹稽首颺言曰：猗與休哉！我國家車書一統之盛，皇上久道化成之效，觀之粵可知也。乾知嘗讀世紀，考輿圖，粵之有土，在南大海之隅，豈非古所稱方外之區哉？堯宅周疆之迹，遐逖難稽。秦漢以來，置郡列藩，漸稱率服。然史言其貢酎之奉不輸大內，則亦羈縻云耳。延及唐宋，人物浸盛，張崔諸賢德業文章，蔚然著矣。然誌敘陽山，猶言其晝
translation_en: …for presentation. I, Qianzhi, unworthily charged with these official duties, ought to provide a preface at the beginning of this record. Reverently bowing my head, I proclaim: Ah, how splendid! The grandeur of our state's unity in carriage gauges and written script, and the transforming effects of His Majesty's long adherence to the Way, may be understood by observing Guangdong. I, Qianzhi, have read historical chronicles and examined maps. Guangdong's territory lies to the south, at the edge of the great sea: was it not what the ancients called a region beyond the bounds of civilization? Traces of the lands settled under Yao and the boundaries established under the Zhou are remote and difficult to verify. From the Qin and Han onward, commanderies and feudatory domains were established, and the region gradually came to be described as obedient to imperial authority. Yet the histories say that its contributions toward the sacrificial ale were not delivered to the imperial treasury; thus its submission amounted merely to loose control. By the Tang and Song, men of distinction grew increasingly numerous, and the virtue, achievements, and literary works of such worthies as Zhang and Cui became illustrious. Yet an account describing Yangshan still speaks of its “daytime” [?] …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
地爲字大都民間亦惟以齒
革草木珠璣犀象之屬相較
量同文之化尚未洽也
天開泰運我
明奮興
皇祖受
命造基幅幘之廣窮天際地維茲
===
嶺表遂奠雄藩而瓊南溟渤
之陬特蒙
天語稱爲奇甸有華夏之風焉山
川效靈人文勃勃乎增煥矣
聖謨弘遠投戈之暇首
詔天下建置庠序延禮學官以長
育賢才乃於甲子歲定科舉
punctuated:
地爲字，大都民間亦惟以齒革、草木、珠璣、犀象之屬相較量，同文之化尚未洽也。
天開泰運，我明奮興。皇祖受命造基，幅幘之廣，窮天際地維。茲嶺表遂奠雄藩，而瓊南溟渤之陬，特蒙天語稱爲奇甸，有華夏之風焉。山川效靈，人文勃勃乎增煥矣。聖謨弘遠，投戈之暇，首詔天下建置庠序，延禮學官，以長育賢才。乃於甲子歲定科舉
translation_en:
…on the ground to form characters [?]. For the most part, the people still measured themselves against one another solely in such things as tusks and hides, plants and trees, pearls, rhinoceroses, and elephants. The civilizing influence of a common written culture had not yet fully reached them.
Heaven inaugurated an auspicious age, and our Ming rose vigorously. The August Ancestor received Heaven’s mandate and laid the dynasty’s foundations; the breadth of its territory [?] extended to the limits of heaven and earth. Lingbiao was thus established as a mighty provincial bulwark, while Qiong, in its remote corner of the southern seas, was specially favored with imperial words calling it an extraordinary domain possessing the customs of the Chinese heartland. Mountains and rivers manifested their spiritual potency, and literary culture flourished with increasing brilliance. The sagely plans were expansive and far-reaching. In a respite from warfare, the emperor’s first command was to establish schools throughout the realm and to invite and honor education officials, thereby nurturing worthy talent. Then, in the jiazi year, he established the civil-service examination…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之法凡三年一賓興而登進
之東粵人士遂濟濟彬彬與
中州相頡頏而寶藏貢賦之
甲於天下蓋弗論已
列聖相承益敷文德惟我
皇上
聖神撫運
===
仁壽同
天四十三年以來
峻德之所潛孚
豐芑之所培植士之生於南服
者薰炙漸摩旣深且徧矧徵
諸歲德值在甲子實與
聖祖初開
punctuated:
之法，凡三年一賓興而登進之。東粵人士遂濟濟彬彬，與中州相頡頏，而寶藏貢賦之甲於天下，蓋弗論已。
列聖相承，益敷文德。惟我皇上，聖神撫運，仁壽同天。四十三年以來，峻德之所潛孚，豐芑之所培植，士之生於南服者，薰炙漸摩旣深且徧。矧徵諸歲德，值在甲子，實與聖祖初開
translation_en:
…the regulations for the examinations, whereby once every three years worthy men were received as honored guests and advanced. Thus the scholars of eastern Yue became numerous and accomplished, rivaling those of the Central Plain; that the region’s precious resources and tribute revenues ranked foremost in the realm need hardly be mentioned.
Successive sage emperors increasingly spread the influence of civil virtue. Our present Emperor, in his sagely and divine wisdom, presides over the age, his benevolence and longevity equaling Heaven’s. For forty-three years, his lofty virtue has exerted its quiet influence, and his nurturing of talent has been like the cultivation of luxuriant millet for future generations. Scholars born in the southern territories have received this formative influence both deeply and widely. Moreover, considering the auspicious character of the year, it falls in a jiazi year, corresponding precisely to the time when our sagely founding emperor first inaugurated…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
文運之期適爲符合焉夫元會
之數運行無窮甲子十二干
支之始也萬物生生變化不
匱亦皆滋萌於子出甲於甲
則逢玆歲紀實爲千百載之
一時凡在寰宇之内含精稟
氣之物莫不思呈祥露彩自
===
赴於
熙運士固天民之秀而庶類之英
者也幸際
昌時彙征而起可無舒奇吐異發
巖穴之珍以需
國家之用蒸蒸然雲合景從哉
今乾知於諸士之應舉而來
punctuated: 文運之期適爲符合焉。夫元會之數，運行無窮。甲子，十二干支之始也。萬物生生，變化不匱，亦皆滋萌於子，出甲於甲。則逢玆歲紀，實爲千百載之一時。凡在寰宇之内，含精稟氣之物，莫不思呈祥露彩，自赴於熙運。士固天民之秀，而庶類之英者也。幸際昌時，彙征而起，可無舒奇吐異，發巖穴之珍，以需國家之用，蒸蒸然雲合景從哉？今乾知於諸士之應舉而來
translation_en:
…the period when literary flourishing began, with which it happened to coincide precisely. The numerical cycles of cosmic epochs and their divisions revolve without end. Jiazi begins the twelve stems and branches [?]. All things continually give birth to new life and undergo inexhaustible transformations: they germinate at zi and break out of their husks at jia. To encounter this year is thus truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand or a hundred years. Among all things under heaven that contain vital essence and receive vital breath, none fails to wish to display auspicious signs and reveal its brilliance, coming of its own accord to share in this flourishing age.

Scholars are surely the finest of Heaven’s people and the flower of all living things. Fortunate to encounter a prosperous age, they rise and advance together. How could they fail to unfold their extraordinary talents, display their exceptional gifts, and bring forth treasures hidden in cliffs and caves to meet the state’s needs, gathering in ever-growing numbers like clouds and following like shadows?

Now I, Qianzhi, among the scholars who have come to sit the examination…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者縱觀其爲文上下古今辯
析義利醇正者經傳之發雄
博者子史之淹詳明者敷奏
之體微婉者規諷之遺雖其
命意騁辭固人人殊而不靡
不蕪不怪不削則灼灼乎若
繁星之燦浩浩乎若長江之
===
沛雝雝乎若祥鳳之和鳴所
謂連城之璧
清廟之材者非耶周南召南詩人
所以美文王之明德也文王
之化自北而南至於江漢汝
墳遵化而兎罝野人皆可爲
公侯之好仇腹心然後爲王
punctuated:
者，縱觀其爲文，上下古今，辯析義利：醇正者，經傳之發；雄博者，子史之淹；詳明者，敷奏之體；微婉者，規諷之遺。雖其命意騁辭，固人人殊，而不靡、不蕪、不怪、不削，則灼灼乎若繁星之燦，浩浩乎若長江之沛，雝雝乎若祥鳳之和鳴。所謂連城之璧、清廟之材者，非耶？
《周南》《召南》，詩人所以美文王之明德也。文王之化，自北而南，至於江漢、汝墳，遵化而兎罝野人皆可爲公侯之好仇、腹心，然後爲王
translation_en:
…surveying their compositions as a whole, I find that they range across antiquity and the present, distinguishing and analyzing moral rightness and profit. Those that are pure and correct elucidate the Classics and their commentaries; those that are vigorous and broad display profound learning in the philosophical masters and histories; those that are detailed and clear embody the manner of reports to the throne; those that are subtle and tactful preserve the legacy of admonition through indirection. Although each writer differs in conceiving ideas and deploying language, their compositions are neither florid nor overgrown, neither bizarre nor meager. They shine like a multitude of brilliant stars, surge like the mighty flow of the Yangzi, and sound harmoniously like the concordant calls of auspicious phoenixes. Are these not what are called jade discs worth a chain of cities, timbers fit for the ancestral temple?
The poets used the “Airs of Zhou and the South” and the “Airs of Shao and the South” to praise King Wen’s illustrious virtue. King Wen’s transforming influence spread from north to south, reaching the Jiang and Han rivers and the banks of the Ru. People followed this transforming influence, so that even the rustic rabbit-netters could all become worthy companions and trusted confidants of dukes and lords; only then was there the kingly …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道之成詩曰周王壽考遐不
作人此之謂也粤去
京師萬里而遠不啻江漢之於
岐豐而已
今日得士若此則
聖天子至德之化悠久不息光于
海隅洽于遠邇駕成周而追
===
===
聖祖蓋有明徵已乾知謂以粤士
而知
國家車書之盛
皇上久道之化非臆也抑猶有說
焉周家得人之盛止于九人
而九人之奮庸熙載垂聲光
於不朽者非徒以其言而已
punctuated:
道之成。詩曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」此之謂也。粤去京師萬里而遠，不啻江漢之於岐豐而已。今日得士若此，則聖天子至德之化，悠久不息，光于海隅，洽于遠邇，駕成周而追聖祖，蓋有明徵已。乾知謂以粤士而知國家車書之盛、皇上久道之化，非臆也。

抑猶有說焉。周家得人之盛，止于九人，而九人之奮庸熙載，垂聲光於不朽者，非徒以其言而已
translation_en:
…the fulfillment of the kingly Way. The Book of Odes says: “May the king of Zhou live long! Does he not nurture men of talent?” This is what it means. Guangdong lies ten thousand li from the capital, farther even than the Jiang and Han rivers lie from Qi and Feng. That men of such quality have been recruited today is clear evidence that the transforming influence of the sagely Son of Heaven’s consummate virtue endures without cease, shines upon the remotest seacoasts, and reaches far and near, surpassing the achievements of Zhou and following those of the sagely dynastic founder. Qianzhi [?] maintains that to discern, through Guangdong’s scholars, the flourishing unity of the realm—its shared carriage gauges and written script—and the transforming influence of His Majesty’s enduring Way is no mere conjecture.

Yet there is something further to say. Even at the height of the Zhou dynasty’s success in obtaining worthy men, they numbered only nine. That these nine exerted themselves in service, brought distinction to their undertakings, and bequeathed an undying reputation and glory was not owing merely to their words…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也今主司之所錄者惟言而
多士之見錄亦惟以其言使
果言皆根心而非飾辭以干
進則自茲對
大廷布有位以養萬民以楨
邦國爲
宗社樹億萬禩靈長之計諸士信
===
無負於地與時而乾知亦與
有光矣如或華其文而嗇其
實言於靜而違於庸主司不
明之罪固無所逃諸士之生
名服應
昌辰求一人之幾於九人而不可
得寧不有愧也已吁文王在
punctuated:
也。今主司之所錄者惟言，而多士之見錄亦惟以其言。使果言皆根心，而非飾辭以干進，則自茲對大廷，布有位，以養萬民，以楨邦國，爲宗社樹億萬禩靈長之計，諸士信無負於地與時，而乾知亦與有光矣。
如或華其文而嗇其實，言於靜而違於庸，主司不明之罪固無所逃。諸士之生名服應昌辰，求一人之幾於九人而不可得，寧不有愧也已？吁！文王在
translation_en:
…Now those presiding over the examination select men solely on their words, and the many scholars gain selection solely through their words. If those words truly spring from the heart, rather than being embellished phrases used to seek advancement, then henceforth these scholars may answer before the imperial court and take their places in office, nourishing the myriad people and serving as pillars of the realm. They may lay plans to secure enduring blessings for the ancestral temples and altars of state for countless ages. You scholars would then truly prove worthy of your place and time, and Qianzhi too would share in your glory.
If, however, you embellish your writing while remaining scant in substance, speaking one way in repose but acting otherwise in practice, those presiding over the examination certainly cannot escape blame for their lack of discernment. As for you scholars, born to reputation and official robes [?] and encountering this flourishing age, if not a single man approaching those nine men could be found among you, would you not feel ashamed? Ah! King Wen is…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
爲仁由己而由人乎哉
久則徵徵則悠遠悠遠則博厚博厚則高
明博厚所以載物也高明所以覆物也
悠久所以成物也博厚配地高明配天
悠久無疆
其自任以天下之重如此
易
===
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
君子之光有孚吉象曰君子之光其暉吉
也
天生神物聖人則之
易之爲書也廣大悉備有天道焉有人道
焉有地道焉兼三才而兩之故六六者
非他也三才之道也
書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣惟帝時舉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？

久則徵，徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。博厚配地，高明配天，悠久無疆。

其自任以天下之重如此。

易

大哉乾元！萬物資始，乃統天。

君子之光，有孚，吉。象曰：「君子之光，其暉吉也。」

天生神物，聖人則之。

易之爲書也，廣大悉備，有天道焉，有人道焉，有地道焉。兼三才而兩之，故六。六者，非他也，三才之道也。

書

萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣，惟帝時舉。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The practice of benevolence depends on oneself; could it depend on others?

Endurance brings manifestation; manifestation brings far-reaching duration; far-reaching duration brings breadth and depth; breadth and depth bring loftiness and luminosity. Breadth and depth serve to bear all things; loftiness and luminosity serve to shelter all things; enduring duration serves to bring all things to completion. Breadth and depth match Earth; loftiness and luminosity match Heaven; enduring duration knows no bounds.

Such was the way he took upon himself the weighty responsibility for all under Heaven.

Book of Changes (Yi)

Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things draw upon it for their beginning, and it governs Heaven.

The noble man's light: there is sincerity; good fortune. The Image Commentary says: “The noble man's light—its radiance brings good fortune.”

Heaven produces numinous objects; the sages take them as their models.

As a book, the Changes is vast and comprehensive. It contains the Way of Heaven, the Way of humanity, and the Way of Earth. It encompasses the Three Powers and doubles them, thus making six lines. These six are nothing other than the Way of the Three Powers.

Book of Documents (Shu)

The many worthy men of the myriad states are all ministers of the emperor; it is the emperor who raises them to office.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
曰天子作民父母以為天下王
小大之臣咸懷忠良
詩
采采芣苢薄言有之
旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕永錫爾極時萬時億
保玆天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
===
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
春秋
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年
公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐僖公十
punctuated:
若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。

皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光，曰：「天子作民父母，以為天下王。」

小大之臣，咸懷忠良。

詩

采采芣苢，薄言有之。

旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億，保玆天子。

生仲山甫，仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫：「式是百辟，纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。」

聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。

春秋

八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。僖公元年。

公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐。僖公十
translation_en:
“If I were making a well-seasoned soup, you would be its salt and sour plums.”

The pronouncements of the sovereign standard are enduring norms and instructions, instruction drawn from the sovereign. All the common people should learn and put into practice the pronouncements of this standard, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven. They say: “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people and thus becomes king of all under Heaven.”

Officials, both lesser and greater, all cherish loyalty and goodness.

Book of Odes

“We gather and gather the plantain; let us collect it.”

“Already orderly, already diligent, already upright, already disciplined: may you forever be granted the highest blessing, for ten thousand years, for a hundred million years, protecting this Son of Heaven.”

“Zhongshan Fu was born. Zhongshan Fu’s virtue takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing is excellent, his expression gracious; he is careful and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and strives to maintain dignified deportment. He follows the Son of Heaven, whose clear commands charge him with distributing affairs of government. The king commands Zhongshan Fu: ‘Be a model for these many lords; continue the work of your forefathers and protect the king’s person. Convey the king’s commands, reporting inward and transmitting outward; be the king’s throat and tongue. Distribute the tasks of government abroad, and the four quarters will respond.’”

“His sagely reverence rises day by day; his radiant influence reaches far and endures. He reveres the Lord on High.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

In the eighth month, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng. First year of Duke Xi.

Gongsun Ao led an army and joined the grandees of the feudal lords in relieving Xu. Duke Xi, year ten…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有五年叔孫豹及諸侯之大夫及陳袁
僑盟襄公三年
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
蕭魚楚人執鄭行人良霄俱襄公十有
一年夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子
滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐
淮夷會于申昭公四年
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田定公十年
===
禮記
以天地為本故物可舉也
朝廷之美濟濟翔翔
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之是故情深而
文明氣盛而化神和順積中而英華發
外
夫義者所以濟志也諸德之發也是故其
德盛者其志厚其志厚者其義章
punctuated:
有五年。叔孫豹及諸侯之大夫及陳袁僑盟，襄公三年。

公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。楚人執鄭行人良霄，俱襄公十有一年。夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申，昭公四年。

齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田，定公十年。

禮記

以天地為本，故物可舉也。

朝廷之美，濟濟翔翔。

詩言其志也，歌咏其聲也，舞動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。是故情深而文明，氣盛而化神，和順積中而英華發外。

夫義者，所以濟志也，諸德之發也。是故其德盛者其志厚，其志厚者其義章。
translation_en:
…the fifteenth year [of Duke Xi]. Shusun Bao joined the great officers of the various lords and Yuan Qiao of Chen in making a covenant. Third year of Duke Xiang.

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng. They assembled at Xiaoyu. The men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the envoy of Zheng. Both passages are from the eleventh year of Duke Xiang. In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquises of Cai and Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscounts of Xu, Teng, Dun, Hu, Shen, and Xiaozhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi assembled at Shen. Fourth year of Duke Zhao.

The men of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. Tenth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites

Heaven and earth are taken as the foundation; thus all things can be comprehended.

The beauty of the court lies in its dignified bearing and graceful movements.

Poetry expresses one's intentions; song gives voice to them; dance sets one's bodily bearing in motion. These three are rooted in the heart, and only then do musical instruments accompany them. Thus, when feeling is deep, its patterned expression is brilliant; when vital energy is abundant, its transforming influence is wondrous. Harmony and compliance accumulate within, and their finest flowering manifests itself without.

Righteousness is the means by which intentions are fulfilled; it is the manifestation of the virtues. Thus, those whose virtue is abundant have profound intentions, and those whose intentions are profound display righteousness clearly.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
知其性則知天
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔文帝二年
擬唐以裴耀卿為黃門侍郎張九齡為中
書侍郎並同平章事誥開元二十一年
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事富弼為樞密副
使謝表慶曆三年
===
判語五條
官員赴任過限
人戶以籍為定
致祭祀典神祇
邊境申索軍需
修理橋梁道路
第參場
策五道
問宋儒有言仁者以天地萬物為一體是
punctuated:
第貳場。
論：知其性則知天。
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔，文帝二年。
擬唐以裴耀卿為黃門侍郎、張九齡為中書侍郎，並同平章事誥，開元二十一年。
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事、富弼為樞密副使謝表，慶曆三年。
判語五條：
官員赴任過限。
人戶以籍為定。
致祭祀典神祇。
邊境申索軍需。
修理橋梁道路。
第參場。
策五道。
問：宋儒有言：「仁者以天地萬物為一體。」是
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse: To know one’s nature is to know Heaven.

One topic from among the edict, proclamation, and memorial forms [?].

Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting the people remission of half of this year’s land tax: the second year of Emperor Wen’s reign.

Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Pei Yaoqing as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Zhang Jiuling as Vice Director of the Secretariat, both concurrently Jointly Administrators of Affairs: the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan.

Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for the appointments of Fan Zhongyan as Vice Grand Councilor and Fu Bi as Military Affairs Vice Commissioner: the third year of Qingli.

Five legal judgments:
An official exceeds the prescribed time limit for taking up his post.
Households are to be determined according to the registers.
Offer sacrifices to deities included in the sacrificial canon.
Frontier areas submit requests for military supplies.
Repair bridges and roads.

Third Session

Five policy questions.

Question: A Song Confucian said, “The benevolent person regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body.” Thus …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以至德之君所以保民性命而納之壽
康者率詳且切粤觀嘗草辨味而醫藥
肇傳內經著論而方脉啓祕故當時之
民瘥札不生龐皓相踵而二君者竝躋
遐永之筭享昇平之休其應詎不章章
明哉周禮周家致太平之書也以醫職
屬之天官而其法制纖悉備具可得而
聞其詳歟嗣是而後有赦太倉令而春
和賑貸者矣有見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背
===
者矣有頒太平聖惠方有輯簡要濟衆
方者矣不知果有合於帝王之仁否歟
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝之開基也
詔郡縣贍疲民以有司之粟而醫學之設載在
令甲我
成祖文皇帝之嗣服也
命太醫院施京民以
內府之劑而惠民之
punctuated:
以至德之君所以保民性命而納之壽康者，率詳且切。粤觀嘗草辨味而醫藥肇傳，內經著論而方脉啓祕，故當時之民瘥札不生，龐皓相踵，而二君者竝躋遐永之筭，享昇平之休，其應詎不章章明哉？周禮，周家致太平之書也，以醫職屬之天官，而其法制纖悉備具，可得而聞其詳歟？嗣是而後，有赦太倉令而春和賑貸者矣，有見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背者矣，有頒太平聖惠方、有輯簡要濟衆方者矣，不知果有合於帝王之仁否歟？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝之開基也，詔郡縣贍疲民以有司之粟，而醫學之設載在令甲。我成祖文皇帝之嗣服也，命太醫院施京民以內府之劑，而惠民之
translation_en:
…Thus the measures by which rulers of consummate virtue preserved their people's lives and brought them longevity and health were generally thorough and attentive. Consider how the tasting of herbs and distinguishing of their flavors first transmitted medical knowledge, and how the discourses set forth in the Inner Canon revealed the mysteries of prescriptions and pulse diagnosis. Consequently, the people of that time suffered neither epidemics nor premature death, and white-haired elders followed one another in succession. Both rulers themselves attained great longevity and enjoyed the blessings of peace. Were these effects not abundantly clear? The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the Zhou ruling house brought about great peace. It assigns medical offices to the Ministry of Heaven, and its regulations are complete in the smallest detail. May we hear a detailed account of them? Subsequently, there were rulers who pardoned the Director of the Grand Granary and provided relief loans in the mild spring weather; rulers who, upon seeing an acupuncture and moxibustion chart, expressly prohibited flogging the back; rulers who promulgated the Prescriptions of Sagely Beneficence for Great Peace; and rulers who compiled the Concise Prescriptions for Universal Relief. Did these measures truly accord with the benevolence of sage emperors and kings?
We reverently reflect that, when our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty, he commanded prefectures and counties to support the distressed people with grain held by the responsible officials, while the establishment of medical schools was recorded in the statutes. When our Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded to the throne, he ordered the Imperial Medical Office to dispense medicines from the palace stores to the people of the capital, and the measures for benefiting the people…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
令申在禮部
仁心美政固以肇萬年靈長之基矣迨我
睿宗獻皇帝仁敷南國德合
天心醫方選要之集允爲濟民利物之寶肆我
皇上純孝體
親至仁育物特
命刋刻普錫中外所以康乂我民者亦云至矣
近又取胡濙所
進衛生簡易方梓而
===
頒之俾遠方貧窶之民咸知調治保全之道
至於藥粥之
施疾苦之
問時行屢下靡可殫述此其
仁卽
天地之仁而其
心卽
祖
考之心矣是以
punctuated: 令申在禮部。仁心美政，固以肇萬年靈長之基矣。迨我睿宗獻皇帝，仁敷南國，德合天心，《醫方選要》之集，允爲濟民利物之寶。肆我皇上純孝體親，至仁育物，特命刋刻，普錫中外，所以康乂我民者，亦云至矣。近又取胡濙所進《衛生簡易方》，梓而頒之，俾遠方貧窶之民咸知調治保全之道。至於藥粥之施、疾苦之問，時行屢下，靡可殫述。此其仁卽天地之仁，而其心卽祖考之心矣。是以
translation_en:
…the order was reiterated by the Ministry of Rites. Such benevolent intentions and excellent governance indeed laid the foundation for an enduring reign lasting ten thousand years. When our Emperor Ruizong Xian spread his benevolence throughout the southern lands, his virtue accorded with the mind of Heaven. His compilation, Selected Essentials of Medical Prescriptions (Yifang xuanyao), was truly a treasure for relieving the people and benefiting all living things. Thus our present Emperor, in his pure filial devotion, gave effect to his father's intentions and nurtured all beings with consummate benevolence. He specially commanded that the work be printed and distributed throughout the capital and the provinces. His measures to secure the health and well-being of our people may indeed be called comprehensive.

Recently, he also had Simple and Easy Prescriptions for Preserving Health (Weisheng jianyi fang), submitted by Hu Ying, printed and distributed, so that even the impoverished people of distant regions might all understand how to treat illness and preserve their health. As for the provision of medicines and gruel and inquiries into the people's illnesses and hardships, these were undertaken from time to time and repeatedly commanded, too often to recount exhaustively. His benevolence is thus the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and his heart is the heart of his ancestors and his father. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
好生之德洽于萬民
太和之氣通于
上帝愛戴之所輸
眷命之所篤
聖躬日以康寧
聖壽日以綿衍即詩所稱萬有千歲猶未足以
擬之也
宗社無疆之慶端在是矣諸士皆沐
聖皇久道之化而囿於
===
===
仁壽之域者也盍颺言之以效天保之
祝
問君子之立言將以明道也道一而已矣
則言道者宜不得異同於其間也顧世
儒之論乃人人殊何哉性命之說自子
思首發之朱子釋之曰天所賦爲命人
所受爲性矣而又曰所賦者氣所受者
理信斯言也性命固有二歟道器之說
自大易始發之程子訓之曰形而上者
punctuated:
好生之德洽于萬民，太和之氣通于上帝，愛戴之所輸，眷命之所篤，聖躬日以康寧，聖壽日以綿衍，即詩所稱「萬有千歲」，猶未足以擬之也。宗社無疆之慶端在是矣。諸士皆沐聖皇久道之化，而囿於仁壽之域者也，盍颺言之，以效天保之祝？

問：君子之立言，將以明道也。道一而已矣，則言道者宜不得異同於其間也。顧世儒之論乃人人殊，何哉？性命之說，自子思首發之，朱子釋之曰：「天所賦爲命，人所受爲性矣。」而又曰：「所賦者氣，所受者理。」信斯言也，性命固有二歟？道器之說，自大易始發之，程子訓之曰：「形而上者
translation_en:
…the virtue of cherishing life reaches all the people, and the vital energy of supreme harmony communicates with the Lord on High. With the people's love and allegiance directed toward him, and Heaven's favor and mandate firmly bestowed upon him, His Majesty grows daily healthier and more tranquil, and his allotted years extend ever further. Even the phrase “ten thousand years, a thousand years” celebrated in the Book of Odes falls short of describing his longevity. Here indeed lies the boundless good fortune of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. You scholars have all benefited from the transforming influence of our sage emperor's enduring Way and dwell within the realm of benevolence and longevity. Why not proclaim this aloud, offering blessings in the manner of the ode “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao)?

Question: When a gentleman sets forth his words, his purpose is to illuminate the Way. The Way is one and nothing more; thus those who speak of it ought not to differ in their accounts. Yet the discussions of scholars of our age vary from person to person. Why is this? The account of human nature and Heaven's decree was first expounded by Zisi. Master Zhu explained it, saying: “What Heaven bestows is called the decree; what a person receives is called human nature.” Yet he also said: “What is bestowed is vital energy; what is received is principle.” If these words are true, are human nature and Heaven's decree indeed two distinct things? The account of the Way and concrete things was first expounded in the Great Book of Changes. Master Cheng explained it, saying: “What is above form…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為理形而下者為物矣而又曰道亦器
器亦道信斯言也道器固惟一歟仁統
四端先儒論之詳矣而有以陰陽五行
四時配之者是又不以四端之統為言
何也心統性情先儒論之備矣而有以
性之有形者為心性之有動者為情是
又以性之統乎心情為言何也知者動
仁者靜則動陽而靜陰矣而解易者乃
有智為陰而仁為陽之說不與孔子之
===
言殊乎成己仁成物智則仁體而智用
矣而釋聖者乃有智自明而仁及物之
論不與子思之言悖乎盡己為忠盡物
為信忠信只一理也而又謂忠為天之
道信為人之道者則信與忠果有異乎
知以明理行以履事知行有先後也而
又謂道之不明由於行之過與不及者
則行視知果尤急耶夫道在天下自有
至當歸一之妙學以明道當得根極要
punctuated: 為理，形而下者為物矣，而又曰：「道亦器，器亦道。」信斯言也，道器固惟一歟？仁統四端，先儒論之詳矣，而有以陰陽五行四時配之者，是又不以四端之統為言，何也？心統性情，先儒論之備矣，而有以性之有形者為心，性之有動者為情，是又以性之統乎心情為言，何也？知者動，仁者靜，則動陽而靜陰矣，而解易者乃有智為陰而仁為陽之說，不與孔子之言殊乎？成己仁，成物智，則仁體而智用矣，而釋聖者乃有智自明而仁及物之論，不與子思之言悖乎？盡己為忠，盡物為信，忠信只一理也，而又謂忠為天之道，信為人之道者，則信與忠果有異乎？知以明理，行以履事，知行有先後也，而又謂道之不明由於行之過與不及者，則行視知果尤急耶？夫道在天下，自有至當歸一之妙，學以明道，當得根極要
translation_en:
…is principle, and what is below form is concrete things.” Yet he also said: “The Way is also concrete things; concrete things are also the Way.” If these words are true, are the Way and concrete things indeed only one? Earlier Confucian scholars discussed in detail how benevolence governs the four beginnings. Yet some correlate it with yin and yang, the Five Phases, and the four seasons, thus speaking of it without reference to its governance of the four beginnings. Why is this? Earlier Confucian scholars discussed fully how the mind governs nature and feelings. Yet some identify the mind as nature possessing form, and feelings as nature in motion, thus speaking instead of nature as governing the mind and feelings. Why is this?
“The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” Thus activity is yang and stillness is yin. Yet interpreters of the Book of Changes maintain that wisdom is yin and benevolence is yang. Does this not differ from the words of Kongzi? “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” Thus benevolence is substance and wisdom is function. Yet those who expound the sages maintain that wisdom brings illumination to oneself while benevolence extends to other things. Does this not contradict the words of Zisi? To fulfill oneself completely is conscientiousness; to fulfill things completely is trustworthiness. Conscientiousness and trustworthiness are but one principle. Yet some also say that conscientiousness is the Way of Heaven and trustworthiness the way of human beings. Are trustworthiness and conscientiousness, then, really different?
Knowledge serves to illuminate principle; action serves to carry out affairs. Knowledge and action have their order of precedence. Yet some also say that the Way is not understood because action goes too far or falls short. Is action, then, truly more urgent than knowledge? Now the Way in the world inherently possesses the subtle capacity to attain perfect appropriateness and converge upon unity. Learning serves to illuminate the Way, and ought to arrive at an account of its ultimate foundations and essential…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
領之論衆言殽亂將安折衷乎諸士其
必有知言窮理之學而不惑於異同之
說者試詳言之以占所養
問用兵者必訓練之有素然後可以應變
而威敵陣法固不可不講也周禮大司
馬萬有二千五百人爲軍小司徒乃會
萬民之卒旅而用之至於春敎振旅夏
敎茇舍秋冬敎大閱治兵並如戰之陳
則營陣有定制矣嗣後兵家相傳謂黃
===
帝立丘井以制兵爲八陣之圖列之爲
天地風雲變之爲虎蛇龍鳥其說載于
握奇篇者詳矣然其義果何所取歟古
之用圖以致勝者亦可指而言之歟漢
時嘗令敷演陣法習之於長樂館矣不
知果合於圖否也精於圖義者莫如諸
葛亮史稱其魚復平沙之上壘石爲行
蓋森然備矣或謂其爲常山蛇勢然歟
否歟至唐李靖用之則更其制而爲六
punctuated:
領之論，衆言殽亂，將安折衷乎？諸士其必有知言窮理之學，而不惑於異同之說者，試詳言之，以占所養。

問：用兵者必訓練之有素，然後可以應變而威敵，陣法固不可不講也。《周禮》，大司馬萬有二千五百人爲軍，小司徒乃會萬民之卒旅而用之。至於春敎振旅，夏敎茇舍，秋冬敎大閱、治兵，並如戰之陳，則營陣有定制矣。嗣後兵家相傳，謂黃帝立丘井以制兵，爲八陣之圖，列之爲天地風雲，變之爲虎蛇龍鳥。其說載于《握奇篇》者詳矣，然其義果何所取歟？古之用圖以致勝者，亦可指而言之歟？漢時嘗令敷演陣法，習之於長樂館矣，不知果合於圖否也。精於圖義者莫如諸葛亮，史稱其魚復平沙之上壘石爲行，蓋森然備矣。或謂其爲常山蛇勢，然歟否歟？至唐李靖用之，則更其制而爲六
translation_en:
…an exposition of the essential principles. When the many opinions are confused and conflicting, how is one to adjudicate among them? You gentlemen surely possess the learning needed to discern the meaning of words and investigate principles, without being bewildered by convergent and divergent doctrines. Explain this in detail, so that we may assess what you have cultivated.

Question: Those who employ troops must first have trained them thoroughly; only then can they respond to changing circumstances and overawe the enemy. Methods of battle formation certainly cannot go unstudied. In the Rites of Zhou, under the Minister of War (Da Sima), twelve thousand five hundred men constitute an army; the Vice Minister of Education (Xiao Situ) assembles the companies and battalions of the populace and employs them. As for instruction in spring in mustering troops, in summer in encampment, and in autumn and winter in the grand review and ordering troops, all follow the dispositions used in battle. Thus camps and battle formations had established regulations. Subsequently, military specialists transmitted the account that Huangdi established the qiu and jing land divisions to organize troops and made diagrams of the Eight Formations. Their arrangements were Heaven, Earth, Wind, and Cloud, and their transformations were Tiger, Snake, Dragon, and Bird. The account recorded in the Treatise on Grasping the Extraordinary (Wo qi pian) is detailed, but from what, precisely, are its principles derived? Can instances from antiquity in which these diagrams were used to achieve victory also be identified and discussed?

During the Han, orders were once given to demonstrate and elaborate methods of formation and to practise them at Changle Hall. Yet we do not know whether these actually accorded with the diagrams. None understood the principles of the diagrams more thoroughly than Zhuge Liang. The histories relate that he piled stones in rows on the level sands at Yufu, where the formations stood arrayed in imposing completeness. Some say that this was the disposition of the snake of Mount Changshan. Is that so or not? When Li Jing employed it in the Tang, he altered its arrangement to make the Six…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
花陣夫八陣即九軍也爲方陣六花即
七軍也爲圓陣似不相蒙矣而謂爲亮
之舊何也兵之數必起於五守則爲營
戰則爲陣奇正相生分合時異然後可
以取勝則教練之法宜莫如圖矣而或
者乃謂古法之環曲者所以固拒後世
之直銳者所以克捷則圖亦有不盡用
歟世之名將如睢陽之善守武穆之善
戰乃云不依古法教戰陣又謂運用之
===
妙在於一心則陣法似又所當略矣其
言果一定而可從歟方今嶺海多警帷
幄資籌則茲亦在所急者願諸士抵掌
談之毋曰軍旅之事未之學也
問記曰今人與居古人與稽則論世固儒
者事也況居其鄉而景其人私淑爲尤
切者乎嶺表百粤之區人文攸萃今考
誌牒所載其經術文章行誼政事之知
名者試舉與諸士評之有進春秋微由
punctuated:
花陣。夫八陣即九軍也，爲方陣；六花即七軍也，爲圓陣。似不相蒙矣，而謂爲亮之舊，何也？兵之數必起於五，守則爲營，戰則爲陣，奇正相生，分合時異，然後可以取勝，則教練之法宜莫如圖矣。而或者乃謂古法之環曲者所以固拒，後世之直銳者所以克捷，則圖亦有不盡用歟？世之名將，如睢陽之善守、武穆之善戰，乃云不依古法教戰陣，又謂運用之妙在於一心，則陣法似又所當略矣。其言果一定而可從歟？方今嶺海多警，帷幄資籌，則茲亦在所急者。願諸士抵掌談之，毋曰軍旅之事未之學也。

問：記曰：「今人與居，古人與稽。」則論世固儒者事也，況居其鄉而景其人，私淑爲尤切者乎？嶺表百粤之區，人文攸萃。今考誌牒所載，其經術、文章、行誼、政事之知名者，試舉與諸士評之。有進《春秋微由》
translation_en:
…Flower Formation. The Eight Formations comprise nine armies and make a square formation; the Six Flowers comprise seven armies and make a circular formation. They appear not to correspond, so why is the latter said to preserve Zhuge Liang’s original arrangement? The numerical organization of troops must begin with five. On the defensive they form encampments; in battle they form arrays. Unorthodox and orthodox methods generate one another, and dispersal and concentration vary with circumstances; only then can victory be secured. Thus, for training troops, surely nothing should surpass the formation diagrams. Yet some say that the curved configurations of ancient methods served to hold firm against attack, whereas the straight, pointed configurations of later ages served to win swift victories. Does this mean that the diagrams are not applicable in every respect? Such renowned commanders as the skilled defender of Suiyang and Wumu [Yue Fei], so adept in battle, nevertheless spoke of not following ancient methods in teaching battle formations. It was also said that the subtlety of employing them rests entirely in the mind. This would seem to suggest that prescribed formations should receive little attention. Are these statements truly definitive and worthy of being followed? At present, alarms are frequent in Linghai, and military headquarters require strategic counsel: this, too, is therefore an urgent matter. I hope that you gentlemen will discuss it spiritedly, and not say that you have never studied military affairs.

Question: The Record says: “Live among the people of the present; seek understanding from the people of antiquity.” Assessing past ages is certainly the scholar’s business. How much more pressing, then, is learning from the example of a predecessor when one lives in his native region and admires him? Lingbiao, the region of the many Yue peoples, is a place where cultural accomplishment flourishes. Examining now the accounts in gazetteers and other records, let us select those renowned for classical scholarship, literary composition, moral conduct, and government service, and discuss them with you gentlemen. There was one who submitted Subtleties of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu weiyou [?])…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者有請立左氏博士者有通毛詩三禮
春秋而屢薦不出者有講五經進易解
而時論不向者可謂精於經術矣有獻
獄空年豐賦頌者有作異物誌水土記
者有作廣樂記太常釋義者有登科作
賦稱李伯夷者可謂富於文章矣至於
當宋儒倡明正學之時又有能聞庸學
述語孟者有師朱子而篤志力學一意
實踐者有師南軒而講明性理學慕濂
===
洛者視前數子又果為孰優歟有因姓
而嶺邑以之著名山陂以之表異者有
因孝而里以參號湖以曾子稱者有名
奉化鄉慕德里者有名慈廉江義江者
其行誼亦云偉矣有正色立朝人薦其
才堪大用者有提刑明允人贈以清通
仁厚者有以能吏顯者有以良吏聞者
其政事亦云傑矣及觀李鼎英稱張姜
劉三人于唐陳璉取余崔二人于宋比
punctuated: 者，有請立左氏博士者，有通《毛詩》、三禮、《春秋》而屢薦不出者，有講五經、進《易解》而時論不向者，可謂精於經術矣。有獻獄空年豐賦頌者，有作《異物誌》《水土記》者，有作《廣樂記》《太常釋義》者，有登科作賦稱李伯夷者，可謂富於文章矣。至於當宋儒倡明正學之時，又有能聞庸學、述語孟者，有師朱子而篤志力學、一意實踐者，有師南軒而講明性理、學慕濂洛者，視前數子，又果為孰優歟？有因姓而嶺邑以之著名、山陂以之表異者，有因孝而里以參號、湖以曾子稱者，有名奉化鄉慕德里者，有名慈廉江義江者，其行誼亦云偉矣。有正色立朝，人薦其才堪大用者，有提刑明允，人贈以清通仁厚者，有以能吏顯者，有以良吏聞者，其政事亦云傑矣。及觀李鼎英稱張姜劉三人于唐，陳璉取余崔二人于宋，比
translation_en:
…; there was one who petitioned for the establishment of an Erudite for the Zuo Commentary; one who mastered the Mao Odes, the Three Ritual Classics, and the Spring and Autumn Annals, yet repeatedly declined to enter service when recommended; and one who lectured on the Five Classics and presented an Explanation of the Changes, yet did not find favor with contemporary opinion. These men may be called accomplished in classical scholarship. There were those who presented rhapsodies and eulogies celebrating empty prisons and abundant harvests; those who composed Records of Unusual Things and Records of Waters and Lands; those who composed Records of Expanded Music and Explanations of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and one who passed the examination and composed rhapsodies, earning the appellation “Li Boyi” [?]. These men may be called prolific in literary composition. Then, when the Confucian scholars of the Song were promoting and elucidating orthodox learning, there were those who received teachings on the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning and expounded the Analects and the Mencius; one who studied under Master Zhu, pursued learning with firm resolve and strenuous effort, and devoted himself wholeheartedly to putting it into practice; and one who studied under Nanxuan, elucidated human nature and principle, and modeled his learning on the masters of Lian and Luo. Compared with the preceding scholars, who indeed was superior?
There were men whose surnames made prefectures or counties in Lingnan famous and gave mountains and slopes their distinctive names; men whose filial devotion caused a neighborhood to be named Shen and a lake to be called Zengzi; men who gave their names to Fenghua Township and Mude Neighborhood; and men who gave their names to the Cilian and Yi rivers. Their conduct and moral integrity may indeed be called magnificent. There was one who stood at court with a solemn demeanor and whose talents others recommended as worthy of great employment; one who administered judicial affairs with discernment and fairness and whom others honored as “incorruptible, discerning, benevolent, and generous”; one renowned as a capable official; and one known as a good official. Their achievements in government may indeed be called outstanding. Now, considering that Li Dingying commended the three men Zhang, Jiang, and Liu of the Tang, and Chen Lian selected the two men Yu and Cui of the Song, compared with …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
前數人又果為孰勝歟逮我
明興治化隆洽人才輩出其克繼前脩而足垂
後範者固班班可紀也諸子尚稽述而
品第之以觀尚友之學毋曰是一鄉之
善士而已
問東廣嶺海之隩區也倭夷山寇頻年告
擾至厪
當宁宵旰之憂近者仰仗
皇威爰加勦蕩然虜情叵測內備當嚴則為地
===
方計靖安者不得不於兵食亟圖之也
廣之兵衛所額戍之外繼之以民壯矣
繼之以打手矣繼之以哨兵矣然空虛
如故防禦罕聞其故何歟至於土兵之
調適進狼之隱憂募充之徒起弄潢之
明釁則兵之足當何道以致之也廣之
食軍民稅糧之外益之以工食矣益之
以舶利矣益之以橋稅矣然支給不時
匱乏屢告其故何歟至於
punctuated:
前數人，又果為孰勝歟？逮我明興，治化隆洽，人才輩出，其克繼前脩而足垂後範者，固班班可紀也。諸子尚稽述而品第之，以觀尚友之學，毋曰是一鄉之善士而已。
問：東廣，嶺海之隩區也。倭夷山寇，頻年告擾，至厪當宁宵旰之憂。近者仰仗皇威，爰加勦蕩。然虜情叵測，內備當嚴，則為地方計靖安者，不得不於兵食亟圖之也。廣之兵，衛所額戍之外，繼之以民壯矣，繼之以打手矣，繼之以哨兵矣，然空虛如故，防禦罕聞，其故何歟？至於土兵之調，適進狼之隱憂；募充之徒，起弄潢之明釁，則兵之足當何道以致之也？廣之食，軍民稅糧之外，益之以工食矣，益之以舶利矣，益之以橋稅矣，然支給不時，匱乏屢告，其故何歟？至於
translation_en:
…compared with the several men mentioned earlier, who indeed was superior? When our Ming dynasty arose, good government and civilizing influence flourished widely, and talented men emerged in succession. Those who could carry on the achievements of earlier worthies and leave models for later generations are certainly numerous and worthy of record. You candidates should examine and recount their deeds and rank them, thereby demonstrating your learning in befriending the worthy men of the past. Do not say that these were merely good men of a single locality.
Question: Eastern Guangdong is a sheltered region amid the mountains and seas. Japanese raiders and mountain bandits have caused disturbances year after year, even burdening His Majesty with cares that keep him awake before dawn and delay his meals until late in the day. Recently, relying upon imperial might, we have undertaken campaigns to eradicate them. Yet the enemy’s intentions are unfathomable, and internal defenses must be strict. Those planning for peace and security in the region must therefore urgently devise measures concerning troops and provisions.
As for Guangdong’s troops, beyond the prescribed garrison complements of the guards and battalions, local militiamen have been added, then fighting men, and then patrol troops. Yet the ranks remain as depleted as before, and effective defense is seldom heard of. Why is this? Moreover, calling up native troops only brings the hidden danger of admitting wolves, while the men recruited into the ranks openly provoke armed disorder [?]. By what means, then, can an adequate supply of troops be secured?
As for Guangdong’s provisions, beyond the grain taxes of military and civilian households, funds for wages and rations have been added, along with revenues from maritime trade and bridge taxes. Yet disbursements are not timely, and shortages are repeatedly reported. Why is this? As for…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
内帑之疏留恐非常久可繼之事市墟之雜
課祗生箕斂無益之姦則食之足當何
計以臻之也議者欲立團保以集鄉兵
刷屯鹽以收額利不知於古法果有合
而於時事果有濟否歟諸士抱剝膚之
虞思寧宇之策其必籌之熟矣幸明以
告我
punctuated: 内帑之疏留，恐非常久可繼之事；市墟之雜課，祗生箕斂無益之姦。則食之足，當何計以臻之也？議者欲立團保以集鄉兵，刷屯鹽以收額利，不知於古法果有合，而於時事果有濟否歟？諸士抱剝膚之虞，思寧宇之策，其必籌之熟矣。幸明以告我。
translation_en: …as for petitioning to retain funds destined for the imperial treasury, this may not be a practice that can be sustained indefinitely; miscellaneous market levies merely foster abuses of excessive exaction without bringing any benefit. By what plan, then, can sufficient provisions be secured? Some propose establishing local defense associations to assemble village troops, and auditing military agricultural colonies and salt revenues to collect the prescribed receipts. Would these measures truly accord with ancient methods and meet present needs? You gentlemen, apprehensive of dangers that threaten you personally and pondering plans to bring peace to the land, must surely have considered these matters thoroughly. Please explain them clearly to me.
