title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
爲仁由己而由人乎哉
李成性
同考試官教諭林批
此篇塲中作者多掇拾
套語且以己之克禮之復對講殊失口氣此作體
認眞切而措詞雅健非苟作者宜錄以式
同考試官教授饒批
渾融典雅發出其機在
我而無難之意殆盡非俗學可到
===
考試官教諭劉批
整潔深邃是亦有得於
心學者
考試官學正楊批
善發聖人告顏子之旨
聖人決爲仁之機在於己示大賢以心學也蓋
仁心德也爲之在我夫何難之有哉夫子告顏
淵之意謂夫學莫要於爲仁機惟決於在己自
今觀之仁通於天下之大宜有所待而後足而
效收於一日之速若有所資而後成矣殊不知
仁者心之理也還吾所固有之理斯有欲之則
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？」
李成性

同考試官教諭林批：此篇塲中作者多掇拾套語，且以己之克、禮之復對講，殊失口氣。此作體認眞切，而措詞雅健，非苟作者，宜錄以式。

同考試官教授饒批：渾融典雅，發出其機在我而無難之意殆盡，非俗學可到。

考試官教諭劉批：整潔深邃，是亦有得於心學者。

考試官學正楊批：善發聖人告顏子之旨。

聖人決爲仁之機在於己，示大賢以心學也。蓋仁，心德也；爲之在我，夫何難之有哉？夫子告顏淵之意，謂夫學莫要於爲仁，機惟決於在己。自今觀之，仁通於天下之大，宜有所待而後足；而效收於一日之速，若有所資而後成矣。殊不知，仁者，心之理也。還吾所固有之理，斯有欲之則
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Practicing benevolence depends on oneself; could it depend on others?”
Li Chengxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Among those who wrote on this topic in the examination, many merely pieced together stock phrases. Moreover, they treated overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety as parallel propositions, quite missing the tenor of the original words. This composition shows a genuine and penetrating understanding, expressed in elegant and vigorous language. It is no careless piece and should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Professor: Integrated, harmonious, and classically elegant, it brings out almost exhaustively the idea that the decisive agency lies in oneself and that there is no difficulty. This is beyond the reach of commonplace scholarship.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Orderly, polished, and profound: this, too, is the work of someone who has gained insight into the learning of the mind.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: It ably elucidates the purport of the Sage’s words to Master Yan.

The Sage established that the decisive agency in practicing benevolence lies in oneself, thereby revealing the learning of the mind to a man of great worth. For benevolence is the virtue of the mind. Its practice rests with me: what difficulty could there be? The meaning of the Master’s words to Yan Yuan was that nothing in learning is more essential than practicing benevolence, and that its decisive agency rests solely with oneself. Viewed from our present standpoint, benevolence extends throughout the vastness of all under Heaven, so it would seem to require something further before it can be complete. Yet its effects are attained within the brief span of a single day, as though some assistance were required for its accomplishment. This wholly overlooks the fact that benevolence is the principle of the mind. Restore the principle inherently possessed within oneself, and there is then the ‘if one desires it, then…’

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
得之妙為仁者吾之心也求吾所自有之心即
有操之則存之神公之與私相為倚伏去私以
全乎公其省察之也由已之心耳果何容於人
之用其力理之與欲相為出入遏欲以全乎理
其克治之也由已之心耳果何藉於人之預其
功以一心之小而體仁道之大豈不至易而天
下之歸蓋自得於近取之餘矣以一念之微而
會仁道之全豈曰難能而一日之效蓋無俟於
遠求之勞矣是雖善取諸人其功之所進非不
===
賴於有相而理足於已其機之所决則在我而
有餘也回也其知所以自任哉抑是道也惟顏
子足以發之請事斯語之後蓋已默識其全體
既竭吾才而三月不違進於是矣此固天德之
純而王道之基也他日為邦之問夫子復斟酌
禮樂以告之則體用全而聖學備矣然則吾人
欲求其要豈有他哉亦曰求之於心始得
久則徵徵則悠遠悠遠則博厚博厚則高
明博厚所以載物也高明所以覆物也
punctuated:
得之妙。為仁者，吾之心也；求吾所自有之心，即有操之則存之神。公之與私，相為倚伏；去私以全乎公，其省察之也，由已之心耳，果何容於人之用其力？理之與欲，相為出入；遏欲以全乎理，其克治之也，由已之心耳，果何藉於人之預其功？以一心之小而體仁道之大，豈不至易？而天下之歸，蓋自得於近取之餘矣。以一念之微而會仁道之全，豈曰難能？而一日之效，蓋無俟於遠求之勞矣。是雖善取諸人，其功之所進，非不賴於有相；而理足於已，其機之所决，則在我而有餘也。回也，其知所以自任哉！抑是道也，惟顏子足以發之。「請事斯語」之後，蓋已默識其全體；既竭吾才而三月不違，進於是矣。此固天德之純而王道之基也。他日為邦之問，夫子復斟酌禮樂以告之，則體用全而聖學備矣。然則吾人欲求其要，豈有他哉？亦曰求之於心始得。

久則徵，徵則悠遠，悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也。
translation_en:
…the wondrous efficacy of obtaining it. It is my own heart that practices humaneness; seeking the heart that I already possess brings the marvelous efficacy of its remaining present when held fast. Public-mindedness and selfishness alternately rise and fall. To remove selfishness and preserve public-mindedness wholly, the work of scrutiny and reflection depends solely on one’s own heart: what room is there for another person to exert effort? Principle and desire alternately enter and depart. To restrain desire and preserve principle wholly, the work of overcoming and governing oneself depends solely on one’s own heart: why should one rely on another person’s contribution? To embody the vast Way of humaneness within a single small heart—is this not supremely easy? And the whole world’s turning toward humaneness follows naturally from seeking what lies close at hand. To comprehend the entirety of the Way of humaneness within a single subtle thought—how could this be called difficult? Its accomplishment in a single day requires no laborious search afar. Although one is adept at drawing upon others, and progress in this work does indeed depend upon assistance, principle is fully present within oneself. The decisive impulse thus lies in oneself, with more than enough capacity to act. Hui, surely you understand how to take this responsibility upon yourself!

Yet only Master Yan could fully bring this Way to light. After saying, “I beg to put these words into practice,” he had already silently apprehended its entirety. Having “exhausted all my abilities” and gone “three months without departing from humaneness,” he had advanced to this point. This is indeed the purity of Heaven’s virtue and the foundation of the Kingly Way. When, on another occasion, he asked about governing a state, the Master again weighed ritual and music in instructing him. Thus substance and function were made whole, and the learning of the sages was complete. If we wish to seek its essentials, then, could there be any other means? We can only say: seek them within the heart, and only then will you attain them.

Endurance brings manifestation; manifestation brings far-reaching duration; far-reaching duration brings breadth and depth; breadth and depth bring loftiness and brilliance. Breadth and depth are the means by which things are sustained; loftiness and brilliance are the means by which things are sheltered.…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
悠乆所以成物也博厚配地高明配天
悠乆無疆
梁譽
同考試官教諭樂批長題不難於敷演而難
於收拾此作意無滲漏而詞獨簡潔俗套為之一
洗耳是文之可式者
同考試官教諭周批認理明確而措詞雅健
讀之宛然子思發明天道口氣佳作也
考試官教諭劉批渾融得旨
===
考試官學正楊批瑩淨無瑕
至誠有恒之業與天地參者也夫至誠之心本
與天地而無間也則其業之發於外有不參於
天地者哉中庸此章言天道也若曰法象莫大
於天地功業莫大於聖人而要之一誠足以貫
之也今至誠不息而乆矣吾見實心之蘊也旣
緝熈於有常則實理之著也必發揮於事業寧
有乆而不徵者乎徵則有漸之化永賴之功亘
萬古而常存焉斯其悠遠也已悠遠則其積也
punctuated:
悠乆所以成物也。博厚配地，高明配天，悠乆無疆。

梁譽

同考試官教諭樂批：「長題不難於敷演，而難於收拾。此作意無滲漏，而詞獨簡潔，俗套為之一洗耳，是文之可式者。」

同考試官教諭周批：「認理明確，而措詞雅健，讀之宛然子思發明天道口氣，佳作也。」

考試官教諭劉批：「渾融得旨。」

考試官學正楊批：「瑩淨無瑕。」

至誠有恒之業，與天地參者也。夫至誠之心，本與天地而無間也，則其業之發於外，有不參於天地者哉？中庸此章言天道也。若曰：法象莫大於天地，功業莫大於聖人，而要之，一誠足以貫之也。今至誠不息而乆矣，吾見實心之蘊也，旣緝熈於有常，則實理之著也，必發揮於事業，寧有乆而不徵者乎？徵則有漸之化、永賴之功，亘萬古而常存焉，斯其悠遠也已。悠遠則其積也
translation_en:
…Enduring constancy is the means by which things are brought to completion. Breadth and depth match Earth; height and brightness match Heaven; enduring constancy is without bounds.

Liang Yu 梁譽

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor: “With a long topic, the difficulty lies not in elaborating it but in drawing it together. This composition leaves no gaps in its meaning, while its wording is exceptionally concise and lucid. It sweeps away conventional formulas and is a composition that can serve as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Its grasp of principle is clear and precise, and its phrasing elegant and vigorous. Reading it, one seems to hear Zisi himself elucidating the Way of Heaven. An excellent composition.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Seamlessly integrated, it captures the essential meaning.”

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “Luminous, pure, and flawless.”

The enduring achievements of utmost sincerity stand alongside Heaven and Earth. The mind of utmost sincerity is fundamentally inseparable from Heaven and Earth; could its achievements, manifested outwardly, fail to stand alongside them? This chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the Way of Heaven. It is as if to say: among models to emulate, none is greater than Heaven and Earth; among accomplishments, none is greater than those of the sage. Yet, in essence, sincerity alone suffices to run through them all. Now utmost sincerity continues unceasingly and endures. I see that, once what is contained within the true mind has been continuously cultivated and illuminated with constancy, the manifestation of true principle must find expression in practical achievements. Could anything endure without becoming manifest? Once manifest, its gradual transforming influence and the accomplishments upon which people forever rely persist through all ages. This is its far-reaching duration. With far-reaching duration, what it accumulates…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
浩蕩之仁磅礴之澤盡一世而甄陶焉斯其博
厚也已博厚則其發也峻極之烈光被之休貫
百王而獨盛焉斯其高明也已至誠之業如此
則天地之體用已全具而不遺矣而有不同於
天地耶蓋覆載萬物而各底于成者天地之用
也至誠之博厚而物由此載焉高明而物由此
覆焉悠久而物由此成焉大用之顯行與天地
之化育者同流於上下建之而非有所悖矣至
誠久道之用孰非天地之用乎博厚高明而恒
===
久不已者天地之體也至誠之足以載物則博
厚一地焉足以覆物則高明一天焉足以成物
則悠久一無疆焉全體之極盛與天地之奠位
者並立於兩間合之而非有所強矣至誠久道
之體孰非天地之體乎夫觀至誠功業之極其
盛如此大哉誠乎斯其至矣雖然聖人固可同
于天地而天地不能無賴于聖人蓋聖人出入
造化而為天地立心者也使天地而非至誠以
相之則無以成其能而造化不幾于息乎此裁
punctuated:
浩蕩之仁，磅礴之澤，盡一世而甄陶焉，斯其博厚也已。博厚則其發也，峻極之烈，光被之休，貫百王而獨盛焉，斯其高明也已。至誠之業如此，則天地之體用已全具而不遺矣，而有不同於天地耶？蓋覆載萬物而各底于成者，天地之用也。至誠之博厚，而物由此載焉；高明，而物由此覆焉；悠久，而物由此成焉。大用之顯行，與天地之化育者同流，於上下建之而非有所悖矣。至誠久道之用，孰非天地之用乎？博厚高明而恒久不已者，天地之體也。至誠之足以載物，則博厚一地焉；足以覆物，則高明一天焉；足以成物，則悠久一無疆焉。全體之極盛，與天地之奠位者並立，於兩間合之而非有所強矣。至誠久道之體，孰非天地之體乎？夫觀至誠功業之極，其盛如此，大哉誠乎！斯其至矣。

雖然，聖人固可同于天地，而天地不能無賴于聖人。蓋聖人出入造化而為天地立心者也。使天地而非至誠以相之，則無以成其能，而造化不幾于息乎？此裁
translation_en:
…vast benevolence and all-pervading beneficence mold and nurture an entire generation: this is its breadth and depth. With breadth and depth, its manifestations are achievements of towering eminence and blessings whose radiance reaches everywhere, surpassing those of a hundred kings: this is its loftiness and luminosity. Such are the accomplishments of utmost sincerity. The substance and functioning of Heaven and Earth are thus fully present, with nothing omitted. How, then, could it differ from Heaven and Earth? To shelter and support the myriad things and bring each to fulfillment is the functioning of Heaven and Earth. Through the breadth and depth of utmost sincerity, things are supported; through its loftiness and luminosity, things are sheltered; through its enduring constancy, things are brought to fulfillment. Its great functioning, manifest in action, flows together with the transforming and nourishing activity of Heaven and Earth. Established above and below, it entails no contradiction. What aspect of the functioning of utmost sincerity’s enduring Way is not the functioning of Heaven and Earth? Breadth and depth, loftiness and luminosity, enduring without cessation: these are the substance of Heaven and Earth. In its capacity to support things, utmost sincerity is one with Earth in breadth and depth; in its capacity to shelter things, it is one with Heaven in loftiness and luminosity; in its capacity to bring things to fulfillment, it is one with the boundless in enduring constancy. Its whole substance, in its fullest flourishing, stands alongside Heaven and Earth established in their positions. United with them within the space between Heaven and Earth, it involves nothing forced. What aspect of the substance of utmost sincerity’s enduring Way is not the substance of Heaven and Earth? Consider the ultimate accomplishments of utmost sincerity: such is their abundance. Great indeed is sincerity! Here it reaches its utmost perfection.

Nevertheless, while the sage can indeed be equal to Heaven and Earth, Heaven and Earth cannot dispense with their reliance upon the sage. For the sage moves within and beyond the processes of creation and transformation and establishes a mind for Heaven and Earth. Were Heaven and Earth without utmost sincerity to assist them, they would have no means of fulfilling their capacities. Would creation and transformation not then come close to ceasing? This ordering…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
成輔相所以賛化育之不及而得一以清得一
以寧者莫非中和之所致也不然何以曰聖人
天地之用
其自任以天下之重如此
陳法
同考試官教諭姚批伊尹濟世之心因遇湯
可爲堯舜之君足以行己所樂之道故慨然自任
此作發揮得旨而格調高朗詞氣充揚讀之一唱
三嘆真傑作也他日必能辦天下之事者
===
考試官教諭劉批高明之識充健之才
考試官學正楊批得趣之文沛然理順
大賢推聖臣自負之重以明其始進之必正也
蓋天下至大也聖臣以之爲已責則所以自任
者誠重矣其肯苟于始進乎哉想昔伊尹樂道
畝畝之中既抱夫天民先覺之具值湯三聘之
日又逢夫親見堯舜之時其相須爲甚殷矣而
尹之自任者何如哉匹夫匹婦分至微也而引
之爲已辜充其量之所包必欲盡萬民而俾乂
punctuated:
成輔相，所以賛化育之不及，而得一以清、得一以寧者，莫非中和之所致也。不然，何以曰聖人天地之用？

其自任以天下之重如此。

陳法

同考試官教諭姚批：伊尹濟世之心，因遇湯可爲堯舜之君，足以行己所樂之道，故慨然自任。此作發揮得旨，而格調高朗，詞氣充揚，讀之一唱三嘆，真傑作也。他日必能辦天下之事者。

考試官教諭劉批：高明之識，充健之才。

考試官學正楊批：得趣之文，沛然理順。

大賢推聖臣自負之重，以明其始進之必正也。蓋天下至大也，聖臣以之爲已責，則所以自任者誠重矣，其肯苟于始進乎哉？想昔伊尹樂道畝畝之中，既抱夫天民先覺之具，值湯三聘之日，又逢夫親見堯舜之時，其相須爲甚殷矣。而尹之自任者何如哉？匹夫匹婦，分至微也，而引之爲已辜。充其量之所包，必欲盡萬民而俾乂
translation_en:
…completing and assisting their operations: this supplements what the transforming and nurturing powers leave unfulfilled. That heaven attains unity and thereby becomes clear, and earth attains unity and thereby becomes tranquil, is entirely brought about by equilibrium and harmony. Otherwise, why say that the sage is the agency through which heaven and earth function?

“Such was the weight of responsibility for the world that he took upon himself.”

Chen Fa

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: Yi Yin’s desire to save the age found its occasion in his encounter with Tang, who could become a ruler like Yao or Shun and enable him to practice the Way in which he delighted. Thus he resolutely took the responsibility upon himself. This composition develops that meaning accurately; its style is lofty and lucid, its language and force abundant and soaring. Reading it, one sings once and sighs three times in admiration: truly a masterpiece. Its author will surely be capable of managing the affairs of the world in days to come.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Lofty and discerning judgment; abundant and vigorous talent.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: A composition that captures the essential import, flowing abundantly with coherent reasoning.

The great worthy expounds the weight of responsibility that the sagely minister assumed, thereby making clear that his initial entry into service necessarily had to be correct. The world is vast indeed. When a sagely minister takes it as his own responsibility, the burden he assumes is truly weighty. How could he be willing to be careless in first entering service? Consider Yi Yin of old, delighting in the Way amid the fields [?]. He already possessed the qualities of one of Heaven’s people who had awakened before others. When Tang invited him three times, he also encountered an opportunity to see a Yao or Shun in person. Their need for one another was therefore most pressing. But what was the responsibility that Yin took upon himself? An ordinary man or woman occupies the humblest station, yet he took their plight as his own fault. Extending the full reach of his capacity, he was determined to embrace all the people and bring them under good governance…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之然後於願為始慰堯舜之澤未易究也而承
之為己責要其志之所存必欲舉一世而兼濟
之然後於心為始安今日之君即堯舜之君也
有堯舜之君而其澤乃未徧於天下其咎在我
而不容辭而孜孜焉必思以共其付託之重今
日之民即唐虞之民也為唐虞之民而猶有未
被堯舜之澤其職在己而不容逭而汲汲焉必
思以副其仰望之殷通天地民物為一體而隱
居求志之日已全具乎輔世長民之道荷經綸
===
參替於一身而君臣相遇之始已預期乎時雍
風動之休是其任之也重故思之也不得不深
思之也深故捄之也不得不切尹之出而將有
所為如此則其進自必以正矣而豈屑於割烹
之事哉雖然聖賢出處莫非天也而其心則惟
為道計耳詩稱降于卿士實左右商王而尹亦
以天生斯民使予先覺信矣尹之為天民也應
聘而出欲以道濟天下者亦以奉天心耳故曰
有天民者達可行而行之者也世乃以割烹疑
punctuated: 之，然後於願為始慰。堯舜之澤未易究也，而承之為己責；要其志之所存，必欲舉一世而兼濟之，然後於心為始安。今日之君，即堯舜之君也。有堯舜之君，而其澤乃未徧於天下，其咎在我而不容辭，而孜孜焉必思以共其付託之重。今日之民，即唐虞之民也。為唐虞之民，而猶有未被堯舜之澤，其職在己而不容逭，而汲汲焉必思以副其仰望之殷。通天地民物為一體，而隱居求志之日，已全具乎輔世長民之道；荷經綸參替於一身，而君臣相遇之始，已預期乎時雍風動之休。是其任之也重，故思之也不得不深；思之也深，故捄之也不得不切。尹之出而將有所為如此，則其進自必以正矣，而豈屑於割烹之事哉？雖然，聖賢出處莫非天也，而其心則惟為道計耳。《詩》稱：「降于卿士，實左右商王。」而尹亦以「天生斯民，使予先覺」。信矣，尹之為天民也！應聘而出，欲以道濟天下者，亦以奉天心耳。故曰：「有天民者，達可行而行之者也。」世乃以割烹疑
translation_en:
…them; only then would his aspiration begin to find fulfillment. The beneficence of Yao and Shun was not easily extended to its fullest reach, yet he took this upon himself as his own responsibility. In essence, his resolve was to bring aid to the entire age; only then would his heart begin to rest easy. The ruler of today was a ruler like Yao and Shun. With such a ruler, if his beneficence had still not spread throughout the realm, Yi Yin considered the fault his own and would not disclaim it. Diligently, he sought to bear the weight of the charge entrusted to him. The people of today were the people of Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun. If such people still remained untouched by the beneficence of Yao and Shun, the responsibility lay with him, and he could not evade it. Urgently, he sought to meet their fervent expectations. He united Heaven, Earth, the people, and all things into one body; even while living in seclusion and pursuing his aspiration, he already fully possessed the Way of assisting the age and leading the people. Taking upon himself the work of ordering the realm and assisting its governance [?], he already anticipated, at the very outset of the meeting between ruler and minister, the blessings of universal harmony and transforming influence. Because his responsibility was weighty, his deliberation necessarily had to be profound; because his deliberation was profound, his efforts to bring relief necessarily had to be earnest. Such were the deeds Yi Yin intended when he emerged to serve. His entry into office therefore had to accord with what was right. How could he have stooped to gaining entry through butchering and cooking?

Nevertheless, whether sages and worthies enter service or withdraw is always determined by Heaven, while in their hearts they consider only the Way. The Book of Odes says: “He sent down the high ministers, who truly assisted the king of Shang.” Yi Yin likewise held: “Heaven gave birth to these people and caused me to awaken first.” Truly, Yi Yin was one of Heaven’s people! In accepting the invitation and coming forth, he wished to use the Way to aid all under Heaven, and thereby simply to honor Heaven’s intent. Thus it is said: “There are those who are Heaven’s people: when they attain a position in which the Way can be put into practice, they put it into practice.” Yet the world, on account of the story of butchering and cooking, casts doubt upon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之豈知聖人之心哉
易
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
梁譽
同考試官教諭樂批始物統天只一氣也人
多不能發此作深識其旨取之
同考試官教諭周批是善於言天道者
考試官教諭劉批精潔無一閑語可式
考試官學正楊批明淨
===
乾元之所以爲大以其妙氣化之全焉夫一氣
流行則物以之始而天亦統于是矣乾元之大
不可見耶且夫天之性情謂之乾而乾之始謂
之元大矣哉乾之元其根柢品彙綱紀造化而
浩乎不可以限量者乎何言乎其大也蓋萬物
寓形于宇內孰其始之也元則陽氣潛噓萬有
賴之以立命一心復見羣動籍之以造端氣雖
未行而太和之保合已基於此焉一元之氣是
固物之所以取足而生出之不窮矣理雖未立
punctuated:
之，豈知聖人之心哉？

易

大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。

梁譽

同考試官教諭樂批：「始物統天，只一氣也。人多不能發，此作深識其旨，取之。」

同考試官教諭周批：「是善於言天道者。」

考試官教諭劉批：「精潔，無一閑語，可式。」

考試官學正楊批：「明淨。」

乾元之所以爲大，以其妙氣化之全焉。夫一氣流行，則物以之始，而天亦統于是矣。乾元之大，不可見耶？且夫天之性情謂之乾，而乾之始謂之元。大矣哉，乾之元！其根柢品彙，綱紀造化，而浩乎不可以限量者乎！何言乎其大也？蓋萬物寓形于宇內，孰其始之也？元則陽氣潛噓，萬有賴之以立命；一心復見，羣動籍之以造端。氣雖未行，而太和之保合已基於此焉。一元之氣，是固物之所以取足，而生出之不窮矣。理雖未立，
translation_en:
…him—how could they understand the mind of the sage?

Book of Changes

“Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! The myriad things depend upon it for their beginning, and it encompasses Heaven.”

Liang Yu

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor: “Giving things their beginning and encompassing Heaven are the workings of a single vital force (qi). Most people cannot elucidate this. This essay deeply grasps the meaning; I select it.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Here is someone skilled at explaining the Way of Heaven.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Refined and concise, without a single superfluous phrase. It can serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “Clear and lucid.”

The originating power of Qian is great because it wondrously embraces the entirety of transformation through vital force. As the single vital force flows and circulates, things receive their beginning from it, and Heaven too is encompassed within it. Can we not see the greatness of Qian’s originating power in this? Now, Heaven’s nature and disposition are called Qian, and Qian’s beginning is called yuan, the originating power. Great indeed is Qian’s originating power! It roots all categories of beings and orders the workings of creation and transformation, vast beyond all measure or limit!

Why do we speak of its greatness? The myriad things take bodily form within the cosmos: what gives them their beginning? In the originating power, yang vital force breathes forth imperceptibly, and all that exists relies upon it to establish its allotted life; the one heart becomes manifest again, and all movements draw upon it to make their beginning. Although vital force has not yet begun to circulate, the preservation and union of supreme harmony already have their foundation here. The vital force of the single originating power is indeed that from which things draw their sufficiency, so that their coming into being is inexhaustible. Although principle has not yet been established, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而性命之各正已兆于此焉一元之理是固物
之所以取給而發生之不息矣然元不但資物
之始而已也由之以推於無端則肇于始而不
盡於始由之以達於不已則卽其終而無間於
終始物者元也而生物長物以馴底於保合之
歸者亦莫非元也氣之所行見其有嗣續而無
停機矣元其獨擅統馭之權者乎出震者元也
而加美亨通以漸至於各正之地者亦莫非元
也理之所運見其有貫徹而無間斷矣元其獨
===
專宰制之柄者乎吁元而曰資始見其有父道
焉元而曰統天見其有君道焉乾元之大如此
信乎不得而竝之也與大抵乾元之義甚大而
惟君克配之君之道乾之道也乾之道生生而
不已者以其體之健也人君象乾而健與乾一
則生生之德卽乾之不已矣不已而治純萬國
咸寧之化與天同其運也是故體乾者人君之
職而至健者又合乾之功
天生神物聖人則之
punctuated:
而性命之各正已兆于此焉。一元之理，是固物之所以取給而發生之不息矣。然元不但資物之始而已也。由之以推於無端，則肇于始而不盡於始；由之以達於不已，則卽其終而無間於終。始物者元也，而生物、長物，以馴底於保合之歸者，亦莫非元也。氣之所行，見其有嗣續而無停機矣。元其獨擅統馭之權者乎？出震者元也，而加美、亨通，以漸至於各正之地者，亦莫非元也。理之所運，見其有貫徹而無間斷矣。元其獨專宰制之柄者乎？吁！元而曰資始，見其有父道焉；元而曰統天，見其有君道焉。乾元之大如此，信乎不得而竝之也與！大抵乾元之義甚大，而惟君克配之。君之道，乾之道也。乾之道，生生而不已者，以其體之健也。人君象乾，而健與乾一，則生生之德卽乾之不已矣。不已而治純，萬國咸寧之化，與天同其運也。是故體乾者，人君之職；而至健者，又合乾之功。
天生神物，聖人則之。
translation_en:
…yet the proper ordering of each being’s nature and allotted destiny is already foreshadowed here. The principle of the primal origin is indeed that upon which things draw for their ceaseless emergence and growth. Yet the primal origin does more than provide things with their beginning. If we follow it back into that which has no beginning, it initiates things but is not exhausted in their inception; if we follow it onward into ceaseless continuance, it reaches their end yet suffers no interruption there. It is the primal origin that begins things; and that which gives them life and nurtures their growth, gradually bringing them to the preservation of supreme harmony, is likewise nothing other than the primal origin. In the movement of vital energy, we see succession without any cessation of its workings. Does not the primal origin alone wield the authority to govern all? It is the primal origin that brings things forth in Zhen, the trigram of thunder; and that which enhances their excellence and brings them to flourishing fulfillment, gradually reaching the point where each is properly ordered, is likewise nothing other than the primal origin. In the operation of principle, we see thorough continuity without interruption. Does not the primal origin alone hold the power to direct and regulate all?

Ah! When the primal origin is said to provide the beginning, we see in it the way of a father; when it is said to command Heaven, we see in it the way of a ruler. Such is the greatness of the primal origin of Qian, the Creative: truly nothing can stand beside it as its equal! In general, the significance of Qian’s primal origin is exceedingly great, and only the ruler can match it. The ruler’s way is the way of Qian. The way of Qian generates life without cease because its essential constitution is vigorous. If the ruler takes Qian as his model and his vigor is one with Qian’s, then his virtue of continually generating life is precisely Qian’s ceaseless activity. Through ceaselessness, his governance becomes pure; the transforming influence by which all realms enjoy peace moves in concert with Heaven. Thus, embodying Qian is the ruler’s duty, while attaining the utmost vigor is the achievement through which he accords with Qian.

Heaven produces numinous objects; the sage takes them as his model.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周裔先
同考試官教諭樂批刋落陳言而詞從理發
讀之便覺不羣
同考試官教諭周批認理真切措詞古雅邃
于易者也敬服敬服
考試官教諭劉批文雅健可味
考試官學正楊批精確
造化呈靈於物聖人法而用之焉夫蓍龜之生
天所以示卜筮之用也聖人則之以立法其憲
===
天之道者乎大傳之意若曰聖心具易書之蘊
而造化實易理之原孰謂卜筮之興果聖人之
强制哉彼天地絪縕而神明得于幽贊遂呈之
為物象之精貞元會合而太和溢於兩間乃鍾
之為文明之瑞以植物則神見乎蓍焉叢以百
莖其示以天地之全數乎而筮之為用此其昭
垂之矣以動物則神見乎龜焉列以五行其告
以變通之神機乎而卜之為用此其默啟之矣
夫天地欲以前民之用不能不洩於物以開其
punctuated:
周裔先

同考試官教諭樂批：刋落陳言，而詞從理發，讀之便覺不羣。

同考試官教諭周批：認理真切，措詞古雅，邃于易者也。敬服！敬服！

考試官教諭劉批：文雅健，可味。

考試官學正楊批：精確。

造化呈靈於物，聖人法而用之焉。夫蓍龜之生，天所以示卜筮之用也。聖人則之以立法，其憲天之道者乎？大傳之意若曰：聖心具易書之蘊，而造化實易理之原，孰謂卜筮之興果聖人之强制哉？彼天地絪縕，而神明得于幽贊，遂呈之為物象之精；貞元會合，而太和溢於兩間，乃鍾之為文明之瑞。以植物，則神見乎蓍焉，叢以百莖，其示以天地之全數乎？而筮之為用，此其昭垂之矣。以動物，則神見乎龜焉，列以五行，其告以變通之神機乎？而卜之為用，此其默啟之矣。夫天地欲以前民之用，不能不洩於物以開其
translation_en:
Zhou Yixian

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor: He has stripped away conventional phrases, letting his language arise from principle. On reading it, one immediately senses its distinction.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: His grasp of principle is accurate and penetrating; his phrasing is classical and elegant. Here is someone deeply versed in the Changes. I admire him! I admire him!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The writing is elegant and vigorous, and rewards reflection.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: Refined and exact.

The transforming power of creation manifests its spiritual efficacy in things; the sages take these as their models and put them to use. Heaven brings forth milfoil and tortoises to reveal their use in divination. The sages follow them in establishing methods: is this not their way of taking Heaven as their model? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as though it said: The sages’ minds encompass the profound content of the Book of Changes, while creation itself is the source of the principles of the Changes. Who could claim that the rise of divination was truly an arbitrary invention imposed by the sages? Heaven and earth intermingle, and spiritual efficacy emerges through their hidden workings, appearing as the finest manifestations of things. Completion and inception converge, and supreme harmony overflows between heaven and earth, becoming concentrated in auspicious signs of luminous pattern.

Among plants, spiritual efficacy appears in milfoil. Growing in clumps of a hundred stalks, does it not display the full number of heaven and earth? Here the use of milfoil divination is plainly disclosed. Among animals, spiritual efficacy appears in the tortoise. Arrayed according to the Five Phases, does it not reveal the wondrous workings of change and adaptation? Here the use of tortoise-shell divination is silently intimated. Now, heaven and earth, wishing to guide the people’s practical undertakings, must disclose their workings through things, thereby opening the way for …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
先則聖人本以成天之能不能不盡其神以繼
其志由是以蓍可筮也則用之以四十有九旣
分揲焉又掛扐焉四營之制孰非本蓍之神者
以爲之準乎以龜可卜也則鑽之七十有二有
雨霽焉有蒙繹克焉五兆之徴孰非本龜之神
者以爲之法乎是蓋聖人以一心通造化之神
而制之用者將以盡參兩成能之道以一人竭
神知之巧而法之備者欲以遂神道設教之心
造化闡其始聖人代其終而民用之神謂不由
===
此也哉雖然有神物而後有卜筮然則神物未
生易書可無作乎蓋造化顯仁則神在物象造
化藏用則神在聖心無行非易書無往非酬酢
佑神之用也又其極則一念之神人皆有之亦
皆易矣彼不求之吾心而欲以擬易亦鑿矣哉
書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣惟帝時舉
陳法
同考試官教諭姚 批 春容雅鬯是善形容
punctuated:
先，則聖人本以成天之能，不能不盡其神以繼其志。由是，以蓍可筮也，則用之以四十有九，旣分揲焉，又掛扐焉。四營之制，孰非本蓍之神者以爲之準乎？以龜可卜也，則鑽之七十有二，有雨霽焉，有蒙繹克焉。五兆之徴，孰非本龜之神者以爲之法乎？是蓋聖人以一心通造化之神而制之用者，將以盡參兩成能之道；以一人竭神知之巧而法之備者，欲以遂神道設教之心。造化闡其始，聖人代其終，而民用之神，謂不由此也哉？雖然，有神物而後有卜筮，然則神物未生，《易》書可無作乎？蓋造化顯仁，則神在物象；造化藏用，則神在聖心。無行非《易》書，無往非酬酢佑神之用也。又其極，則一念之神，人皆有之，亦皆《易》矣。彼不求之吾心而欲以擬《易》，亦鑿矣哉！

書
萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣，惟帝時舉。
陳法
同考試官教諭姚批：春容雅鬯，是善形容
translation_en:
…the way beforehand, then the sages, whose fundamental purpose was to fulfill Heaven’s capacities, could not but exhaust their spiritual insight to carry on its intent. Thus, because milfoil could be used for divination, they employed forty-nine stalks, dividing and counting them, and also setting one aside and placing the remainders between the fingers. Of the procedures for these four operations, which did not take the spiritual potency of milfoil as its standard? Because tortoise shells could be used for divination, they drilled seventy-two hollows in them. There were the signs called rain and clearing, and those called clouding, disentangling [?], and crossing. Which of these five kinds of omen did not take the spiritual potency of the tortoise as its rule?

The sages used their single mind to comprehend the spiritual workings of creation and instituted their practical use, seeking fully to realize the Way of taking three and two as numerical bases and bringing capacities to completion. Each, as a single person, exhausted the ingenuity of spiritual wisdom and made the methods complete, seeking to fulfill the intention of establishing instruction through the spiritual Way. Creation disclosed the beginning; the sages acted on its behalf to bring it to completion. Could one say that the marvelous efficacy of the people’s practices did not derive from this?

Nevertheless, if divination with shells and stalks arose only after spiritually potent things appeared, could the Book of Changes have remained unwritten before those things came into being? When creation manifests benevolence, its spirit resides in the forms of things; when creation conceals its workings, its spirit resides in the sages’ minds. No action lies outside the Book of Changes, and nowhere are its functions of responding to circumstances and assisting spiritual powers absent. At the utmost level, everyone possesses the spiritual efficacy of a single thought: all of this, too, is the Changes. Those who do not seek it within their own minds but wish to emulate the Changes are surely forcing the matter!

Book of Documents

“The worthy men among the people of the myriad states are all the emperor’s servants; it is these whom the emperor raises to office.”

Chen Fa

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: “Unhurried, elegant, and fluent: this skillfully depicts…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝世得人之盛者可錄
考試官敎諭劉批純暢得旨
考試官學正楊批意明辭藻
大臣期聖君欲其致天下之賢而用之也甚矣
德之足以感人也舉萬邦共臣之賢而惟君所
用焉其所感於明德深矣大禹欲舜之純任乎
德也意謂人君以舉賢爲功尤以明德爲本帝
德光天之下而至于海隅蒼生也則其感人何
如哉夫萬邦至遠矣黎獻之生於其間至無盡
===
矣皆視君德之脩否以行藏其道者也今則聖
人在上旣啓其利見之心而明德所孚又動其
觀光之誠懷忠以待舉者則思效明時而爲帝
之忠臣焉身雖未列乎臣鄰而志已切於用賓
矣秉直以待用者則願立聖朝而爲帝之直臣
焉位雖未膺乎弼直而志已奮於從王矣是一
德敷而足以來天下之賢如此則是賢也其致
也有所自而其出也有所爲者也帝於此當何
以處之乎蓋奮庸之志雖存乎賢而登庸之舉
punctuated:
帝世得人之盛者，可錄。
考試官敎諭劉批：純暢得旨。
考試官學正楊批：意明辭藻。
大臣期聖君，欲其致天下之賢而用之也。甚矣，德之足以感人也！舉萬邦共臣之賢，而惟君所用焉，其所感於明德深矣。大禹欲舜之純任乎德也，意謂人君以舉賢爲功，尤以明德爲本。帝德光天之下，而至于海隅蒼生也，則其感人何如哉？夫萬邦至遠矣，黎獻之生於其間至無盡矣，皆視君德之脩否，以行藏其道者也。今則聖人在上，旣啓其利見之心，而明德所孚，又動其觀光之誠。懷忠以待舉者，則思效明時，而爲帝之忠臣焉。身雖未列乎臣鄰，而志已切於用賓矣。秉直以待用者，則願立聖朝，而爲帝之直臣焉。位雖未膺乎弼直，而志已奮於從王矣。是一德敷而足以來天下之賢如此，則是賢也，其致也有所自，而其出也有所爲者也。帝於此當何以處之乎？蓋奮庸之志雖存乎賢，而登庸之舉
translation_en:
…the flourishing abundance of worthy men secured in the age of the sage emperor. Worth recording.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Pure and fluent; it captures the meaning.”
Examiner Yang, School Director, comments: “Clear in conception and elegant in expression.”
What a great minister expects of a sage ruler is that he attract the worthy men of the realm and employ them. How powerful is virtue in moving people! The worthy men of all the myriad states together offer themselves as ministers, ready for the ruler to employ: profoundly have they been moved by his luminous virtue. The Great Yu wished Shun to rely wholly upon virtue. His meaning was that a ruler’s achievement lies in raising worthy men to office, but that its foundation lies above all in making his virtue shine. The emperor’s virtue illuminates all beneath Heaven and reaches the common people in the remotest coastal regions. How great, then, must be its power to move people!
The myriad states extend to the utmost distances, and the worthy men born among their people are inexhaustible in number. All look to whether the ruler has cultivated his virtue in deciding whether to put their Way into practice or keep it hidden. Now a sage occupies the throne. He has already awakened their desire for the beneficial encounter with him; the trust inspired by his luminous virtue further stirs their sincere wish to behold the glory of his realm. Those who cherish loyalty while awaiting advancement think of serving in this enlightened age and becoming loyal ministers of the emperor. Though they have not yet joined the ranks of his close ministers, their hearts are already set upon being received as guests at court. Those who hold fast to uprightness while awaiting employment wish to take their places in the sage’s court and become upright ministers of the emperor. Though they have not yet received appointments to assist him through their rectitude, their determination to follow the king is already roused.
Thus, the diffusion of this single virtue suffices to attract the worthy men of the whole realm. These worthy men, then, have a reason for being drawn to court and a purpose in entering service. How should the emperor deal with them? For although the resolve to exert themselves in service rests with the worthy, the act of raising them to office…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則存乎帝心也大旁招之典而揚于側陋廣僉
受之公而簡在王庭以忠而願臣乎帝者則時
舉以顯其忠起之萬邦之遠而置諸百僚之近
股肱耳目行將斯人任之矣以直而願臣乎帝
者則時舉以遂其直拔之黎民之中而列之庶
官之上翼爲明聽行將斯人身之矣夫黎獻共
帝臣之願則野無遺賢惟帝盡時舉之道則賢
無遺用允若玆雖有頑讒者皆化爲黎獻之歸
矣此固承之庸之之大機也而奚必以威爲哉
===
雖然舜之意固惓惓於在朝之臣矣而禹乃以
在野之賢爲言何歟噫是固聖人之心無窮也
其欲頑讒之威者儆于有位之意也不以治之
已至而忘戒于臣也其欲黎獻之舉者不廢困
窮之意也不以臣之已良而蔽賢于野也君臣
一心明揚得人九德事俊乂官而庶績其凝也
有以夫
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
punctuated:
則存乎帝心也。大旁招之典，而揚于側陋；廣僉受之公，而簡在王庭。以忠而願臣乎帝者，則時舉以顯其忠，起之萬邦之遠，而置諸百僚之近，股肱耳目，行將斯人任之矣。以直而願臣乎帝者，則時舉以遂其直，拔之黎民之中，而列之庶官之上，翼爲明聽，行將斯人身之矣。夫黎獻共帝臣之願，則野無遺賢；惟帝盡時舉之道，則賢無遺用。允若玆，雖有頑讒者，皆化爲黎獻之歸矣。此固承之庸之之大機也，而奚必以威爲哉？

雖然，舜之意固惓惓於在朝之臣矣，而禹乃以在野之賢爲言，何歟？噫！是固聖人之心無窮也。其欲頑讒之威者，儆于有位之意也，不以治之已至而忘戒于臣也；其欲黎獻之舉者，不廢困窮之意也，不以臣之已良而蔽賢于野也。君臣一心，明揚得人，九德事，俊乂官，而庶績其凝也，有以夫！

皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。
translation_en:
…rests in the emperor’s heart. Let him enlarge the established practice of seeking worthy men far and wide, bringing to prominence those in obscure and humble circumstances; let him extend the impartiality with which all are received, selecting them for the royal court. Those whose loyalty makes them wish to serve the emperor should be raised up at the proper time so that their loyalty may be manifest. Summoned from the distant myriad states and placed close at hand among the hundred officials, these men will take on the duties of his limbs, ears, and eyes. Those whose uprightness makes them wish to serve the emperor should be raised up at the proper time so that their uprightness may find fulfillment. Drawn from among the common people and ranked above the various officials, these men will themselves assist him in seeing clearly and hearing discerningly [?]. When the worthy among the people share the wish to become the emperor’s servants, no worthy man will be left neglected outside office. When the emperor fully follows the way of raising them up at the proper time, no worthy man’s talents will go unused. If this is truly so, even the obstinate and slanderous will all be transformed and join the ranks of the worthy. This is indeed the great key to advancing and employing men. What need, then, is there to resort to intimidation?

Nevertheless, Shun’s concern was earnestly directed toward the ministers at court, whereas Yu spoke of worthy men outside office. Why was this? Ah, the sage’s concern is indeed without limit! His wish to intimidate the obstinate and slanderous expressed his intention to admonish those holding office: he did not forget to caution his ministers merely because government had already attained perfection. His wish to raise up the worthy among the people expressed his intention not to abandon those in hardship and obscurity: he did not allow worthy men outside office to remain hidden merely because his ministers were already good. Ruler and ministers were of one mind; by bringing the worthy clearly to prominence, they obtained the right men. Those possessing the nine virtues served, and men of outstanding ability held office. There was good reason, indeed, that all their undertakings were firmly established!

The fully expounded words of the August Standard are the constant rule and the instruction; they are the instruction of the Supreme Sovereign. Let all the common people take the fully expounded words of the Standard as their instruction and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the brilliance of the Son of Heaven…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰天子作民父母以為天下王
陳一定
同考試官教諭姚批敷言之訓通乎天人是
作簡明詳盡亦可謂善發天人之蘊者矣可錄以
式
考試官教諭劉批清雅
考試官學正楊批得旨
君子於敷言賛其合乎天著其感乎人也蓋敷
言之訓一天也庶民由訓以近君而莫不尊親
===
焉其感人之深哉箕子更端其言為武王告也
蓋曰君人者上承天道下治人情者也敷言之
訓固欲臣民諷詠以歸於極矣而其通於天人
之際不有可言者乎彼維皇以極之理敷之為
言非高遠而難明狹小而難行也易知簡能是
為天下之常理公平廣遠是為天下之大訓夫
理之大原出於天而君之大訓純乎理焉則是
訓在君也而所以為訓者天也太極之精因言
以示而天道有至教矣天不言也而所以代言
punctuated:
曰：「天子作民父母，以為天下王。」

陳一定

同考試官教諭姚批：「敷言之訓，通乎天人。是作簡明詳盡，亦可謂善發天人之蘊者矣。可錄以式。」
考試官教諭劉批：「清雅。」
考試官學正楊批：「得旨。」

君子於敷言，賛其合乎天，著其感乎人也。蓋敷言之訓，一天也。庶民由訓以近君，而莫不尊親焉，其感人之深哉！箕子更端其言，為武王告也。蓋曰：君人者，上承天道，下治人情者也。敷言之訓，固欲臣民諷詠以歸於極矣，而其通於天人之際，不有可言者乎？彼維皇以極之理，敷之為言，非高遠而難明、狹小而難行也。易知簡能，是為天下之常理；公平廣遠，是為天下之大訓。夫理之大原出於天，而君之大訓純乎理焉，則是訓在君也，而所以為訓者天也。太極之精，因言以示，而天道有至教矣。天不言也，而所以代言
translation_en:
…saying: “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, and thus becomes king of all under Heaven.”

Chen Yiding

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: “The instruction conveyed in these proclaimed words connects Heaven and humanity. This composition is concise and clear, thorough and complete. It may indeed be said to bring out well the profound significance of Heaven and humanity. It merits inclusion as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Clear and elegant.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, Schoolmaster: “Grasps the purport.”

Regarding the proclaimed words, the gentleman praises their accord with Heaven and makes manifest their power to move people. For the instruction conveyed in these words is one with Heaven. Through this instruction, the common people draw near to their ruler, and none fail to revere and love him as a parent. How profoundly it moves them! Jizi takes up a new strand of his exposition in addressing King Wu.

His meaning is this: one who rules others receives the Way of Heaven above and orders human feelings below. The instruction conveyed in his proclaimed words certainly aims to have officials and people recite and chant them, and thereby return to the supreme standard. Yet is there not something to be said about how these words establish communication between Heaven and humanity? The sovereign expounds in words the principle of the supreme standard. These words are neither so lofty and remote as to be difficult to understand, nor so narrow and restrictive as to be difficult to put into practice. Easy to understand and simple to carry out, they constitute the constant principle of all under Heaven; impartial, equitable, broad, and far-reaching, they constitute the great instruction for all under Heaven.

Now, the great source of principle issues from Heaven, and the ruler’s great instruction accords entirely with principle. Thus, although the instruction resides in the ruler, what makes it instruction is Heaven. The essence of the Supreme Ultimate is disclosed through words, and the Way of Heaven thereby provides the highest teaching. Heaven does not speak, but the one who speaks on its behalf …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者君也於穆之蘊因言以宣而帝天有明命矣
敷言之妙其合天如此故不曰君而曰帝以見
君之未始不爲天也由是凡厥庶民極之敷言
奉之以爲訓而守之以爲行也諷詠深而天機
融庶幾於道德之華踐履熟而天則見漸被夫
明光之化又且感德而思其自頌美以歸於君
樂其所以恩育我也而頌之曰天子作民父母
焉愛而知勞藹乎一體之義也樂其所以君長
我也而頌之曰以爲天下王焉克綏厥猷允矣元
===
后之宜也敷言之訓其感人如此故雖言民不
言臣要之臣之未始不同於民也是始焉敷言
以合天之德君錫極以與民矣旣焉由訓以頌
君之德民保極以與君矣君臣相與皇極之盛
也以是訓民彝倫有不敘哉雖然建極其本也
天有太極聖有心極其理一也人君以天之心
爲心故能以天之訓爲訓天下之人信而從之
非從訓也從以心也從以天也苟心極不建而
徒以歌詠爲訓則言敎而訟民幾何不疑哉此
punctuated: 者君也。於穆之蘊，因言以宣，而帝天有明命矣。敷言之妙，其合天如此，故不曰君而曰帝，以見君之未始不爲天也。由是凡厥庶民，極之敷言，奉之以爲訓，而守之以爲行也。諷詠深而天機融，庶幾於道德之華；踐履熟而天則見，漸被夫明光之化。又且感德而思其自，頌美以歸於君。樂其所以恩育我也，而頌之曰：「天子作民父母」焉，愛而知勞，藹乎一體之義也。樂其所以君長我也，而頌之曰：「以爲天下王」焉，克綏厥猷，允矣元后之宜也。敷言之訓，其感人如此，故雖言民不言臣，要之臣之未始不同於民也。是始焉敷言以合天之德，君錫極以與民矣；旣焉由訓以頌君之德，民保極以與君矣。君臣相與，皇極之盛也。以是訓民，彝倫有不敘哉？雖然，建極其本也。天有太極，聖有心極，其理一也。人君以天之心爲心，故能以天之訓爲訓。天下之人信而從之，非從訓也，從以心也，從以天也。苟心極不建，而徒以歌詠爲訓，則言敎而訟，民幾何不疑哉？此
translation_en: …it is the ruler who speaks on Heaven’s behalf. Through his words, the profundities of Heaven’s solemn mysteries are proclaimed, and Heaven above thus has a manifest command. Such is the subtle power of promulgating words to accord with Heaven. Hence the text says “Sovereign” rather than “ruler,” showing that the ruler never ceases to act as Heaven. Thus all the common people revere the promulgated words of the supreme standard as instruction and observe them as a rule of conduct. As their recitation deepens, Heaven’s workings permeate them, and they approach the flowering of the Way and virtue; as their practice matures, Heaven’s norms become manifest, and they gradually receive the transforming influence of its radiant light. Moreover, moved by this virtue, they reflect upon its source and direct their praises toward the ruler. Delighting in the gracious nurture he gives them, they praise him, saying, “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people.” He loves them and knows how to toil for them: abundant indeed is the moral bond that makes them one body. Delighting in his leadership, they praise him, saying, “He becomes king of all under Heaven.” Able to establish his Way in peace, he truly fulfils what befits the sovereign. Such is the power of these promulgated teachings to move people. Thus, although the text speaks of the people and not of ministers, ministers ultimately have never differed from the people in this respect. At first, by promulgating words that accord with Heaven’s virtue, the ruler bestows the supreme standard upon the people; subsequently, through these teachings, the people praise the ruler’s virtue, preserving the supreme standard together with him. This mutual engagement of ruler and ministers is the flourishing of the August Ultimate. With such instruction for the people, could the constant human relationships fail to be ordered? Nevertheless, establishing the supreme standard is the foundation. Heaven has the Supreme Ultimate, and the sage has the ultimate standard within his heart; their principle is one. The ruler takes Heaven’s heart as his own, and therefore can take Heaven’s instruction as his instruction. When all under Heaven trust and follow him, they follow not merely his instruction: they follow his heart, and they follow Heaven. If the ultimate standard is not established within his heart, and he merely uses songs and recitations as instruction, then his verbal teaching becomes contentious [?]; how could the people fail to doubt him? This …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
虞廷九歌之勸必先善政之德云
詩
保玆天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
李成性
同考試官敎諭林批題意重在天眷宣王中
===
興故生賢佐而與之以德職之隆者以為君也此
作發明得旨而二章末德職交互言之尤有見識
蓋深於詩者录用錄之
同考試官敎授饒批詞意明盡體裁嚴整經
學之雋者可以為式矣
考試官敎諭劉批善發天眷明德之意
考試官學正楊批深得吉甫贈言之旨
天眷明君而生賢佐故德與職之並隆焉蓋天
之生賢以為君也則周臣之德與職而並隆者
punctuated:
虞廷九歌之勸，必先善政之德云。

詩

保玆天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫：式是百辟，纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌。賦政于外，四方爰發。

李成性

同考試官敎諭林批：題意重在天眷宣王中興，故生賢佐，而與之以德職之隆者，以為君也。此作發明得旨，而二章末德職交互言之，尤有見識，蓋深於詩者。录用錄之。

同考試官敎授饒批：詞意明盡，體裁嚴整，經學之雋者，可以為式矣。

考試官敎諭劉批：善發天眷明德之意。

考試官學正楊批：深得吉甫贈言之旨。

天眷明君而生賢佐，故德與職之並隆焉。蓋天之生賢，以為君也，則周臣之德與職而並隆者……
translation_en:
…the exhortations of the Nine Songs at the court of Shun must first be grounded in the virtue of good government.

The Book of Odes

To protect this Son of Heaven, Heaven brought forth Zhong Shanfu. Zhong Shanfu’s virtue takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing and expression are admirable; he is cautious and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and strives to maintain an imposing, dignified bearing. He obeys the Son of Heaven and is charged with promulgating his clear commands. The king commands Zhong Shanfu: “Be a model for the many lords; continue the work of your forefathers and protect the king’s person.” He conveys the king’s commands outward and brings reports inward, serving as the king’s throat and tongue. He distributes government directives abroad, and the four quarters respond with action.

Li Chengxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: The main point of the topic is Heaven’s solicitude for King Xuan’s restoration. Thus Heaven brought forth a worthy assistant and endowed him with lofty virtue and high office, all for the ruler’s sake. This composition elucidates the intended meaning. Its interwoven discussion of virtue and office at the ends of the two sections shows particular discernment: its author has a deep understanding of the Odes. Accept and record it [?].

Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Professor: Its language and meaning are clear and exhaustive, its structure rigorous and orderly. An outstanding work of Classical scholarship, it may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: It ably develops the idea of Heaven’s solicitude for luminous virtue.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: It profoundly grasps the intent of Jifu’s parting words.

Heaven cherishes an enlightened ruler and brings forth a worthy assistant; hence both the assistant’s virtue and his office are exalted. For Heaven brings forth worthy men for the ruler’s sake. Thus, that this minister of Zhou possessed both lofty virtue and high office…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
寧非天意之獨厚與詩人作此以送仲山甫之
城齊若曰天之眷我周也舊矣明德如吾君固
帝心之簡在者是以寵綏所萃而保祐加焉將
以弘其中興之烈斯良弼于焉而攸資敷錫所
及而保定隆焉欲以致其德業之成斯賢臣于
焉而特出山甫之有生實天心之所厚也豈凡
民之所可幾哉今觀其德也柔順之貞允協于
中正之軌外之則儀色令嘉內之則小心抑慎
表裏其合一矣遠之則成憲是師近之則自脩
===
不懈知行其並進矣以至順于王心而一德之
交孚宣乎王命而四達之不悖其見之設施措
之事業如此是德為全德而所以膺乎其職者
有本矣孰非天之所厚耶又觀其職也綸綍之
命爰畀以責任之隆位冢宰而百辟為憲諸侯
賴之以統領矣嗣世官而王躬是保君德賴之
以輔養矣以至王言攸代為喉舌之司德政爰
敷應臣民之望其入而柄政出而宣勞如此是
職為全職而所以闡乎其德者有徵矣孰非天
punctuated: 寧非天意之獨厚與？詩人作此以送仲山甫之城齊，若曰：天之眷我周也舊矣，明德如吾君，固帝心之簡在者。是以寵綏所萃而保祐加焉，將以弘其中興之烈，斯良弼于焉而攸資；敷錫所及而保定隆焉，欲以致其德業之成，斯賢臣于焉而特出。山甫之有生，實天心之所厚也，豈凡民之所可幾哉？今觀其德也，柔順之貞，允協于中正之軌。外之則儀色令嘉，內之則小心抑慎，表裏其合一矣；遠之則成憲是師，近之則自脩不懈，知行其並進矣。以至順于王心而一德之交孚，宣乎王命而四達之不悖，其見之設施、措之事業如此。是德為全德，而所以膺乎其職者有本矣，孰非天之所厚耶？又觀其職也，綸綍之命，爰畀以責任之隆。位冢宰而百辟為憲，諸侯賴之以統領矣；嗣世官而王躬是保，君德賴之以輔養矣。以至王言攸代，為喉舌之司；德政爰敷，應臣民之望。其入而柄政、出而宣勞如此。是職為全職，而所以闡乎其德者有徵矣，孰非天
translation_en:
…could this not be Heaven’s exceptional favor? The poet composed this poem to see Zhong Shanfu off to build the walls of Qi, as if to say: Heaven has long cherished our Zhou. With luminous virtue such as our ruler’s, he is surely one whom the Supreme Lord has chosen in his heart. Thus divine favor and reassurance gather upon him, and protection is bestowed upon him. To magnify the achievements of his restoration, an excellent assistant is accordingly provided for him to rely upon. Heaven’s blessings extend to him, and its safeguarding grows abundant. To bring his virtuous undertakings to fulfillment, this worthy minister accordingly emerges. Shanfu’s birth indeed manifests the special favor of Heaven’s heart. How could ordinary people hope to equal him?

Now consider his virtue. His steadfast gentleness and obedience truly accord with the standard of centrality and correctness. Outwardly, his bearing and expression are admirable; inwardly, he is attentive, modest, and cautious: his inner and outer selves are united. Looking to the distant past, he takes established precedents as his teachers; attending to what lies close at hand, he cultivates himself without respite: his knowledge and conduct advance together. Moreover, he accords with the king’s heart, so that they trust one another through their shared virtue; he promulgates the king’s commands, so that they reach all quarters without contravention. Such is his virtue as manifested in practical measures and applied to affairs. His virtue is thus complete, and his fitness to undertake his office has a firm foundation. Which of these qualities does not manifest Heaven’s special favor?

Consider also his office. By solemn royal command he is entrusted with weighty responsibilities. Occupying the position of Grand Steward, he serves as a model for the many lords, and the feudal lords rely upon him for leadership. Succeeding to a hereditary office, he safeguards the king’s person, and the ruler’s virtue relies upon him for support and nurture. Moreover, he speaks on the king’s behalf, performing the duty of his mouthpiece; he spreads virtuous government, fulfilling the hopes of subjects and people. Such is his conduct: within the court he directs government, and beyond it he renders diligent service. His fulfillment of office is thus complete, and there is visible evidence of how he makes his virtue manifest. Which of these was not Heaven’s…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之所厚耶夫如是則措之天下裕如矣于城齊
也何有雖然山甫當周之中葉而弼成宣王復
古之盛治其振起之功豈少哉而詩顧以柔嘉
言之其諸易之坤乎盖臣道也地道也柔順而
應乎天無成而代有終者也况非宣王之銳志
于中興仲山甫其孰庸之故觀是詩而知周家
有君有臣之盛
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
陳大諫
===
同考試官教諭林批墽中作此篇者昭假與
是祗看不透徹故講多混淆或至重疊惟此作旨
趣渾融而字眼挑剔且瑩潔順鬯詩之精者也允
宜錄式
同考試官教授饒批意精而密詞健而雅非
有得於心學者不能道此
考試官教諭劉批善狀聖人敬德之純
考試官學正楊批能言天人感通之際
聖君純一敬以事天而受命之原可稽矣夫敬
punctuated:
之所厚耶？夫如是，則措之天下裕如矣，于城齊也何有？雖然，山甫當周之中葉，而弼成宣王復古之盛治，其振起之功豈少哉？而詩顧以柔嘉言之，其諸《易》之坤乎？盖臣道也，地道也，柔順而應乎天，無成而代有終者也。况非宣王之銳志于中興，仲山甫其孰庸之？故觀是詩，而知周家有君有臣之盛。
聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。
陳大諫
同考試官教諭林批：墽中作此篇者，昭假與是祗看不透徹，故講多混淆，或至重疊。惟此作旨趣渾融，而字眼挑剔，且瑩潔順鬯，詩之精者也，允宜錄式。
同考試官教授饒批：意精而密，詞健而雅，非有得於心學者不能道此。
考試官教諭劉批：善狀聖人敬德之純。
考試官學正楊批：能言天人感通之際。
聖君純一敬以事天，而受命之原可稽矣。夫敬
translation_en:
…bestowed Heaven’s favor? With such qualities, he could manage the affairs of the whole realm with ease. What difficulty, then, could there be in fortifying Qi? Nevertheless, Shanfu lived in the middle period of the Zhou and assisted King Xuan in achieving the flourishing government that restored ancient ways. Could his contribution to that revival have been slight? Yet the poem describes him in terms of gentleness and goodness. Does this not correspond to Kun, the Receptive, in the Book of Changes? This is the way of the minister and the way of Earth: yielding and compliant, responding to Heaven, claiming no achievement of its own yet bringing things to completion on Heaven’s behalf. Moreover, had King Xuan not been resolutely intent on restoring the dynasty, who would have employed Zhong Shanfu? Thus, reading this poem, we recognize the flourishing condition of the Zhou house, blessed with both a worthy ruler and a worthy minister.
“His sagely reverence daily advanced; his radiant approach to Heaven was unhurried; he revered the Lord on High.”
Chen Dajian
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Among those composing on this passage in the examination grounds [?], many failed to understand thoroughly “radiant approach” and “revered.” Their explanations therefore often confused the two, sometimes even repeating themselves. This composition alone integrates the meaning fully while carefully distinguishing the key expressions. Moreover, it is clear, polished, fluent, and free-flowing—a refined essay on the Book of Poetry. It certainly deserves to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Instructor: Its ideas are refined and closely reasoned; its language vigorous and elegant. Someone without personal attainment in the learning of the mind could not express this.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: It aptly depicts the purity of the sage’s reverent virtue.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: It succeeds in describing the point at which Heaven and humanity respond to and communicate with one another.
The sage ruler serves Heaven with pure and undivided reverence, and thus the source of his receiving the Mandate can be traced. Now, reverence…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者德之聚也聖君純乎敬以事天此天命之所
由歸歟是詩頌成湯之德意謂天心之所眷者
德人君之所奉者天湯之受天明命也豈徒以
生之得其時哉蓋其紹精一之眞傳而聖學緝
熈於無斁宗祧台之心法而敬德常切於中涵
不邇不殖全其天也而愼脩之益勵恒見其與
日而俱升制心制事密其守也而操存之愈熟
若見其維日之不足以至精誠之極明格于於
穆之神聖心與天心相爲流通矣而一敬之悠
===
久不息者惟凜乎上帝之是事篤恭之至感通
于冲漠之表聖德與天德相爲孚契矣而一敬
之恒永不渝者惟儼乎天載之是虔如此而始
如此而終出往游衍之間莫非終日對越之時
也敢曰德已至矣而或容之以一念之怠哉天
固不已敬亦不已陟降出入之際莫非欽崇天
道之地也敢曰敬已純矣而或容之以一息之
逸哉噫天有顯道其命也時矣惟聖時憲其德
也至矣湯之受命以此商家之王業不於是而
punctuated: 者，德之聚也。聖君純乎敬以事天，此天命之所由歸歟？是詩頌成湯之德，意謂天心之所眷者德，人君之所奉者天。湯之受天明命也，豈徒以生之得其時哉？蓋其紹精一之眞傳，而聖學緝熈於無斁；宗祧台之心法，而敬德常切於中涵。不邇不殖，全其天也，而愼脩之益勵，恒見其與日而俱升；制心制事，密其守也，而操存之愈熟，若見其維日之不足。以至精誠之極，明格于於穆之神，聖心與天心相爲流通矣，而一敬之悠久不息者，惟凜乎上帝之是事；篤恭之至，感通于冲漠之表，聖德與天德相爲孚契矣，而一敬之恒永不渝者，惟儼乎天載之是虔。如此而始，如此而終，出往游衍之間，莫非終日對越之時也。敢曰德已至矣，而或容之以一念之怠哉？天固不已，敬亦不已，陟降出入之際，莫非欽崇天道之地也。敢曰敬已純矣，而或容之以一息之逸哉？噫！天有顯道，其命也時矣；惟聖時憲，其德也至矣。湯之受命以此，商家之王業不於是而
translation_en: …is where virtue gathers. The sage ruler serves Heaven with pure reverence: is this not why Heaven’s Mandate comes to him? This ode praises the virtue of Cheng Tang. Its meaning is that what Heaven’s heart cherishes is virtue, and what the ruler of men serves is Heaven. Could Tang’s receipt of Heaven’s luminous Mandate have been merely a matter of being born at the right time? He continued the authentic transmission of refinement and single-mindedness, tirelessly advancing and illuminating the learning of the sages. He took as his model the method of cultivating the mind described as “zong tiao tai” [?], and constantly nurtured reverent virtue within himself. Neither approaching sensual pleasures nor accumulating wealth, he preserved his Heaven-endowed nature intact; ever more earnest in careful self-cultivation, he seemed always to rise with each new day. Regulating his mind and his affairs, he guarded himself closely; ever more practiced in maintaining his moral awareness, he seemed to find each day insufficient for his efforts. At the utmost pitch of sincerity, he luminously reached the profound and majestic spirit: the sage’s heart and Heaven’s heart communicated with one another. Yet his single-minded reverence continued without cease, solely through his awe in serving the Lord on High. At the utmost pitch of deep respect, his influence reached beyond the silent and formless: the sage’s virtue and Heaven’s virtue accorded with one another. Yet his single-minded reverence remained constant and unchanging, solely through his solemn devotion to Heaven’s workings. Thus he began, and thus he ended. Whenever he went forth or moved about at leisure, he was throughout the day in the presence of Heaven. Would he dare say that his virtue had already reached perfection and allow himself even one negligent thought? Heaven never ceases, and his reverence likewise never ceases. Whether ascending or descending, going out or coming in, he was everywhere honoring and revering the Way of Heaven. Would he dare say that his reverence was already pure and allow himself even a moment’s ease? Ah! Heaven has its manifest Way, and its Mandate comes in due season; only the sage takes this as his model, and his virtue reaches perfection. It was through this that Tang received the Mandate. Was it not through this that the royal enterprise of the house of Shang…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
成哉抑是道也百王基命之端亦千聖傳心之
要也蓋自帝堯以欽明之德啓其原而聖主明
王相與率由不越一德格天而曆數之傳有自
來矣商人敘祖德受命之祥而推極於此其知
本之論也噫敬止者膺假哉之眷執競者荷成
命之休君子合而觀之益信
春秋
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于
===
蕭魚楚人執鄭行人良霄〔已上襄公十一〕
〔年〕夏楚子蔡侯陳侯鄭伯許男徐子
滕子頓子胡子沈子小邾子宋世子佐
淮夷會于申〔昭公四年〕
劉守元
同考試官教諭韓批講不戰不欺簡切明白
具見楚鄭屈服於晉之心可式
考試官教諭劉批深得駕外服內之旨
考試官學正楊批謹嚴得體
punctuated:
成哉？抑是道也，百王基命之端，亦千聖傳心之要也。蓋自帝堯以欽明之德啓其原，而聖主明王相與率由，不越一德格天，而曆數之傳有自來矣。商人敘祖德受命之祥，而推極於此，其知本之論也。噫！敬止者膺假哉之眷，執競者荷成命之休，君子合而觀之，益信。
春秋
公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。楚人執鄭行人良霄。〔已上襄公十一〕〔年〕夏，楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。〔昭公四年〕
劉守元
同考試官教諭韓批：講不戰不欺，簡切明白，具見楚鄭屈服於晉之心，可式。
考試官教諭劉批：深得駕外服內之旨。
考試官學正楊批：謹嚴得體。
translation_en:
…was it not thereby accomplished? Moreover, this Way is the foundation upon which the hundred kings established their mandate, and also the essential teaching transmitted from mind to mind among the thousand sages. Emperor Yao opened its source through his reverent and enlightened virtue; thereafter, sage rulers and enlightened kings followed it together. They did no more than reach Heaven through undivided virtue, and thus the transmission of the imperial succession had its origin. When the people of Shang recounted their ancestor’s virtue and the auspicious signs of his receiving the mandate, they traced them ultimately to this: theirs was a judgment that understood the root. Ah! Those who “maintain reverence” receive the favor of Heaven’s “great” regard; those who “hold fast to strength” bear the blessing of the established mandate. Considering these together, the gentleman believes this all the more firmly.

Spring and Autumn Annals

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Duke of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. The men of Chu seized Liang Xiao, the envoy of Zheng. 〔The preceding passages are from Duke Xiang’s eleventh〕〔year.〕 In summer, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Viscount of Xu, the Viscount of Teng, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Shen, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, Zuo, heir apparent of Song, and the Huai Yi met at Shen. 〔Duke Zhao’s fourth year.〕

Liu Shouyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: “The discussion of refraining from battle and refraining from deception is concise, pertinent, and clear. It fully reveals the disposition of Chu and Zheng to submit to Jin. It can serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “It deeply grasps the purport of controlling those outside and securing the submission of those within.”

Comment by Examiner Yang, Director of Studies: “Careful, rigorous, and appropriate in form.”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春秋美霸主制外服内之功兩卽事以徵之焉
夫謀以敝楚而不敢爭誠以待鄭而不敢叛蕭
魚之績偉矣春秋美之也宜哉昔晉悼脩文襄
之業復中國之霸怒鄭叛也而申撻伐之威喜
鄭服也而講蕭魚之好君子以為美悼公者何
耶蓋楚負江漢之險未可以戰勝也鄭懷晉楚
之疑未可以力爭也悼也知之於楚則禦之以
不戰焉納魏絳息民之諫從智罃分軍之謨好
謀而成將無敵於天下矣制人而不制於人偉
===
哉其謀之善也於鄭也則示之以不疑焉禮鄭
囚而遣之歸命叔肸以告于衆忠信是尚將可
貫於金石矣相好而無復相猶至哉其誠之孚
也果而楚也疲於奔命三駕之後不敢啓爭鄭
之圖逮良霄之執姑遷怒焉由悼之用謀有以
勝之也不然方城漢水楚所常恃者豈帖然出
晉之下哉鄭也堅於內附二十餘年不敢萌背
晉之心至于申之會方卽楚焉由悼之推誠有
以固之也不然犧牲玉帛鄭巳久待者豈安然
punctuated:
春秋美霸主制外服内之功，兩卽事以徵之焉。

夫謀以敝楚而不敢爭，誠以待鄭而不敢叛，蕭魚之績偉矣，春秋美之也宜哉！昔晉悼脩文襄之業，復中國之霸，怒鄭叛也，而申撻伐之威；喜鄭服也，而講蕭魚之好。君子以為美悼公者何耶？蓋楚負江漢之險，未可以戰勝也；鄭懷晉楚之疑，未可以力爭也。悼也知之，於楚則禦之以不戰焉，納魏絳息民之諫，從智罃分軍之謨，好謀而成，將無敵於天下矣。制人而不制於人，偉哉，其謀之善也！於鄭也，則示之以不疑焉，禮鄭囚而遣之歸，命叔肸以告于衆，忠信是尚，將可貫於金石矣。相好而無復相猶，至哉，其誠之孚也！果而楚也疲於奔命，三駕之後，不敢啓爭鄭之圖，逮良霄之執，姑遷怒焉，由悼之用謀有以勝之也。不然，方城漢水，楚所常恃者，豈帖然出晉之下哉？鄭也堅於內附，二十餘年不敢萌背晉之心，至于申之會，方卽楚焉，由悼之推誠有以固之也。不然，犧牲玉帛，鄭巳久待者，豈安然
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals praises the hegemon’s achievement in restraining outside powers and securing allegiance within, adducing events on two occasions as evidence.

Through strategy he exhausted Chu so that it dared not contend; through sincerity he treated Zheng so that it dared not rebel. Great indeed was the achievement at Xiaoyu! How fitting that the Spring and Autumn Annals should praise it! Formerly, Duke Dao of Jin continued the undertaking of Dukes Wen and Xiang and restored Jin’s hegemony over the central states. Angered by Zheng’s rebellion, he displayed the might of punitive warfare; pleased by Zheng’s submission, he established friendly relations at Xiaoyu. Why do gentlemen regard this as praise of Duke Dao? Chu relied on the natural defenses of the Yangzi and Han rivers and could not readily be defeated in battle. Zheng wavered between Jin and Chu and could not readily be won over by force. Duke Dao understood this. Against Chu, he therefore defended himself without fighting. He accepted Wei Jiang’s remonstrance urging respite for the people and followed Zhi Ying’s plan to divide the army. Delighting in planning and bringing his plans to fruition, he would become invincible throughout the realm. He controlled others without being controlled by them. How magnificent was the excellence of his strategy!

Toward Zheng, he demonstrated freedom from suspicion. He treated its prisoners courteously and sent them home, and ordered Shu Xi to make a proclamation to the assembled forces. Esteeming loyalty and trustworthiness above all, his sincerity could penetrate even metal and stone. The two states maintained friendly relations and no longer schemed against one another. How consummate was the trust inspired by his sincerity!

Indeed, Chu became exhausted by rushing to respond to military demands. After the three campaigns, it dared not devise plans to contest control of Zheng. Only when Liang Xiao was seized did it vent its anger on him. This was because Duke Dao’s strategy had enabled him to prevail over Chu. Otherwise, with Fangcheng and the Han River—the defenses on which Chu had always relied—how could it have meekly accepted a position beneath Jin? Zheng, meanwhile, remained firm in its allegiance. For more than twenty years it dared not entertain thoughts of turning against Jin; only at the meeting at Shen did it join Chu. This was because Duke Dao’s sincere dealings had secured its loyalty. Otherwise, given the sacrificial animals, jade, and silk that Zheng had long kept ready, how could it have contentedly …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
猶晉之依哉故春秋前書伐鄭會蕭魚之事以
表悼公駕楚服鄭之謀後書執良霄會申之事
以徵悼公駕楚服鄭之效比而觀之美自著矣
吁先儒謂悼公有君子之資於此可見雖然悼
誠賢矣然陳鄭一也知救鄭而失於存陳吳楚
等也知抑楚而闇於通吳凡此皆不學之過也
是故帝王之道至誠無息伯者之業假而遽歸
君子貴王道而賤伯術也良有以哉
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田定公十年
===
王文明
同考試官教諭韓批時作多講序績意此篇
專就歸田上發揮得旨宜錄以式多士
考試官教諭劉批講以天自處辭不煩而
意自足
考試官學正楊批嚴正可誦
春秋紀大國歸地之誠而化強之績著矣此見
三田之歸聖人秉禮之化之所致也春秋據事
直書而何嫌於序績哉鄆讙龜陰魯故田也齊
punctuated:
猶晉之依哉？故春秋前書伐鄭、會蕭魚之事，以表悼公駕楚服鄭之謀；後書執良霄、會申之事，以徵悼公駕楚服鄭之效。比而觀之，美自著矣。吁！先儒謂悼公有君子之資，於此可見。雖然，悼誠賢矣，然陳鄭一也，知救鄭而失於存陳；吳楚等也，知抑楚而闇於通吳。凡此皆不學之過也。是故帝王之道，至誠無息；伯者之業，假而遽歸。君子貴王道而賤伯術也，良有以哉！
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田。定公十年。
王文明
同考試官教諭韓批：「時作多講序績意，此篇專就歸田上發揮，得旨，宜錄以式多士。」
考試官教諭劉批：「講以天自處，辭不煩而意自足。」
考試官學正楊批：「嚴正可誦。」
春秋紀大國歸地之誠，而化強之績著矣。此見三田之歸，聖人秉禮之化之所致也。春秋據事直書，而何嫌於序績哉？鄆讙龜陰，魯故田也。齊
translation_en:
…would it still have contentedly relied upon Jin? Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals first records the attack on Zheng and the meeting at Xiaoyu to reveal Duke Dao’s strategy for overcoming Chu and bringing Zheng into submission; later it records the seizure of Liang Xiao and the meeting at Shen to attest to the effects of that strategy. Read together, these entries make his merits manifest. Ah! Earlier Confucian scholars said that Duke Dao possessed the qualities of a gentleman: here we can see them. Nevertheless, although Duke Dao was indeed worthy, Chen and Zheng stood on the same footing, yet he knew to rescue Zheng while failing to preserve Chen; Wu and Chu were alike, yet he knew to restrain Chu while failing to understand the implications of establishing relations with Wu. All these were faults arising from a lack of learning. Thus the Way of the sage emperors and kings consists in utmost sincerity without cessation; the achievement of a hegemon rests on borrowed virtue, soon relinquished. There is good reason why the gentleman esteems the kingly Way and disdains the methods of hegemons!
“The people of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Wang Wenming.
Comment by Associate Examiner Han, an Instructor: “Contemporary essays mostly discuss the idea of recounting achievements. This essay develops its argument specifically from the return of the lands and grasps the essential meaning. It should be included as a model for the many candidates.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “It expounds the idea of taking Heaven as one’s own standpoint [?]. Its wording is economical, yet its meaning is complete.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, a School Instructor: “Grave and correct, and worthy of recitation.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the sincerity with which a great state returned territory, thereby making manifest the achievement of transforming the powerful. This shows that the return of the three territories resulted from the transforming influence of the sage’s adherence to ritual propriety. The Spring and Autumn Annals records events directly as they occurred: why should there be any objection to its recounting achievements? Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were formerly lands of Lu. Qi…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之侵久矣至是來歸謂齊人心悅而歸之者何
耶蓋自夾谷設會而齊志不睦孔子相禮而魯
化大行千盟倡好之語有以卻萊夷之兵而奪
其謀其辭一何嚴也愆義失禮之戒有以罷野
享之設而沮其姦其義一何正也由是齊也良
心生於文德之感而悟之也深善念萌於古道
之孚而悔之也切君以夷俗責其臣求蓋其旣
往之愆臣以謝過勸其君深冀其將來之善數
百里之侵地一旦奉而歸之不吝之改將以求
===
惠徵於魯國庶婚姻之好猶舊也數十年之疆
土一旦舉而復之降心之從將以免獲戾於魯
君庶邦交之禮如故也來歸旣出於齊之誠心
則非卑屈以邀之也以禮為國之效也前此之
歸濟西非所論矣歸田旣非為齊之勉强則非
悔禍以致之也以禮化强之徵也後此之歸讙
闡不足言矣故春秋特書齊人來歸與屈完之
來盟同一序績焉所謂齊人章章歸其侵疆者
是已亦何嫌之有哉吁此聖人以天自處之心
punctuated: 之侵久矣。至是來歸，謂齊人心悅而歸之者，何耶？蓋自夾谷設會，而齊志不睦，孔子相禮，而魯化大行。「千盟倡好」之語，有以卻萊夷之兵而奪其謀，其辭一何嚴也！「愆義失禮」之戒，有以罷野享之設而沮其姦，其義一何正也！由是齊也，良心生於文德之感，而悟之也深；善念萌於古道之孚，而悔之也切。君以夷俗責其臣，求蓋其旣往之愆；臣以謝過勸其君，深冀其將來之善。數百里之侵地，一旦奉而歸之，不吝之改，將以求惠徵於魯國，庶婚姻之好猶舊也；數十年之疆土，一旦舉而復之，降心之從，將以免獲戾於魯君，庶邦交之禮如故也。來歸旣出於齊之誠心，則非卑屈以邀之也，以禮為國之效也，前此之歸濟西非所論矣；歸田旣非為齊之勉强，則非悔禍以致之也，以禮化强之徵也，後此之歸讙闡不足言矣。故《春秋》特書「齊人來歸」，與屈完之來盟同一序績焉。所謂「齊人章章歸其侵疆」者是已，亦何嫌之有哉！吁！此聖人以天自處之心
translation_en:
…had long been occupied by Qi. Now they were returned. Why say that the people of Qi returned them with heartfelt willingness? At the meeting convened at Jiagu, Qi's intentions were unfriendly; but Confucius assisted in conducting the rites, and Lu's transforming influence prevailed. His words about “violating the covenant and initiating friendly relations” [?] served to repel the troops of the Lai tribes and thwart their designs. How stern his language was! His warning against “transgressing righteousness and violating ritual propriety” served to halt the proposed banquet in the open country and frustrate their treachery. How upright his principles were!

Thereupon, moved by civil virtue, Qi's people felt their conscience awaken and came to a profound realization; won over by the ancient Way, they conceived good intentions and felt deep remorse. The ruler reproached his ministers for their barbarian customs, seeking to efface his past faults; the ministers urged their ruler to apologize for his wrongdoing, earnestly hoping for goodness in his future conduct. In a single day they respectfully returned several hundred li of occupied territory. By correcting their faults without reluctance, they sought a token of favor from Lu, hoping that the amity of their marriage ties would remain as before. In a single day they restored territory they had held for several decades. By humbling themselves and submitting, they sought to avoid incurring the displeasure of Lu's ruler, hoping that the rites governing relations between the states would continue as of old.

Since the return sprang from Qi's sincerity, it had not been obtained through abject submission: it was the effect of governing a state through ritual propriety. The earlier return of Jixi therefore does not belong in this discussion. Since Qi had not returned the lands under compulsion, their restoration had not been brought about by remorse over calamity: it demonstrated the transformation of the powerful through ritual propriety. The later return of Huan and Chan is therefore scarcely worth mentioning.

Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records, “The people of Qi came and returned [the lands].” Like its record of Qu Wan coming to conclude a covenant, this recounts an achievement. This is what is meant by “the people of Qi openly returned the borderlands they had seized.” What objection, then, could there be? Ah! Here is the sage's resolve to take Heaven as his own standard…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也抑孔子之聖晏子之賢齊魯可變之機也二
國之君竟有所沮而不之用噫二君不足惜也
晏子齊之良也能敎其君以改過而不能敎之
以用人此所以止於以其君顯也歟雖然聖人
爲國以禮之意固已見之行事矣如有用我朞
月而可豈虛語哉
禮記
朝廷之美濟濟翔翔
梁棟材
===
同考試官敎諭劉批說出濟濟翔翔之儀宛
然在
朝廷之上蓋知以禮事君者
考試官敎諭劉批明飭可嘉
考試官學正楊批典雅得體
記者著君子在朝之儀一至敬之形容也蓋禮
莫嚴於朝廷也君子濟濟其出入而翔翔其翕
張其斯以爲敬君之至乎記者立敎之意蓋曰
朝廷爲禮法所自出而威儀係上下之具瞻君
punctuated:
也。抑孔子之聖、晏子之賢，齊魯可變之機也。二國之君竟有所沮而不之用。噫！二君不足惜也。晏子，齊之良也，能敎其君以改過，而不能敎之以用人，此所以止於以其君顯也歟？雖然，聖人爲國以禮之意，固已見之行事矣。「如有用我，朞月而可」，豈虛語哉？

禮記
朝廷之美，濟濟翔翔。
梁棟材

同考試官敎諭劉批：說出濟濟翔翔之儀，宛然在朝廷之上，蓋知以禮事君者。
考試官敎諭劉批：明飭可嘉。
考試官學正楊批：典雅得體。

記者著君子在朝之儀，一至敬之形容也。蓋禮莫嚴於朝廷也，君子濟濟其出入，而翔翔其翕張，其斯以爲敬君之至乎？記者立敎之意，蓋曰：朝廷爲禮法所自出，而威儀係上下之具瞻，君
translation_en:
…such indeed was his mind. Moreover, the sageliness of Kongzi and the worthiness of Yanzi offered an opportunity for Qi and Lu to be transformed. Yet the rulers of both states ultimately allowed something to deter them and failed to employ these men. Alas! The two rulers are not worth lamenting. Yanzi was an outstanding man of Qi: he could teach his ruler to correct his faults, but could not teach him to employ worthy men. Was this why his achievement went no further than bringing distinction to his ruler? Even so, the sage’s intention to govern a state through ritual propriety had already been manifested in his deeds. “If someone were to employ me, within a full year something could be accomplished”—could these have been empty words?

Record of Rites (Liji)
“The beauty of the court lies in its dignified order and graceful movement.”
Liang Dongcai

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “He describes the bearing conveyed by ‘dignified order and graceful movement’ so vividly that one seems to be present at court. He evidently understands serving one’s ruler through ritual propriety.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Lucid and well ordered; commendable.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: “Classically elegant and appropriate in form.”

The recorder sets forth the gentleman’s bearing at court: it is wholly an expression of the utmost reverence. For nowhere is ritual propriety more exacting than at court. The gentleman is dignified and orderly in his entrances and departures, graceful in drawing in and extending his movements. Is this not the utmost expression of reverence for his ruler? The recorder’s intention in establishing this teaching is, in effect, to say: the court is the source from which ritual and law proceed, and its dignified deportment is what those above and below alike look to. The gentleman…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子之在朝宜如何其爲儀哉彼其儼天顏於咫
尺而堂陛之森嚴者有以峻等威之防天下之
分莫辨於此矣覲天子之耿光而左右之趨蹌
者無非懐欽翼之念人臣之心莫愼於此矣故
自其出入之齊言之則尊卑循其等凡北面以
趨進者若有範圍之而不越大小順其序凡退
食以趨出者若有聨屬之而不違一出一入而
濟濟其盛者其一敬之整肅乎自其翕張之善
言之則升降雖至煩也而手容之翼如者泯其
===
矜持之勞俛仰雖殊致也而端拱之凝然者適
其安舒之休其翕其張而翔翔攸宜者殆一敬
之發揚乎濟濟於出入非勉强也祗承之恪不
忘於步趨之頃而威儀之淑愼自以肅天下之
觀翔翔於翕張非矯飾也翼戴之忱懋昭於容
觀之際而朝儀之丕振自以秩百僚之度何莫
而非敬君之至也哉吁此記者所以著之以爲
敎而人臣立朝之儀其斯以爲至當之矩也與
抑是道也吾於孔子而得其的矣觀其鞠躬於
punctuated: 子之在朝，宜如何其爲儀哉？彼其儼天顏於咫尺，而堂陛之森嚴者，有以峻等威之防，天下之分莫辨於此矣。覲天子之耿光，而左右之趨蹌者，無非懐欽翼之念，人臣之心莫愼於此矣。故自其出入之齊言之，則尊卑循其等，凡北面以趨進者，若有範圍之而不越；大小順其序，凡退食以趨出者，若有聨屬之而不違。一出一入，而濟濟其盛者，其一敬之整肅乎？自其翕張之善言之，則升降雖至煩也，而手容之翼如者，泯其矜持之勞；俛仰雖殊致也，而端拱之凝然者，適其安舒之休。其翕其張，而翔翔攸宜者，殆一敬之發揚乎？濟濟於出入，非勉强也，祗承之恪不忘於步趨之頃，而威儀之淑愼，自以肅天下之觀；翔翔於翕張，非矯飾也，翼戴之忱懋昭於容觀之際，而朝儀之丕振，自以秩百僚之度。何莫而非敬君之至也哉？吁！此記者所以著之以爲敎，而人臣立朝之儀，其斯以爲至當之矩也與？抑是道也，吾於孔子而得其的矣。觀其鞠躬於
translation_en:
…what, then, should the gentleman’s deportment at court be? Standing solemnly within a few feet of the imperial countenance, he encounters the imposing majesty of hall and steps, which reinforces the boundaries of rank and dignity. Nowhere are the distinctions of the realm more clearly marked. Beholding the Son of Heaven’s radiant virtue, those who move with measured steps to his left and right all cherish thoughts of reverence and circumspection. Nowhere is a minister’s heart more watchful.

Thus, speaking of the orderliness of their entering and departing: the honored and the lowly each observe their rank, and all who advance facing north seem held within bounds they do not overstep; the greater and the lesser each follow their proper sequence, and all who withdraw to take their meal seem linked together in an order they do not violate. In every departure and entrance, their splendid dignity—is this not the disciplined composure of undivided reverence? Speaking of the excellence of their drawing in and extending their movements: although ascending and descending are exceedingly intricate, their hands, held like wings, efface the strain of deliberate restraint; although bowing and straightening require different postures, their composed stillness, standing upright with hands joined, accords with the beauty of ease and repose. Drawing in and extending, moving with effortless grace as each occasion requires—is this not the outward expression of undivided reverence?

Their dignified order in entering and departing is not forced. The devotion with which they reverently serve is not forgotten even for the moment of a step, and the care and circumspection of their bearing naturally inspire solemn respect in all who behold them. Their effortless grace in drawing in and extending is not affected. Their sincere loyalty in supporting their sovereign shines fully through their demeanor, and the great flourishing of court ceremonial naturally orders the conduct of all officials. How could any of this be other than the utmost reverence for the ruler?

Ah! This is why the recorder set it down as instruction. For the deportment of ministers standing at court, should this not serve as the most fitting standard? Indeed, for this way of conduct, I find the true exemplar in Confucius. Observe how he bowed his body when…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
入門足躩於過位趨翼於下階其濟濟翔翔之
盛何如哉此聖人所以爲事君盡禮要之莫非
盛德之至也故欲希聖人敬君之儀者其必求
聖人敬君之心而後可
詩言其志也歌咏其聲也舞動其容也三
者本於心然後樂器從之是故情深而
文明氣盛而化神和順積中而英華發
外
李伯芳
===
同考試官教諭劉批詩歌舞是引此以發明
樂之有本此作能收拾警拔不泛不支可與論樂
矣錄之
考試官教諭劉批詞不費而意周匝
考試官學正楊批說理精當
記者推樂本於心而有內外相孚之盛焉蓋樂
由人心生也觀詩歌舞之本於心而被於器可
知矣其積中發外之盛宜何如哉記樂記者意
謂大哉樂之爲道乎本之於德性之精發之極
punctuated:
入門，足躩於過位，趨翼於下階，其濟濟翔翔之盛何如哉！此聖人所以爲事君盡禮，要之莫非盛德之至也。故欲希聖人敬君之儀者，其必求聖人敬君之心而後可。

詩言其志也，歌咏其聲也，舞動其容也。三者本於心，然後樂器從之。是故情深而文明，氣盛而化神，和順積中而英華發外。

李伯芳

同考試官教諭劉批：詩歌舞是引此以發明樂之有本。此作能收拾，警拔，不泛不支，可與論樂矣。錄之。
考試官教諭劉批：詞不費而意周匝。
考試官學正楊批：說理精當。

記者推樂本於心，而有內外相孚之盛焉。蓋樂由人心生也，觀詩歌舞之本於心而被於器，可知矣。其積中發外之盛宜何如哉！記《樂記》者意謂：大哉，樂之爲道乎！本之於德性之精，發之極
translation_en:
…when entering the gate, stepping cautiously when passing the ruler’s place, and moving with winglike grace when descending the steps—how splendid were his dignity and ease! This is how the sage fulfilled every ritual requirement in serving his ruler; ultimately, all of it was the highest expression of abundant virtue. Thus, anyone wishing to emulate the sage’s bearing in revering his ruler must first seek the sage’s heart of reverence for his ruler.

“Poetry expresses one’s intent; song gives melodic expression to one’s voice; dance sets one’s bodily bearing in motion. These three are rooted in the heart, and only then do musical instruments follow them. Thus, when feeling is deep, its patterned expression is brilliant; when vital energy is abundant, its transforming power is numinous. Harmony and compliance accumulate within, and their flowering radiance manifests itself without.”

Li Bofang

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The passage on poetry, song, and dance is cited here to elucidate the foundation of music. This composition draws its argument together effectively and is striking and distinguished, neither diffuse nor digressive. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss music. Include it in the record.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The wording is economical, yet the meaning is comprehensive.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: “The exposition of principle is precise and apt.”

The author of the Record traces music to its root in the heart and shows the splendid correspondence between the inward and the outward. For music arises from the human heart: this can be understood by observing how poetry, song, and dance are rooted in the heart and expressed through instruments. How splendid must be what accumulates within and manifests itself without! The author of the Record of Music means to say: Great indeed is the Way of music! It is rooted in the essence of moral nature, and its expression reaches the utmost…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聲容之盛樂固為德之華矣果何以見之彼樂
必有詩也由志之動於中者而宣諸詞說之際
樂必有歌也由詩之形於言者而調諸音曲之
餘樂必有舞也由聲之發於外者而協諸容觀
之度是三者皆樂之所由生也然是聲容之肇
端於志非無所本也內焉感於心而欣喜萌其
端歡愛洩其蘊樂之啓其始者如是矣然後志
之形見於聲容不能無飾也外焉被於器而音
律以宣之干羽以舞之樂之成其終者如是矣
===
是故聖人之作樂也情之感觸者深自溢於中
聲之暢志之蘊藉者厚自闡於德容之光其視
天地之氣積之盛而生物之妙發之神者不有
同機乎故志和行成實德之中孚不能遏則呈
露於歌舞者足以動四氣之和而聖人以一心
會聲氣之元豈徒囿於物者哉審一定和大順
之內蘊不容祕則顯設於聲容者有以著萬物
之理而聖人以一德端制作之本豈徒假於外
者哉吁樂之本原於心則德之盛者樂斯備心
punctuated:
聲容之盛，樂固為德之華矣。果何以見之？彼樂必有詩也，由志之動於中者而宣諸詞說之際；樂必有歌也，由詩之形於言者而調諸音曲之餘；樂必有舞也，由聲之發於外者而協諸容觀之度。是三者，皆樂之所由生也。然是聲容之肇端於志，非無所本也。內焉感於心，而欣喜萌其端，歡愛洩其蘊，樂之啓其始者如是矣。然後志之形見於聲容，不能無飾也。外焉被於器，而音律以宣之，干羽以舞之，樂之成其終者如是矣。

是故聖人之作樂也，情之感觸者深，自溢於中聲之暢；志之蘊藉者厚，自闡於德容之光。其視天地之氣，積之盛而生物之妙，發之神者，不有同機乎？故志和行成，實德之中孚不能遏，則呈露於歌舞者足以動四氣之和，而聖人以一心會聲氣之元，豈徒囿於物者哉？審一定和，大順之內蘊不容祕，則顯設於聲容者有以著萬物之理，而聖人以一德端制作之本，豈徒假於外者哉？吁！樂之本原於心，則德之盛者樂斯備；心
translation_en:
…the fullness of sound and movement. Music is indeed the flowering of virtue. How can this be demonstrated? Music necessarily includes poetry: aspirations stirring within are expressed in words. Music necessarily includes singing: poetry taking shape in words is modulated through musical melodies. Music necessarily includes dance: sounds issuing outward are coordinated with measured bodily movements. These three are all means through which music arises. Yet these sounds and movements originate in aspiration; they are not without a foundation. Inwardly, the heart is moved: delight first sprouts, and joy and affection disclose what lies within. Thus does music begin. Then, as aspiration becomes manifest in sound and movement, it necessarily receives embellishment. Outwardly, it is imparted to instruments, expressed through musical pitches, and danced with shields and feathers. Thus does music reach completion.

Therefore, when the sage makes music, deeply stirred feelings naturally overflow in the free expression of harmonious tones; richly nurtured aspirations naturally reveal themselves in the radiance of a virtuous bearing. Compared with the energies of Heaven and Earth, whose abundant accumulation issues forth with wondrous efficacy in the generation of living things, does this not share the same workings? Thus, when aspirations are harmonious and conduct is perfected, the inward sincerity of true virtue cannot be restrained. What appears in song and dance can stir the harmonious energies of the four seasons. With a single heart, the sage apprehends the source of sound and vital energy: how could he be confined merely to material things? By discerning unity and establishing harmony [?], the inward abundance of perfect accord cannot remain concealed. What is displayed in sound and movement can reveal the principles of the myriad things. Through a unified virtue, the sage sets right the foundation of musical creation: how could he merely borrow from externals? Ah! Since music has its source in the heart, abundant virtue brings music to completeness. The heart…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之德通於樂則樂之備者德斯彰樂其信爲德
之華也與大抵樂之爲道與人心通也聖人始
以心德之和形之聲歌而成樂繼以大樂之敎
洽之人心而成治大章蕭韶之樂固洋洋太和
之響也何者而非和德之感召耶故曰聖人作
樂以感人心而天下和平
第貳塲
論
知其性則知天
黃守謙
同考試官敎授饒批塲中作論多因體認欠
眞非澁則蔓獨此作出入經傳及宋儒諸說融會
通徹發揮明盡且又體裁峻雅宜錄以式
考試官敎諭劉批立意切當而措詞精健
考試官學正楊批善發性命之旨
大哉人心之理乎其通性命而一之者乎君子
知盡性之學而至命之理在是矣夫性也者人
也未始不原于命也命也者天也未始不付于
punctuated:
之德通於樂，則樂之備者德斯彰。樂其信爲德之華也與！大抵樂之爲道，與人心通也。聖人始以心德之和形之聲歌而成樂，繼以大樂之敎洽之人心而成治。大章、蕭韶之樂，固洋洋太和之響也，何者而非和德之感召耶？故曰：「聖人作樂以感人心，而天下和平。」

第貳塲
論
知其性則知天
黃守謙

同考試官敎授饒批：塲中作論，多因體認欠眞，非澁則蔓。獨此作出入經傳及宋儒諸說，融會通徹，發揮明盡，且又體裁峻雅，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭劉批：立意切當，而措詞精健。
考試官學正楊批：善發性命之旨。

大哉，人心之理乎！其通性命而一之者乎！君子知盡性之學，而至命之理在是矣。夫性也者，人也，未始不原于命也；命也者，天也，未始不付于
translation_en:
…the virtue of the heart communicates with music; thus, when music is complete, virtue becomes manifest. Is music not indeed the flowering of virtue! Broadly speaking, the Way of music communicates with the human heart. The sage first gives expression to the harmony of the heart’s virtue in sounds and songs, thereby creating music; then, through the teaching of great music, he imbues human hearts with it and achieves good government. The music of Dazhang and Xiaoshao is assuredly the abundant resonance of supreme harmony. What part of it is not evoked by harmonious virtue? Hence it is said: “The sage creates music to move human hearts, and all under Heaven becomes peaceful and harmonious.”

Second Session
Discourse
“To Know One’s Nature Is to Know Heaven”
Huang Shouqian

Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Instructor: Discourses written in the examination hall mostly suffer from a lack of genuine understanding: they are either obscure or rambling. This composition alone ranges through the classics and their commentaries, as well as the various teachings of Song Confucians, integrating them with thorough understanding and expounding them clearly and fully. Its form and style are also elevated and elegant. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The conception is apt and fitting, and the phrasing precise and vigorous.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: It ably elucidates the meaning of human nature and Heaven’s mandate.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人也性也命也天也未始不具于心也不知其
性可以言天乎不知其天可以言性乎不知其
性其天又可以言心乎是以君子不求天于天
也而求天于性不求性于性也而求性于天不
求性于天也而求性于心盡則皆盡知則皆知
而性天之理一以貫之矣彼外心以求性者不
知性者也外性以言天者不知天者也性也者
命之立乎命也者性之存乎心也者命之基乎
此之謂知天之學今夫天之說何所始乎詩曰
===
上天之載無聲無臭又曰維天之命於穆不已
夫天無聲不可聞也無臭不可卽也於穆則玄
默而難窮也而天可以易知之乎噫天不可知
而可知者性也性不可知而可知者理也天卽
理也理卽性也性卽心也盡性盡天也知性知
天也而可以不可聞不可卽不可窮言乎此知
天之說非深于道者不可也易曰窮理盡性以
至于命則知性也天也心也一以貫之也故言
性命者必本之乾道焉乾道莫非天也性也言
