punctuated: 人也。性也，命也，天也，未始不具于心也。不知其性，可以言天乎？不知其天，可以言性乎？不知其性其天，又可以言心乎？是以君子不求天于天也，而求天于性；不求性于性也，而求性于天；不求性于天也，而求性于心。盡則皆盡，知則皆知，而性天之理一以貫之矣。彼外心以求性者，不知性者也；外性以言天者，不知天者也。性也者，命之立乎？命也者，性之存乎？心也者，命之基乎？此之謂知天之學。今夫天之說何所始乎？詩曰：「上天之載，無聲無臭。」又曰：「維天之命，於穆不已。」夫天無聲，不可聞也；無臭，不可卽也；於穆，則玄默而難窮也。而天可以易知之乎？噫！天不可知，而可知者性也；性不可知，而可知者理也。天卽理也，理卽性也，性卽心也。盡性，盡天也；知性，知天也。而可以不可聞、不可卽、不可窮言乎？此知天之說，非深于道者不可也。易曰：「窮理盡性，以至于命。」則知性也，天也，心也，一以貫之也。故言性命者，必本之乾道焉。乾道莫非天也，性也。言
translation_en:
…to human beings. Human nature, Heaven’s mandate, and Heaven itself are all invariably present in the mind. Without knowing one’s nature, can one speak of Heaven? Without knowing one’s Heaven, can one speak of human nature? Without knowing one’s nature and one’s Heaven, can one speak of the mind? Thus the gentleman does not seek Heaven in Heaven, but seeks Heaven in human nature; he does not seek human nature in human nature, but seeks it in Heaven; he does not seek human nature in Heaven, but seeks it in the mind. To realize one fully is to realize all fully; to know one is to know all. A single principle thus runs through human nature and Heaven. Those who seek human nature apart from the mind do not understand human nature; those who speak of Heaven apart from human nature do not understand Heaven. Is human nature not that in which Heaven’s mandate is established? Is Heaven’s mandate not that in which human nature subsists? Is the mind not the foundation of Heaven’s mandate? This is what is called the learning of knowing Heaven.

Now, where does discourse on Heaven begin? The Book of Odes says: “The workings of Heaven above have neither sound nor smell.” It also says: “Heaven’s mandate—ah, how profound and unceasing!” Heaven has no sound and cannot be heard; it has no smell and cannot be approached; its profundity is mysterious and silent, and difficult to fathom. Can Heaven, then, be easily known? Ah! Heaven cannot be known, yet human nature can be known; human nature cannot be known, yet principle can be known. Heaven is precisely principle; principle is precisely human nature; human nature is precisely the mind. Fully to realize human nature is fully to realize Heaven; to know human nature is to know Heaven. Can we then speak of these as impossible to hear, approach, or fathom? This account of knowing Heaven is possible only for someone deeply versed in the Way. The Book of Changes says: “Fathom principle and fully realize human nature, thereby reaching Heaven’s mandate.” Thus we know that a single principle runs through human nature, Heaven, and the mind. Hence those who speak of human nature and Heaven’s mandate must ground their discussion in the Way of Qian, the Creative. The Way of Qian is entirely Heaven and human nature. Those who speak of …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
恒性者必先之降衷焉降衷莫非天也性也言
秉彞者必先之物則焉物則莫非天也性也是
以君子知吾性之外無餘天斯知吾性之外無
餘理也知吾性之外無餘理則知吾心之外無
餘學也是天一則性一性一則天一天一則心
一而知性知天盡心之學而豈可以二言哉夫
易之爲書開物成務冒天下之道也然舉全經
之旨不外元亨利貞四德而已而聖人一舉而
歸之乾乾固所爲天也故吾心仁義禮智卽四
===
德之原也莫非乾也莫非天也可以上下言而
可以上下判哉是故元亨利貞非妙于無而仁
義禮智非滯于有也仁義禮智非妙于無而惻
隱羞惡是非辭讓非滯于有也元亨利貞仁義
禮智非妙于無而天下五常百行萬事萬物非
滯于有也有無一而性天之說盡之矣是故探
之則淵然微者其體幽以深者也存之則渾然
純者其用粹以精者也本之則湛然虛者其用
神以化者也莫非天也亦莫非性也人惟性有
punctuated:
恒性者，必先之降衷焉。降衷莫非天也，性也。言秉彞者，必先之物則焉。物則莫非天也，性也。是以君子知吾性之外無餘天，斯知吾性之外無餘理也。知吾性之外無餘理，則知吾心之外無餘學也。是天一則性一，性一則天一，天一則心一，而知性知天盡心之學，而豈可以二言哉？
夫《易》之爲書，開物成務，冒天下之道也。然舉全經之旨，不外元亨利貞四德而已。而聖人一舉而歸之乾，乾固所爲天也。故吾心仁義禮智，卽四德之原也，莫非乾也，莫非天也。可以上下言，而可以上下判哉？是故元亨利貞非妙于無，而仁義禮智非滯于有也；仁義禮智非妙于無，而惻隱羞惡是非辭讓非滯于有也；元亨利貞仁義禮智非妙于無，而天下五常百行萬事萬物非滯于有也。有無一，而性天之說盡之矣。
是故探之則淵然微者，其體幽以深者也；存之則渾然純者，其用粹以精者也；本之則湛然虛者，其用神以化者也。莫非天也，亦莫非性也。人惟性有
translation_en:
…when speaking of the constant nature, one must first speak of Heaven’s bestowal of the inner moral norm. This bestowal is nothing other than Heaven and human nature. When speaking of holding fast to the enduring norms, one must first speak of the principles inherent in things. These principles are nothing other than Heaven and human nature. Thus, when the gentleman knows that there is no Heaven beyond his own nature, he knows that there is no principle beyond his own nature. Knowing that there is no principle beyond his own nature, he knows that there is no learning beyond his own mind. Thus, if Heaven is one, human nature is one; if human nature is one, Heaven is one; and if Heaven is one, the mind is one. How, then, could the learning that consists in knowing one’s nature, knowing Heaven, and fully realizing one’s mind be spoken of as two?
The Book of Changes discloses things, brings undertakings to completion, and encompasses the Way of all under Heaven. Yet the purport of the entire classic extends no further than the four virtues of origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy. The sage gathers them all together and attributes them to Qian, the Creative; Qian is precisely what is meant by Heaven. Thus, the benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom of my mind are the very source of these four virtues. They are all Qian; they are all Heaven. Though one may speak of them as above and below, can one divide them into above and below? Accordingly, origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy do not have their subtlety solely in nonbeing, nor are benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom confined to being. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom do not have their subtlety solely in nonbeing, nor are compassion, shame and aversion, discernment of right and wrong, and deference confined to being. Origination, flourishing, benefit, and constancy, together with benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, do not have their subtlety solely in nonbeing, nor are the five constant virtues, the hundred forms of conduct, and the myriad affairs and things of the world confined to being. Being and nonbeing are one: this exhausts the account of human nature and Heaven.
Thus, when one probes it, its profound subtlety is its underlying substance, hidden and deep; when one preserves it, its undivided purity is its functioning, pure and refined; when one takes it as the foundation, its limpid emptiness is its functioning, numinous and transformative. All is Heaven, and all is likewise human nature. If people, with regard to their nature, have …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
未知則于心有所未盡于天有所不達故謂性
爲惡謂性爲外謂性爲三品謂性爲善惡混謂
性爲明心見性紛紛然求勝其說非惟不知天
亦不知性也非惟不知性亦不知心也是以君
子以性也即命也非命外別有性也命也即性
也非性外別有命也性也命也即心也非心外
別有性命也故于天有不知必其性有不知也
性有不知必其於心有未盡也而可語一貫之
理哉是以君子神而明之會而歸之故灑掃應
===
對精義入神一原也志于爲學從心不踰一理
也格致誠正脩齊治平一道也致曲有誠形著
動變一機也善信美大聖神不知一本也而天
性可易知之哉昔者子貢謂文章性與天道有
聞有不聞未免見文章天道爲二也曾子聞夫
子之一貫即以忠恕言之悟也使曾子又以一
貫告之則泥矣惟以忠恕明一貫焉則一理渾
然隨感而發蓋通性天而一之者也故曰曾子
傳道于夫子也他日夫子又以告曾子者語之
punctuated:
未知，則于心有所未盡，于天有所不達。故謂性爲惡，謂性爲外，謂性爲三品，謂性爲善惡混，謂性爲明心見性，紛紛然求勝其說，非惟不知天，亦不知性也；非惟不知性，亦不知心也。是以君子以性也即命也，非命外別有性也；命也即性也，非性外別有命也；性也、命也即心也，非心外別有性命也。故于天有不知，必其性有不知也；性有不知，必其於心有未盡也，而可語一貫之理哉？是以君子神而明之，會而歸之。故灑掃應對、精義入神，一原也；志于爲學、從心不踰，一理也；格致誠正、脩齊治平，一道也；致曲有誠、形著動變，一機也；善信美大、聖神不知，一本也。而天性可易知之哉？

昔者子貢謂文章、性與天道，有聞、有不聞，未免見文章、天道爲二也。曾子聞夫子之一貫，即以忠恕言之，悟也。使曾子又以一貫告之，則泥矣。惟以忠恕明一貫焉，則一理渾然，隨感而發，蓋通性天而一之者也。故曰曾子傳道于夫子也。他日夫子又以告曾子者語之
translation_en:
…is not understood, there remains something not fully realized in the mind and something not comprehended concerning Heaven. Thus some call human nature evil, some regard it as external, some divide it into three grades, some call it a mixture of good and evil, and some describe it in terms of “illuminating the mind and seeing one’s nature” [?]. In their contention, each seeks to make his explanation prevail. They understand neither Heaven nor human nature; they understand neither human nature nor the mind. The gentleman therefore regards human nature as precisely Heaven’s endowment: there is no separate nature outside that endowment. Heaven’s endowment is precisely human nature: there is no separate endowment outside that nature. Human nature and Heaven’s endowment are precisely the mind: neither exists separately outside the mind. Thus, if something concerning Heaven is not understood, something concerning one’s nature must remain unknown; if something concerning one’s nature is not understood, something in one’s mind must remain unrealized. How, then, can one discuss the principle of the single thread running through all things? The gentleman therefore apprehends it with spiritual insight, brings its manifestations together, and returns them to their source. Sweeping and cleaning, responding and conversing, and refining one’s understanding of principles until one penetrates the spiritual all have one source. Setting one’s heart on learning and following the heart’s desires without overstepping the bounds share one principle. Investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world constitute one Way. Developing goodness in particular respects until sincerity is attained, and its taking form, becoming manifest, moving others, and producing change, constitute one activating process. Goodness, genuineness, beauty, greatness, sagehood, and unfathomable spirituality have one root. Can Heaven and human nature, then, be easily understood?

Formerly, Zigong said that the Master’s cultural accomplishments could be heard about, whereas his teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not. He thus still regarded cultural accomplishments and the Way of Heaven as two separate things. When Zengzi heard the Master speak of the single thread running through all, he immediately explained it in terms of doing one’s utmost and treating others with consideration: this was understanding. Had Zengzi merely repeated the phrase “a single thread running through all” to those who asked, he would have been clinging to the words. Only by explaining that single thread through doing one’s utmost and treating others with consideration could he show how the one principle forms an undivided whole and manifests itself in response to circumstances. This indeed joins human nature and Heaven into one. Hence it is said that Zengzi received the transmission of the Way from the Master. On another day, the Master again spoke the teaching he had given Zengzi to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子貢子貢尤有非歟之疑是未免岐天人而二
之固不如曾子之唯也孟子之知性似有得于
曾子之一貫而無疑于子貢之文章天道也雖
然非孟子之言也甞聞之子思矣子思曰天命
之謂性亦非子思之言也夫子曰思知人不可
不知天夫子言性自人而歸之天子思言性自
天而歸之人孟子言知天知性蓋知天之未始
不爲人知人之未始不爲天也此孟子受學于子
思而私淑于孔子也雖然孟子之言不止此也
===
他日論耳目口鼻原之于性而歸之于命言仁
義禮智原之于命而歸之于性蓋理在于命則
返命而爲性理在于性返性而爲命學至于返
命爲性返性爲命則造化在胸中矣故孟子曰
我知言
表
擬宋以范仲淹參知政事富弼爲樞密副
使謝表〔慶曆三年〕
張翼
punctuated:
子貢，子貢尤有「非歟」之疑，是未免岐天人而二之，固不如曾子之「唯」也。孟子之知性，似有得于曾子之一貫，而無疑于子貢之文章天道也。雖然，非孟子之言也，甞聞之子思矣。子思曰：「天命之謂性。」亦非子思之言也。夫子曰：「思知人，不可不知天。」夫子言性，自人而歸之天；子思言性，自天而歸之人。孟子言知天知性，蓋知天之未始不爲人，知人之未始不爲天也。此孟子受學于子思而私淑于孔子也。雖然，孟子之言不止此也。他日論耳目口鼻，原之于性而歸之于命；言仁義禮智，原之于命而歸之于性。蓋理在于命，則返命而爲性；理在于性，返性而爲命。學至于返命爲性，返性爲命，則造化在胸中矣。故孟子曰：「我知言。」

表

擬宋以范仲淹參知政事、富弼爲樞密副使謝表〔慶曆三年〕

張翼
translation_en:
…to Zigong. Yet Zigong still harbored the doubt expressed in “Is that not so?” He thus could not avoid dividing Heaven and humanity into two, and certainly fell short of Zengzi’s unqualified assent. Mengzi’s understanding of human nature seems to have grasped something of Zengzi’s “single thread,” without Zigong’s uncertainty concerning cultural teachings and the Way of Heaven. Yet this was not a teaching originating with Mengzi: he had heard it from Zisi. Zisi said, “What Heaven commands is called human nature.” Nor did this teaching originate with Zisi. The Master said, “To understand humanity, one must understand Heaven.” In speaking of human nature, the Master began with humanity and traced it back to Heaven; Zisi began with Heaven and traced it back to humanity. When Mengzi spoke of knowing Heaven and knowing human nature, he meant knowing that Heaven has never been separate from humanity, and that humanity has never been separate from Heaven. In this, Mengzi received Zisi’s teaching and cultivated himself through the legacy of Kongzi. Yet Mengzi’s teaching did not stop there. On another occasion, discussing the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose, he traced their origin to human nature but assigned them to Heaven’s allotment; speaking of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, he traced their origin to Heaven’s allotment but assigned them to human nature. For when principle resides in Heaven’s allotment, tracing that allotment back yields human nature; when principle resides in human nature, tracing that nature back yields Heaven’s allotment. When learning reaches the point of tracing Heaven’s allotment back to human nature, and human nature back to Heaven’s allotment, the workings of creation and transformation lie within one’s own breast. Thus Mengzi said, “I understand words.”

Memorial

A memorial of thanks, composed as if under the Song, for the appointment of Fan Zhongyan as Participant in Determining Governmental Matters and Fu Bi as Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. 〔Third year of Qingli, 1043〕

By Zhang Yi.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭樂批體裁莊重詞語典雅且
忠愛之意每溢於言外宛然二臣口氣非特長於
四六而已宜錄以式
同考試官敎諭周批此表不難於富麗而難
於典則是作用事核實而不誕措詞溫雅而不靡
是表中之獨步者宜稱傑士
考試官敎諭劉批兼立格造詞之善
考試官學正楊批得臣子對揚之體
慶曆三年八月某日具官臣范仲淹臣富
===
弼伏蒙
聖恩以臣等參知政事及爲樞密副使臣謹稱
謝者
黃扉賛化道隆弼直之司
丹地分謨義重安攘之託
台座望高于三省
鴻樞秩冠乎六卿
寵錫同升榮叨
異數臣仲淹臣弼誠惶誠恐稽首頓首
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭樂批：體裁莊重，詞語典雅，且忠愛之意每溢於言外，宛然二臣口氣，非特長於四六而已。宜錄以式。
同考試官敎諭周批：此表不難於富麗，而難於典則。是作用事核實而不誕，措詞溫雅而不靡，是表中之獨步者，宜稱傑士。
考試官敎諭劉批：兼立格造詞之善。
考試官學正楊批：得臣子對揚之體。
慶曆三年八月某日，具官臣范仲淹、臣富弼，伏蒙聖恩，以臣等參知政事及爲樞密副使，臣謹稱謝者。
黃扉賛化，道隆弼直之司；丹地分謨，義重安攘之託。台座望高于三省，鴻樞秩冠乎六卿。寵錫同升，榮叨異數。臣仲淹、臣弼誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor, comments: “The composition is dignified, its language classically elegant. Moreover, sentiments of loyalty and devotion repeatedly overflow beyond the words, sounding exactly like the voices of these two ministers. Its excellence is not confined to parallel prose in four- and six-character phrases. It should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The difficulty in this memorial lies not in achieving richness and splendor, but in adhering to classical standards. This composition employs allusions accurately, without extravagance; its phrasing is gentle and elegant, without being ornate to excess. It stands unrivaled among memorials: its author deserves to be called an outstanding talent.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “It combines excellence in establishing the form and crafting the language.”

Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “It captures the proper manner in which a subject acknowledges and extols his sovereign’s favor.”

On a certain day of the eighth month of the third year of Qingli [1043], your servants Fan Zhongyan and Fu Bi, holding the requisite offices, have humbly received your sagely favor in appointing us respectively as Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Military Affairs Commissioner, and respectfully offer our thanks.

At the Yellow Doors, assisting your transforming rule: exalted is the Way upheld by the office charged with aiding and correcting the sovereign. On the vermilion palace grounds, sharing in deliberations: weighty is the duty entrusted to those who secure peace within and repel threats from without. The ministerial seat commands prestige above the Three Departments; the great military pivot holds rank above the Six Ministers. Favored with promotion together, we are honored beyond our deserts by exceptional distinctions. Your servants Zhongyan and Bi, in utmost trepidation and fear, bow our heads to the ground and kowtow…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上言竊惟虞廷亮采咨庶岳以宅百揆周典
建官詔司馬以專九伐仲山補袞丕揚順
治之休方叔壯猷懋著來威之績安危注
意賴平勃之交驩謀斷相資羨杜房之濟
美齊収芳譽高譚騁雙驥於長衢共拜臺
儀崔馬應列星於南斗稽文武之竝用代
著徽猷致內外之乂安人皆碩德但三臺
互建舊惟兼秩之虛名而兩府宏開今見
清朝之勝事佐
玄功於
北極文昌實政理之司分景緯於
中樞武庫屬兵車之府曩蒙
藝祖屢注
宸衷納陶穀之言薛居正首膺妙選當建隆之
始李處耘特進兼銜
累朝名臣如沆如端如蒙正咸賛襄於左右一
時元老若賢若準若知節竝敭歷於後先
睠惟
punctuated: 上言：竊惟虞廷亮采，咨庶岳以宅百揆；周典建官，詔司馬以專九伐。仲山補袞，丕揚順治之休；方叔壯猷，懋著來威之績。安危注意，賴平勃之交驩；謀斷相資，羨杜房之濟美。齊収芳譽，高譚騁雙驥於長衢；共拜臺儀，崔馬應列星於南斗。稽文武之竝用，代著徽猷；致內外之乂安，人皆碩德。但三臺互建，舊惟兼秩之虛名；而兩府宏開，今見清朝之勝事。佐玄功於北極，文昌實政理之司；分景緯於中樞，武庫屬兵車之府。曩蒙藝祖屢注宸衷，納陶穀之言，薛居正首膺妙選；當建隆之始，李處耘特進兼銜。累朝名臣，如沆、如端、如蒙正，咸賛襄於左右；一時元老，若賢、若準、若知節，竝敭歷於後先。睠惟
translation_en:
…submit: We humbly reflect that the court of Shun brought lustre to its undertakings by consulting the chiefs of the sacred mountains and appointing a director of the hundred offices; the institutions of Zhou established offices and charged the Minister of War with sole responsibility for the nine kinds of punitive expedition. Zhongshan repaired the royal robes, greatly advancing the glory of orderly government; Fang Shu displayed mighty counsels, achieving distinction by inspiring awe among those who came to court. With the security of the realm at stake, reliance was placed upon the friendship of Chen Ping and Zhou Bo; in the mutual support of planning and decision, the combined excellence of Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling was admired. Winning fine reputations together, Gao and Tan [?] were like two thoroughbreds galloping along a broad avenue; jointly receiving appointment to the highest offices, Cui and Ma corresponded to the stars arrayed in the Southern Dipper. Examining the joint employment of civil and military talent, we find splendid achievements in every age; those who brought peace and order within and beyond the realm were all men of eminent virtue.

Yet the coordinated establishment of the Three Terraces formerly amounted only to the empty distinction of concurrent ranks; now the full establishment of the Two Administrations manifests a glorious achievement of our enlightened court. Assisting the mysterious workings of the Northern Pole, Wenchang is indeed the office governing civil affairs; sharing the celestial radiance at the central pivot, the Military Arsenal belongs to the administration of armed forces. Formerly, the dynastic founder repeatedly bestowed his imperial attention upon these matters. Accepting Tao Gu’s advice, he first selected Xue Juzheng for this distinguished appointment; at the beginning of the Jianlong era, Li Chuyun was specially advanced to hold a concurrent title. Celebrated ministers of successive reigns—such as Hang, Duan, and Mengzheng—all assisted the sovereign at his side; senior statesmen of their day—such as Xian [?], Zhun, and Zhijie—successively served with distinction. Considering now…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今日西北用人之秋正值
聖明夢卜求賢之際詎期
寵命猥及凡庸伏念臣仲淹臣弼肄業南都謬
負先憂之志掄材
北闕誤收方正之科胷中數萬甲兵慙韓琦之
竝列境外二字獻納幸夷簡之易書犬馬
徒勤未遂橫山之志封疆在望常馳易水
之思樗櫟散材甘辭榮於
聖世泥塗末品忽晉貳於崇階感
===
恩自天措躬無地玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
應期出震
握紀御乾
寬仁上邁乎成湯
勤儉遠符乎大禹承
三朝之泰運
文治聿新大
一統之輿圖
punctuated:
今日西北用人之秋，正值聖明夢卜求賢之際，詎期寵命猥及凡庸！伏念臣仲淹、臣弼，肄業南都，謬負先憂之志；掄材北闕，誤收方正之科。胷中數萬甲兵，慙韓琦之竝列；境外二字獻納，幸夷簡之易書。犬馬徒勤，未遂橫山之志；封疆在望，常馳易水之思。樗櫟散材，甘辭榮於聖世；泥塗末品，忽晉貳於崇階。感恩自天，措躬無地。
玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，應期出震，握紀御乾，寬仁上邁乎成湯，勤儉遠符乎大禹。承三朝之泰運，文治聿新；大一統之輿圖，
translation_en:
…today, when the northwest needs men of ability, precisely at this time when Your sagacious Majesty seeks worthy men through dreams and divination, how could we have expected your gracious appointment to fall upon such ordinary men as ourselves! We, your servants Zhongyan and Bi, humbly reflect: studying in the Southern Capital, we presumptuously cherished the resolve to bear concern before others; when talent was selected at the imperial court, we were undeservedly admitted through the examination for the upright and correct. With tens of thousands of armored soldiers in our breasts, we are ashamed to stand alongside Han Qi; in presenting counsel on affairs beyond the borders, we were fortunate that Yijian altered the document’s two characters [?]. Though we have toiled like dogs and horses in your service, our ambition concerning Hengshan remains unfulfilled; gazing toward the frontier, our thoughts constantly race to the Yi River. Useless timber like the ailanthus and oak, we were content to forgo honors in this sagely age; lowly men in the mud, we have suddenly been advanced to exalted rank as deputies. Receiving grace from Heaven, we find nowhere to place ourselves in our gratitude.
This is because we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [an unfilled designation?], who emerged in the east at the appointed time and holds the guiding order while ruling under Heaven. Your magnanimity and benevolence surpass those of Cheng Tang; your diligence and frugality match those of Yu the Great of distant antiquity. Inheriting the flourishing fortunes of three reigns, you have renewed civil governance; the territorial expanse of the great unified realm…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
淳風四達
孝思謹
重闈之奉
惜費忍中夜之饑遇水旱而密禱
禁庭
志存民瘼
聞鼓鼙而
躬親騎射
念切邊防
===
禮御辟廱化作九圍之式
威宣靈武風清萬里之塵蓋休養生息者已二
十年而
久安長治者自千萬世也然猶
注意鈞衡
寤寐憶濟川之舟楫
留情鎖鑰
拊髀思細柳之旌旗顧
黃閣清嚴黼黻恒輸於
punctuated:
淳風四達，孝思謹重闈之奉，惜費忍中夜之饑；遇水旱而密禱禁庭，志存民瘼；聞鼓鼙而躬親騎射，念切邊防。
禮御辟廱，化作九圍之式；威宣靈武，風清萬里之塵。蓋休養生息者已二十年，而久安長治者自千萬世也。然猶注意鈞衡，寤寐憶濟川之舟楫；留情鎖鑰，拊髀思細柳之旌旗。顧黃閣清嚴，黼黻恒輸於
translation_en:
…pure customs spread in all directions. In filial devotion, Your Majesty attends reverently to the needs of the senior imperial household; to spare expense, you endure hunger in the middle of the night. When floods or droughts occur, you pray privately within the palace, keeping the people's suffering in mind. Hearing the war drums, you personally practise mounted archery, deeply concerned for the frontier's defence.
You preside with due ceremony at the imperial academy, making your transforming influence a model for all nine regions. Your awe-inspiring might manifests itself in wondrous martial power, sweeping the dust of war from ten thousand li. Indeed, the people have now enjoyed twenty years of rest and recuperation, while enduring peace and good government will extend through countless generations. Yet you still give close attention to the chief ministers: waking or sleeping, you think of the boats and oars that will carry you across the river—the men who can aid your rule. You remain mindful of the strategic strongholds, slapping your thigh as you long for the banners of Xiliu—for a commander like Zhou Yafu. Considering the purity and dignity of the Yellow Hall, its ministers constantly contribute their embroidered adornments to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
龍袞而
紫樞重寄韜鈐特慎於虎符何期二臣偶諧
四輔臣仲淹懼辱諫官之薦荷
聖恩未允其懇辭臣弼恐緣奉使之勞蒙
天語復諭以特用集夔龍於
沼上欲敷禮樂三千收頗牧於
禁中思壯山河百二蓋
聖主期致太平之盛匪愚臣徒叨爵祿之榮臣
等旣忝為輔相之司敢自負
===
責成之意鹽梅交和沛霖雨於蒼生尊俎折衝
消烽煙於紫塞畢江湖之素志敬陳民事
數千言竭薪膽之愚衷願上安邊十二策
同心輔政敢云周召之希蹤協力宣勞共
慶唐虞之親見賛
一人之斡旋元化陰陽順而風雨時脩五代以
控制遐方萬國寧而四夷服伏願
祚昌天保
慶衍日恒
punctuated: 龍袞，而紫樞重寄，韜鈐特慎於虎符。何期二臣，偶諧四輔！臣仲淹懼辱諫官之薦，荷聖恩未允其懇辭；臣弼恐緣奉使之勞，蒙天語復諭以特用。集夔龍於沼上，欲敷禮樂三千；收頗牧於禁中，思壯山河百二。蓋聖主期致太平之盛，匪愚臣徒叨爵祿之榮。臣等旣忝為輔相之司，敢自負責成之意？鹽梅交和，沛霖雨於蒼生；尊俎折衝，消烽煙於紫塞。畢江湖之素志，敬陳民事數千言；竭薪膽之愚衷，願上安邊十二策。同心輔政，敢云周召之希蹤；協力宣勞，共慶唐虞之親見。賛一人之斡旋元化，陰陽順而風雨時；脩五代以控制遐方，萬國寧而四夷服。伏願祚昌天保，慶衍日恒。
translation_en:
…the imperial dragon robe; and in the Bureau of Military Affairs, entrusted with weighty responsibilities, the arts of military command demand particular care in wielding the tiger tally. Who could have expected that we two servants would happen to join the four chief assistants? Your servant Zhongyan feared that he would disgrace the recommendation of the remonstrance officials, yet received Your Majesty’s gracious refusal of his earnest request to decline. Your servant Bi feared that his appointment rested on his labors as an envoy, yet again received Your Majesty’s express assurance that he was being specially employed.

Gathering men like Kui and Long beside the imperial pool, You wish to spread the three thousand observances of ritual and music; bringing men like Lian Po and Li Mu within the palace, You seek to strengthen the land’s strategic defenses, such that two may withstand a hundred. For our sagely sovereign hopes to achieve the flourishing of perfect peace, rather than merely allow us foolish servants to enjoy undeserved rank and emoluments. Having unworthily assumed the duties of chief ministers, how could we fail the intention that we be held responsible for results [?]?

Like salt and sour plums blending harmoniously, we shall pour down timely rain upon the common people; through negotiations at the ceremonial table, we shall turn back aggression and extinguish the smoke of war along the northern frontier. To fulfill the aspirations we have long cherished away from court, we respectfully set forth several thousand words on the people’s affairs; exhausting our humble devotion, tempered by hardship like sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall, we wish to submit twelve policies for securing the frontier. United in assisting the government, we dare speak of aspiring to follow the Dukes of Zhou and Shao; joining forces in devoted service, we rejoice together at witnessing in person an age like those of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. We shall assist the One Man, the sovereign, in directing the primal processes of transformation, so that yin and yang are harmonious and wind and rain arrive in season; we shall cultivate the Five Dynasties [?] to govern distant regions, so that the myriad states are at peace and the peoples of the four quarters submit. Prostrate, we pray that Your imperial fortune may flourish, as in “Heaven Protects,” and that Your blessings may increase, as enduring as the sun …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
舞干羽於
兩階茂著文明之化
垂衣裳於
五位彙征俊乂之良
居重馭輕滄海全歸于禹貢
蓄威昭德薊門永固于堯封瞻
皇極之尊
鴻圖億世效華封之祝
鳳曆萬年臣等無任瞻
===
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
梁棟材
punctuated:
舞干羽於兩階，茂著文明之化；垂衣裳於五位，彙征俊乂之良。居重馭輕，滄海全歸于禹貢；蓄威昭德，薊門永固于堯封。瞻皇極之尊，鴻圖億世；效華封之祝，鳳曆萬年。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策
第一問
梁棟材
translation_en:
…May the dance of shields and feather plumes between the two stairways splendidly manifest the transforming power of civil virtue; may your rule, with robes hanging down, gather worthy and talented men into the five positions. Holding the commanding center and governing the outlying regions, may all within the seas come fully under the order described in the Tribute of Yu; storing up might and displaying virtue, may Jimen remain forever secure within the bounds of Yao’s realm. Looking up to the exalted imperial standard, we wish your grand dominion a hundred million generations; offering the blessings of the border warden of Hua, we wish your imperial calendar ten thousand years. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sageliness with boundless fervor and reverent apprehension. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude for your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Liang Dongcai

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭劉批我
皇上仰體
祖宗仁民至意刋布醫書以全斯民之命
恩至渥矣是以
上天篤愛而錫以
億萬年無疆之壽職有所自此作敷對有條揄颺詳悉而忠誠之意
溢於言外宜錄以傳
考試官教諭劉批揄揚
聖壽之隆而本于
===
聖學之敬
聖治之神有識之士也
考試官學正楊批敷答有條而賛揚得體
子其沐
聖化之深而忠愛之情見乎詞者歟
聖人之愛民也深是以其衞民之生也切
聖人之體天也至是以其受天之眷也隆
何則莫不欲生者民之情也聖人以民之
情爲情凡可保合性命而納之生全之域
punctuated:
同考試官教諭劉批：我皇上仰體祖宗仁民至意，刋布醫書，以全斯民之命，恩至渥矣！是以上天篤愛，而錫以億萬年無疆之壽，職有所自。此作敷對有條，揄颺詳悉，而忠誠之意溢於言外，宜錄以傳。

考試官教諭劉批：揄揚聖壽之隆，而本于聖學之敬、聖治之神，有識之士也。

考試官學正楊批：敷答有條，而賛揚得體。子其沐聖化之深，而忠愛之情見乎詞者歟？

聖人之愛民也深，是以其衞民之生也切；聖人之體天也至，是以其受天之眷也隆。何則？莫不欲生者，民之情也。聖人以民之情爲情，凡可保合性命而納之生全之域
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Our Emperor reverently embodies his ancestors’ utmost concern for benevolence toward the people. He has had medical books cut on blocks and distributed to preserve the lives of the people: his bounty is exceedingly generous! Thus Heaven loves him deeply and bestows upon him boundless longevity, lasting hundreds of millions of years; this assuredly has its source. This composition presents its response in an orderly manner and offers full and detailed praise, while its loyal sincerity overflows beyond the words themselves. It deserves to be recorded and transmitted.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He extols the abundance of the imperial longevity, grounding it in the reverence of the Emperor’s learning and the wondrous efficacy of his governance. He is a man of discernment.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: The response is orderly, and its praise is fitting. Might you be one who has received deeply the influence of the Emperor’s transforming virtue, and whose feelings of loyalty and love find expression in his words?

The sage’s love for the people is profound; therefore his concern to protect their lives is earnest. The sage’s embodiment of Heaven is consummate; therefore the favor he receives from Heaven is abundant. Why is this? To desire life without exception is the disposition of the people. The sage takes the people’s disposition as his own. All that can preserve their nature and life and bring them into a realm where life is secure and whole …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者莫非愛民之無窮也而好生之德洽于
民心矣欲民之生者天之心也聖人以天
之心爲心凡其誠和小民而躋之仁壽之
治者莫非體天之無巳也而太和之氣通
于上帝矣好生之德洽則民生安而邦本
固以迓雍熈之衡以綿悠久之化其所以
壽萬民也卽所以壽一身也太和之氣通
則天意得而眷命凝以受康寧之祉以衍
靈長之祚其所以錫福於民也卽所以斂
===
福于天也君民一體上下一機帝王之治
於斯爲盛矣觀此則我
皇上之法
天弘化推仁育物光揚
祖宗超越隆古而寧
聖躬衍
聖壽者不可以揄揚其萬一乎恭惟
皇上秉
至神
punctuated: 者，莫非愛民之無窮也，而好生之德洽于民心矣。欲民之生者，天之心也。聖人以天之心爲心，凡其誠和小民而躋之仁壽之治者，莫非體天之無巳也，而太和之氣通于上帝矣。好生之德洽，則民生安而邦本固，以迓雍熈之衡，以綿悠久之化。其所以壽萬民也，卽所以壽一身也。太和之氣通，則天意得而眷命凝，以受康寧之祉，以衍靈長之祚。其所以錫福於民也，卽所以斂福于天也。君民一體，上下一機，帝王之治於斯爲盛矣。觀此，則我皇上之法天弘化、推仁育物、光揚祖宗、超越隆古，而寧聖躬、衍聖壽者，不可以揄揚其萬一乎？恭惟皇上秉至神
translation_en:
…all express his boundless love for the people, and his life-loving virtue permeates their hearts. Heaven’s heart desires that the people should live. The sage takes Heaven’s heart as his own. Whenever he sincerely brings the common people into harmony and raises them to a state of benevolent rule and longevity, this expresses his ceaseless embodiment of Heaven; thus the vital energy of supreme harmony reaches the Lord on High. When life-loving virtue permeates the people, their livelihoods are secure and the foundations of the state are firm, ushering in a condition [?] of harmony and prosperity and perpetuating an enduring moral transformation. The means by which he grants longevity to all the people are precisely those by which he grants longevity to himself. When the vital energy of supreme harmony reaches above, Heaven’s wishes are fulfilled and its favor and mandate become firmly established, bringing blessings of health and peace and extending his enduring good fortune. The means by which he bestows blessings upon the people are precisely those by which he gathers blessings from Heaven. Ruler and people form one body; those above and below share a single animating impulse. Here the government of emperors and kings reaches its fullness.
In light of this, can we not praise even a ten-thousandth part of how our Emperor models himself upon Heaven and extends its transforming influence, spreads benevolence and nurtures all things, glorifies his ancestors and surpasses high antiquity, thereby securing his sacred person and prolonging his sacred lifespan? We reverently consider that our Emperor possesses the supremely numinous…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
極聖之資撫
重熙累洽之運
盛德
大業之美輝映乎天地
深仁厚澤之布淪洽乎遠邇洋洋哉盛美乎其
不可一二殫述也明問欲諸生效
祝天保以颺言
聖壽乃舉
頒賜醫書為言得非以民命之於
===
國脉所係甚重而醫方之於民命所關最切
者乎善哉宋儒程頤有言曰仁者以天地
萬物為一體夫言天地而必及萬物見天
之於民其理不殊也言天地萬物而必曰
一體見君之敬天恤民其機不二也故奉
天而惠民則元后父母之責盡因民而得
天則祈天永命之慶衍此相因之理而泰
隆之治也盡此道者神農黃帝其選乎神
農氏之王也五穀熟而人民育矣乃為之
punctuated: 極聖之資，撫重熙累洽之運，盛德大業之美輝映乎天地，深仁厚澤之布淪洽乎遠邇。洋洋哉，盛美乎！其不可一二殫述也。明問欲諸生效祝天保以颺言聖壽，乃舉頒賜醫書為言，得非以民命之於國脉所係甚重，而醫方之於民命所關最切者乎？善哉！宋儒程頤有言曰：「仁者以天地萬物為一體。」夫言天地而必及萬物，見天之於民，其理不殊也；言天地萬物而必曰一體，見君之敬天恤民，其機不二也。故奉天而惠民，則元后父母之責盡；因民而得天，則祈天永命之慶衍。此相因之理，而泰隆之治也。盡此道者，神農、黃帝其選乎？神農氏之王也，五穀熟而人民育矣，乃為之
translation_en: …and consummate sagacity, Your Majesty presides over an age of accumulated splendor and enduring harmony. The beauty of your abundant virtue and great achievements shines throughout Heaven and Earth; your profound benevolence and generous blessings spread everywhere, reaching near and far. How vast! How magnificent! These things cannot be exhaustively recounted one by one. Your illuminating question asks us students to emulate the blessings of the ode Heaven Protects You (Tianbao) in proclaiming your sacred longevity, and specifically raises the bestowal of medical books. Is this not because the lives of the people bear so heavily upon the vitality of the state, while medical prescriptions are most closely bound up with the people's lives? Excellent indeed! The Song Confucian Cheng Yi said: “The benevolent person regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body.” To speak of Heaven and Earth and necessarily include the myriad things shows that the principle linking Heaven and the people is no different. To speak of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things and necessarily call them one body shows that the ruler's reverence for Heaven and care for the people spring from a single impulse. Thus, by serving Heaven and benefiting the people, the sovereign fulfills his parental responsibilities; by winning Heaven's favor through the people, he extends the blessings sought in praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. This is the principle of their mutual dependence and the governance that brings peace and prosperity. Were not Shennong and the Yellow Emperor outstanding among those who fully realized this Way? When Shennong ruled, the five grains ripened and the people were nourished. Then, on their behalf, he…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
味草木之滋妙神化之術察寒溫平熱之
性辯君臣佐使之義而醫藥傳焉黃帝之
興也衣裳垂而天下治矣又從而探天下
之賾原性命之理明榮衛之清濁究順逆
之盈虛而內經著焉二聖人體天愛民開
物成務其所以仁天下之法甚精且詳也
故其民旣享龐皓之福而二君亦躋遐永
之年明效大驗豈不章章較著哉周禮周
公致太平之書也今觀醫師掌醫之政令
===
率官分治而統之於天官歲終則稽其失
全之多寡而上下之焉藏氷出氷出火納
火皆所以助陰陽之運而療民疾于未然
也食醫疾醫瘍醫皆所以扶血氣之和而
療民疾于已然也法制纖悉莫備於玆是
以疾苦不貽於黎庶太和洋溢於宇宙卜
世三十卜年八百厥有繇哉嗣是而後漢
文帝赦太倉令而春和賑貸唐太宗見鍼
灸圖而特禁鞭背太平聖惠方頒於宋太
punctuated: 味草木之滋，妙神化之術，察寒溫平熱之性，辯君臣佐使之義，而醫藥傳焉。黃帝之興也，衣裳垂而天下治矣，又從而探天下之賾，原性命之理，明榮衛之清濁，究順逆之盈虛，而內經著焉。二聖人體天愛民，開物成務，其所以仁天下之法甚精且詳也。故其民旣享龐皓之福，而二君亦躋遐永之年，明效大驗，豈不章章較著哉？周禮，周公致太平之書也。今觀醫師掌醫之政令，率官分治，而統之於天官，歲終則稽其失全之多寡而上下之焉。藏氷出氷，出火納火，皆所以助陰陽之運而療民疾于未然也。食醫、疾醫、瘍醫，皆所以扶血氣之和而療民疾于已然也。法制纖悉，莫備於玆，是以疾苦不貽於黎庶，太和洋溢於宇宙。卜世三十，卜年八百，厥有繇哉！嗣是而後，漢文帝赦太倉令而春和賑貸，唐太宗見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背，太平聖惠方頒於宋太
translation_en:
…tasted the flavors of plants, perfected the arts of wondrous transformation, investigated their cold, warm, neutral, and hot properties, and distinguished the functions of sovereign, minister, assistant, and envoy ingredients; thus medicine was transmitted. When Huangdi arose, he let his robes hang down and the world was well governed. He further explored the world's deepest mysteries, traced the principles of human nature and life, clarified the purity and turbidity of nutritive and defensive qi, and investigated fullness and depletion in their proper and contrary courses. Thus the Inner Canon was written. These two sages embodied Heaven and cherished the people, disclosed the potential of things, and brought undertakings to completion. Their methods of extending benevolence throughout the world were exceptionally refined and thorough. Thus their people enjoyed blessings of abundant well-being [?], while the two rulers themselves attained great longevity. Were these clear effects and substantial proofs not conspicuously evident?

The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Consider its provisions: the Chief Physician administered medical regulations and directives, leading the officials in their respective duties under the Ministry of Heaven. At year's end, their failures and successful cures were assessed, and they were ranked accordingly. Storing and issuing ice, and bringing out and putting away fire, all served to assist the workings of yin and yang and to remedy the people's illnesses before they arose. Dietetic Physicians, Physicians for Diseases, and Physicians for Sores all served to sustain harmony in blood and qi and to treat the people's illnesses after they arose. No laws and institutions were more minutely comprehensive than these. Consequently, the common people were spared illness and suffering, and supreme harmony filled the universe. The divined span of thirty generations and eight hundred years surely had its reasons!

Thereafter, Emperor Wen of Han pardoned the Director of the Imperial Granary and provided relief and loans in the mild spring season. Emperor Taizong of Tang saw an illustration of acupuncture and moxibustion and expressly prohibited flogging the back. The Formulas of Sagely Beneficence for the Era of Great Peace was promulgated under the Song emperor Tai…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗焉簡要濟眾方頒於宋仁宗焉雖其有
限之仁未足以媲美於帝王之盛而即其
愛民之念皆不失為一時之賢君也巳洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
寶籙再闢渾淪乃於
開基之五年
詔天下郡縣凡民之疲癃不能自全者官為養
贍督醫治療而醫學之設徧于郡邑且又
===
中
諭曰仁政所先常加存恤焉
成祖文皇帝光造
丕基聿垂
洪緒乃於
嗣服之四年
命太醫院凡民之疾苦不能得醫者出
內府藥劑隨宜散施而
惠民藥局之
punctuated:
宗焉，《簡要濟眾方》頒於宋仁宗焉。雖其有限之仁，未足以媲美於帝王之盛，而即其愛民之念，皆不失為一時之賢君也巳。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，誕膺寶籙，再闢渾淪，乃於開基之五年，詔天下郡縣，凡民之疲癃不能自全者，官為養贍，督醫治療，而醫學之設徧于郡邑。且又中諭曰：「仁政所先，常加存恤焉。」
成祖文皇帝，光造丕基，聿垂洪緒，乃於嗣服之四年，命太醫院，凡民之疾苦不能得醫者，出內府藥劑，隨宜散施，而惠民藥局之
translation_en:
…under Taizong of the Song; the Concise Prescriptions for Relieving the Multitude was promulgated under Renzong of the Song. Although their limited benevolence could not rival the magnificent achievements of the ancient emperors and kings, their concern for the people nevertheless qualified each as a worthy ruler of his time.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Exalted Emperor, received the precious register of Heaven’s mandate and opened the primordial chaos anew. In the fifth year after founding the dynasty, he decreed that throughout the empire’s prefectures and counties, officials should provide sustenance for all people so infirm or disabled that they could not support themselves, and oversee their medical treatment. Medical schools were established throughout the prefectures and counties. Furthermore, an instruction from within the palace [?] declared: “This takes priority in benevolent government; constantly extend care and relief to them.”
Chengzu, the Cultured Emperor, gloriously established the great foundation and handed down a vast imperial legacy. In the fourth year after succeeding to the throne, he ordered the Imperial Medical Office to distribute medicines from the palace stores as appropriate to all sick and suffering people unable to obtain medical care; and, concerning the Pharmacy for the Benefit of the People, …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
令申在禮部且又加
勅曰必有實惠勿為文具焉是
心也固天地萬物一體之心也其所以下濟乎
民上承乎
天登斯世萬年生成之域綿
國家萬年靈長之祚蓋已肇於茲矣迨我
睿宗獻皇帝仁敷江漢德合
蒼旻爰集醫方選要之篇實為濟民利物之寶
惟
===
天陰隲下民則是書之懿能不布護流行使四
海九州之眾咸緣是以登於竝育不害之
天哉肆我
皇上以
聖人居
君師之位以
孝思盡繼述之責特
命刋刻普錫中外天下臣民咸莊誦稽首曰我
皇上純孝體
punctuated: 令申在禮部，且又加勅曰：「必有實惠，勿為文具焉。」是心也，固天地萬物一體之心也。其所以下濟乎民，上承乎天，登斯世萬年生成之域，綿國家萬年靈長之祚，蓋已肇於茲矣。迨我睿宗獻皇帝，仁敷江漢，德合蒼旻，爰集《醫方選要》之篇，實為濟民利物之寶。惟天陰隲下民，則是書之懿，能不布護流行，使四海九州之眾咸緣是以登於竝育不害之天哉？肆我皇上以聖人居君師之位，以孝思盡繼述之責，特命刋刻，普錫中外。天下臣民咸莊誦稽首曰：「我皇上純孝體
translation_en:
…the directive was reiterated to the Ministry of Rites, and a further imperial injunction declared: “There must be tangible benefits; do not let this become mere paperwork.” This concern was indeed the concern of one who regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as a single body. Through it, relief reached down to the people and accorded above with Heaven. Bringing this age into a realm of life and nurture for ten thousand years, and extending the dynasty’s enduring blessings for ten thousand years—all this had its beginnings here.
When our Emperor Xian, Ruizong, spread his benevolence throughout the Jiang and Han region, his virtue accorded with azure Heaven. He then compiled the Essential Selections of Medical Prescriptions (Yifang xuanyao), truly a treasure for relieving the people and benefiting all beings. Since Heaven silently provides for the people below, could the excellence of this book fail to be disseminated for their protection [?], enabling all the multitudes within the Four Seas and Nine Provinces thereby to enter a world where all are nurtured together without harming one another?
Thus our present emperor, occupying the position of sovereign and teacher as a sage, and fulfilling through filial devotion his responsibility to carry forward his predecessor’s work, specially commanded that the book be printed from woodblocks and bestowed widely within and beyond the court. All officials and people throughout the realm reverently recited it and bowed their heads to the ground, saying: “Our emperor, in his pure filial piety, embodies…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
親仁及萬民若此也近又取禮部尚書胡濙所
進衛生易簡方再
命鋟梓頒布遐邇天下臣民又莊誦稽首曰我
皇上至仁同
天施及不匱若此也肆茲遐陬僻壤海隅窮谷
皆得良方要術家諭戶曉受讀珍藏保全
調攝天下舉欣欣然躋於
仁壽之域沐於
浩蕩之恩而
===
皇上藥粥之
施覃被邦畿疾苦之
問廣延下國他如蠲租有
詔憫水有
令賑饑有
命勸農有詩時行屢下尤難言罄蓋
天地生物之心無已故物之成大成小者雖各
正性命而栽培之化無一時之少間
皇上生民之心不已故民之竝育竝生者雖各
punctuated: 親，仁及萬民若此也。」近又取禮部尚書胡濙所進《衛生易簡方》，再命鋟梓，頒布遐邇。天下臣民又莊誦稽首曰：「我皇上至仁同天，施及不匱若此也。」肆茲遐陬僻壤、海隅窮谷，皆得良方要術，家諭戶曉，受讀珍藏，保全調攝。天下舉欣欣然躋於仁壽之域，沐於浩蕩之恩。而皇上藥粥之施覃被邦畿，疾苦之問廣延下國。他如蠲租有詔，憫水有令，賑饑有命，勸農有詩，時行屢下，尤難言罄。蓋天地生物之心無已，故物之成大成小者，雖各正性命，而栽培之化無一時之少間。皇上生民之心不已，故民之竝育竝生者，雖各
translation_en:
…his parents, and extends benevolence to all the people in this way.” Recently, he also took the Easy and Simple Prescriptions for Preserving Health (Weisheng yijian fang), presented by Hu Ying, Minister of Rites, and again ordered it engraved on woodblocks and distributed far and near. The empire’s officials and people again reverently recited it and bowed their heads to the ground, saying: “Our Emperor’s supreme benevolence equals Heaven’s; such is the inexhaustible reach of his bounty.” Thus even distant corners and remote regions, coastal settlements and secluded valleys, have all obtained effective prescriptions and essential techniques. Every family is instructed and every household informed; they receive and read these works, treasuring and preserving them, to safeguard their health and regulate their care. All under Heaven joyfully enter the realm of benevolence and longevity, bathing in his boundless grace.

The Emperor’s provision of medicines and gruel extends throughout the capital region, while his inquiries into illness and suffering reach far into the provinces. Other instances include edicts remitting land taxes, orders expressing concern for flood victims, commands to relieve famine, and poems encouraging agriculture. Issued repeatedly as circumstances require, these are especially difficult to recount in full. For Heaven and Earth never cease in their purpose of bringing forth living things. Thus, although things that grow great or remain small each attain their proper nature and allotted destiny, the transforming work that nurtures them never pauses for a moment. The Emperor likewise never ceases in his purpose of sustaining the people. Thus the people grow and live together, although each …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
保合太和而撫綏之念無一時之少疎允
矣其
仁卽
天地之仁
心卽
祖
考之心也是以
好生洽于民心而
國家之元氣厚
===
太和通于
上帝而
天地之和氣應其愛戴所輸則四海之廣億兆
之衆莫不歡欣鼓舞以祝
聖壽於無極如江漢所謂天子萬年令聞不已
殷武所謂壽考且寧以保我後生焉其
眷命之所篤則思或啓之行或翼之莫不單厚
多益以增
聖壽於無窮如天保所謂受天百禄降爾遐福
punctuated: 保合太和，而撫綏之念無一時之少疎。允矣，其仁卽天地之仁，心卽祖考之心也。是以好生洽于民心，而國家之元氣厚；太和通于上帝，而天地之和氣應。其愛戴所輸，則四海之廣、億兆之衆，莫不歡欣鼓舞，以祝聖壽於無極，如《江漢》所謂「天子萬年，令聞不已」，《殷武》所謂「壽考且寧，以保我後生」焉。其眷命之所篤，則思或啓之，行或翼之，莫不單厚多益，以增聖壽於無窮，如《天保》所謂「受天百禄，降爾遐福」
translation_en:
…preserve and unite in supreme harmony, while his concern to comfort and pacify them never slackens for a moment. Truly, his benevolence is the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and his heart is the heart of his imperial forebears. Thus his love of life permeates the hearts of the people, strengthening the vital force of the state; supreme harmony reaches the Lord on High, and the harmonious forces of Heaven and Earth respond. In the devotion and affection offered to him, throughout the vast lands within the Four Seas, among the countless multitudes, all rejoice and exult, praying that His Majesty’s life may know no limit. As “The Jiang and Han Rivers” (Jiang Han) says, “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years, his good renown never ceasing”; and as “The Martial Might of Yin” (Yin Wu) says, “May he live long and in peace, to protect us who come after.”

As for the abundant favor of Heaven’s gracious mandate, his thoughts receive enlightenment and his actions receive support; all bring ample blessings and further benefits [?], extending His Majesty’s life without end. As “Heaven Protects You” (Tian Bao) says, “Receive Heaven’s hundred blessings; may it bestow enduring good fortune upon you”…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉樂所謂保佑命之自天申之焉
聖躬之日以康寧
聖壽之日以綿衍蓋將與
天同運應地無疆而詩所稱萬有千年豈足以
擬之哉方今普天之下民物熈熈華夏以
奠蠻夷以服山川以寧海宇以謐草木以
蕃鳥獸以若何者非
皇上萬壽之所錫乎頻年以來
瑞應穰穰
===
壽星現焉卿雲爛焉甘露零焉芝草挺焉瑞兎
毓焉白鹿出焉何者非
皇上萬壽之所徵乎此無他民有欲生之情而
聖人者維持調護錫以生全之慶則
德洽於無外而維祺之吉以集
天有好生之心而
聖人者敷斂錫類代厥生育之工則
仁周於不息而滋至之祥以孚我
皇上所以紹
punctuated: 《嘉樂》所謂「保佑命之，自天申之」焉。聖躬之日以康寧，聖壽之日以綿衍，蓋將與天同運，應地無疆，而《詩》所稱「萬有千年」，豈足以擬之哉？方今普天之下，民物熈熈，華夏以奠，蠻夷以服，山川以寧，海宇以謐，草木以蕃，鳥獸以若，何者非皇上萬壽之所錫乎？頻年以來，瑞應穰穰：壽星現焉，卿雲爛焉，甘露零焉，芝草挺焉，瑞兎毓焉，白鹿出焉，何者非皇上萬壽之所徵乎？此無他，民有欲生之情，而聖人者維持調護，錫以生全之慶，則德洽於無外，而維祺之吉以集；天有好生之心，而聖人者敷斂錫類，代厥生育之工，則仁周於不息，而滋至之祥以孚。我皇上所以紹
translation_en:
…as expressed in “Joy” (Jia le): “He protects and assists him, grants him his mandate, and renews it from Heaven.” As Your Majesty’s sacred person grows daily more hale and tranquil, and your sacred lifespan daily lengthens, you will surely move in concert with Heaven and endure without limit like Earth. How could the “ten thousand years and a thousand more” praised in the Book of Odes suffice as a comparison?

Today, throughout all under Heaven, the people and all living things flourish in harmony. The Chinese lands are secure; the non-Chinese peoples submit; mountains and rivers are at peace; the realm is tranquil; plants and trees thrive; birds and beasts live in accord with their nature. Which of these is not a blessing bestowed through Your Majesty’s boundless longevity? In recent years, auspicious signs have abounded: the Star of Longevity has appeared; auspicious clouds have shone brilliantly; sweet dew has fallen; numinous mushrooms have sprung up; auspicious rabbits have bred; and white deer have emerged. Which of these is not a portent of Your Majesty’s boundless longevity?

There is no other reason for this: the people desire to live, and the sage sustains, nurtures, and protects them, bestowing the blessing of preserving their lives intact. Thus his virtue reaches everywhere, leaving nothing beyond its bounds, and good fortune gathers about him. Heaven cherishes life, and the sage distributes and gathers blessings, extending them to others and carrying out Heaven’s work of bringing forth and nurturing life. Thus his benevolence extends everywhere without cease, and ever-increasing auspicious signs bear witness to it. That by which our emperor carries forward…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
祖宗億萬年之統膺
天地億萬年之曆者孰非大哉
皇心一念至仁之所致哉執事乃欲以颺言之
雅望庠序之士則愚也亦竊甞推本而揄
揚之矣伏覩我
皇上至德淵微
聖學之緝熈者亹亹也其
宣布而為臣民所服膺則
敬一有箴
===
四箴有註
欽天有紀微詞奧旨上接唐虞精一之訓而萬
世心學之傳胥此發焉不有以壽道統之
脉乎
聖德廣運治功之昭揭者炳炳也其注措而為
民物所快覩者則
明倫有典
秩祀有儀
耕桑有制宏綱大紀上繼唐虞昭明之治而
punctuated:
祖宗億萬年之統，膺天地億萬年之曆者，孰非大哉皇心一念至仁之所致哉？執事乃欲以颺言之雅望庠序之士，則愚也亦竊甞推本而揄揚之矣。伏覩我皇上至德淵微，聖學之緝熈者亹亹也。其宣布而為臣民所服膺，則敬一有箴，四箴有註，欽天有紀。微詞奧旨，上接唐虞精一之訓，而萬世心學之傳胥此發焉，不有以壽道統之脉乎？
聖德廣運，治功之昭揭者炳炳也。其注措而為民物所快覩者，則明倫有典，秩祀有儀，耕桑有制。宏綱大紀，上繼唐虞昭明之治，而
translation_en:
…the imperial succession of his ancestors for countless ages, and receives Heaven and Earth’s allotted span of countless ages—what part of this does not arise from the supreme benevolence of a single thought in His Majesty’s great heart? You, sir, now look to the scholars of the schools to offer words of praise. Foolish though I am, I too have ventured to trace these blessings to their source and extol them. I humbly observe that our Emperor’s consummate virtue is profound and subtle, and that he works tirelessly to continue and illuminate sagely learning. Among the teachings he has promulgated, which his officials and subjects reverently take to heart, are the Admonition on Reverent Unity, the Commentary on the Four Admonitions, and the Record of Revering Heaven. Their subtle language and profound meaning reach back to the teaching of refinement and singleness of mind under Tang Yao and Yu Shun; from these writings unfolds the transmission of the learning of the mind for all ages. Do they not thereby perpetuate the lineage of the Way?
His sagely virtue extends far and wide, and the manifest achievements of his governance shine brilliantly. Among the measures he has put into practice, which people and all living things behold with delight, are the Canon on Clarifying Human Relations, the Ritual Regulations for Ordering Sacrifices, and the Regulations for Ploughing and Sericulture. Their grand guiding principles and great ordinances carry forward the enlightened governance of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬世太平之澤胥此開焉不有以壽治統
之脉乎道統明則所以合
天地之德者愈久而愈昌治化宣則所以和
天地之氣者愈厚而愈長斯世斯民相與永賴
于
皇仁覆載之內而
皇上之壽自宜與
天地相為悠久矣愚跧伏嶺嶠游于
久道之化
===
仁壽之域也非一日矣雖模寫天地難於形
容然華封之祝則豈敢後於康衢擊壤之
歌哉謹對
第二問
劉體元
同考試官教諭韓批諸儒發明道學之言異
同各有攸當子能考據詳明辨析精確末段又
恐多言之晦道而欲求之於心是可以觀所養矣
考試官教諭劉批蘊藉深富而敷答詳盡
punctuated:
萬世太平之澤胥此開焉，不有以壽治統之脉乎？道統明，則所以合天地之德者愈久而愈昌；治化宣，則所以和天地之氣者愈厚而愈長。斯世斯民，相與永賴于皇仁覆載之內，而皇上之壽自宜與天地相為悠久矣。愚跧伏嶺嶠，游于久道之化、仁壽之域也，非一日矣。雖模寫天地難於形容，然華封之祝，則豈敢後於康衢擊壤之歌哉？謹對。

第二問
劉體元

同考試官教諭韓批：諸儒發明道學之言，異同各有攸當。子能考據詳明，辨析精確，末段又恐多言之晦道而欲求之於心，是可以觀所養矣。

考試官教諭劉批：蘊藉深富，而敷答詳盡。
translation_en:
…and the blessings of enduring peace for ten thousand generations all begin here. Does this not serve to perpetuate the lineage of governance? When the lineage of the Way is illuminated, that which accords with the virtue of Heaven and Earth flourishes ever more with time; when transforming governance spreads, that which harmonizes with the vital energies of Heaven and Earth grows ever deeper and more enduring. This age and its people will together forever enjoy the shelter and support of imperial benevolence, and Your Majesty’s longevity will naturally match the enduring span of Heaven and Earth. Humbly secluded among the mountains of Lingjiao, I have long lived under the transforming influence of the enduring Way, in a realm of benevolence and longevity. Though Heaven and Earth are difficult to portray in words, how could I dare let my blessings, like those of the border warden of Hua, lag behind the songs sung on the broad thoroughfare and by those striking the earth? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Liu Tiyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: The various Confucian scholars’ statements elucidating the Learning of the Way, whether they agree or differ, each have their appropriate grounds. Your examination of the evidence is thorough and clear, and your distinctions and analyses are precise. In the final section, moreover, you fear that excessive words might obscure the Way and wish to seek it within the mind. This reveals the quality of your self-cultivation.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Rich in depth and substance, with a thorough and detailed response.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正楊批論理明悉而措詞醇雅
儒者之明道也以言故說之必極其詳學
者之會道也以心故析之必極其精夫道
統於心寓於言本至一者也說之詳則雖
散於殊途而要不外乎一致之理析之精
則雖岐於衆說而皆可約以一定之歸故
以心會道謂道之一可也以道觀言謂言
之一亦可也知乎此則可以立衆言之折
衷而不惑於諸說之異同矣非知言窮理
===
之學孰能與於此哉愚生泝濂洛之淵源
誦儒先之緒論則嘗究心理學而欲就正
有道也乆矣明問及焉敢不述之以對今
夫性命之說自子思發之朱子釋之曰天
所賦爲命人所受爲性其言天人之際甚
明也而又曰所賦者氣所受者理蓋自其
與形俱形而言之則涉於氣自其稟受一
定而言之則主夫理然論氣不論性不明
論性不論氣不備則其實非二物矣朱子
punctuated:
考試官學正楊批：「論理明悉，而措詞醇雅。」

儒者之明道也以言，故說之必極其詳；學者之會道也以心，故析之必極其精。夫道統於心，寓於言，本至一者也。說之詳，則雖散於殊途，而要不外乎一致之理；析之精，則雖岐於衆說，而皆可約以一定之歸。故以心會道，謂道之一可也；以道觀言，謂言之一亦可也。知乎此，則可以立衆言之折衷，而不惑於諸說之異同矣。非知言窮理之學，孰能與於此哉？愚生泝濂洛之淵源，誦儒先之緒論，則嘗究心理學，而欲就正有道也乆矣。明問及焉，敢不述之以對？今夫性命之說，自子思發之。朱子釋之曰：「天所賦爲命，人所受爲性。」其言天人之際甚明也。而又曰：「所賦者氣，所受者理。」蓋自其與形俱形而言之，則涉於氣；自其稟受一定而言之，則主夫理。然論氣不論性，不明；論性不論氣，不備。則其實非二物矣。朱子
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: “The discussion of principle is clear and thorough, and the wording refined and elegant.”

Confucian scholars elucidate the Way through words; hence their explanations must be exhaustive in detail. Learners comprehend the Way through the mind; hence their analyses must attain the utmost precision. The Way is gathered together in the mind and embodied in words; fundamentally, it is supremely one. When explanations are detailed, though they branch into different paths, their essentials never depart from a single, coherent principle. When analysis is precise, though it diverges among numerous doctrines, all can be brought back to one definite conclusion. Thus, when comprehending the Way through the mind, one may speak of the unity of the Way; when examining words in light of the Way, one may likewise speak of the unity of words. Understanding this, one can establish a standard for adjudicating among the many statements and avoid being bewildered by the similarities and differences among doctrines. Without the learning that understands words and exhaustively investigates principle, who could attain this?

I, an unworthy student, have traced the intellectual sources of the Lian and Luo traditions and recited the teachings handed down by earlier Confucian scholars. I have long devoted my mind to the learning of principle and wished to seek correction from those who possess the Way. Since your discerning question touches upon this, how could I fail to set forth what I know in reply?

Now, the doctrine of human nature and Heaven’s mandate was first expounded by Zisi. Master Zhu explained it, saying: “What Heaven confers is called the mandate; what human beings receive is called their nature.” His account of the relationship between Heaven and humanity is very clear. Yet he also said: “What is conferred is material force; what is received is principle.” Viewed in terms of its taking form together with bodily form [?], it concerns material force; viewed in terms of the fixed character of its endowment, it concerns primarily principle. Yet to discuss material force without discussing human nature is to lack clarity; to discuss human nature without discussing material force is to lack completeness. Thus, in reality, they are not two separate things. Master Zhu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之言豈固爲二耶道器之說自大易發之
程子訓之曰形而上者爲理形而下者爲
物其言物理之分甚辨也而又曰道亦器
器亦道蓋自其涉於形象之質則謂之器
自其原於物則之良則謂之道然道非器
不顯器非道不立則其原不相離矣程子
之言豈自爲異耶仁統四端程子專言仁
也而朱子之答袁機仲又以陰陽五行四
時配之者則是分言其性而各指其用耳
===
要之仁之貫徹於四端之中猶五行之根
乎木四時之本乎春條理雖極其分明而
脉絡則實相流通焉必如是而後四端之
旨無遺論矣心統性情張子專言心也而
程叔子之論又以性之有形爲心性之有
動爲情者則言心之主宰而性之發用耳
要之人受天地之中以爲心而性者即心
所具之理情者即心所達之用故言心而
性情皆在其中治心而性情皆得其正焉
punctuated: 之言豈固爲二耶？道器之說，自大易發之，程子訓之曰：「形而上者爲理，形而下者爲物。」其言物理之分甚辨也，而又曰：「道亦器，器亦道。」蓋自其涉於形象之質，則謂之器；自其原於物則之良，則謂之道。然道非器不顯，器非道不立，則其原不相離矣。程子之言豈自爲異耶？仁統四端，程子專言仁也，而朱子之答袁機仲，又以陰陽五行四時配之者，則是分言其性，而各指其用耳。要之，仁之貫徹於四端之中，猶五行之根乎木，四時之本乎春。條理雖極其分明，而脉絡則實相流通焉。必如是而後四端之旨無遺論矣。心統性情，張子專言心也，而程叔子之論，又以性之有形爲心，性之有動爲情者，則言心之主宰，而性之發用耳。要之，人受天地之中以爲心，而性者即心所具之理，情者即心所達之用。故言心而性情皆在其中，治心而性情皆得其正焉。
translation_en:
…could Master Zhu’s words really treat them as two separate things? The account of the Way and concrete things originated in the great Book of Changes. Master Cheng explained it thus: “What is above form is principle; what is below form is concrete things.” His words distinguish things from principle very clearly, yet he also said: “The Way is also concrete things; concrete things are also the Way.” Considered in terms of their material substance, involving shape and appearance, they are called concrete things; considered in terms of their origin in the inherent goodness of the norms governing things, they are called the Way. Yet without concrete things the Way cannot manifest itself, and without the Way concrete things cannot be established. Thus, at their source, they are inseparable. Could Master Cheng’s words contradict themselves?

In saying that benevolence encompasses the four moral beginnings, Master Cheng was speaking specifically of benevolence. When Master Zhu, in his reply to Yuan Jizhong, also correlated them with yin and yang, the Five Phases, and the four seasons, he was merely discussing their natures separately and indicating their respective functions. In essence, benevolence pervades the four moral beginnings, just as the Five Phases are rooted in Wood and the four seasons have their basis in spring. Although their ordered distinctions are perfectly clear, their connecting channels do indeed flow into one another. Only with this understanding can an account of the meaning of the four moral beginnings leave nothing unaddressed.

In saying that the mind governs both human nature and the feelings, Master Zhang was speaking specifically of the mind. When the younger Master Cheng, in his discussion, further identified human nature having form as the mind, and human nature in motion as the feelings, he was merely speaking of the mind’s governing role and human nature’s manifestation in operation. In essence, human beings receive the central harmony of Heaven and Earth as their mind. Human nature is precisely the principle inherent in the mind, and the feelings are precisely the functioning expressed through the mind. Thus, when one speaks of the mind, human nature and the feelings are both included within it; when one puts the mind in order, human nature and the feelings both attain their proper condition.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
必如是而後心性情之論無餘蘊矣孔子
之論仁智也曰知者動仁者靜矣而朱子
之解易則有仁陽智陰之說疑於異也殊
不知以本體言則知動而仁靜以生稟言
則仁陽而智陰義固各有所屬耳况明通
足以公溥則動而未嘗無靜也無私足以
有覺則靜而未嘗無動也動靜無端陰陽
無始觀仁知者合而一之斯可矣子思之
論仁智也曰成己仁成物智矣而朱子之
===
釋聖則有自明及物之說疑於殊也殊不
知成己成物者思誠一貫之功不厭不倦
者成德合一之妙意固各有所指耳况存
神妙於應物則成己固成物之本也達順
由於體信則成物固成己之推也體用一
原人己無間論仁智者一以貫之而已矣
盡己爲忠盡物爲信程子嘗示人以立誠
之要矣而乃謂有天道人道之別者則似
以內外人己分之也要之存於內而無不
punctuated:
必如是而後心性情之論無餘蘊矣。孔子之論仁智也，曰：「知者動，仁者靜。」矣。而朱子之解易，則有仁陽智陰之說，疑於異也。殊不知，以本體言，則知動而仁靜；以生稟言，則仁陽而智陰，義固各有所屬耳。况明通足以公溥，則動而未嘗無靜也；無私足以有覺，則靜而未嘗無動也。動靜無端，陰陽無始，觀仁知者合而一之，斯可矣。子思之論仁智也，曰：「成己仁，成物智。」矣。而朱子之釋聖，則有自明及物之說，疑於殊也。殊不知，成己成物者，思誠一貫之功；不厭不倦者，成德合一之妙，意固各有所指耳。况存神妙於應物，則成己固成物之本也；達順由於體信，則成物固成己之推也。體用一原，人己無間，論仁智者一以貫之而已矣。
盡己爲忠，盡物爲信，程子嘗示人以立誠之要矣。而乃謂有天道人道之別者，則似以內外人己分之也。要之，存於內而無不
translation_en:
…Only in this way can a discussion of the mind, human nature, and the feelings leave none of their profound meaning unexplored. Confucius, discussing benevolence and wisdom, said: “The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” Yet Zhu Xi, in his explanation of the Book of Changes, speaks of benevolence as yang and wisdom as yin. These statements seem to differ. What this overlooks is that, in terms of their fundamental substance, wisdom is active and benevolence still; in terms of the endowment received at birth, benevolence is yang and wisdom yin. Each formulation has its own proper reference. Moreover, when lucid understanding suffices for impartial breadth, activity is never without stillness; when selflessness suffices for awareness, stillness is never without activity. Activity and stillness have no starting point; yin and yang have no beginning. Those who consider benevolence and wisdom need only bring them together as one. Zisi, discussing benevolence and wisdom, said: “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” Yet Zhu Xi, in explaining sagehood, speaks of extending one's own understanding to things. These statements seem divergent. What this overlooks is that perfecting oneself and perfecting things are the work of seeking sincerity, threaded together by one principle; being neither satiated nor weary is the subtle unity of perfected virtue. Each formulation has its own intended reference. Moreover, preserving the spiritual within enables a subtle responsiveness to things, so perfecting oneself is indeed the foundation for perfecting things. Extending harmonious accord proceeds from embodying trustworthiness, so perfecting things is indeed the extension of perfecting oneself. Substance and function have a single source; others and oneself admit no separation. Those who discuss benevolence and wisdom need only thread them together by one principle.
To fulfill oneself completely is loyalty; to fulfill things completely is trustworthiness. Master Cheng once used these words to show people the essentials of establishing sincerity. Yet to speak of a distinction between the Way of Heaven and the human Way seems to divide them into the internal and external, oneself and others. In essence, what abides within and is in no respect…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
實者忠也卽信之存也發於外而無不實
者信也卽忠之驗也其殆有體用而無二
致者乎知以明理行以履事朱子嘗示人
以進道之序矣而又謂道之不明由於行
之過不及者則專以氣稟之偏言之也要
之致知之功深則所以翼其行者益裕力
行之功至則所以發其知者益精其殆交
相進而不可偏廢者乎是故自其異者而
觀之則隨在而命名指事以立敎猶之江
===
淮河漢之異其流也東西南北之殊其方
也先後彼此之間雖諸儒不能相爲謀耳
自其同者而觀之則名殊而旨一敎異而
道同猶之千流萬派而惟海是趨也千蹊
萬徑而惟國是適也至當歸一之極蓋諸
儒不待期而合耳甚矣諸儒立言之詳而
有功於道也雖然道以有言而明亦以多
言而晦學以知言爲始尤以忘言爲終爻
彖文言之作視乾坤之畫爲已詳典謨訓
punctuated:
實者，忠也，卽信之存也；發於外而無不實者，信也，卽忠之驗也。其殆有體用而無二致者乎？知以明理，行以履事，朱子嘗示人以進道之序矣。而又謂道之不明由於行之過不及者，則專以氣稟之偏言之也。要之，致知之功深，則所以翼其行者益裕；力行之功至，則所以發其知者益精。其殆交相進而不可偏廢者乎？

是故，自其異者而觀之，則隨在而命名，指事以立敎，猶之江淮河漢之異其流也，東西南北之殊其方也。先後彼此之間，雖諸儒不能相爲謀耳。自其同者而觀之，則名殊而旨一，敎異而道同，猶之千流萬派而惟海是趨也，千蹊萬徑而惟國是適也。至當歸一之極，蓋諸儒不待期而合耳。甚矣，諸儒立言之詳而有功於道也！

雖然，道以有言而明，亦以多言而晦。學以知言爲始，尤以忘言爲終。爻彖文言之作，視乾坤之畫爲已詳；典謨訓
translation_en:
…genuine is wholeheartedness: it is trustworthiness abiding within. What issues outwardly and is entirely genuine is trustworthiness: it is the verification of wholeheartedness. Might these have substance and function, yet admit of no divergence in their ultimate purport? Knowledge serves to illuminate principle; action serves to carry out affairs. Master Zhu once showed people through these the sequence for advancing in the Way. Yet when he also said that the Way’s failure to become clear arose from excess or deficiency in conduct, he was speaking specifically of imbalances in one’s endowment of vital energy. In essence, the deeper one’s work of extending knowledge, the more ample the support it provides for action; the more fully one’s work of earnest practice is accomplished, the more refined its capacity to bring forth understanding. Do these not advance one another, so that neither may be neglected?

Thus, viewed in terms of their differences, names are assigned according to the particular circumstances, and teachings are established with reference to particular matters. This is like the differing courses of the Jiang, Huai, He, and Han rivers, or the distinct directions of east, west, south, and north. Across different times and places, even the various Confucian scholars could not consult with one another. Viewed in terms of their common ground, however, their names differ but their purport is one; their teachings differ but their Way is the same. This is like a thousand streams and ten thousand tributaries all tending toward the sea, or a thousand paths and ten thousand roads all leading to the capital. At the ultimate point where perfect rightness converges in unity, the various scholars agree without prior arrangement. How detailed the formulations of these scholars are, and how great their service to the Way!

Nevertheless, the Way is made clear through words, but it is also obscured by too many words. Learning begins with understanding words, yet its culmination lies especially in forgetting words. The composition of the Line Statements, the Judgments, and the Commentary on the Words of the Text already provided fuller detail than the drawn lines of Qian and Kun; the Canons, Counsels, and Instructions…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
誥之篇視精一之言爲已演而況於後世
諸儒之紛紛哉孔子性與天道不可得而
聞而才辨如賜則以予欲無言告之其爲
斯道慮也至深遠矣然則吾人當如何亦
曰求之諸儒之言以盡其博反之吾心之
眞以守其約而必先之知行以密其功主
之忠信以務其實會之仁義禮智以體其
全則道也器也貫而通之矣性也命也盡
而至之矣心以會道道以致一蓋至是則
===
六經語孟皆筌蹄也諸子百家皆贅龐也
而況於異同之說足以惑之耶方今
聖人在君師之位心極明而經術正道德一而
風俗同愚知執事必不望諸生之求道於
言也故敢以是質之不知以爲何如
第三問
李上馨
同考試官敎諭周批兵法兵機不可闕一惟
在神而明之耳此作敷答詳明而規扠嚴切可謂
punctuated:
誥之篇，視精一之言爲已演，而況於後世諸儒之紛紛哉！孔子性與天道不可得而聞，而才辨如賜，則以「予欲無言」告之，其爲斯道慮也至深遠矣。然則吾人當如何？亦曰：求之諸儒之言，以盡其博；反之吾心之眞，以守其約。而必先之知行，以密其功；主之忠信，以務其實；會之仁義禮智，以體其全。則道也、器也，貫而通之矣；性也、命也，盡而至之矣。心以會道，道以致一。蓋至是，則六經語孟皆筌蹄也，諸子百家皆贅龐也，而況於異同之說足以惑之耶？方今聖人在君師之位，心極明而經術正，道德一而風俗同。愚知執事必不望諸生之求道於言也，故敢以是質之，不知以爲何如？

第三問
李上馨

同考試官敎諭周批：兵法兵機，不可闕一，惟在神而明之耳。此作敷答詳明，而規扠嚴切，可謂
translation_en:
…the chapters of “Announcements” already represent an elaboration upon the words about refinement and singleness of purpose; how much more so the profusion of statements by later Confucian scholars! Confucius’s teachings about human nature and the Way of Heaven could not be heard; even to someone as talented and eloquent as Ci, he said, “I wish to say nothing.” His concern for this Way was profound and far-reaching indeed. What, then, should we do? Seek it in the words of the Confucian scholars to comprehend its breadth; return to the truth within our own hearts to preserve its essentials. We must begin with knowledge and practice to make our efforts thorough, take loyalty and trustworthiness as our guiding principles to pursue what is substantial, and bring together benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom to embody the whole. Then we shall comprehend the Way and concrete things as interconnected, and fully realize human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Through the heart we apprehend the Way; through the Way we attain unity. At this point, the Six Classics, the Analects, and the Mencius are all merely fish traps and rabbit snares, while the various masters and hundred schools are extraneous clutter. How, then, could arguments about similarities and differences suffice to bewilder us? Today the sage occupies the position of ruler and teacher: his heart is supremely enlightened and classical learning is correct; the Way and its virtue are unified and customs are alike. I humbly know that you, honored examiners, surely do not expect us students to seek the Way in words. I therefore venture to submit this for your judgment, not knowing what you will think of it.

Third Question
Li Shangxin

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Neither military methods nor tactical judgment can be dispensed with; everything depends upon grasping and applying them with inspired understanding. This essay’s response is detailed and clear, and its prescriptions [?] are rigorous and pertinent. Its author may be called…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
知兵者矣
同考試官教諭樂批榷評古人陣法如指諸
掌而末引陶崔教閲之事有益於粤中之兵政子
其庶幾胸懷甲兵者乎
考試官教諭劉批不事雕辭而事核文健
自是談兵之體
考試官學正楊批詞氣渾雄而體裁嚴飭
蓋文之有步驟者
善治兵者練之有其法而運之有其機練
===
之無法則無節之兵不可用也運之無機
則執一之見不可通也是故必法練於有
素而奇正之相生者使兵無所不可由機
運於一心而權變之無迹者使人有所不
可測隨事迭施因時妙應則兵之所出其
衆如漠其重如山其不可禦如川其神速
而難備如疾雷迅電不及掩耳瞬目也而
又何攻之不克何堅之不瑕何海邦之氛
不可奏功而朝食耶易曰師出以律否臧
punctuated:
知兵者矣。
同考試官教諭樂批：榷評古人陣法，如指諸掌，而末引陶崔教閲之事，有益於粤中之兵政。子其庶幾胸懷甲兵者乎！
考試官教諭劉批：不事雕辭，而事核文健，自是談兵之體。
考試官學正楊批：詞氣渾雄，而體裁嚴飭，蓋文之有步驟者。
善治兵者，練之有其法，而運之有其機。練之無法，則無節之兵不可用也；運之無機，則執一之見不可通也。是故必法練於有素，而奇正之相生者，使兵無所不可；由機運於一心，而權變之無迹者，使人有所不可測。隨事迭施，因時妙應，則兵之所出，其衆如漠，其重如山，其不可禦如川，其神速而難備，如疾雷迅電，不及掩耳瞬目也。而又何攻之不克，何堅之不瑕，何海邦之氛不可奏功而朝食耶？《易》曰：「師出以律，否臧……」
translation_en:
…one who understands warfare indeed.

Comment by Associate Examiner Le, Instructor: His appraisal of the battle formations of the ancients makes them as clear as something pointed out in one’s palm. At the end, he cites the training and inspection of troops by Tao and Cui, matters beneficial to military administration in Guangdong. Are you not perhaps one who carries armies within his breast?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He does not pursue ornate diction; his treatment of affairs is sound and his writing vigorous. This is precisely the proper manner for discussing warfare.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: The language and spirit are full and powerful, while the composition is rigorous and orderly. This is writing that proceeds in measured stages.

Those skilled in managing troops have methods for training them and a grasp of opportunity in deploying them. If training lacks method, undisciplined troops cannot be employed; if deployment lacks a grasp of opportunity, rigid adherence to a single view cannot accommodate changing circumstances. Thus methods must be thoroughly practiced beforehand, and the mutually generative use of unorthodox and orthodox tactics must leave the troops capable of anything. Opportunities must be handled through the commander’s single directing mind, and expedient adaptations must leave no trace, so that others cannot fathom them. Apply these in turn as circumstances require, responding deftly to the occasion. Then, wherever the troops advance, their numbers will be like the desert’s expanse, their weight like a mountain, their irresistible force like a river. Their extraordinary speed will make them as difficult to guard against as crashing thunder and flashing lightning, leaving no time to cover one’s ears or blink. What attack, then, would fail to conquer? What stronghold would not be breached? What menace along the coast could not be subdued before the morning meal? The Book of Changes says: “An army goes forth according to regulations; if these are not sound…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
凶言兵之不可無制也兵志曰微乎微乎
至於無形神乎神乎至於無聲言法之不
可盡執也通乎此者可以抵掌談戎矣且
師曷為而有陣也師者眾也眾之所萃易
於混亂而無統將兵者無法以制之則分
而不知所以合合而不知所以分金鼓之
聲旌旗之節雜陳莫辨一遇衝擊則彼此
不相顧而獸奔鳥散不可阻遏卽自謀且
不暇也而暇於謀人乎哉吁此陣法之不
===
可不講也考之於古營陣之法備於周禮
而尤莫詳於握奇篇大司馬三軍之制萬
有二千五百人為一軍小司徒乃合萬民
之卒旅而用之伍兩軍師之中四奇四正
而陣法寓焉至於四時之教仲春振旅仲
夏茇舍仲秋治兵仲冬大閱又孰非使之
習坐作進退之宜徐疾疏數之節乎黃帝
征蚩尤之迹遐不可稽矣而戰國之時兵
家著述謂八陣圖乃黃帝臣風后所製以
punctuated:
凶。」言兵之不可無制也。《兵志》曰：「微乎微乎，至於無形；神乎神乎，至於無聲。」言法之不可盡執也。通乎此者，可以抵掌談戎矣。且師曷為而有陣也？師者，眾也。眾之所萃，易於混亂而無統。將兵者無法以制之，則分而不知所以合，合而不知所以分。金鼓之聲、旌旗之節，雜陳莫辨，一遇衝擊，則彼此不相顧，而獸奔鳥散，不可阻遏。卽自謀且不暇也，而暇於謀人乎哉？吁！此陣法之不可不講也。
考之於古，營陣之法備於《周禮》，而尤莫詳於《握奇篇》。大司馬三軍之制，萬有二千五百人為一軍；小司徒乃合萬民之卒旅而用之。伍兩軍師之中，四奇四正，而陣法寓焉。至於四時之教，仲春振旅，仲夏茇舍，仲秋治兵，仲冬大閱，又孰非使之習坐作進退之宜、徐疾疏數之節乎？黃帝征蚩尤之迹，遐不可稽矣。而戰國之時，兵家著述謂八陣圖乃黃帝臣風后所製，以
translation_en:
…“misfortune.” This means that troops cannot be without regulation. The Military Records says: “Subtle, so subtle as to reach formlessness; wondrous, so wondrous as to reach soundlessness.” This means that methods cannot all be rigidly adhered to. Whoever understands this can confidently discourse on warfare. Moreover, why does an army have formations? An army is a multitude. Wherever a multitude gathers, it readily falls into confusion and loses cohesion. If its commander has no methods for controlling it, then, once dispersed, the soldiers do not know how to unite, and, once united, they do not know how to disperse. The sounds of gongs and drums and the signals of banners and flags mingle indistinguishably. At the first assault, the soldiers cannot look after one another: they flee like beasts and scatter like birds, beyond all restraint. They have scarcely time to devise their own escape; how could they have time to devise a plan against the enemy? Ah! This is why the methods of military formation must be studied.
Examining antiquity, we find the methods of encampment and formation fully provided in the Rites of Zhou, but nowhere set out in greater detail than in the Treatise on Grasping the Unorthodox (Woqi pian). Under the Minister of War’s system of three armies, 12,500 men constituted one army; the Vice Minister of Education assembled the companies and battalions of the common people and put them into service. Within the squads, platoons, armies, and regiments were four unorthodox and four orthodox formations, embodying the methods of deployment. As for training in the four seasons—mustering the troops in mid-spring, encamping in mid-summer, preparing for battle in mid-autumn, and holding the grand review in mid-winter—was any of this other than a means of teaching them the proper ways to sit and rise, advance and retreat, and the prescribed rhythms of slow and rapid movement and open and close spacing? The events of Huangdi’s campaign against Chiyou are too remote to verify. Yet military writings from the Warring States period say that the Diagram of the Eight Formations was devised by Huangdi’s minister Feng Hou, in order to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
取勝于涿鹿之野者今觀握竒所載八其
圖所以定位衡抗於外軸布于內風雲附
其四維所以備物而虎踞蛇蟠飛龍翔鳥
弛張掎角離合不窮竒哉圖也雖未必出
於風后之製而後之欲立營陣之法者孰
能外之乎周之文武大聖人也神武不殺
其用兵宜不必於圖矣而降崇之績鉤陳
之壘且不廢焉宣王中興亦用此以制淮
夷詩人歌之曰截彼淮浦王師之所又曰
===
繇繇翼翼不測不克蓋美王師之無敵也
漢興去周未遠陣法猶有能通之者而其
君相亦究心武略敷演陣法以五營士為
六十四壘習之於長樂館故當時將兵諸
臣俱能勒功萬里之外大振中國之威豈
非陣法章明而將士有所憑藉與自後精
於圖者于三國有諸葛孔明焉鼎立之時
魏已有天下之半孔明提孤軍出斜谷司
馬懿以蓋世之英雄率步騎四十萬而不
punctuated:
取勝于涿鹿之野者。今觀《握竒》所載，八其圖，所以定位；衡抗於外，軸布于內，風雲附其四維，所以備物。而虎踞蛇蟠，飛龍翔鳥，弛張掎角，離合不窮。竒哉，圖也！雖未必出於風后之製，而後之欲立營陣之法者，孰能外之乎？
周之文武，大聖人也，神武不殺，其用兵宜不必於圖矣。而降崇之績，鉤陳之壘，且不廢焉。宣王中興，亦用此以制淮夷。詩人歌之曰：「截彼淮浦，王師之所。」又曰：「繇繇翼翼，不測不克。」蓋美王師之無敵也。
漢興，去周未遠，陣法猶有能通之者，而其君相亦究心武略，敷演陣法，以五營士為六十四壘，習之於長樂館。故當時將兵諸臣，俱能勒功萬里之外，大振中國之威，豈非陣法章明，而將士有所憑藉與？
自後精於圖者，于三國有諸葛孔明焉。鼎立之時，魏已有天下之半，孔明提孤軍出斜谷，司馬懿以蓋世之英雄，率步騎四十萬而不
translation_en:
…to win victory on the plain of Zhuolu. Now, examining what is recorded in the Grasping the Wondrous (Wo qi), its diagrams are eight in number [?], providing the means to establish positions. The transverse formations stand on the outside, the axial formations are arrayed within, and the Wind and Cloud formations adjoin their four corners, thus providing a full complement of elements. There are crouching tigers and coiling snakes, flying dragons and soaring birds; formations relax and tighten, support one another from opposite angles, and separate and combine without end. How wondrous these diagrams are! Although they need not have been devised by Feng Hou, who among those who later sought to establish methods for encampments and battle formations could dispense with them?
Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou were great sages, possessed of divine martial power without killing; one might suppose that their use of troops would not have required diagrams. Yet in the achievement of bringing Chong to submission, the hooked encampments were not dispensed with. During his restoration of the dynasty, King Xuan likewise used these methods to subdue the Huai Yi. The poet celebrated this, saying: “Well ordered are those banks of the Huai, where the royal army is stationed.” And again: “Composed and disciplined, they cannot be fathomed or overcome.” These words praise the invincibility of the royal army.
When the Han arose, the Zhou was not yet far in the past, and there were still men who understood the methods of battle formation. Its rulers and chief ministers also applied themselves to military strategy, elaborating the methods of formation and organizing the soldiers of the Five Encampments into sixty-four fortified positions, which they practiced at Changle Hall. Thus the officials commanding troops at that time were all able to win achievements worthy of inscription ten thousand li away, greatly enhancing the military prestige of the Central Kingdom. Was this not because the methods of battle formation were clearly set forth, giving officers and soldiers something on which to rely?
Among those subsequently expert in these diagrams was Zhuge Kongming of the Three Kingdoms. At the time of the tripartite division, Wei already possessed half the realm. Kongming led a lone army out through Xie Valley. Sima Yi, a hero whose prowess surpassed his age, commanded four hundred thousand infantry and cavalry, yet did not…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
敢決戰者知其陣之不可犯也至今魚復
平沙之上舊蹟不磨六十四壘布于前者
八陣也二十四壘環于後如却月者遊兵
也或直而方或曲而圓出入無方變化不
滯其奪造化之神機乎晋桓温見之謂為
常山蛇勢蓋會之意象之表而非妄言者
矣孔明而下能通其術者于唐有李靖焉
靖之陣法雖授於韓擒虎而六花之陣方
圓異其形九軍七軍異其數矣但七軍即
===
九軍之變六花者內外俱圓八陣又未甞
不外方而內圓也觀其對太宗自言臣本
諸葛亮八陣法但靖以時久戰伐將帥通
達是法者頗多故更亮之制使人不能窺
耳若宋蘇軾謂司馬之法主於環曲所以
固拒管子之法主於直銳所以克捷則是
古法局于營守後世專于進戰二者殆不
相為用矣豈所以盡圖法之妙哉夫圖以
決勝則治兵者之練士盡于圖可也而張
punctuated: 敢決戰者，知其陣之不可犯也。至今魚復平沙之上，舊蹟不磨。六十四壘布于前者，八陣也；二十四壘環于後如却月者，遊兵也。或直而方，或曲而圓，出入無方，變化不滯，其奪造化之神機乎！晋桓温見之，謂為常山蛇勢，蓋會之意象之表，而非妄言者矣。孔明而下，能通其術者，于唐有李靖焉。靖之陣法雖授於韓擒虎，而六花之陣，方圓異其形，九軍七軍異其數矣。但七軍即九軍之變，六花者內外俱圓，八陣又未甞不外方而內圓也。觀其對太宗，自言：「臣本諸葛亮八陣法。」但靖以時久戰伐，將帥通達是法者頗多，故更亮之制，使人不能窺耳。若宋蘇軾謂司馬之法主於環曲，所以固拒；管子之法主於直銳，所以克捷，則是古法局于營守，後世專于進戰，二者殆不相為用矣。豈所以盡圖法之妙哉！夫圖以決勝，則治兵者之練士盡于圖可也，而張
translation_en:
…dared not engage in a decisive battle because he knew that those formations could not be assailed. Even today, on the level sands of Yufu, their ancient traces remain unerased. The sixty-four ramparts arrayed in front constitute the Eight Formations; the twenty-four ramparts encircling the rear like a crescent moon are for the mobile troops. Sometimes straight and square, sometimes curved and round, they enter and emerge without a fixed pattern and transform without impediment. Might they have captured the wondrous workings of creation itself? When Huan Wen of the Jin saw them, he called them the serpent disposition of Mount Chang. He surely grasped something beyond their outward appearance; these were no idle words.

After Kongming, one who understood this art was Li Jing of the Tang. Although Jing received his methods of deployment from Han Qinhu, his Six Flowers Formation differed in its square and round configurations, and the Nine Armies and Seven Armies differed in number. Yet the Seven Armies were simply a variation of the Nine Armies. The Six Flowers were round both within and without, while the Eight Formations, too, were square outside and round within. Consider his reply to Emperor Taizong, in which he himself said: “Your servant took Zhuge Liang’s Eight Formations as his basis.” But Jing considered that, after so many years of warfare, quite a few commanders thoroughly understood this method. He therefore altered Liang’s arrangements merely to prevent others from fathoming them.

As for Su Shi of the Song, he held that the methods of the Sima relied chiefly on encircling curves, thereby providing firm resistance, while the methods of Guanzi relied chiefly on straight, pointed formations, thereby securing victory. This would mean that ancient methods were confined to defending encampments and later methods devoted exclusively to advancing into battle, with the two scarcely capable of serving each other’s purposes. How could this exhaust the subtleties of formation diagrams? If diagrams determine victory, then it would be acceptable for those who organize armies to confine all their training of soldiers to diagrams. Yet Zhang…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
巡之教戰惟使士知將意將識士情岳武
穆之言亦曰陣而後戰兵家之常運用之
妙存乎一心則二子之見有自得於陣法
之外者故睢陽之守卒致江淮之保全而
朱仙鎮之捷黠虜如兀朮且將棄城遠避
焉此其故何也蓋法寓乎機而心寄於法
可相和而不可相離者養由基以射名天
下其法不盡於彀率而公輸子之巧又未
有舍繩墨而專以目中者也是故孔明李
===
靖精于法者兵固極天下之至安矣而機
以神之又未嘗不極天下之至變張巡武
穆妙于機者兵固極天下之至變矣而法
以紀之又未嘗不極天下之至安辟之醫
焉岐黃製方者也用方治病百無不中者
而庸醫用之則反有以古方而誤人者盧
醫扁鵲不用方者也膏肓之疾一望之而
可知焉故有岐黃盧扁之術則用方可也
不用方亦可也若非其人則用方不應不
punctuated: 巡之教戰，惟使士知將意，將識士情。岳武穆之言亦曰：「陣而後戰，兵家之常；運用之妙，存乎一心。」則二子之見，有自得於陣法之外者。故睢陽之守，卒致江淮之保全；而朱仙鎮之捷，黠虜如兀朮，且將棄城遠避焉。此其故何也？蓋法寓乎機，而心寄於法，可相和而不可相離者。養由基以射名天下，其法不盡於彀率；而公輸子之巧，又未有舍繩墨而專以目中者也。是故孔明、李靖精于法者，兵固極天下之至安矣，而機以神之，又未嘗不極天下之至變；張巡、武穆妙于機者，兵固極天下之至變矣，而法以紀之，又未嘗不極天下之至安。辟之醫焉，岐黃製方者也，用方治病，百無不中者；而庸醫用之，則反有以古方而誤人者。盧醫、扁鵲不用方者也，膏肓之疾，一望之而可知焉。故有岐黃、盧扁之術，則用方可也，不用方亦可也。若非其人，則用方不應，不…
translation_en:
…Xun, in teaching his men to fight, sought only to make the soldiers understand their commander's intentions and the commander understand his soldiers' dispositions. Yue Wumu also said: “To deploy in formation before fighting is the ordinary practice of military commanders; mastery in its application resides in the mind alone.” These two men thus possessed insights of their own beyond the rules of battle formations. Hence the defense of Suiyang ultimately secured the preservation of the Jiang and Huai regions; and after the victory at Zhuxianzhen, even so cunning an enemy as Wuzhu was about to abandon the city and withdraw far away. Why was this? Established methods reside within responses to changing circumstances, while the mind finds expression through those methods: the two can work in harmony but cannot be separated. Yang Youji was renowned throughout the realm for archery, yet his method was not exhausted by the rules for drawing a bow. Nor did the skill of Master Gongshu ever involve abandoning the marking line and relying entirely on the eye for accuracy.

Thus Kongming and Li Jing, who excelled in established methods, brought warfare to the utmost stability; yet by giving those methods inspired application through responsiveness to circumstances, they also attained the utmost adaptability. Zhang Xun and Wumu, who excelled in responding to circumstances, brought warfare to the utmost adaptability; yet by ordering it through established methods, they also attained the utmost stability. Consider medicine as an analogy. Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor devised prescriptions: used to treat illness, these invariably hit the mark. Yet when mediocre physicians employ them, they may instead harm people with ancient prescriptions. Lu Yi and Bian Que did not rely on prescriptions: they could recognize even a disease lodged deep in the vital organs at a glance. Thus, if one possesses the arts of Qi Bo, the Yellow Emperor, Lu Yi, and Bian Que, it is acceptable to use prescriptions, and equally acceptable not to use them. But if one lacks their abilities, using prescriptions will prove ineffective, and not…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
用方亦不應何者方不出於心而心又無
以神乎方故也治兵者亦若是而已孔明
李靖非所謂岐黃而張巡武穆非所謂盧
扁耶不然趙括知書長平蹶績任福違制
易水隳功皆往事之明鑒也法之與機其
可偏廢哉方今嶺南之區山海之寇雖云
就殄而嘯聚竊發者日爲吾民患兵固不
可一日去也但謂之兵者出於召募則市
井無藉之夫也隸于兵籍則豢養脆弱之
===
輩也平居選之不精練之無法以之臨敵
何怪其如潰癰潰土而莫可倚賴耶吁神
兵不留訣八陣之圖不可傳矣愚聞陶侃
刺廣州患兵不堪用而所教五營士卽大
將居中外列四營之制崔清獻爲帥日分
諸軍爲三等教閲不一歲而淮東軍聲大
振此二公者陣法雖未必如古而誌之所
載皆鑿鑿可行者也今當事者誠能選其
什伍厚其資給又倣二公之法而神明于
punctuated:
用方亦不應。何者？方不出於心，而心又無以神乎方故也。治兵者亦若是而已。孔明、李靖非所謂岐黃，而張巡、武穆非所謂盧扁耶？不然，趙括知書，長平蹶績；任福違制，易水隳功，皆往事之明鑒也。法之與機，其可偏廢哉？
方今嶺南之區，山海之寇雖云就殄，而嘯聚竊發者日爲吾民患，兵固不可一日去也。但謂之兵者，出於召募，則市井無藉之夫也；隸于兵籍，則豢養脆弱之輩也。平居選之不精，練之無法，以之臨敵，何怪其如潰癰潰土而莫可倚賴耶？吁！神兵不留訣，八陣之圖不可傳矣。愚聞陶侃刺廣州，患兵不堪用，而所教五營士，卽大將居中、外列四營之制。崔清獻爲帥日，分諸軍爲三等，教閲不一歲，而淮東軍聲大振。此二公者，陣法雖未必如古，而誌之所載皆鑿鑿可行者也。今當事者誠能選其什伍，厚其資給，又倣二公之法而神明于
translation_en:
…nor will dispensing with prescriptions prove effective. Why is this? Because the prescriptions do not arise from the mind, and the mind lacks the means to give them inspired application. Managing troops is just the same. Are not Kongming and Li Jing the counterparts of Qi Bo and the Yellow Emperor, and Zhang Xun and Wumu the counterparts of Physician Lu and Bian Que?
