Otherwise, consider Zhao Kuo: he knew the military books, yet suffered defeat at Changping. Ren Fu disobeyed orders and ruined his campaign at Yishui [?]. These are all clear warnings from past events. Can either established methods or adaptive judgment be neglected?
At present, in the Lingnan region, although the bandits of the mountains and seas are said to have been nearly exterminated, those who gather in bands and launch sudden raids daily afflict our people. Troops certainly cannot be dispensed with for even a day. Yet those called soldiers, if recruited by enlistment, are disreputable fellows from the marketplaces; if borne on the military registers, they are pampered and weak. In ordinary times, they are selected without care and trained without method. When they are sent against the enemy, what wonder that they collapse like a bursting abscess or crumbling earth, and cannot be relied upon? Alas! Inspired commanders have left no secret instructions, and the diagram of the Eight Formations can no longer be transmitted.
I have heard that when Tao Kan served as Regional Inspector of Guangzhou, he was troubled by the troops’ unfitness for service. He trained the men of five camps in a system whereby the commanding general occupied the center and four camps were arrayed around him. When Cui Qingxian was commander, he divided the armies into three grades. After less than a year of training and inspections, the military reputation of Huaidong rose greatly. Although these two men’s methods of deployment were not necessarily identical to those of antiquity, everything recorded about them in the gazetteers is concrete and practicable. If those now in charge can truly select the men of their squads and files carefully, provide them with generous supplies and pay, and also emulate these two men’s methods, applying them with inspired understanding in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
心時演習其士卒則兵皆可用何寇之足
貽民患哉愚生之見若此執事以爲何如
第四問
陳法
同考試官教諭姚批品第嶺表人物若燭照
數計而末段立志之論尤爲希賢希聖之階執此
以往殆不止爲一鄉一國之善士而已錄之非徒
以其文也
考試官教諭劉批稽覈詳明而品題雅當
===
蓋留心景行者
考試官學正楊批論人明悉而責己遠大
蓋有志之士也
古之君子所以樹休光於當時而垂芳譽
於後世者有四美焉窮之經術以致用也
宣之文章以述志也脩之行誼以立德也
措諸政事以表業也隨其學之所得而不
求其全則凡爲經術爲文章苟有一之幾
乎道皆尚論者所不棄也然進之以身心
punctuated:
心，時演習其士卒，則兵皆可用，何寇之足貽民患哉？愚生之見若此，執事以爲何如？

第四問
陳法

同考試官教諭姚批：品第嶺表人物，若燭照數計，而末段立志之論，尤爲希賢希聖之階。執此以往，殆不止爲一鄉一國之善士而已。錄之，非徒以其文也。

考試官教諭劉批：稽覈詳明，而品題雅當，蓋留心景行者。

考試官學正楊批：論人明悉，而責己遠大，蓋有志之士也。

古之君子所以樹休光於當時而垂芳譽於後世者，有四美焉：窮之經術以致用也，宣之文章以述志也，脩之行誼以立德也，措諸政事以表業也。隨其學之所得而不求其全，則凡爲經術、爲文章，苟有一之幾乎道，皆尚論者所不棄也。然進之以身心
translation_en:
…in their minds, and regularly drill their soldiers, then all the troops can be put to use. What bandits could then bring suffering upon the people? Such is this humble student's view. What do you, honored sir, think of it?

Fourth Question
Chen Fa

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: His ranking of the notable figures of Lingbiao is as clear as illumination by a lamp and as precise as counting. His discussion of establishing one's aspirations in the final section is especially a step toward emulating worthies and sages. If he proceeds on this basis, he will surely become more than merely a good scholar of one village or one state. We have selected this essay not merely for its literary merits.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: His examination of the evidence is detailed and lucid, and his judgments are fitting. He is evidently someone who gives thought to exemplary conduct.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: His discussion of others is clear and thorough, while the demands he places upon himself are far-reaching and ambitious. He is evidently a scholar with high aspirations.

There were four admirable qualities through which the gentlemen of antiquity established a glorious reputation in their own time and left an honored name to later generations: they pursued classical learning exhaustively to put it to practical use; they expressed themselves in literary compositions to articulate their aspirations; they cultivated their conduct to establish virtue; and they applied themselves to government affairs to manifest their achievements. If we judge according to what each attained in learning, without demanding completeness, then among those devoted to classical learning or literary composition, anyone who approached the Way in even one respect would not be rejected by those who appraise the ancients. Yet if we advance the assessment by reference to the body and mind…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
性命之大原則義理之學其見卓矣據其
善之所造而不責之備則凡爲行誼爲政
事苟有一之合乎道皆遠稽者所不遺也
然律之以可久可大之極致則德業之賢
其造深矣特此四者以進退古今表裏人
物寧不足以定臧否之評而決趨舎之衷
也哉執事以粤才爲問蓋亦啓諸生以高
山仰止之思乎則愚請得而論其世矣吾
粤僻居嶺表由周以前未通中國也秦漢
===
而下畫野分疆風氣漸開文物始盛晉司
馬彪甞著九州春秋而略於嶺服王範見
而病之乃蒐羅粤典名曰交廣春秋而人
文賴以不闕歷世旣遠荒寥靡傳尚論君
子猶惜於文獻之不盡徵焉姑即誌牒所
載明問所指者而評之可乎試以經術文
章言之高固進春秋微由以開楚之文治
陳元請立左氏博士以存漢之經學通毛
詩三禮春秋雖屢辟而不就者則董正其
punctuated:
性命之大原，則義理之學其見卓矣。據其善之所造而不責之備，則凡爲行誼、爲政事，苟有一之合乎道，皆遠稽者所不遺也。然律之以可久可大之極致，則德業之賢其造深矣。特此四者，以進退古今、表裏人物，寧不足以定臧否之評，而決趨舎之衷也哉？執事以粤才爲問，蓋亦啓諸生以高山仰止之思乎？則愚請得而論其世矣。
吾粤僻居嶺表，由周以前，未通中國也。秦漢而下，畫野分疆，風氣漸開，文物始盛。晉司馬彪甞著《九州春秋》，而略於嶺服。王範見而病之，乃蒐羅粤典，名曰《交廣春秋》，而人文賴以不闕。歷世旣遠，荒寥靡傳，尚論君子猶惜於文獻之不盡徵焉。姑即誌牒所載、明問所指者而評之，可乎？
試以經術、文章言之，高固進《春秋微》，由以開楚之文治；陳元請立左氏博士，以存漢之經學；通《毛詩》、《三禮》、《春秋》，雖屢辟而不就者，則董正其
translation_en:
…the great source of human nature and destiny, then the learning of moral principles affords a lofty vision indeed. If we judge people by the excellence they have attained without demanding completeness, then anyone whose conduct or administration accords with the Way in even one respect will not be overlooked by those who examine the distant past. Yet if we measure them against the highest ideal of what can endure and attain greatness, then the achievements of those eminent in virtue and accomplishment are profound indeed. Are these four criteria alone, used to rank people ancient and modern and assess them inwardly and outwardly, not sufficient to settle judgments of praise and blame and determine what one should pursue or reject? In asking about Guangdong’s talented men, are you, honored examiners, also awakening in us students the wish to gaze up at lofty mountains—that is, to admire worthy exemplars? Then permit me, in my humble capacity, to discuss the ages in which they lived.
Our Guangdong lies remotely beyond the mountains. From the Zhou period backward, it had no communication with the Central States. From the Qin and Han onward, territories were delineated and boundaries established; prevailing customs gradually became enlightened, and cultural institutions began to flourish. Sima Biao of the Jin once composed the Annals of the Nine Provinces, but treated the Lingnan region only briefly. Wang Fan saw this and regretted it, so he gathered Guangdong’s records into a work called the Annals of Jiao and Guang. Thanks to it, the region’s cultural record was preserved from omission. Yet those ages are now far distant, and much has vanished without transmission. Gentlemen who appraise the ancients still regret that the documentary record and surviving testimony cannot be fully verified. May I provisionally assess those recorded in local histories and registers and indicated in your illuminating question?
Let us begin with classical scholarship and literary composition. Gao Gu presented the Subtle Meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals [?], thereby initiating civil governance through culture in Chu. Chen Yuan requested the establishment of an Erudite for the Zuo Commentary, thereby preserving Han classical scholarship. As for the man versed in the Mao Book of Odes, the Three Ritual Classics, and the Spring and Autumn Annals, who repeatedly declined summonses to office, Dong Zheng was that…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人也講五經進易解雖時論有不徇者則
石汝礪其人也之四子者在朝廷則崇正
闢邪而治教興在畝畝則講書陳禮而道
義明謂非經術之精不可也林從周賦頌
之獻名曰獄空年豐而其意本於尚寬和
楊孚誌記之作名曰異物水土而其志在
於端貢獻作廣樂記太常釋文則有如馮
元焉登科作賦人稱李伯夷則有如李渤
焉之數子者以獻納則可格心而正事以
===
著作則可立言而垂訓謂非文章之富不
可也夫均之為經術均之為文章則隨其
所得皆有可取而求其進於是者則周濂
溪傳二程之學於北而梅鼎臣父子述庸
學于其時朱元晦定敬夫之交於南而李
用父子述語孟于其後鄭南升郭叔雲皆
師事朱子者也一則篤志於力學一則用
意於實踐黃執矩簡克已皆師事張子者
也一則講明乎性理一則學慕乎濂洛夫
punctuated:
人也。講五經、進易解，雖時論有不徇者，則石汝礪其人也。之四子者，在朝廷則崇正闢邪而治教興，在畝畝則講書陳禮而道義明，謂非經術之精不可也。林從周賦頌之獻，名曰《獄空年豐》，而其意本於尚寬和；楊孚誌記之作，名曰《異物水土》，而其志在於端貢獻。作《廣樂記》《太常釋文》，則有如馮元焉；登科作賦，人稱李伯夷，則有如李渤焉。之數子者，以獻納則可格心而正事，以著作則可立言而垂訓，謂非文章之富不可也。
夫均之為經術，均之為文章，則隨其所得皆有可取。而求其進於是者，則周濂溪傳二程之學於北，而梅鼎臣父子述《庸》《學》于其時；朱元晦定敬夫之交於南，而李用父子述《語》《孟》于其後。鄭南升、郭叔雲皆師事朱子者也，一則篤志於力學，一則用意於實踐；黃執矩、簡克已皆師事張子者也，一則講明乎性理，一則學慕乎濂洛。夫
translation_en:
…was such a man. As for lecturing on the Five Classics and presenting an Explanation of the Changes, even when contemporary opinion did not concur, Shi Ruli was such a man. These four men, when at court, upheld orthodoxy and rejected heterodoxy, so that governance and moral instruction flourished; when among the fields [?], they expounded texts and set forth ritual, so that the Way and righteousness became clear. One cannot deny their mastery of classical learning. Lin Congzhou presented a rhapsody and eulogy entitled Prisons Empty, Harvests Abundant, whose underlying intent was to esteem leniency and harmony. Yang Fu composed a descriptive record entitled Unusual Things, Waters, and Soils, intending to put tribute offerings in proper order. For composing the Record of Grand Music and Explanations of Texts for the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, there was Feng Yuan; for passing the examination and composing rhapsodies, earning the appellation “Li Boyi,” there was Li Bo. Through their submissions to the throne, these men could rectify the ruler’s mind and set affairs right; through their writings, they could establish enduring teachings and transmit instruction to posterity. One cannot deny the richness of their literary accomplishments.
Now, insofar as these were all forms of classical learning and literary composition, each had something worthy of adoption according to his attainments. Yet if we seek those who advanced beyond this, Zhou Lianxi transmitted learning to the two Cheng brothers in the north, while Mei Dingchen and his son expounded the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning in that period. Zhu Yuanhui established his friendship with Jingfu in the south, while Li Yong and his son subsequently expounded the Analects and the Mencius. Zheng Nansheng and Guo Shuyun both studied under Master Zhu: the former devoted himself resolutely to diligent study, the latter directed his efforts toward putting learning into practice. Huang Zhiju and Jian Keyi both studied under Master Zhang: the former elucidated human nature and principle, the latter studied and admired the teachings of Lianxi and the Luo school. Now…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
諸子非不窮經也而無經術之名何者講
究之功多也非不著述也而無文章之名
何者踐履之學勝也其視前數子專攻藝
文之譽者不爲優之哉以行誼政事言之
義梅鋗者目居地爲梅嶺義程旼者目居
邑爲程鄕而吳覇之招復流徙有吳山之
名張夔之築陂灌田有張陂之稱是皆因
乎姓者也孝黃舒者名其里爲曾參孝羅
孟郊者名其湖爲曾子而李廷珙之奉化
===
卿孫元勳之慕德里李祉仁之慈廉江陳
紀之義江是皆因乎人者也地因姓著則
仰其人而克知其爲地之光居因人顯則
履其地而卽仰其爲人之實數子之行誼
亦不可爲不偉矣張宋卿正色立朝鯁介
鮮交胡銓以才堪大用而薦之于廷吳純
臣提刑明允不事鉤鉅鄒應隆以清通仁
厚而書之爲贈化徭酋復流民人號之爲
能吏者廖顒也課耕牛興文學人號之爲
punctuated: 諸子非不窮經也，而無經術之名，何者？講究之功多也。非不著述也，而無文章之名，何者？踐履之學勝也。其視前數子專攻藝文之譽者，不爲優之哉？以行誼政事言之，義梅鋗者，目居地爲梅嶺；義程旼者，目居邑爲程鄕。而吳覇之招復流徙，有吳山之名；張夔之築陂灌田，有張陂之稱。是皆因乎姓者也。孝黃舒者，名其里爲曾參；孝羅孟郊者，名其湖爲曾子。而李廷珙之奉化卿、孫元勳之慕德里、李祉仁之慈廉江、陳紀之義江，是皆因乎人者也。地因姓著，則仰其人而克知其爲地之光；居因人顯，則履其地而卽仰其爲人之實。數子之行誼，亦不可爲不偉矣。張宋卿正色立朝，鯁介鮮交，胡銓以才堪大用而薦之于廷。吳純臣提刑明允，不事鉤鉅，鄒應隆以清通仁厚而書之爲贈。化徭酋，復流民，人號之爲能吏者，廖顒也；課耕牛，興文學，人號之爲
translation_en:
…These masters certainly investigated the Classics thoroughly, yet they were not renowned for expertise in the Classics. Why? Because their work of inquiry went deeper. They certainly produced writings, yet they were not renowned for literary composition. Why? Because their learning through practice was preeminent. Were they not superior to those previously mentioned, whose reputations rested on their exclusive pursuit of literary accomplishment?

As for virtuous conduct and administrative achievement, Mei Xuan was honored for his righteousness by naming his place of residence Meiling; Cheng Min was honored for his righteousness by naming his county Chengxiang. Wu Ba’s recall and resettlement of displaced people gave rise to the name Wushan; Zhang Kui’s construction of a reservoir to irrigate fields gave rise to the name Zhangbei. All these names derived from surnames. Huang Shu was honored for filial devotion by naming his neighborhood Zeng Shen; Luo Mengjiao was honored for filial devotion by naming his lake Zengzi. Then there were Li Tinggong’s Fenghua township [?], Sun Yuanxun’s Mude neighborhood, Li Zhiren’s Cilian River, and Chen Ji’s Yi River. All these names derived from the men themselves. When a place becomes renowned through a surname, admiration for the man enables one to recognize how he brought glory to that place. When a locality becomes distinguished through a person, visiting it immediately inspires admiration for the substance of his character. The virtuous conduct of these men must indeed be called great.

Zhang Songqing maintained a grave and upright bearing at court; uncompromising in integrity, he formed few personal connections. Hu Quan recommended him to the court as a man whose talents fitted him for major responsibilities. Wu Chunchen, as Judicial Commissioner, was discerning and impartial, making no use of devious investigative tactics. Zou Yinglong wrote a tribute for him praising his integrity, sound judgment, benevolence, and generosity. The man who transformed the Yao chieftains through moral influence and brought displaced people back, whom people called an able official, was Liao Yong. The man who encouraged the use of plow oxen [?] and promoted literary learning, whom people called …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
良吏者黃勳也或以正直之風采而臺紳
推重或以卓異之政績而吏傳有聲數子
之政事亦不可爲不傑矣夫均之爲行誼
均之爲政事則據其所造皆有可錄而求
其進於是者則李昴英謂曲江之張九齡
日南之姜公輔湟中之劉瞻三人者皆唐
士之最陳璉謂余忠襄之遺芳百載崔與
之之行高一時二人者皆宋士之英今觀
公輔炳幾先之見劉瞻却四方之賂器度
===
遠矣然盡忠輸誠文章相業卓冠士林則
九齡尤唐之傑出已余靖屢言邊情三使
契丹才猷著矣然澄清海上力辭樞命出
處合宜則與之尤宋之特立已是二子者
其處也有以養其出可久之德幾焉其出
也有以用其入可大之業具焉較前數子
各擅政行之稱者不爲勝之哉逮我
明興治化隆洽海表人文彬彬輩出如李質黃
哲之通經也蘇福黃克義之文章也關敏
punctuated:
良吏者黃勳也。或以正直之風采而臺紳推重，或以卓異之政績而吏傳有聲，數子之政事亦不可爲不傑矣。夫均之爲行誼，均之爲政事，則據其所造，皆有可錄。而求其進於是者，則李昴英謂曲江之張九齡、日南之姜公輔、湟中之劉瞻三人者，皆唐士之最；陳璉謂余忠襄之遺芳百載、崔與之之行高一時，二人者皆宋士之英。今觀公輔炳幾先之見，劉瞻却四方之賂，器度遠矣。然盡忠輸誠，文章相業卓冠士林，則九齡尤唐之傑出已。余靖屢言邊情，三使契丹，才猷著矣。然澄清海上，力辭樞命，出處合宜，則與之尤宋之特立已。是二子者，其處也有以養其出，可久之德幾焉；其出也有以用其入，可大之業具焉。較前數子各擅政行之稱者，不爲勝之哉？
逮我明興，治化隆洽，海表人文彬彬輩出，如李質、黃哲之通經也，蘇福、黃克義之文章也，關敏
translation_en:
… the man called a good official was Huang Xun. Some won the esteem of high officials through their upright bearing; others earned renown in officials’ biographies through their exceptional achievements in government. These men’s accomplishments in administration, too, must be considered outstanding. Whether in moral conduct or in government service, each had achievements worthy of record. Yet if we seek those who surpassed them, Li Maoying called Zhang Jiuling of Qujiang, Jiang Gongfu of Rinan, and Liu Zhan of Huangzhong the finest scholars of the Tang. Chen Lian said that Yu Zhongxiang’s good name endured for a hundred years and that Cui Yuzhi’s conduct stood above his contemporaries: both were eminent scholars of the Song.
Now Gongfu displayed brilliant foresight into events before they unfolded, while Liu Zhan rejected bribes from every quarter: their capacities and breadth of character were far-reaching indeed. Yet in utter loyalty and wholehearted devotion, and in literary achievement and service as chief councilor that towered above the community of scholars, Jiuling was especially outstanding among men of the Tang. Yu Jing repeatedly reported on frontier conditions and went three times as an envoy to the Khitan; his abilities and strategic judgment were manifest. Yet in bringing order to the coastal region, firmly declining appointment to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and acting appropriately both in taking office and in retirement, Yuzhi was especially distinguished among men of the Song.
These two men, while in retirement, cultivated what would sustain their public service, approaching a virtue capable of enduring. When they entered public service, they put to use what they had nurtured in retirement, possessing all that was needed for achievements capable of greatness. Did they not surpass the earlier men, each of whom enjoyed distinction for either administration or moral conduct?
When our Ming arose, its governance and transforming influence flourished and spread throughout the realm. Here, beyond the seas, men of elegant learning emerged in succession: Li Zhi and Huang Zhe in mastery of the classics, Su Fu and Huang Keyi in literary composition, Guan Min …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鄧顒之忠義也周新陳鼎之明政刑也視
漢唐宋諸先哲固不多讓求其經術文章
行誼政事可以繼前脩而垂後範者不有
陳獻章丘濬乎或病獻章之學有體無用
而不知日用常行洞見鳶飛魚躍之妙者
獻章之體也才與誠合而治化可興者獻
章之用也造詣如伊人豈徒理學可稱雖
試之功業何歉哉至於丘濬律己之嚴理
學之博尤人所難及今觀家禮儀節推風
===
教也世史正綱明正統也朱子學的治身
心也大學衍義補陳王道也博雅如伊人
豈徒相業可觀雖謂之道學何愧哉愚也
考理學名臣之篇觀嶺南人物之志能無
動思齊之念發躍羣之心也哉雖然窺河
而數星凡象緯皆星也觀斗極薇垣之象
則衆星之光微矣倚臺而見山凡丘陵皆
山也登泰岱嵩華之巔則衆山之形卑矣
故觀才于一方之近則今之諸子自陳丘
punctuated:
鄧顒之忠義也，周新、陳鼎之明政刑也，視漢唐宋諸先哲，固不多讓。求其經術、文章、行誼、政事可以繼前脩而垂後範者，不有陳獻章、丘濬乎？或病獻章之學有體無用，而不知日用常行洞見鳶飛魚躍之妙者，獻章之體也；才與誠合而治化可興者，獻章之用也。造詣如伊人，豈徒理學可稱？雖試之功業，何歉哉？至於丘濬，律己之嚴、理學之博，尤人所難及。今觀《家禮儀節》，推風教也；《世史正綱》，明正統也；《朱子學的》，治身心也；《大學衍義補》，陳王道也。博雅如伊人，豈徒相業可觀？雖謂之道學，何愧哉？愚也考理學名臣之篇，觀嶺南人物之志，能無動思齊之念、發躍羣之心也哉？

雖然，窺河而數星，凡象緯皆星也；觀斗極薇垣之象，則衆星之光微矣。倚臺而見山，凡丘陵皆山也；登泰岱嵩華之巔，則衆山之形卑矣。故觀才于一方之近，則今之諸子自陳丘
translation_en:
…Deng Yong for loyalty and righteousness, and Zhou Xin and Chen Ding for their enlightened administration and handling of punishments: compared with the earlier worthies of the Han, Tang, and Song, they certainly concede little. If we seek men whose classical learning, literary accomplishments, moral conduct, and public service could carry on the work of earlier worthies and leave models for posterity, do we not have Chen Xianzhang and Qiu Jun? Some criticize Xianzhang’s learning as having substance but no practical application. They do not understand that his substance lay in perceiving, within everyday activities and ordinary conduct, the subtle workings exemplified by kites flying and fish leaping; his practical application lay in uniting ability with sincerity so that good government and moral transformation could flourish. With attainments such as his, how could he deserve praise only for his learning of principle? Even if put to the test in practical achievements, how would he fall short? As for Qiu Jun, the rigor of his self-discipline and breadth of his learning of principle were especially difficult for others to match. Consider his Ceremonial Procedures for Family Rituals: it advances moral instruction through customary practice. His Correct Framework of World History clarifies legitimate dynastic succession. His Essentials of Master Zhu’s Learning addresses the cultivation of body and mind. His Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning sets forth the kingly way. With erudition and refinement such as his, how could only his achievements as a grand secretary merit admiration? Even if he were called a scholar of the Way, how would he be unworthy of the name? When I, in my humble capacity, examine accounts of eminent ministers learned in principle and read records of notable figures of Lingnan, how could I fail to feel the desire to equal them and the resolve to rise above the multitude?

Even so, when one peers at the Milky Way and counts the stars, all the celestial bodies are stars; but when one beholds the Dipper, the Pole Star, and the Wei Enclosure [?], the light of the other stars grows faint. When one leans against a terrace and views the mountains, every hill and ridge is a mountain; but when one ascends the summits of Tai, Song, and Hua, the forms of all the other mountains seem low. Thus, when assessing talent within the nearby bounds of a single region, the various men of recent times, beginning with Chen and Qiu…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以下皆所當取法也而况古之才乎觀才
於天下古今之遠則古之諸子自張崔而
外猶不能無遺論焉而况今之才也此愚
所以有感於人才之難也非才之難也而
立志之難也志苟立焉而復充之以義理
之學使天下之道融會貫通於吾心由是
明之爲經術而經術皆道也發之爲文章
而文章皆道也措之爲行誼施之爲政事
而行誼政事皆道也則近而爲陳爲丘可
===
也遠而爲張爲崔可也等而上之則周程
也張朱也韓范也富歐也吾從而並駕焉
可也又進而上之則孔孟也伊傅也周召
也吾從而效軌焉可也此正士君子終身
之所誦法而不以一善成名者也若曰徒
友一鄉之善士而足焉則豈愚生所安哉
第五問
梁棟隆
同考試官教諭林批兵食之計今日粵中最
punctuated:
以下，皆所當取法也，而况古之才乎？觀才於天下古今之遠，則古之諸子自張崔而外，猶不能無遺論焉，而况今之才也？此愚所以有感於人才之難也。非才之難也，而立志之難也。志苟立焉，而復充之以義理之學，使天下之道融會貫通於吾心，由是明之爲經術，而經術皆道也；發之爲文章，而文章皆道也；措之爲行誼，施之爲政事，而行誼政事皆道也。則近而爲陳爲丘可也，遠而爲張爲崔可也。等而上之，則周程也，張朱也，韓范也，富歐也，吾從而並駕焉可也。又進而上之，則孔孟也，伊傅也，周召也，吾從而效軌焉可也。此正士君子終身之所誦法，而不以一善成名者也。若曰徒友一鄉之善士而足焉，則豈愚生所安哉？

第五問
梁棟隆

同考試官教諭林批：兵食之計，今日粵中最
translation_en:
…and those below them are all men whom one ought to take as models; how much more so the talented men of antiquity! If we survey talent throughout the realm and across the vast span of past and present, then even among the men of antiquity, apart from Zhang and Cui, there remain grounds for criticism; how much more so among the talented men of today! This is why I feel so keenly the difficulty of finding men of talent. Yet the difficulty lies not in talent, but in establishing one's resolve. Once that resolve is established, one must further develop it through the study of moral principles, so that the Way throughout the world becomes fully integrated and comprehended within one's own mind. When one elucidates it through classical learning, that learning will wholly embody the Way; when one expresses it in literary composition, that writing will wholly embody the Way; when one puts it into practice through personal conduct and applies it to government, both conduct and government will wholly embody the Way. Thus one may become a Chen or a Qiu among the more recent exemplars, or a Zhang or a Cui among those of the distant past. Rising higher by degrees, one may advance alongside Zhou and Cheng, Zhang and Zhu, Han and Fan, or Fu and Ou. Advancing still higher, one may follow the tracks of Kong and Meng, Yi and Fu, or Zhou and Shao. These are precisely the exemplars whom a gentleman should study and emulate throughout his life, rather than making his name through a single virtue. If it is said that merely befriending the worthy men of one district is enough, how could a humble student such as I rest content with that?

Liang Donglong

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
切者子能錯綜問意斟酌時宜皆鑿鑿可行之論
且文意精密體裁嚴峻宜錄以備當事者採
同考試官教授饒批談兵食强弱盈縮之際
不襲陳說而獨見端原且末言城堡守令之說皆
地方至計書生而議事若此其識時務之俊傑歟
考試官教諭劉批議論精明處置詳妥
考試官學正楊批憂時之志用世之才
昔唐臣陸贄有言備禦國家之重事兵食
備禦之大經兵不理則無可用之師食不
===
足則無可固之地理兵在制置得所足食
在斂導有方諒哉其言之也豈惟陸贄之
言為然哉守邊勸農之議晁錯以言於漢
矣作內政寓軍令通鹽筴重五穀管仲以
告於齊矣豈惟管仲晁錯言之哉周禮一
書周家致太平之書也體國經野纖悉備
具其詳至鄉遂皆兵山澤皆賦所以固邦
本而張國威其孰不以此為重務乎知此
則明問可得而復矣愚也生長海邦涵濡
punctuated:
切者。子能錯綜問意，斟酌時宜，皆鑿鑿可行之論。且文意精密，體裁嚴峻，宜錄以備當事者採。
同考試官教授饒批：談兵食强弱盈縮之際，不襲陳說，而獨見端原。且末言城堡守令之說，皆地方至計。書生而議事若此，其識時務之俊傑歟！
考試官教諭劉批：議論精明，處置詳妥。
考試官學正楊批：憂時之志，用世之才。
昔唐臣陸贄有言：「備禦，國家之重事；兵食，備禦之大經。兵不理，則無可用之師；食不足，則無可固之地。理兵在制置得所，足食在斂導有方。」諒哉，其言之也！豈惟陸贄之言為然哉？守邊勸農之議，晁錯以言於漢矣；作內政，寓軍令，通鹽筴，重五穀，管仲以告於齊矣。豈惟管仲、晁錯言之哉？《周禮》一書，周家致太平之書也。體國經野，纖悉備具，其詳至鄉遂皆兵，山澤皆賦，所以固邦本而張國威，其孰不以此為重務乎？知此，則明問可得而復矣。愚也生長海邦，涵濡
translation_en:
…most pressing. You have drawn together the implications of the question and weighed what present circumstances require; all your proposals are concrete and practicable. Moreover, the thought is meticulous and the composition rigorous and forceful. It deserves to be recorded for those in charge to draw upon.
Associate Examiner Rao, Prefectural School Instructor, comments: In discussing military strength and weakness and the surplus and shortage of provisions, you do not repeat conventional arguments but independently discern their underlying causes. Moreover, your concluding proposals concerning fortifications and prefects and magistrates are all measures of the greatest importance for local affairs. A scholar who deliberates on affairs in this way must surely be an outstanding talent who understands the needs of the times!
Examiner Liu, County School Instructor, comments: The arguments are penetrating and clear; the proposed measures are detailed and sound.
Examiner Yang, Departmental School Instructor, comments: The resolve to care for the troubles of the times; the talent to serve the world.
Lu Zhi, a minister of the Tang, once said: “Defensive preparedness is a major concern of the state; troops and provisions are its essential foundations. If troops are not properly organized, there is no army fit for use; if provisions are insufficient, there is no territory that can be securely held. Organizing troops depends on making appropriate arrangements; ensuring adequate provisions depends on sound methods of collection and distribution.” How true his words are! Yet was Lu Zhi alone in saying this? Chao Cuo presented proposals to the Han for defending the frontiers and encouraging agriculture. Guan Zhong advised Qi to organize internal administration so as to incorporate military commands, facilitate the administration of salt revenues, and give weight to grain production. Were Guan Zhong and Chao Cuo alone in speaking of these things? The Rites of Zhou is a book through which the Zhou house brought about Great Peace. Its arrangements for the capital and the countryside are complete in every minute detail, extending even to military organization throughout the xiang and sui rural districts and revenues from all the mountains and marshes. In securing the foundations of the realm and extending the state's might, who would not regard these as urgent concerns? With this understood, I can offer a response to your discerning question. I, an unworthy scholar, was born and raised in this coastal land, steeped in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太平熈皥之化有年矣顧承平日久姦宄漸
生頻年以來海倭山寇迭相為難賴藉
天威遠布文武重臣下及將校咸殫心宣力不
崇朝而嶺海肅清百姓鼓舞更生矣此其
故豈無以致之哉夫廣東嶺海隩區土地
聯絡接荆吳帶閩越南控交桂地方數千
里而島夷時出入邊陲張帆倏至山林洞
壑雜以猺獞姦民往往依險為盜有司急
不能制往時寇至然後調兵比兵至則寇
===
已去兵行然後給食比食至則兵已疲今
皆先期而集之兵先事而備之食故成功
最速以此言之理兵足食之策即此可以
占端倪矣請因明問而悉陳之夫廣之兵
衛所額戍其來舊矣此外有民壯有打手
又益之以召募增之以調集兵非不多也
然名籍空存而技擊非素練之卒白徒應
募而不戢有自焚之虞是數者果可恃乎
議者欲立團保以集鄉兵集之誠是也然
punctuated:
太平熈皥之化有年矣。顧承平日久，姦宄漸生。頻年以來，海倭山寇迭相為難。賴藉天威遠布，文武重臣，下及將校，咸殫心宣力，不崇朝而嶺海肅清，百姓鼓舞更生矣。此其故，豈無以致之哉？夫廣東嶺海隩區，土地聯絡，接荆吳，帶閩越，南控交桂，地方數千里。而島夷時出入邊陲，張帆倏至；山林洞壑，雜以猺獞，姦民往往依險為盜，有司急不能制。往時寇至然後調兵，比兵至則寇已去；兵行然後給食，比食至則兵已疲。今皆先期而集之兵，先事而備之食，故成功最速。以此言之，理兵足食之策，即此可以占端倪矣。請因明問而悉陳之。
夫廣之兵，衛所額戍，其來舊矣。此外有民壯，有打手，又益之以召募，增之以調集，兵非不多也。然名籍空存，而技擊非素練之卒；白徒應募而不戢，有自焚之虞。是數者，果可恃乎？議者欲立團保以集鄉兵，集之誠是也，然
translation_en:
…under the influence of a peaceful, flourishing, and harmonious age for many years. Yet peace has endured so long that lawlessness has gradually arisen. In recent years, Japanese pirates at sea and bandits in the mountains have taken turns causing trouble. Fortunately, the imperial might has spread far abroad, and senior civil and military officials, down to commanders and officers, have all devoted their utmost thought and strength to their duties. In less than a morning [?], the region of the mountains and sea was cleared of disorder, and the common people rejoiced at their renewed lives. Surely there were reasons why this was achieved?
Guangdong is a sheltered region among mountains and sea. Its interconnected lands adjoin Jing and Wu, border Min and Yue, and command the approaches to Jiao and Gui to the south, extending several thousand li. Yet island barbarians periodically enter and leave its frontiers, arriving suddenly under sail. Yao and Tong peoples live interspersed among its mountain forests, caves, and ravines, and lawless inhabitants often take advantage of the rugged terrain to become bandits. The responsible officials cannot bring them under control in an emergency. Formerly, troops were mobilized only after the bandits arrived; by the time the troops reached the scene, the bandits had already left. Provisions were supplied only after the troops set out; by the time the provisions arrived, the troops were already exhausted. Now troops are assembled ahead of time, and provisions prepared before the need arises. Success has therefore come most swiftly. Viewed in this light, the outlines of a policy for organizing troops and ensuring adequate provisions can already be discerned here. Allow me to set it out fully in response to your discerning question.
As for Guangdong’s troops, the prescribed garrison establishments of the guards and battalions have long existed. Besides these, there are local militiamen and fighting men, supplemented by volunteers and reinforced by troops transferred and assembled from elsewhere. Troops are certainly not few. Yet muster rolls exist in name only, while the soldiers are not regularly trained in combat skills. Untrained men enlist but remain undisciplined, raising the danger of bringing destruction upon oneself. Can these various forces truly be relied upon? Those discussing the matter wish to establish local defense associations to assemble village troops. Assembling them is certainly right, but…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
或居處有遠近則勢不相援攻擊非素習
則力不可支心志非結於平時則臨難不
能以共濟貧民不農殖不土著輕棄其家
鄉如鳥獸然而豪猾之徒復倚藉官勢而
魚肉其鄉之人且一籍名在官寧逃走而
不願為兵者有矣是團保可易集乎夫民
見害不見利而欲其鼓舞以赴公上之急
自古及今未之前聞也玆欲行之存乎良
有司耳往時
===
廷議曾一及之矣其曰召民為軍已失軍衞
定籍倉卒應募類非土著居人欲令所司
查原編火夫內家有二丁以上者再加精
選以備鄉兵之籍無事則放歸農仍復其
身之役今所行保甲法非此意乎以是比
其什伍堅其約束時為簡閱而賞賚行焉
如古寓兵於農之法寇至則鳴金召集有
不相援者罰無赦寇退則公舉有功之人
貧者厚其資富者復其役或時給冠帶旌
punctuated:
或居處有遠近，則勢不相援；攻擊非素習，則力不可支；心志非結於平時，則臨難不能以共濟。貧民不農殖，不土著，輕棄其家鄉如鳥獸，然而豪猾之徒復倚藉官勢，而魚肉其鄉之人。且一籍名在官，寧逃走而不願為兵者有矣。是團保可易集乎？夫民見害不見利，而欲其鼓舞以赴公上之急，自古及今，未之前聞也。玆欲行之，存乎良有司耳。
往時廷議曾一及之矣。其曰：「召民為軍，已失軍衞定籍；倉卒應募，類非土著居人。欲令所司查原編火夫內家有二丁以上者，再加精選，以備鄉兵之籍。無事則放歸農，仍復其身之役。」今所行保甲法，非此意乎？以是比其什伍，堅其約束，時為簡閱，而賞賚行焉。如古寓兵於農之法，寇至則鳴金召集，有不相援者，罰無赦；寇退則公舉有功之人，貧者厚其資，富者復其役，或時給冠帶，旌
translation_en:
…If their dwellings are scattered at varying distances, their positions prevent them from supporting one another; if they have not regularly practised combat, their strength cannot hold out; if their resolve has not been united in ordinary times, they cannot cooperate to overcome danger when it comes. Poor people who neither cultivate the land nor have a settled residence readily abandon their homes and native places, like birds and beasts. Meanwhile, powerful and unscrupulous men exploit official authority to prey upon the people of their own locality. Moreover, there are those who, once their names have been entered on the official register, would rather flee than serve as soldiers. Can these local defence associations, then, be readily assembled? To expect the people, seeing harm but no benefit, to respond enthusiastically to the urgent needs of the authorities—this has never been heard of, from antiquity to the present. To implement this now depends solely upon good local officials.
Court deliberations once addressed this matter, saying: “Recruiting commoners as soldiers already departs from the fixed registration system of the military guards. Those who enlist in haste are generally not settled local residents. We propose that the responsible authorities examine the households of previously registered fire-service labourers and, from those with two or more adult males, make a further careful selection to fill the local militia registers. When there is no emergency, let them return to farming, while exempting them from their own labour-service obligations.” Is this not the intent of the baojia system now being implemented? On this basis, organize them into groups of ten and five, make their rules binding, conduct inspections from time to time, and distribute rewards. Following the ancient method of incorporating soldiers among the farmers, when raiders arrive, sound the gong to assemble them; punish without pardon any who fail to support one another. When the raiders withdraw, publicly nominate those who have rendered meritorious service. Give generous material assistance to the poor and exempt the wealthy from labour service; at times, grant caps and girdles of rank and confer public honours…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
閭里以榮其身家如是而民有弗勸乎故
集鄉兵有五利焉非有期會徵發而輒至
一利也民各為其父母妻子人自為戰家
自為守二利也不費餉於官而坐得制勝
之術三利也熟諳道路險阻能伏而能擊
四利也永守其鄉閭非如官兵之倏聚倏
散賊得乘其虛五利也夫團保旣集矣而
民壯而軍兵而召募可無以處之乎以愚
計之軍兵汰其老弱籍其精壯務以取足
===
于原額民兵稽其名籍選其驍勇不使占
役於公家不足則召募打手以繼之而召
募非有常數也視時為盈縮而已是數者
皆必習之於簡教夜戰聲相知則足以相
救晝戰目相見則足以相識如是而勸以
厚賞威以重罰則前赴不旋踵矣故兵一
也集鄉兵為常守之兵用官兵為應敵之
兵陸贄所謂制置得宜者非此謂乎若夫
遠調狼兵或不得已而偶為之耳非長算
punctuated: 閭里，以榮其身家。如是而民有弗勸乎？故集鄉兵有五利焉：非有期會徵發而輒至，一利也；民各為其父母妻子，人自為戰，家自為守，二利也；不費餉於官而坐得制勝之術，三利也；熟諳道路險阻，能伏而能擊，四利也；永守其鄉閭，非如官兵之倏聚倏散，賊得乘其虛，五利也。夫團保旣集矣，而民壯，而軍兵，而召募，可無以處之乎？以愚計之，軍兵汰其老弱，籍其精壯，務以取足于原額；民兵稽其名籍，選其驍勇，不使占役於公家；不足則召募打手以繼之。而召募非有常數也，視時為盈縮而已。是數者，皆必習之於簡教。夜戰聲相知，則足以相救；晝戰目相見，則足以相識。如是而勸以厚賞，威以重罰，則前赴不旋踵矣。故兵一也，集鄉兵為常守之兵，用官兵為應敵之兵。陸贄所謂制置得宜者，非此謂乎？若夫遠調狼兵，或不得已而偶為之耳，非長算
translation_en:
…in their neighborhoods, thereby bringing honor to themselves and their families. With such measures, would any among the people fail to be encouraged? Thus, assembling local militia has five advantages. They come readily without scheduled musters or orders for mobilization: this is the first advantage. Each fights for his own parents, wife, and children; every man fights and every household defends itself: this is the second advantage. The government incurs no expense for military provisions, yet readily obtains a means of securing victory: this is the third advantage. They know the roads and difficult terrain thoroughly and can both lay ambushes and launch attacks: this is the fourth advantage. They permanently defend their own communities, unlike government troops who suddenly assemble and disperse, allowing bandits to exploit the gaps they leave: this is the fifth advantage.

Once the community defense units have been assembled, can we leave the civilian guards, regular soldiers, and recruited men without appropriate arrangements? In my humble judgment, the regular forces should discharge the old and weak and register the strong and fit, making every effort to fill their original quota. The civilian militia rolls should be checked and the brave and vigorous selected; they must not be appropriated for service in government offices. If their numbers are insufficient, fighting men should be recruited to supplement them. Recruitment should have no fixed quota: numbers should simply increase or decrease as circumstances require. All these forces must be accustomed to inspection and training. When fighting at night, they should recognize one another by voice so that they can come to one another’s aid; when fighting by day, they should be able to recognize one another by sight. If they are then encouraged with generous rewards and overawed by severe punishments, they will advance without turning back.

Thus, the forces form a single whole: assemble local militia as a permanent defensive force, and employ government troops as a force to engage the enemy. Is this not what Lu Zhi meant by making appropriate arrangements? As for summoning lang troops from afar, this may occasionally be done when there is no alternative, but it is no lasting strategy…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也昔者越王句踐一小國耳十年生聚教
訓卒得志於吳未甞借兵於他境矧以全
盛之東粤行之而謂兵不足用也是可不
思其故哉廣之食軍民稅糧其來遠矣此
外有工食有夷舶有橋稅而又益之以市
墟請之以
內帑宜乎有餘食也然賦稅雖有定額而徵
入或無全數雜稅雖仍其初而費用實倍
於昔是數者可盡恃乎議者欲刷屯鹽以
===
收額利收之誠是也然鹽塲轄於瀕海盜
賊之區屯田設於建立州縣之後係乎地
者多空名鹽法阻於私販之盛行屯田苦
於豪右之欺併係乎人者多敝政而所司
不能履畝而驗盡室而稽也故上之無以
完納課粒供三邊百府之用下之無以抽
取餘利為本處軍餉之資督責雖甚嚴祗
具虛文而已屯鹽可易議乎夫民見利不
見義而欲其畢力以完公家之稅自古及
punctuated: 也。昔者越王句踐，一小國耳，十年生聚教訓，卒得志於吳，未甞借兵於他境。矧以全盛之東粤行之，而謂兵不足用也，是可不思其故哉？廣之食軍民稅糧，其來遠矣。此外有工食，有夷舶，有橋稅，而又益之以市墟，請之以內帑，宜乎有餘食也。然賦稅雖有定額，而徵入或無全數；雜稅雖仍其初，而費用實倍於昔。是數者可盡恃乎？議者欲刷屯鹽以收額利，收之誠是也。然鹽塲轄於瀕海盜賊之區，屯田設於建立州縣之後，係乎地者多空名；鹽法阻於私販之盛行，屯田苦於豪右之欺併，係乎人者多敝政。而所司不能履畝而驗，盡室而稽也。故上之無以完納課粒，供三邊百府之用；下之無以抽取餘利，為本處軍餉之資。督責雖甚嚴，祗具虛文而已。屯鹽可易議乎？夫民見利不見義，而欲其畢力以完公家之稅，自古及
translation_en:
…such is the case. In former times, Goujian, king of Yue, ruled only a small state. After ten years of increasing its population, accumulating resources, and training its people, he finally prevailed over Wu, without ever borrowing troops from another territory. How much more could this be done with Dongyue’s full strength! If troops are nevertheless said to be insufficient, should we not reflect on the reason? Guangdong has long fed its troops with grain taxes levied on the people. Besides these, there are funds for laborers’ provisions [?], revenues from foreign ships, and bridge taxes, further supplemented by market revenues and requests for funds from the imperial privy treasury. There ought, then, to be provisions to spare. Yet although the regular taxes have fixed quotas, collections sometimes fall short of the full amount; and although miscellaneous taxes remain as originally established, expenditure has actually doubled since former times. Can all these sources be relied upon completely?

Those discussing the matter wish to audit military agricultural colonies and salt revenues in order to collect the prescribed returns. Collecting them is certainly right. Yet the saltworks lie in coastal areas infested with bandits, and the military agricultural colonies were established after the prefectures and counties had been set up: much of what is registered against the land exists in name only. Salt administration is obstructed by widespread illicit trading, while the military agricultural colonies suffer from fraudulent encroachment and consolidation by powerful local families: abuses abound in matters dependent on people. The responsible officials cannot inspect every field or investigate every household. Thus, at the higher level, they cannot remit the full grain-tax quota to supply the needs of the three frontier regions and the many prefectures; at the local level, they cannot extract surplus revenues to fund military supplies in their own area. However stern the demands for compliance, they amount only to empty paperwork. Can military agricultural colonies and salt revenues be dealt with so readily? The people perceive profit but not righteousness; yet one would have them exert themselves fully to pay the government’s taxes—from antiquity down to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
今未之前聞也玆欲行之存乎有官守者
耳頃者
廷議曾屢及之矣大要講求立法之根源究
極今日之弊政課額有無增於前也丁口
有無減於舊也今所講論經畫者非以是
乎以是抑兼併阻私販稽其訟牒而撫綏
加焉如古通商重農之政而又官吏之剝
削者有罰課粒之逋負者有懲其能加意
職守利興而民不告病者以異等擢之如
===
是而政有不舉乎故舉屯鹽有三善焉出
天地自然之利而民不加賦一善也安庶
物便百姓兩利而俱贍二善也不待轉輸
飛輓而兵食賴焉爲安邊足用之本三善
也屯鹽旣舉矣而夷舶而橋稅諸所須者
可無以處之乎以愚計之夷舶禁其欺僞
不責諸夷而責諸通夷之商賈橋稅稽其
漏報不責諸商而責諸所司之廉察無已
則量查墟市之稅以益之而墟稅非正額
punctuated:
今，未之前聞也。玆欲行之，存乎有官守者耳。頃者廷議曾屢及之矣。大要講求立法之根源，究極今日之弊政：課額有無增於前也？丁口有無減於舊也？今所講論經畫者，非以是乎？以是抑兼併，阻私販，稽其訟牒，而撫綏加焉。如古通商重農之政，而又官吏之剝削者有罰，課粒之逋負者有懲，其能加意職守、利興而民不告病者，以異等擢之。如此而政有不舉乎？故舉屯鹽有三善焉：出天地自然之利而民不加賦，一善也；安庶物，便百姓，兩利而俱贍，二善也；不待轉輸飛輓而兵食賴焉，爲安邊足用之本，三善也。
屯鹽旣舉矣，而夷舶、而橋稅，諸所須者，可無以處之乎？以愚計之，夷舶禁其欺僞，不責諸夷而責諸通夷之商賈；橋稅稽其漏報，不責諸商而責諸所司之廉察。無已，則量查墟市之稅以益之，而墟稅非正額
translation_en:
…down to the present, no such thing has ever been heard of. To put this into practice now depends solely upon those holding official responsibility. Recently, deliberations at court have repeatedly touched upon it. The essential task is to examine the foundations of the regulations and investigate thoroughly the abuses in present administration: have tax quotas increased over earlier levels? Has the population declined from what it once was? Are these not the matters now being discussed and planned for? On this basis, curb the concentration of landholdings, obstruct illicit trading, examine litigation documents, and further extend measures to reassure and pacify the people. Follow the ancient policies of facilitating commerce and giving priority to agriculture. Furthermore, punish officials and clerks who exact oppressive levies, and penalize those in arrears on taxes and grain payments. Those who attend diligently to their official duties, increasing revenues without causing the people to complain of hardship, should receive exceptional promotion. With such measures, how could administration fail to function? Thus, putting military agricultural colonies and the salt administration in order has three benefits. Drawing upon the natural resources of Heaven and Earth without imposing additional taxes on the people is the first. Ensuring that all things flourish and making life easier for the common people, benefiting both and providing adequately for both, is the second. Supplying provisions for the troops without depending upon long-distance transport and urgent haulage, thereby laying the foundation for secure frontiers and adequate resources, is the third.
Once military agricultural colonies and the salt administration have been put in order, can foreign shipping, bridge tolls, and the other necessary sources of revenue be left without arrangements? In my humble judgment, fraud involving foreign shipping should be prohibited by holding accountable the merchants who trade with foreigners, rather than the foreigners themselves. Underreporting of bridge tolls should be investigated by holding the responsible authorities accountable for honest scrutiny, rather than holding the merchants accountable. If there is no alternative, the taxes on periodic markets may be assessed as appropriate to supplement these revenues. But market taxes are not part of the regular quota…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也終當減除之而後已夫與其多方以求
益乎軍餉不若精選以嚴定乎軍制若夫
竭賦稅以養不戰之卒糜膏脂以優坐食
之徒非國之善謀也故食一也取正額以
為養兵之費刷餘利以充應募之資陸贄
所謂斂導有方者非此謂乎若夫求益
內帑不得已而偶一請之非可數得也昔者
管仲用於齊諸葛亮用於蜀皆以一隅之
地庸濟時艱矧以全盛之東粵為之而曰
===
民未足食也是可不加之意哉雖然理兵
足食可矣抑尤有繫於此者二焉城堡不
可以不建也良牧守不可以不重用之也
夫地廣而無以聯絡之則勢易為亂民衆
而莫與憑藉之則居無固志東自潮惠西
及高廉其間曠數百里不相及者宜建立
城堡為通塗溪洞山巖瀕海之區盜得出
入為患者宜多築營寨為固守而會省要
地尤宜厚其防焉昔人所謂屯水陸兵萬
punctuated:
也，終當減除之而後已。夫與其多方以求益乎軍餉，不若精選以嚴定乎軍制。若夫竭賦稅以養不戰之卒，糜膏脂以優坐食之徒，非國之善謀也。故食一也，取正額以為養兵之費，刷餘利以充應募之資，陸贄所謂斂導有方者，非此謂乎？若夫求益內帑，不得已而偶一請之，非可數得也。昔者管仲用於齊，諸葛亮用於蜀，皆以一隅之地庸濟時艱，矧以全盛之東粵為之，而曰民未足食也，是可不加之意哉？

雖然，理兵足食可矣，抑尤有繫於此者二焉：城堡不可以不建也，良牧守不可以不重用之也。夫地廣而無以聯絡之，則勢易為亂；民衆而莫與憑藉之，則居無固志。東自潮惠，西及高廉，其間曠數百里不相及者，宜建立城堡為通塗；溪洞山巖瀕海之區，盜得出入為患者，宜多築營寨為固守。而會省要地，尤宜厚其防焉。昔人所謂屯水陸兵萬
translation_en:
…and these taxes must ultimately be reduced and abolished. Rather than seek every possible means of increasing military provisions, it would be better to select troops carefully and rigorously establish the military organization. Exhausting tax revenues to support soldiers who do not fight, and squandering the people's lifeblood to favor those who consume their rations in idleness, is no sound strategy for the state. Thus, as regards provisioning, use the regular tax quota to cover the expense of maintaining troops, and collect surplus revenues to fund volunteers. Is this not what Lu Zhi meant by having proper methods for collecting and directing resources [?]? As for seeking additional funds from the palace treasury, one may occasionally petition for them when no alternative remains, but they cannot be obtained repeatedly. In former times, Guan Zhong served in Qi and Zhuge Liang in Shu; each overcame the difficulties of his age with the resources of a single corner of the realm. How much more could be accomplished with Dongyue—Guangdong—in its full prosperity! If it is nevertheless said that the people still lack sufficient food, can this fail to command our attention?

Nevertheless, although organizing the troops and ensuring sufficient food are proper measures, two further matters have an especially important bearing on them: fortified towns and forts must be built, and capable local administrators must be entrusted with important responsibilities. When territory is extensive but lacks means of linking its parts, conditions readily give rise to disorder; when the population is numerous but has nothing to rely upon, people lack a settled resolve to remain in their homes. From Chaozhou and Huizhou in the east to Gaozhou and Lianzhou in the west, wherever stretches of several hundred li lie disconnected, fortified towns and forts should be established to link the routes. In areas of streams and ravines, rocky mountains, and the seacoast where bandits can come and go and cause harm, more fortified camps should be built to secure their defense. The provincial capital and other strategic locations [?] should have their defenses strengthened still further. As a man of former times put it, station naval and land forces numbering ten thousand…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
餘之衆貯十萬人三載之糧非此其時乎
至如牧守者民之所懸命也理兵足食皆
牧守之所有事也夫人勞未息不可以歲
辱大征民隱難知不可以日徵公聽所恃
以足食足兵爲地方建不拔之業者惟是
良牧守大以深根固本之治施之而今固
不可不愼其選也是故牧守良而化可究
也城堡建而民可依也食足兵强而威可
振也保邦固本之猷太平萬載之功也書
===
生常談知不足以裨
廟謨之萬一惟執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 餘之衆，貯十萬人三載之糧，非此其時乎？至如牧守者，民之所懸命也，理兵足食，皆牧守之所有事也。夫人勞未息，不可以歲辱大征；民隱難知，不可以日徵公聽。所恃以足食足兵，爲地方建不拔之業者，惟是良牧守，大以深根固本之治施之，而今固不可不愼其選也。是故牧守良而化可究也，城堡建而民可依也，食足兵强而威可振也。保邦固本之猷，太平萬載之功也。書生常談，知不足以裨廟謨之萬一，惟執事進而教之，幸甚！
translation_en:
…a force of over ten thousand, and store enough grain to feed a hundred thousand people for three years—is this not the time for such measures? As for the local magistrates and prefects, the people's lives depend upon them. Managing troops and ensuring sufficient food are both their responsibilities. The people's toil has not yet abated; they cannot be burdened with major campaigns every year. Their hidden sufferings are difficult to ascertain; these cannot be brought before public hearings every day [?]. To secure sufficient food and troops and establish an enduring foundation for the region, we must rely upon worthy local magistrates and prefects, broadly applying measures that deepen the roots and strengthen the foundations. At present, therefore, their selection must indeed receive careful attention.

Thus, when local magistrates and prefects are worthy, their civilizing influence can reach everywhere; when fortified towns and strongholds are built, the people have places of refuge; and when food is plentiful and troops are strong, authority can be asserted. Plans that safeguard the realm and secure its foundations will achieve peace for ten thousand years. These are a scholar's commonplace observations, which I know cannot contribute even one ten-thousandth to the court's deliberations. I ask only that you, honored examiners, advance and instruct me; I would be most grateful.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
嘉靖甲子歲廣東鄉試事竣
旣撤棘循例讌諸貢士于藩
司自御史藩臬而下百執事
咸在焉酒行樂作雅歌幣將
諸士子咸雍雍與與揖而升
堂有章之儀粲然外見御史
色喜曰掄材重務〔聯芳〕謬司
監臨自載事以來凜凜焉惟
弗獲真才以仰副
德意是懼百執事亦分猷共惕罔
敢自寧迺今觀所錄士之文
與其人信所選無留良也藉
是可以報
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

嘉靖甲子歲，廣東鄉試事竣，旣撤棘，循例讌諸貢士于藩司。自御史、藩臬而下，百執事咸在焉。酒行樂作，雅歌幣將。諸士子咸雍雍與與，揖而升堂，有章之儀粲然外見。御史色喜曰：「掄材重務，〔聯芳〕謬司監臨。自載事以來，凜凜焉，惟弗獲真才以仰副德意是懼。百執事亦分猷共惕，罔敢自寧。迺今觀所錄士之文與其人，信所選無留良也。藉是可以報
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

In the jiazi year of Jiajing (1564), the Guangdong Provincial Examination concluded. Once the thorn barriers had been removed, a banquet was held, according to precedent, for the successful candidates at the Provincial Administration Commission. All the officials concerned were present, from the censor and the provincial administration and surveillance officials downward. Wine was served and music played; elegant songs were sung and ceremonial gifts presented. The candidates, all harmonious and dignified in bearing, bowed and ascended the hall, their conduct brilliantly displaying the prescribed forms of ceremony. Looking pleased, the censor said: “Selecting talent is a weighty responsibility. I, 〔Lianfang〕, have undeservedly served as Supervising Official. Ever since taking up this duty, I have been filled with apprehension, fearing only that I might fail to obtain truly talented men and thereby fulfill His Majesty’s benevolent intentions. All the officials concerned have likewise shared in planning and vigilance, none daring to take his ease. Now, however, having examined the writings of the men admitted and observed the men themselves, I am convinced that our selection has left no worthy talent behind. With this, we may render our report to …”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
天子矣崇禮叨校士役聞御史言
喜而且懼迺肅諸士而申之
曰夫人才之產於世也負奇
懷異孰不欲脫穎而出襃然
自見於世哉然而抱璞不售
終其身而文采弗章者則所
遇之非其時也尓諸士幸生
===
===
聖天子壽考作人之世沐
棫樸菁莪之化在庶民中旣進
而為士矣今又得以其文見
錄於主司偕計吏上南宮獻
策
大廷駸駸乎事業炳見可不謂之
遇乎即觀今日之讌諸士一
punctuated: 天子矣。」崇禮叨校士役，聞御史言，喜而且懼，迺肅諸士而申之曰：「夫人才之產於世也，負奇懷異，孰不欲脫穎而出，襃然自見於世哉？然而抱璞不售，終其身而文采弗章者，則所遇之非其時也。尓諸士幸生聖天子壽考作人之世，沐棫樸菁莪之化，在庶民中旣進而為士矣。今又得以其文見錄於主司，偕計吏上南宮，獻策大廷，駸駸乎事業炳見，可不謂之遇乎？即觀今日之讌，諸士一
translation_en:
…the Son of Heaven.”

I, Chongli, undeservedly entrusted with examining the candidates, felt both joy and apprehension upon hearing the Censor’s words. I then respectfully addressed the gentlemen, elaborating as follows: “When talented men emerge into the world, endowed with exceptional gifts and unusual abilities, who does not wish to distinguish himself and appear prominently before the world? Yet those who hold uncut jade that finds no buyer, whose literary brilliance remains unmanifest throughout their lives, have simply encountered an unpropitious age.

“You gentlemen are fortunate to have been born in an age when our sagely Son of Heaven enjoys long life and nurtures men of talent. Bathed in the transforming influence celebrated in ‘The Oak Trees’ (Yupu) and ‘The Luxuriant Mugwort’ (Jing E), you have already risen from among the common people to become scholars. Now, moreover, your writings have secured your selection by the presiding examiners. You may accompany the officials bringing accounts to the capital, proceed to the Ministry of Rites for examination, and present policy essays at the imperial court. Advancing steadily, you will manifest brilliant achievements. Can this not be called meeting a favorable age? Consider just today’s banquet: you gentlemen are but…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書生耳曩固梛林葦澤之產
繩樞甕牖之儔也一旦薦錄
賢書與縉紳大人揖讓堂階
之上不為踰越及撤讌而歸
則里中父老子弟咸羣然歆
艶之亦不以為侈大者則以
諸士負俶儻異常之才別於
===
凡民足以當之也今取諸其
三試之文而讀之雖文質殊
尚輕重異調長短各裁不相
為侔然率皆言引詩書動合
矩度美哉洋洋文其盛矣然
劔遇割則知利事遇辨則知
才所貴於士者謂其才之足
punctuated:
書生耳，曩固梛林葦澤之產，繩樞甕牖之儔也。一旦薦錄賢書，與縉紳大人揖讓堂階之上，不為踰越；及撤讌而歸，則里中父老子弟咸羣然歆艶之，亦不以為侈大者，則以諸士負俶儻異常之才，別於凡民，足以當之也。
今取諸其三試之文而讀之，雖文質殊尚，輕重異調，長短各裁，不相為侔，然率皆言引詩書，動合矩度。美哉，洋洋，文其盛矣！然劔遇割則知利，事遇辨則知才。所貴於士者，謂其才之足
translation_en:
…mere scholars, formerly inhabitants of woodlands and reed marshes [?], men whose humble homes had rope-hinged doors and broken jars for windows. Once recommended and entered in the register of worthies, they exchange bows and courtesies with eminent officials upon the hall steps, without overstepping their station. When the banquet ends and they return home, the elders and younger men of their villages all gather in admiration and envy, yet do not consider these honors excessive. This is because you scholars possess outstanding and extraordinary talents that distinguish you from ordinary people and make you worthy of such treatment.
Now, taking up and reading your compositions from the three examination sessions, I find that, although you differ in your preference for ornament or substance, in the weight and lightness of your expression, and in the length and structure of your compositions, your words generally draw upon the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents, and at every turn conform to proper standards. How fine, how abundant—what a flourishing of literary accomplishment! Yet a sword’s sharpness is known when it is put to cutting, and talent is known when affairs must be handled. What is prized in scholars is that their talent suffices to…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以辦天下事也非徒以其文
焉已也玆所錄士之文信美
矣使異時宅揆亮采寅工錯
事以其所行者質諸所言之
文如投左券然一一符合人
將按錄而求之曰是科所選
士殆彬彬篤行君子也其永
===
聞于世矣倘或侈言無當實
行不揜則如木騮不駕鉛刀
不割卽飾以金韉橐以玉琫
外雖燁然華美其實無所用
已抑又聞之仲尼曰國有道
不變塞焉而訓者謂不變其
未達之所守云夫士窮居在
punctuated:
以辦天下事也，非徒以其文焉已也。玆所錄士之文信美矣，使異時宅揆亮采，寅工錯事，以其所行者質諸所言之文，如投左券然，一一符合，人將按錄而求之，曰：「是科所選士，殆彬彬篤行君子也。」其永聞于世矣！倘或侈言無當，實行不揜，則如木騮不駕，鉛刀不割，卽飾以金韉，橐以玉琫，外雖燁然華美，其實無所用已。
抑又聞之，仲尼曰：「國有道，不變塞焉。」而訓者謂不變其未達之所守云。夫士窮居在
translation_en:
…to manage the affairs of the realm, not merely to produce literary compositions. The writings of the scholars recorded here are indeed fine. If, in years to come, they occupy the chief minister’s position or assist in administering affairs, work reverently with their colleagues and undertake their duties, let their deeds be tested against the words of their compositions. If these match point for point, like the matching halves of a contract, people will consult this record to seek them out and say, “The scholars selected in this examination are surely gentlemen of cultivated refinement and steadfast conduct.” Their renown will endure in the world! If, however, their extravagant words prove unfounded and their actual conduct fails to bear them out, they will be like wooden steeds that cannot be harnessed or leaden knives that cannot cut. Even adorned with golden saddlecloths or sheathed in scabbards with jade fittings, they may look splendid and beautiful, yet in substance they are of no use.
Moreover, I have heard Zhongni say, “When the state possesses the Way, he does not change what he upheld in adversity.” Commentators explain this as not changing the principles he maintained before attaining office. Now, when a scholar lives in straitened circumstances in…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
膠序中其所挟持孰不欲希
蹤伊呂執鞭周孔自管晏而
下即藐乎卑之勿論也此其
志豈不傑然壯哉及至脫燕
爵之困鼓鴻漸之翼遠迹圭
竇之間致身風雲之上則忘
初筮之志昧終克之戒沿風
===
靡之習渝如石之操移情於
膏潤奪志於溫飽回心易行
毀玉改度舉平生而盡弃之
不啻若弁髦然是鄙人之行
也何以為士哉崇禮向以受
聘之粤也見道周之橘纍然
下垂僕夫指余曰此橘也味
punctuated:
膠序中，其所挟持，孰不欲希蹤伊呂，執鞭周孔？自管晏而下，即藐乎卑之，勿論也。此其志豈不傑然壯哉！及至脫燕爵之困，鼓鴻漸之翼，遠迹圭竇之間，致身風雲之上，則忘初筮之志，昧終克之戒，沿風靡之習，渝如石之操，移情於膏潤，奪志於溫飽，回心易行，毀玉改度，舉平生而盡弃之，不啻若弁髦然。是鄙人之行也，何以為士哉？
崇禮向以受聘之粤也，見道周之橘，纍然下垂。僕夫指余曰：「此橘也，味
translation_en:
…within the schools, who, in the aspirations he cherishes, does not wish to follow in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, and to serve as a whip-bearing attendant to the Duke of Zhou and Kongzi? As for Guan Zhong and Yan Ying and those below them, he dismisses them as beneath his notice, unworthy even of discussion. Are these ambitions not outstanding and grand! Yet once he escapes the straitened circumstances of swallows and sparrows, spreads his wings to rise like a wild goose, leaves far behind the narrow doorway of his humble dwelling, and gains a position amid the winds and clouds of high office, he forgets his resolve upon first entering service and disregards the admonition to persevere to the end. He follows the habit of bending with the prevailing wind and abandons his once rock-firm integrity. His affections shift toward wealth, and warmth and a full belly overcome his resolve. He changes his heart and conduct, destroys his jade-like virtue, and alters his standards, casting aside all that he has upheld throughout his life as though it were a discarded cap or childhood forelocks. This is the conduct of a base man. How can he count as a scholar?
When I, Chongli, previously traveled to Guangdong upon accepting an invitation, I saw orange trees beside the road, their fruit hanging down in clusters. My servant pointed them out to me and said, “These are oranges. Their flavor…”

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
至甘美然爲南土所宜木一
渡江而北則化而爲枳矣崇
禮因感而悟之曰以南北易
地而移其性者凡木也非美
植也以窮達易位而移其守
者凡民也非良士也故松柏
不因時而改柯良士不虧志
===
===
而渝守彼豈其所植之性然
哉今日薦士里中人固嘖嘖
然以爲俶儻異常別於凡民
矣尔諸士其忍甘自隳之以
負
國家盛典蒙誚於鄉人如僕夫
之所指議哉崇禮爲諸士字
punctuated: 至甘美，然爲南土所宜，木一渡江而北，則化而爲枳矣。」崇禮因感而悟之，曰：「以南北易地而移其性者，凡木也，非美植也；以窮達易位而移其守者，凡民也，非良士也。故松柏不因時而改柯，良士不虧志而渝守。彼豈其所植之性然哉？今日薦士，里中人固嘖嘖然以爲俶儻異常，別於凡民矣。尔諸士其忍甘自隳之，以負國家盛典，蒙誚於鄉人，如僕夫之所指議哉？」崇禮爲諸士字。
translation_en: …is exceedingly sweet and delicious, but it is suited to the southern soil. Once the tree crosses the Yangtze northward, it changes into a trifoliate orange.” Moved by this, Chongli came to a realization and said: “Trees that alter their nature when transplanted between south and north are ordinary trees, not fine specimens. People who change their principles when their circumstances shift between adversity and success are ordinary people, not worthy scholars. Thus pines and cypresses do not change their boughs with the seasons, and worthy scholars do not compromise their aspirations and abandon their principles. Might this be due to the nature rooted within them? Today, as scholars are recommended, the people of your home communities are already praising you as outstanding and extraordinary, distinct from ordinary people. Could you scholars willingly allow yourselves to fall, thereby betraying the state's grand institution and incurring the mockery of your fellow townspeople, like the tree the servant pointed out and discussed?” Chongli writes these words for the scholars [?].

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
若作和羹爾惟鹽梅
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
曰天子作民父母以為天下王
小大之臣咸懷忠良
詩
采采芣苢薄言有之
既齊既稷既匡既敕永錫爾極時萬時億
保茲天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
===
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
春秋
八月公會齊侯宋公鄭伯曹伯邾人于檉
僖公元年
公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐〔僖公十〕
punctuated:
若作和羹，爾惟鹽梅。
皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。曰：「天子作民父母，以為天下王。」
小大之臣，咸懷忠良。
詩
采采芣苢，薄言有之。
既齊既稷，既匡既敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億。
保茲天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則，令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力，天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫：「式是百辟，纘戎祖考，王躬是保。出納王命，王之喉舌，賦政于外，四方爰發。」
聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。
春秋
八月，公會齊侯、宋公、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人于檉。僖公元年。
公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐〔僖公十〕。
translation_en:
“If I were preparing a harmonious broth, you would be its salt and sour plums.”

The words promulgated by the sovereign as the supreme standard are enduring rules and instruction; they accord with the instruction of the Supreme Ruler. All the common people should learn and practice the words promulgating this standard, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven. They say: “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people and thus becomes king of all under Heaven.”

“Let ministers great and small all cherish loyalty and goodness.”

Book of Odes

“We gather and gather the plantain; come, let us collect it.”

“Once you have put things in order and acted diligently, once you have rectified and regulated them, may you forever be granted the highest blessing, for tens of thousands and hundreds of millions of years.”

“To protect this Son of Heaven, Heaven brought forth Zhongshan Fu. Zhongshan Fu’s virtue takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing is fine, his expression gracious; he is careful and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and strives to maintain dignified conduct. He obeys the Son of Heaven, whose clear commands charge him with distributing government duties. The king commanded Zhongshan Fu: ‘Be a model for these many lords; continue the work of your ancestors, and protect the king’s person. Convey the king’s commands within and without; be the king’s throat and tongue. Distribute the affairs of government abroad, and the four quarters will respond.’”

“His sagely reverence rose daily; his illustrious influence reached far, enduring and unhurried. He revered the Lord on High.”

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In the eighth month, the duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, and a representative of Zhu at Cheng.” First year of Duke Xi.

“Gongsun Ao led an army and, together with the grandees of the feudal lords, came to the aid of Xu.” 〔Duke Xi, year ten … [?]〕

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以至德之君所以保民性命而納之壽
康者率詳且切粤觀嘗草辨味而醫藥
肇傳內經著論而方脉啓祕故當時之
民瘥札不生龐皓相踵而二君者竝躋
遐永之筭享昇平之休其應詎不章章
明哉周禮周家致太平之書也以醫職
屬之天官而其法制纖悉備具可得而
聞其詳歟嗣是而後有赦太倉令而春
和賑貸者矣有見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背
===
===
者矣有頒太平聖惠方有輯簡要濟衆
方者矣不知果有合於帝王之仁否歟
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝之開基也
詔郡縣贍疲民以有司之粟而醫學之設載在
令甲我
成祖文皇帝之嗣服也
命太醫院施京民以
內府之劑而惠民之
punctuated:
以至德之君，所以保民性命而納之壽康者，率詳且切。粤觀嘗草辨味而醫藥肇傳，內經著論而方脉啓祕，故當時之民瘥札不生，龐皓相踵，而二君者竝躋遐永之筭，享昇平之休，其應詎不章章明哉？周禮，周家致太平之書也，以醫職屬之天官，而其法制纖悉備具，可得而聞其詳歟？嗣是而後，有赦太倉令而春和賑貸者矣，有見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背者矣，有頒太平聖惠方、有輯簡要濟衆方者矣，不知果有合於帝王之仁否歟？
洪惟我太祖高皇帝之開基也，詔郡縣贍疲民以有司之粟，而醫學之設載在令甲。我成祖文皇帝之嗣服也，命太醫院施京民以內府之劑，而惠民之
translation_en:
…As rulers of consummate virtue, their measures for preserving the people’s lives and bringing them longevity and health were generally thorough and attentive. Consider how the tasting of herbs and discrimination of their flavors first transmitted medical knowledge, and how the exposition of doctrines in the Inner Canon revealed the secrets of prescriptions and pulse diagnosis. Thus, among the people of that time, sickness and premature death did not arise, and white-haired elders followed one another in succession. Both rulers themselves attained great longevity and enjoyed the blessings of peace. Were the responses to their virtue not abundantly clear? The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the house of Zhou brought about Great Peace. It placed medical offices under the Ministry of Heaven, and its regulations were complete in every detail. May we hear a detailed account of them? Thereafter, there were rulers who pardoned the Director of the Imperial Granary and, in the mild spring season, provided relief loans [?]; rulers who, upon seeing an acupuncture and moxibustion chart, specifically prohibited flogging the back; rulers who promulgated the Prescriptions of Sagely Beneficence for Great Peace; and rulers who compiled the Concise Essential Prescriptions for Relieving the Multitude. Did these measures truly accord with the benevolence of emperors and kings?
We reverently reflect that, when our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty, he ordered prefectures and counties to support distressed people with grain from the responsible authorities, and the establishment of medical schools was recorded in the statutes. When our Emperor Chengzu Wen succeeded to the throne, he ordered the Imperial Medical Office to dispense medicines from the palace stores to the people of the capital, and the measures for benefiting the people…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
令申在禮部
仁心美政固以肇萬年靈長之基矣迨我
睿宗獻皇帝仁敷南國德合
天心醫方選要之集允為濟民利物之寶肆我
皇上純孝體
親至仁育物特
命刊刻普錫中外所以康乂我民者亦云至矣
近又取胡濙所
進衛生簡易方梓而
===
頒之俾遠方貧瞢之民咸知調治保全之道
至於藥粥之
施疾苦之
問時行屢下靡可殫述此其
仁卽
天地之仁而其
心卽
祖
考之心矣是以
punctuated: 令申在禮部。仁心美政，固以肇萬年靈長之基矣。迨我睿宗獻皇帝，仁敷南國，德合天心，《醫方選要》之集，允為濟民利物之寶。肆我皇上純孝體親，至仁育物，特命刊刻，普錫中外，所以康乂我民者亦云至矣。近又取胡濙所進《衛生簡易方》，梓而頒之，俾遠方貧瞢之民咸知調治保全之道。至於藥粥之施、疾苦之問，時行屢下，靡可殫述。此其仁卽天地之仁，而其心卽祖考之心矣。是以
translation_en:
…the ordinance was reiterated by the Ministry of Rites. Such benevolent intentions and excellent governance surely laid the foundation for an enduring reign lasting ten thousand years. When our Emperor Ruizong Xian came, his benevolence spread throughout the southern lands, and his virtue accorded with Heaven’s purposes. His compilation, Selected Essentials of Medical Prescriptions (Yifang xuanyao), was truly a treasure for relieving the people and benefiting living beings. Thus our present emperor, in his pure filial devotion, embodied his father’s intentions and nurtured living beings with consummate benevolence. He specially commanded that it be printed and distributed widely within and beyond the capital. His measures to secure the health and well-being of our people may indeed be called complete.

Recently, he also had the Simple and Easy Prescriptions for Preserving Health (Weisheng jianyi fang), submitted by Hu Ying, printed from woodblocks and distributed, so that even poor and uninformed people in distant places might all learn ways to treat illness and preserve their health. As for distributions of medicines and gruel and inquiries into illness and suffering, these were carried out from time to time under repeatedly issued orders, too numerous to recount exhaustively. His benevolence is thus the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and his heart is the heart of his ancestors and deceased father. Therefore…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為理形而下者為物矣而又曰道亦器
器亦道信斯言也道器固惟一歟仁統
四端先儒論之詳矣而有以陰陽五行
四時配之者是又不以四端之統為言
何也心統性情先儒論之備矣而有以
性之有形者為心性之有動者為情是
又以性之統乎心情為言何也知者動
仁者靜則動陽而靜陰矣而解易者乃
有智為陰而仁為陽之說不與孔子之
===
言殊乎成己仁成物智則仁體而智用
矣而釋聖者乃有智自明而仁及物之
論不與子思之言悖乎盡己為忠盡物
為信忠信只一理也而又謂忠為天之
道信為人之道者則信與忠果有異乎
知以明理行以履事知行有先後也而
又謂道之不明由於行之過與不及者
則行視知果尤急耶夫道在天下自有
至當歸一之妙學以明道當得根極要
punctuated:
為理，形而下者為物矣。而又曰：「道亦器，器亦道。」信斯言也，道器固惟一歟？仁統四端，先儒論之詳矣，而有以陰陽五行四時配之者，是又不以四端之統為言，何也？心統性情，先儒論之備矣，而有以性之有形者為心，性之有動者為情，是又以性之統乎心情為言，何也？知者動，仁者靜，則動陽而靜陰矣，而解易者乃有智為陰而仁為陽之說，不與孔子之言殊乎？成己仁，成物智，則仁體而智用矣，而釋聖者乃有智自明而仁及物之論，不與子思之言悖乎？盡己為忠，盡物為信，忠信只一理也，而又謂忠為天之道，信為人之道者，則信與忠果有異乎？知以明理，行以履事，知行有先後也，而又謂道之不明由於行之過與不及者，則行視知果尤急耶？
夫道在天下，自有至當歸一之妙。學以明道，當得根極要
translation_en:
…is principle, while what is below form is a concrete thing. Yet it is also said: “The Way is also concrete implements, and concrete implements are also the Way.” If these words are true, are the Way and concrete implements indeed one? Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed in detail how benevolence unifies the four beginnings of virtue. Yet some correlate them with yin and yang, the Five Phases, and the four seasons, thus no longer speaking in terms of what unifies the four beginnings. Why is this? Earlier Confucian scholars have discussed fully how the mind governs human nature and the emotions. Yet some regard the mind as human nature having form, and the emotions as human nature in motion, thus speaking instead of human nature as governing the mind and the emotions. Why is this? “The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” Thus activity is yang and stillness yin. Yet interpreters of the Book of Changes maintain that wisdom is yin and benevolence yang. Does this not differ from Confucius’s words? “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” Thus benevolence is substance and wisdom is function. Yet those who expound the sages maintain that wisdom brings illumination to oneself, while benevolence extends to other things. Does this not contradict Zisi’s words? Doing one’s utmost within oneself is wholeheartedness; doing one’s utmost with respect to things is trustworthiness. Wholeheartedness and trustworthiness are but a single principle. Yet some say that wholeheartedness is the Way of Heaven, and trustworthiness the human Way. Are trustworthiness and wholeheartedness, then, truly different? Knowledge serves to illuminate principle, and action to carry out affairs: knowledge and action have an order of precedence. Yet it is also said that failure to understand the Way arises from excess and deficiency in action. Is action, then, truly more urgent than knowledge?
The Way in the world inherently possesses the subtle capacity to be supremely fitting and converge upon unity. Learning serves to illuminate the Way, and one should grasp its root, ultimate ground, and essentials …

punctuated: 者；有請立左氏博士者，有通毛詩、三禮、春秋而屢薦不出者，有講五經、進易解而時論不徇者，可謂精於經術矣。有獻獄空年豐賦頌者，有作異物誌、水土記者，有作廣樂記、太常釋義者，有登科作賦稱李伯夷者，可謂富於文章矣。至於當宋儒倡明正學之時，又有能聞庸學、述語孟者，有師朱子而篤志力學、一意實踐者，有師南軒而講明性理、學慕濂洛者，視前數子，又果為孰優歟？有因姓而嶺邑以之著名、山陂以之表異者，有因孝而里以參號、湖以曾子稱者，有名奉化鄉、慕德里者，有名慈廉江、義江者，其行誼亦云偉矣。有正色立朝、人薦其才堪大用者，有提刑明允、人贈以清通仁厚者，有以能吏顯者，有以良吏聞者，其政事亦云傑矣。及觀李鼎英稱張、姜、劉三人于唐，陳璉取余、崔二人于宋，比
translation_en:
…; there were those who requested the establishment of an Erudite for the Zuo Commentary; those versed in the Mao recension of the Book of Odes, the Three Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals who repeatedly declined to take office despite recommendations; and those who expounded the Five Classics and submitted an Explanation of the Book of Changes without conforming to contemporary opinion [?]. They may indeed be called masters of classical learning. There were those who presented rhapsodies and encomia on empty prisons and abundant harvests; those who wrote Records of Strange Things and Records of Waters and Lands; those who wrote Records of Grand Music and Explanations of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and those who passed the examination and composed rhapsodies, earning the appellation “Li Boyi” [?]. They may indeed be called richly accomplished in literary composition.

Then, when the Confucians of the Song were promoting and elucidating orthodox learning, there were also those who learned the teachings of the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning and expounded the Analects and the Mencius; those who studied under Master Zhu, applied themselves resolutely to learning, and devoted themselves wholeheartedly to putting it into practice; and those who studied under Nanxuan, elucidated human nature and principle, and admired the learning of the Lian and Luo traditions. Compared with the preceding worthies, which were truly superior?

There were those whose surnames gave prominence to districts in Lingnan and distinguished mountains and embankments; those whose filial devotion caused a neighborhood to be named after Shen and a lake to be called Master Zeng; those who occasioned the names Fenghua Township and Mude Neighborhood; and those who occasioned the names Cilian River and Yi River. Their conduct and moral character may indeed be called magnificent. There were those who maintained a stern and upright bearing at court, whom others recommended as talented enough for great responsibilities; those who administered judicial affairs with discernment and fairness, whom others praised as incorruptible, perceptive, benevolent, and generous; those renowned as capable officials; and those known as good officials. Their achievements in government may indeed be called outstanding.

第壹場

同考試官教諭林批此篇場中作者多掇拾
套語且以己之克禮之復對講殊失口氣此作體
認眞切而措詞雅健非苟作者宜錄以式

我而無難之意殆盡非俗學可到
===
考試官教諭劉批整潔深邃是亦有得於
心學者
考試官學正楊批善發聖人告顏子之旨
聖人决爲仁之機在於己示大賢以心學也蓋
仁心德也爲之在我夫何難之有哉夫子告顏
淵之意謂夫學莫要於爲仁機惟决於在己自

punctuated:
第壹場

四書

爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？

李成性

同考試官教諭林批：此篇場中作者多掇拾套語，且以己之克、禮之復對講，殊失口氣。此作體認眞切，而措詞雅健，非苟作者，宜錄以式。

同考試官教授饒批：渾融典雅，發出其機在我而無難之意殆盡，非俗學可到。

考試官教諭劉批：整潔深邃，是亦有得於心學者。

考試官學正楊批：善發聖人告顏子之旨。

聖人决爲仁之機在於己，示大賢以心學也。蓋仁，心德也；爲之在我，夫何難之有哉？夫子告顏淵之意，謂夫學莫要於爲仁，機惟决於在己。自今觀之，仁通於天下之大，宜有所待而後足；而效收於一日之速，若有所資而後成矣。殊不知仁者，心之理也。還吾所固有之理，斯有欲之則
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Practicing benevolence depends on oneself; could it depend on others?”

Li Chengxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Among those in the examination who wrote on this topic, many merely gathered stock phrases. Moreover, they treated “overcoming the self” and “returning to ritual propriety” as parallel propositions, badly missing the tenor of the original utterance. This composition shows genuine and precise understanding, and its language is elegant and vigorous. It is no careless work and should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Professor: Thoroughly integrated, classically refined, and elegant, it brings out almost exhaustively the meaning that the decisive impetus lies within oneself and that there is no difficulty. This is beyond the reach of commonplace learning.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Orderly, polished, and profound: this too is the work of someone who has gained insight into the learning of the mind.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: It skillfully elucidates the purport of the Sage’s instruction to Master Yan.

The Sage determined that the decisive impetus for practicing benevolence lies within oneself, thereby revealing the learning of the mind to a great worthy. Benevolence is the virtue of the mind; its practice rests with me. What difficulty, then, can there be? The meaning of the Master’s instruction to Yan Yuan was that nothing in learning is more essential than practicing benevolence, and that its decisive impetus lies solely within oneself. Viewed from our present standpoint, benevolence extends throughout the vastness of all under Heaven, so it would seem to require something further before it could be complete; yet its effects are achieved as swiftly as in a single day, as though some assistance were needed for its accomplishment. This entirely overlooks the fact that benevolence is the principle of the mind. Restore the principle that is inherently ours, and thus, if one desires it, then…

===

至誠有恒之業與天地參者也夫至誠之心本
與天地而無間也則其業之發於外有不參於
天地者哉中庸此章言天道也若曰法象莫大
於天地功業莫大於聖人而要之一誠足以貫
之也今至誠不息而久矣吾見實心之蘊也旣
緝熈於有常則實理之著也必發揮於事業寧

至誠有恒之業，與天地參者也。夫至誠之心，本與天地而無間也，則其業之發於外，有不參於天地者哉？《中庸》此章言天道也，若曰：「法象莫大於天地，功業莫大於聖人，而要之，一誠足以貫之也。今至誠不息而久矣，吾見實心之蘊也，旣緝熈於有常，則實理之著也，必發揮於事業，寧有久而不徵者乎？徵則有漸之化、永賴之功，亘萬古而常存焉，斯其悠遠也巳。悠遠則其積也
translation_en:
“Enduring constancy is the means by which things are brought to completion. Breadth and depth match Earth; loftiness and brightness match Heaven; enduring constancy is without bounds.”

Liang Yu

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor: With a long topic, the difficulty lies not in elaboration but in drawing everything together. This composition leaves no gaps in its reasoning, yet its language is exceptionally concise and clear. It sweeps away conventional formulas: this is an essay worthy of serving as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Its grasp of principle is clear and precise, and its phrasing elegant and vigorous. Reading it, one seems to hear Zisi himself elucidating the Way of Heaven. An excellent composition.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Thoroughly integrated, it captures the essential meaning.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: Lustrous, pure, and flawless.

The enduring achievement of utmost sincerity ranks alongside Heaven and Earth. The heart of utmost sincerity is fundamentally inseparable from Heaven and Earth; could its achievements, as manifested outwardly, fail to rank alongside them? This chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of Heaven. It is as though it said: “Among models to emulate, none is greater than Heaven and Earth; among accomplishments, none is greater than those of the sage. Yet, in essence, sincerity alone suffices to run through them all. Now utmost sincerity continues without ceasing and thus endures. I see that, once what the true heart holds within has attained constant, continuing brightness, the manifestation of true principle must find full expression in practical achievements. Could anything endure without becoming manifest? Once manifest, its gradual transforming influence and its accomplishments, upon which people may forever rely, persist through all ages. This is its far-reaching endurance. With such far-reaching endurance, what it accumulates …
