之爲已辜充其量之所包必欲盡萬民而俾乂
punctuated:
成輔相，所以賛化育之不及，而得一以清、得一以寧者，莫非中和之所致也。不然，何以曰「聖人天地之用」？

其自任以天下之重如此。

陳法

同考試官教諭姚批：伊尹濟世之心，因遇湯可爲堯舜之君，足以行己所樂之道，故慨然自任。此作發揮得旨，而格調髙朗，詞氣充暢，讀之一唱三嘆，真傑作也！他日必能辦天下之事者。

考試官教諭劉批：髙明之識，充健之才。

考試官學正楊批：得趣之文，沛然理順。

大賢推聖臣自負之重，以明其始進之必正也。蓋天下至大也，聖臣以之爲已責，則所以自任者誠重矣，其肯苟于始進乎哉？想昔伊尹樂道畝畝之中，旣抱夫天民先覺之具，值湯三聘之日，又逢夫親見堯舜之時，其相須爲甚殷矣。而尹之自任者何如哉？匹夫匹婦，分至微也，而引之爲已辜。充其量之所包，必欲盡萬民而俾乂
translation_en:
…bringing to completion and assisting [?], thereby supplementing what the transforming and nurturing powers leave unfinished. That which attains the One and becomes clear, and that which attains the One and becomes tranquil, are alike brought about by equilibrium and harmony. Otherwise, why say, “The sage is the agency through which Heaven and Earth act”?

“Such was the weight of responsibility for all under Heaven that he took upon himself.”

Chen Fa

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: Yi Yin’s desire to bring aid to the world found its opportunity when he encountered Tang, who could become a ruler like Yao or Shun and enable him to put into practice the Way in which he delighted. Thus he resolutely took this responsibility upon himself. This composition develops the essential meaning correctly; its style is lofty and lucid, its language vigorous and fluent. Reading it, one sings once and sighs in admiration three times. It is truly a masterpiece! Its author will surely be capable of managing the affairs of all under Heaven one day.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Lofty and penetrating discernment; abundant and vigorous talent.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: A composition that captures the true purport, flowing abundantly with orderly reasoning.

The great worthy expounds the weight of responsibility borne by the sagely minister to show that his first entry into service must accord with what is right. All under Heaven is vast indeed. When a sagely minister makes it his own responsibility, the burden he assumes is truly heavy. How could he be willing to act carelessly in first entering service? Consider Yi Yin of old, delighting in the Way amid the fields [?]: he already possessed the qualities of one of Heaven’s people who had awakened before others. When Tang invited him three times, he also encountered an opportunity to see a Yao or Shun in person. Their need for one another was therefore exceedingly pressing. But what was the responsibility Yi Yin took upon himself? An ordinary man or woman occupies the humblest station, yet he accounted their plight his own fault. Extending his capacious concern to its fullest reach, he was determined to embrace all the people and bring them under good governance…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之然後於願為始慰堯舜之澤未易究也而承
之為已責要其志之所存必欲舉一世而兼濟
之然後於心為始安今日之君即堯舜之君也
有堯舜之君而其澤乃未徧於天下其咎在我
而不容辭而孜孜焉必思以共其付託之重今
日之民即唐虞之民也為唐虞之民而猶有未
被堯舜之澤其職在已而不容逭而汲汲焉必
思以副其仰望之殷通天地民物為一體而隱
居求志之日已全具乎輔世長民之道荷經綸
===
叅賛於一身而君臣相遇之始已預期乎時雍
風動之休是其任之也重故思之也不得不深
思之也深故捄之也不得不切尹之出而將有
所為如此則其進自必以正矣而豈屑於割烹
之事哉雖然聖賢出處莫非天也而其心則惟
為道計耳詩稱降于卿士實左右商王而尹亦
以天生斯民使予先覺信矣尹之為天民也應
聘而出欲以道濟天下者亦以奉天心耳故曰
有天民者達可行而行之者也世乃以割烹疑
punctuated: 之，然後於願為始慰。堯舜之澤未易究也，而承之為已責；要其志之所存，必欲舉一世而兼濟之，然後於心為始安。今日之君，即堯舜之君也。有堯舜之君，而其澤乃未徧於天下，其咎在我而不容辭，而孜孜焉必思以共其付託之重。今日之民，即唐虞之民也。為唐虞之民，而猶有未被堯舜之澤，其職在已而不容逭，而汲汲焉必思以副其仰望之殷。通天地民物為一體，而隱居求志之日，已全具乎輔世長民之道；荷經綸叅賛於一身，而君臣相遇之始，已預期乎時雍風動之休。是其任之也重，故思之也不得不深；思之也深，故捄之也不得不切。尹之出而將有所為如此，則其進自必以正矣，而豈屑於割烹之事哉！雖然，聖賢出處莫非天也，而其心則惟為道計耳。詩稱「降于卿士，實左右商王」，而尹亦以「天生斯民，使予先覺」。信矣，尹之為天民也！應聘而出，欲以道濟天下者，亦以奉天心耳。故曰：「有天民者，達可行而行之者也。」世乃以割烹疑
translation_en:
…them; only then would his aspiration begin to be fulfilled. The beneficence of Yao and Shun was not easily extended to its fullest reach, yet he undertook this as his own responsibility. The essential purpose of his resolve was to bring aid to everyone throughout the age; only then would his heart begin to rest easy. The ruler of his own day was a ruler like Yao and Shun. With such a ruler, if that ruler’s beneficence had still not reached everyone under Heaven, “the fault lies with me, and I cannot disclaim it.” Thus he labored tirelessly, intent on fulfilling the weighty trust placed in him. The people of his own day were the people of Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun. If such people still included any who had not received the beneficence of Yao and Shun, “the responsibility lies with me, and I cannot evade it.” Thus he applied himself urgently, intent on answering their fervent expectations. He embraced Heaven, Earth, the people, and all things as one body. Even while living in retirement and pursuing his aspirations, he already fully possessed the Way of assisting the world and governing the people. Taking upon himself the work of ordering the world and assisting the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth, he already anticipated, at the very beginning of his encounter with his ruler, the blessings of universal harmony and transformation through moral influence. Because the responsibility he assumed was weighty, his deliberations necessarily ran deep; because his deliberations ran deep, his efforts to save the people necessarily became urgent. Since these were the things Yi Yin intended to accomplish upon entering public service, his entry into office would assuredly accord with righteousness. How could he have stooped to gaining access through butchery and cookery?

Nevertheless, whether sages and worthies enter service or remain in retirement is always determined by Heaven; in their hearts, however, they consider only the Way. The Book of Odes declares, “He sent down a high minister, who truly aided the king of Shang.” Yi Yin likewise held that “Heaven gave birth to these people and caused me to awaken first.” Truly, Yi Yin was one of Heaven’s people! In accepting the invitation to enter service and seeking to bring aid to all under Heaven through the Way, he was simply carrying out Heaven’s intent. Hence the saying: “There are those who are Heaven’s people: when, upon attaining a position, they can put the Way into practice, they do so.” Yet people in the world invoke butchery and cookery to cast doubt upon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之豈知聖人之心哉
易
大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天
梁譽
同考試官教諭樂批始物統天只一氣也人
多不能發此作深識其旨取之
同考試官教諭周批是善於言天道者
考試官教諭劉批精潔無一閑語可式
考試官學正楊批明淨
===
乾元之所以為大以其妙氣化之全焉夫一氣
流行則物以之始而天亦統于是矣乾元之大
不可見耶且夫天之性情謂之乾而乾之始謂
之元大矣哉乾之元其根柢品彙綱紀造化而
浩乎不可以限量者乎何言乎其大也蓋萬物
寓形于宇内孰其始之也元則陽氣潜嘘萬有
賴之以立命一心復見羣動籍之以造端氣雖
未行而太和之保合已基於此焉一元之氣是
固物之所以取足而生出之不窮矣理雖未立
punctuated:
之，豈知聖人之心哉？

易
大哉乾元，萬物資始，乃統天。
梁譽

同考試官教諭樂批：始物統天，只一氣也。人多不能發，此作深識其旨，取之。
同考試官教諭周批：是善於言天道者。
考試官教諭劉批：精潔，無一閑語，可式。
考試官學正楊批：明淨。

乾元之所以為大，以其妙氣化之全焉。夫一氣流行，則物以之始，而天亦統于是矣。乾元之大，不可見耶？且夫天之性情謂之乾，而乾之始謂之元。大矣哉，乾之元！其根柢品彙，綱紀造化，而浩乎不可以限量者乎！何言乎其大也？蓋萬物寓形于宇内，孰其始之也？元則陽氣潜嘘，萬有賴之以立命；一心復見，羣動籍之以造端。氣雖未行，而太和之保合已基於此焉。一元之氣，是固物之所以取足，而生出之不窮矣。理雖未立
translation_en:
…him on this account—how could they understand the sage’s heart?

Book of Changes
“Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! The myriad things depend upon it for their beginnings, and it encompasses Heaven.”
By Liang Yu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yue, Instructor: “Giving things their beginnings and encompassing Heaven are simply the work of a single qi. Most people cannot elucidate this. This composition profoundly understands its meaning; I select it.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “Here is someone skilled at explaining the Way of Heaven.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Refined and concise, without a single superfluous phrase. It can serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Yang, School Director: “Clear and lucid.”

The originating power of Qian is great because it wondrously embraces the whole process of transformation through qi. As the single qi circulates, things receive their beginnings from it, and Heaven, too, is encompassed within it. Is not the greatness of Qian’s originating power thereby apparent? Heaven’s nature and disposition are called Qian, and Qian’s beginning is called yuan, the originating power. Great indeed is Qian’s originating power! It roots the myriad kinds of things and orders the processes of creation and transformation; vast indeed, it cannot be bounded or measured! Why do we speak of its greatness? The myriad things assume their forms within the universe: what gives them their beginnings? In this originating power, yang qi silently breathes forth, and all beings depend upon it to establish their allotted existence; the single heart appears again [?], and all that moves relies upon it to make its beginning. Though qi has not yet begun to circulate, the preservation and union of Supreme Harmony already have their foundation here. The qi of this single originating power is assuredly that from which things draw their sufficiency, coming into being without exhaustion. Though principle has not yet been established…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而性命之各正已兆于此焉一元之理是固物
之所以取給而發生之不息矣然元不但資物
之始而已也由之以推於無端則肇于始而不
盡於始由之以達於不已則即其終而無間於
終始物者元也而生物長物以馴底於保合之
歸者亦莫非元也氣之所行見其有嗣續而無
停機矣元其獨擅統馭之權者乎出震者元也
而加美亨通以漸至於各正之地者亦莫非元
也理之所運見其有貫徹而無間斷矣元其獨
===
專宰制之柄者乎吁元而曰資始見其有父道
焉元而曰統天見其有君道焉乾元之大如此
信乎不得而並之也與大抵乾元之義甚大而
惟君克配之君之道乾之道也乾之道生生而
不已者以其體之健也人君象乾而健與乾一
則生生之德即乾之不已矣不已而治純萬國
咸寧之化與天同其運也是故體乾者人君之
職而至健者又合乾之功
天生神物聖人則之
punctuated:
而性命之各正已兆于此焉。一元之理，是固物之所以取給而發生之不息矣。然元不但資物之始而已也。由之以推於無端，則肇于始而不盡於始；由之以達於不已，則即其終而無間於終。始物者元也，而生物長物以馴底於保合之歸者，亦莫非元也。氣之所行，見其有嗣續而無停機矣。元其獨擅統馭之權者乎？出震者元也，而加美亨通以漸至於各正之地者，亦莫非元也。理之所運，見其有貫徹而無間斷矣。元其獨專宰制之柄者乎？吁！元而曰資始，見其有父道焉；元而曰統天，見其有君道焉。乾元之大如此，信乎不得而並之也與！大抵乾元之義甚大，而惟君克配之。君之道，乾之道也。乾之道，生生而不已者，以其體之健也。人君象乾，而健與乾一，則生生之德即乾之不已矣。不已而治純，萬國咸寧之化，與天同其運也。是故體乾者人君之職，而至健者又合乾之功。

天生神物，聖人則之。
translation_en:
…yet the signs that each thing’s nature and allotted destiny will be correctly established are already present here. The principle of the primal origin is indeed that upon which things draw for their inexhaustible emergence and growth. Yet the origin does more than supply things with their beginnings. Follow it back into the beginningless, and it initiates things at their beginning without being exhausted in that beginning; follow it onward into the unceasing, and even at their end its operation remains uninterrupted. It is the origin that initiates things; and what generates and nourishes them, gradually bringing them to the preservation of supreme harmony, is likewise nothing other than the origin. In the movement of vital energy, we see succession without any cessation of its workings. Does not the origin alone command the power to govern and direct? It is the origin that brings things forth in Zhen, the trigram of Thunder; and what increases their excellence and brings them to flourishing development, gradually reaching the state in which each is correctly established, is likewise nothing other than the origin. In the operation of principle, we see continuity throughout, without interruption. Does not the origin alone wield the authority to rule and regulate?

Ah! When we say of the origin that things draw upon it for their beginnings, we see that it possesses the Way of a father; when we say that it governs Heaven, we see that it possesses the Way of a ruler. Such is the greatness of the primal origin of Qian, the Creative! Truly, nothing can equal it! The significance of Qian’s primal origin is exceedingly great, and only the ruler can match it. The ruler’s Way is the Way of Qian. The Way of Qian generates life without ceasing because its essential constitution is vigorous. If the ruler takes Qian as his model and becomes one with it in vigor, then his virtue of continually generating life embodies Qian’s own ceaselessness. Through this ceaselessness, government attains perfection, and the transforming influence through which the myriad states all find peace moves in concert with Heaven. Thus, embodying Qian is the ruler’s duty, while attaining utmost vigor is the achievement through which he accords with Qian.

Heaven produces numinous objects; the sage takes them as models.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
周裔先
同考試官教諭樂批刋落陳言而詞從理發
讀之便覺不羣
同考試官教諭周批認理真切措詞古雅邃
于易者也敬服敬服
考試官教諭劉批文雅健可味
考試官學正楊批精確
造化呈靈於物聖人法而用之焉夫蓍龜之生
天所以示卜筮之用也聖人則之以立法其憲
===
天之道者乎大傳之意若曰聖心具易書之蘊
而造化實易理之原孰謂卜筮之興果聖人之
强制哉彼天地絪縕而神明得于幽賛遂呈之
爲物象之精貞元會合而太和溢於兩間乃鍾
之爲文明之瑞以植物則神見乎蓍焉叢以百
莖其示以天地之全數乎而筮之爲用此其昭
垂之矣以動物則神見乎龜焉列以五行其告
以變通之神機乎而卜之爲用此其默啓之矣
夫天地欲以前民之用不能不洩於物以開其
punctuated:
周裔先

同考試官教諭樂批：刋落陳言，而詞從理發，讀之便覺不羣。

同考試官教諭周批：認理真切，措詞古雅，邃于易者也。敬服！敬服！

考試官教諭劉批：文雅健，可味。

考試官學正楊批：精確。

造化呈靈於物，聖人法而用之焉。夫蓍龜之生，天所以示卜筮之用也。聖人則之以立法，其憲天之道者乎！大傳之意若曰：聖心具易書之蘊，而造化實易理之原，孰謂卜筮之興果聖人之强制哉？彼天地絪縕，而神明得于幽賛，遂呈之爲物象之精；貞元會合，而太和溢於兩間，乃鍾之爲文明之瑞。以植物，則神見乎蓍焉，叢以百莖，其示以天地之全數乎？而筮之爲用，此其昭垂之矣。以動物，則神見乎龜焉，列以五行，其告以變通之神機乎？而卜之爲用，此其默啓之矣。夫天地欲以前民之用，不能不洩於物以開其
translation_en:
Zhou Yixian 周裔先

Comment by Associate Examiner Le, Instructor: He cuts away hackneyed expressions, letting his language arise from principle. Reading it, one immediately senses its distinction.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: His grasp of principle is precise and penetrating, his phrasing classical and elegant. Here is someone deeply versed in the Book of Changes. Admirable! Admirable!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The writing is elegant and vigorous, and rewards contemplation.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: Refined and exact.

The creative transformations of nature manifest spiritual efficacy in things; the sage takes these as models and puts them to use. Heaven brings forth milfoil and tortoises to reveal the uses of divination by shells and stalks. The sage follows these models to establish methods: is this not his way of taking Heaven as his rule? The meaning of the Great Commentary is as if to say: the sage’s mind contains the profundities of the Book of Changes, while nature’s creative transformations are truly the source of the principles of the Changes. Who could claim that the origins of divination lay in something arbitrarily imposed by the sage? Heaven and earth intermingle, and spiritual illumination arises through their unseen assistance, manifesting itself as the finest of material forms. Completion and inception converge, and supreme harmony suffuses the space between heaven and earth, concentrating itself into auspicious signs of luminous order. Among plants, spiritual efficacy appears in milfoil. Growing in clusters of a hundred stalks, does it not display the complete number of heaven and earth? Here the use of stalk divination is plainly disclosed. Among animals, spiritual efficacy appears in the tortoise. Arrayed according to the Five Phases [?], does it not reveal the wondrous workings of change and adaptation? Here the use of shell divination is silently revealed. Now, heaven and earth, wishing to guide the people in their practical undertakings, cannot but disclose their workings in things, thereby opening their …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝世得人之盛者可錄
考試官敎諭劉批純暢得旨
考試官學正楊批意明辭藻
大臣期聖君欲其致天下之賢而用之也甚矣
德之足以感人也舉萬邦共臣之賢而惟君所
用焉其所感於明德深矣大禹欲舜之純任乎
德也意謂人君以舉賢爲功尤以明德爲本帝
德光天之下而至于海隅蒼生也則其感人何
如哉夫萬邦至遠矣黎獻之生於其間至無盡
===
矣皆視君德之脩否以行藏其道者也今則聖
人在上旣啓其利見之心而明德所孚又動其
觀光之誠懷忠以待舉者則思效明時而爲帝
之忠臣焉身雖未列乎臣鄰而志已切於用賓
矣秉直以待用者則願立聖朝而爲帝之直臣
焉位雖未膺乎弼直而志已奮於從王矣是一
德敷而足以來天下之賢如此則是賢也其致
也有所自而其出也有所爲者也帝於此當何
以處之乎蓋奮庸之志雖存乎賢而登庸之舉
punctuated:
帝世得人之盛者可錄。
考試官敎諭劉批：純暢得旨。
考試官學正楊批：意明辭藻。
大臣期聖君，欲其致天下之賢而用之也。甚矣，德之足以感人也！舉萬邦共臣之賢，而惟君所用焉，其所感於明德深矣。大禹欲舜之純任乎德也，意謂人君以舉賢爲功，尤以明德爲本。帝德光天之下，而至于海隅蒼生也，則其感人何如哉？夫萬邦至遠矣，黎獻之生於其間至無盡矣，皆視君德之脩否以行藏其道者也。今則聖人在上，旣啓其利見之心，而明德所孚，又動其觀光之誠。懷忠以待舉者，則思效明時而爲帝之忠臣焉。身雖未列乎臣鄰，而志已切於用賓矣。秉直以待用者，則願立聖朝而爲帝之直臣焉。位雖未膺乎弼直，而志已奮於從王矣。是一德敷而足以來天下之賢如此，則是賢也，其致也有所自，而其出也有所爲者也。帝於此當何以處之乎？蓋奮庸之志雖存乎賢，而登庸之舉
translation_en:
…the abundance of worthy men obtained in the emperor’s age merits recording.

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “Pure and fluent; it captures the essential meaning.”

Examiner Yang, Director of Studies, comments: “Clear in meaning and ornate in expression.”

What a great minister expects of a sage ruler is that he should attract the worthy men of the world and employ them. How great is virtue’s power to move people! All the worthy men of the myriad states offer themselves as ministers, to be employed solely as the ruler chooses: so deeply have they been moved by his luminous virtue. Great Yu wished Shun to rely wholly upon virtue. His meaning was that a ruler’s achievement lies in raising worthy men to office, but that cultivating luminous virtue is still more fundamental. When the emperor’s virtue illuminates all beneath Heaven and reaches the common people at the farthest shores, how profoundly must it move people!

The myriad states extend to the remotest distances, and the worthy men born among their people are inexhaustible in number. All look to whether the ruler cultivates his virtue in deciding whether to put their Way into practice or keep it concealed. Now that a sage occupies the throne, he has already awakened their desire for the favorable opportunity of an audience; the trust inspired by his luminous virtue further stirs their sincere desire to behold the realm’s splendor. Those who cherish loyalty while awaiting recommendation think of rendering service in this enlightened age and becoming the emperor’s loyal ministers. Although they have not yet joined the ranks of his close ministers, their resolve to be received as guests is already ardent. Those who uphold integrity while awaiting employment wish to take their place at the sage court and become the emperor’s upright ministers. Although they have not yet been entrusted with office to assist and correct him, their determination to follow the king is already roused.

Thus, the diffusion of one ruler’s virtue suffices to attract the worthy men of the world. These worthy men therefore have a source of inspiration that draws them to court and a purpose for which they enter public service. How should the emperor deal with them? For although the aspiration to exert themselves in service resides in the worthy, the act of raising them to employment…

text:
猶晉之依哉故春秋前書伐鄭會蕭魚之事以
表悼公駕楚服鄭之謀後書執良霄會申之事
以徵悼公駕楚服鄭之效比而觀之美自著矣
吁先儒謂悼公有君子之資於此可見雖然悼
誠賢矣然陳鄭一也知救鄭而失於存陳吳楚
等也知抑楚而闇於通吳凡此皆不學之過也
是故帝王之道至誠無息伯者之業假而遽歸
君子貴王道而賤伯術也良有以哉
齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田定公十年
===
王文明
同考試官教諭韓　批　時作多講序績意此篇
專就歸田上發揮得旨宜錄以式多士
考試官教諭劉　批　講以天自處辭不煩而
意自足
考試官學正楊　批　嚴正可誦
春秋紀大國歸地之誠而化強之績著矣此見
三田之歸聖人秉禮之化之所致也春秋據事
直書而何嫌於序績哉鄆讙龜陰魯故田也齊
punctuated:
猶晉之依哉！故春秋前書伐鄭會蕭魚之事，以表悼公駕楚服鄭之謀；後書執良霄會申之事，以徵悼公駕楚服鄭之效。比而觀之，美自著矣。吁！先儒謂悼公有君子之資，於此可見。雖然，悼誠賢矣，然陳鄭一也，知救鄭而失於存陳；吳楚等也，知抑楚而闇於通吳。凡此皆不學之過也。是故帝王之道，至誠無息；伯者之業，假而遽歸。君子貴王道而賤伯術也，良有以哉！
「齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田。」定公十年。
王文明
同考試官教諭韓　批：時作多講序績意，此篇專就歸田上發揮，得旨，宜錄以式多士。
考試官教諭劉　批：講以天自處，辭不煩而意自足。
考試官學正楊　批：嚴正可誦。
春秋紀大國歸地之誠，而化強之績著矣。此見三田之歸，聖人秉禮之化之所致也。春秋據事直書，而何嫌於序績哉？鄆讙龜陰，魯故田也。齊
translation_en:
…still relied upon Jin! Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals first records the attack on Zheng and the meeting at Xiaoyu to reveal Duke Dao’s strategy for outmaneuvering Chu and bringing Zheng into submission; later it records the seizure of Liang Xiao and the meeting at Shen to attest to the results of that strategy. Viewed together, these accounts make his excellence manifest. Ah! Earlier scholars said that Duke Dao possessed the qualities of a gentleman; here we can see them. Nevertheless, although Duke Dao was indeed worthy, Chen and Zheng stood in the same position: he knew to rescue Zheng but failed to preserve Chen. Wu and Chu were equivalent: he knew to restrain Chu but was blind to the importance of establishing relations with Wu. All these were faults arising from a lack of learning. Thus the Way of the ancient emperors and kings rests on utmost sincerity without ceasing, whereas the undertaking of a hegemon rests on borrowed virtue, soon relinquished. There is good reason why the gentleman esteems the kingly Way and holds the methods of hegemons in low regard!
“The men of Qi came to return the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin.” Tenth year of Duke Ding.
Wang Wenming.
Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: Contemporary essays mostly discuss the idea of recounting achievements. This essay develops its argument specifically around the return of the lands and grasps the essential meaning. It should be recorded as a model for the candidates.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The exposition presents taking Heaven as one’s own position [?]. Its language is concise, yet its meaning is complete.
Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: Grave and upright, worthy of recitation.
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the sincerity with which a great state returned territory, thereby making manifest the achievement of morally transforming the powerful. The return of these three tracts shows what the sage accomplished through his transforming influence, upholding ritual propriety. The Spring and Autumn Annals writes directly according to the facts: why should it shy away from recounting achievements? Yun, Huan, and Guiyin were lands formerly belonging to Lu. Qi…

嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聲容之盛樂固爲德之華矣果何以見之彼樂
必有詩也由志之動於中者而宣諸詞說之際
樂必有歌也由詩之形於言者而調諸音曲之
餘樂必有舞也由聲之發於外者而協諸容觀
之度是三者皆樂之所由生也然是聲容之肇
端於志非無所本也內焉感於心而欣喜萌其
端歡愛洩其蘊樂之啓其始者在是矣然後志
之形見於聲容不能無飾也外焉被於器而音
律以宣之干羽以舞之樂之成其終者在是矣
===
是故聖人之作樂也情之感觸者深自溢於中
聲之暢志之蘊藉者厚自闡於德容之光其視
天地之氣積之盛而生物之妙發之神者不有
同機乎故志和行成實德之中孚不能遏則呈
露於歌舞者足以動四氣之和而聖人以一心
會聲氣之元豈徒囿於物者哉審一定和大順
之內蘊不容祕則顯設於聲容者有以著萬物
之理而聖人以一德端制作之本豈徒假於外
者哉吁樂之本原於心則德之盛者樂斯備心
punctuated:
聲容之盛，樂固爲德之華矣，果何以見之？彼樂必有詩也，由志之動於中者而宣諸詞說之際；樂必有歌也，由詩之形於言者而調諸音曲之餘；樂必有舞也，由聲之發於外者而協諸容觀之度。是三者皆樂之所由生也。然是聲容之肇端於志，非無所本也。內焉感於心，而欣喜萌其端，歡愛洩其蘊，樂之啓其始者在是矣。然後志之形見於聲容，不能無飾也。外焉被於器，而音律以宣之，干羽以舞之，樂之成其終者在是矣。

是故聖人之作樂也，情之感觸者深，自溢於中聲之暢；志之蘊藉者厚，自闡於德容之光。其視天地之氣積之盛，而生物之妙發之神者，不有同機乎？故志和行成，實德之中孚不能遏，則呈露於歌舞者足以動四氣之和，而聖人以一心會聲氣之元，豈徒囿於物者哉？審一定和，大順之內蘊不容祕，則顯設於聲容者有以著萬物之理，而聖人以一德端制作之本，豈徒假於外者哉？

吁！樂之本原於心，則德之盛者樂斯備；心
translation_en:
…the magnificence of sound and movement: music is indeed the flowering of virtue. How can this actually be seen? Music must have poetry: what stirs inwardly as intent is expressed in words. Music must have song: poetry given verbal form is harmonized in melodies and their lingering resonance. Music must have dance: sounds issuing outward are coordinated with measured movements and gestures. These three are all means by which music comes into being. Yet the origin of these sounds and movements in intent is not without a foundation. Inwardly, the heart is moved; delight first sprouts, and joy and affection pour forth what lies within. Here is where music begins. Thereafter, as intent becomes manifest in sound and movement, it cannot be without embellishment. Outwardly, it is imparted to instruments: musical tones and pitches express it, and dancers with shields and feathers enact it. Here is where music reaches completion.

Thus, when the sage creates music, deeply stirred feelings naturally overflow in the free expression of balanced tones; richly stored intent naturally unfolds in the radiance of movements embodying virtue. Does this not share the same workings as the abundant accumulation of the vital energies of Heaven and Earth, whose wondrous power to generate living things manifests itself with marvelous efficacy? Thus, when intent is harmonious and conduct perfected, the inward sincerity of true virtue cannot be restrained. What appears in song and dance can stir the harmony of the vital energies of the four seasons. With a single heart, the sage comprehends the source of sound and vital energy: how could he merely be confined by material things? Unity is examined and harmony established [?]; the inward abundance of supreme accord cannot remain concealed. What is visibly displayed in sound and movement can reveal the principles of all things. Through unified virtue, the sage sets right the foundation for instituting music: how could he merely borrow from external things?

Ah! Since music has its root in the heart, where virtue flourishes, music is complete. The heart…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之德通於樂則樂之備者德斯彰樂其信爲德
之華也與大抵樂之爲道與人心通也聖人始
以心德之和形之聲歌而成樂繼以大樂之敎
洽之人心而成治大章蕭韶之樂固洋洋太和
之響也何者而非和德之感召耶故曰聖人作
樂以感人心而天下和平
第貳塲
論
知其性則知天
===
黃守謙
同考試官敎授饒批塲中作論多因體認欠
真非澁則蔓獨此作出入經傳及宋儒諸說融會
通徹發揮明盡且又體裁峻雅宜錄以式
考試官敎諭劉批立意切當而措詞精健
考試官學正楊批善發性命之旨
大哉人心之理乎其通性命而一之者乎君子
知盡性之學而至命之理在是矣夫性也者人
也未始不原于命也命也者天也未始不付于
punctuated:
之德通於樂，則樂之備者德斯彰。樂其信爲德之華也與！大抵樂之爲道，與人心通也。聖人始以心德之和形之聲歌而成樂，繼以大樂之敎洽之人心而成治。大章、蕭韶之樂，固洋洋太和之響也，何者而非和德之感召耶？故曰：「聖人作樂以感人心，而天下和平。」

第貳塲
論
知其性則知天

黃守謙

同考試官敎授饒批：塲中作論，多因體認欠真，非澁則蔓。獨此作出入經傳及宋儒諸說，融會通徹，發揮明盡，且又體裁峻雅，宜錄以式。

考試官敎諭劉批：立意切當，而措詞精健。

考試官學正楊批：善發性命之旨。

大哉，人心之理乎！其通性命而一之者乎！君子知盡性之學，而至命之理在是矣。夫性也者，人也，未始不原于命也；命也者，天也，未始不付于
translation_en:
…when the virtue of the heart finds expression in music, virtue becomes manifest as music attains perfection. Is music not indeed the flowering of virtue! In general, the Way of music communicates with the human heart. The sages first gave expression to the harmony of their hearts’ virtue in sounds and songs, thereby creating music; they then suffused people’s hearts with the teaching of great music, thereby bringing about good government. The music of Great Splendor (Dazhang) and Xiao Shao was indeed the abundant resonance of supreme harmony. What in it was not evoked by harmonious virtue? Thus it is said: “The sages created music to move people’s hearts, and all under Heaven became peaceful and harmonious.”

Second Session
Discourse
“To Know One’s Nature Is to Know Heaven”

Huang Shouqian

Comment by Associate Examiner Rao, Professor: Discourses written in this examination mostly suffer from a lack of genuine understanding: they are either obscure or rambling. This composition alone moves freely through the Classics, their commentaries, and the various teachings of the Song Confucians, integrating them with thorough understanding and expounding them clearly and fully. Moreover, its form and style are elevated and elegant. It should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The central conception is apt and precise, and the wording refined and vigorous.

Comment by Examiner Yang, School Instructor: It ably elucidates the meaning of human nature and Heaven’s mandate.

Great indeed is the principle of the human heart! Does it not connect human nature and Heaven’s mandate, uniting them as one? When the gentleman understands the learning by which one fully realizes one’s nature, the principle by which one reaches Heaven’s mandate is contained therein. Now, nature pertains to the human, yet it has never failed to originate in Heaven’s mandate; the mandate pertains to Heaven, yet it has never failed to be bestowed upon…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
未知則于心有所未盡于天有所不達故謂性
爲惡謂性爲外謂性爲三品謂性爲善惡混謂
性爲明心見性紛紛然求勝其說非惟不知天
亦不知性也非惟不知性亦不知心也是以君
子以性也卽命也非命外別有性也命也卽性
也非性外別有命也性也命也卽心也非心外
別有性命也故于天有不知必其性有不知也
性有不知必其於心有未盡也而可語一貫之
理哉是以君子神而明之會而歸之故灑掃應
===
對精義入神一原也志于爲學從心不踰一理
也格致誠正脩齊治平一道也致曲有誠形著
動變一機也善信美大聖神不知一本也而天
性可易知之哉昔者子貢謂文章性與天道有
聞有不聞未免見文章天道爲二也曾子聞夫
子之一貫卽以忠恕言之悟也使曾子又以一
貫告之則泥矣惟以忠恕明一貫焉則一理渾
然隨感而發蓋通性天而一之者也故曰曾子
傳道于夫子也他日夫子又以告曾子者語之
punctuated:
未知，則于心有所未盡，于天有所不達。故謂性爲惡，謂性爲外，謂性爲三品，謂性爲善惡混，謂性爲明心見性，紛紛然求勝其說，非惟不知天，亦不知性也；非惟不知性，亦不知心也。是以君子以性也卽命也，非命外別有性也；命也卽性也，非性外別有命也；性也命也卽心也，非心外別有性命也。故于天有不知，必其性有不知也；性有不知，必其於心有未盡也，而可語一貫之理哉？是以君子神而明之，會而歸之。故灑掃應對、精義入神，一原也；志于爲學、從心不踰，一理也；格致誠正、脩齊治平，一道也；致曲有誠、形著動變，一機也；善信美大、聖神不知，一本也。而天性可易知之哉？

昔者子貢謂文章、性與天道，有聞有不聞，未免見文章、天道爲二也。曾子聞夫子之一貫，卽以忠恕言之，悟也。使曾子又以一貫告之，則泥矣。惟以忠恕明一貫焉，則一理渾然，隨感而發，蓋通性天而一之者也。故曰曾子傳道于夫子也。他日夫子又以告曾子者語之
translation_en:
…If this is not understood, there is something in the mind that has not been fully realized, and something in Heaven that has not been comprehended. Thus some say that human nature is evil, that it is external, that it falls into three grades, that it is a mixture of good and evil, or that it consists in “illuminating the mind and seeing one’s nature” [?]. Amid this profusion, each seeks to make his explanation prevail. They fail to understand not only Heaven but also human nature; not only human nature but also the mind. The gentleman therefore considers human nature to be precisely Heaven’s mandate: there is no separate nature outside that mandate. The mandate is precisely human nature: there is no separate mandate outside that nature. Human nature and Heaven’s mandate are precisely the mind: there is no separate nature or mandate outside the mind. Thus, if there is something one does not understand about Heaven, there must be something one does not understand about one’s nature; if there is something one does not understand about one’s nature, one must not yet have fully realized one’s mind. How, then, could one speak of the principle of the single thread running through all things? The gentleman therefore apprehends it with spiritual insight, bringing its manifestations together and tracing them back to their source. Sweeping and cleaning, responding to others, and refining one’s understanding of principles until one penetrates the spiritual all share one source. Setting one’s purpose on learning and following one’s heart without overstepping the bounds share one principle. Investigating things, extending knowledge, making intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating oneself, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world constitute one Way. Developing particular aspects of goodness until sincerity is attained, and sincerity’s taking form, becoming manifest, moving others, and bringing change constitute one animating process. Goodness, genuineness, beauty, greatness, sagehood, and spiritual inscrutability share one root. Can Heaven and human nature, then, be easily understood?

Formerly, Zigong said that the Master’s cultural accomplishments could be heard about, whereas his teachings on human nature and the Way of Heaven could not. He thus could not avoid regarding cultural accomplishments and the Way of Heaven as two separate things. When Zengzi heard the Master speak of the single thread running through all things, he immediately explained it in terms of doing one’s utmost for others and treating others as oneself: this was understanding. Had Zengzi merely repeated the words “a single thread” to those he addressed, that would have been rigid adherence to the wording. Only by elucidating the single thread through doing one’s utmost and treating others as oneself could he show that the one principle is an undivided whole, manifesting itself in response to whatever it encounters. This connects human nature and Heaven and unites them. Hence it is said that Zengzi received the transmission of the Way from the Master. On another occasion, the Master again spoke to him of what he had told Zengzi…

text:
龍衮而
紫樞重寄韜鈐特慎於虎符何期二臣偶諧
四輔臣仲淹懼辱諫官之薦荷
聖恩未允其懇辭臣弼恐緣奉使之勞蒙
天語復諭以特用集夔龍於
沼上欲敷禮樂三千收頗牧於
禁中思壯山河百二蓋
聖主期致太平之盛匪愚臣徒叨爵祿之榮臣
等旣忝為輔相之司敢自負
===
責成之意鹽梅交和沛霖雨於蒼生尊俎折衝
消烽煙於紫塞畢江湖之素志敬陳民事
數千言竭薪膽之愚衷願上安邊十二策
同心輔政敢云周召之希蹤協力宣勞共
慶唐虞之親見賛
一人之斡旋元化陰陽順而風雨時脩五代以
控制遐方萬國寧而四夷服伏願
祚昌天保
慶衍日恒
banxin: 山東鄉試錄 五十七
punctuated: 龍衮而紫樞重寄，韜鈐特慎於虎符。何期二臣偶諧四輔！臣仲淹懼辱諫官之薦，荷聖恩未允其懇辭；臣弼恐緣奉使之勞，蒙天語復諭以特用。集夔龍於沼上，欲敷禮樂三千；收頗牧於禁中，思壯山河百二。蓋聖主期致太平之盛，匪愚臣徒叨爵祿之榮。臣等旣忝為輔相之司，敢自負責成之意？鹽梅交和，沛霖雨於蒼生；尊俎折衝，消烽煙於紫塞。畢江湖之素志，敬陳民事數千言；竭薪膽之愚衷，願上安邊十二策。同心輔政，敢云周召之希蹤；協力宣勞，共慶唐虞之親見。賛一人之斡旋元化，陰陽順而風雨時；脩五代以控制遐方，萬國寧而四夷服。伏願祚昌天保，慶衍日恒。
translation_en:
…dragon robes, and the weighty trust of the Privy Council; in military strategy, particular care is exercised over the tiger tallies of command. Who could have expected that we two servants would happen to join the four chief advisers! Your servant Zhongyan, fearing that he would dishonor the remonstrance officials’ recommendation, received Your Majesty’s gracious refusal of his earnest request to decline. Your servant Bi, apprehensive that his appointment arose from his service as an envoy, again received Your Majesty’s declaration that he was being specially employed.

You gather men like Kui and Long beside the imperial pool, wishing to spread the three thousand observances of ritual and music; you bring men like Lian Po and Li Mu into the palace, intending to strengthen a realm whose mountains and rivers allow two men to withstand a hundred. For our sagely sovereign seeks to bring about the fullness of Great Peace; it is not merely that we foolish servants should undeservedly enjoy the honors of rank and emolument. Having unworthily assumed the duties of chief ministers, would we dare betray your intention in holding us responsible for their fulfillment?

Like salt and plums harmonizing their flavors, we shall pour life-giving rain upon the people; overcoming opposition at the ceremonial vessels of diplomatic banquets, we shall extinguish the beacon fires along the northern frontier. To fulfill the aspirations long cherished in retirement among rivers and lakes, we respectfully submit several thousand words on the people’s affairs. To exhaust our humble devotion, sustained through hardship like sleeping on firewood and tasting gall, we wish to present twelve proposals for securing the frontier. United in assisting your government, dare we claim to aspire to follow the Dukes of Zhou and Shao? Joining our efforts in diligent service, we rejoice together at witnessing in person an age like that of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. We shall assist the One Man, the sovereign, in directing the primal processes of transformation, so that yin and yang are harmonious and wind and rain arrive in season; we shall cultivate the five dynasties [?] to govern distant regions, so that the myriad states are at peace and the peoples of the four quarters submit.

We humbly wish that your dynastic fortune may flourish under Heaven’s protection, and that your blessings may spread like the rising sun and the enduring moon.…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
舞干羽於
兩階茂著文明之化
垂衣裳於
五位彙征俊乂之良
居重馭輕滄海全歸于禹貢
蓄威昭德薊門永固于堯封瞻
皇極之尊
鴻圖億世效華封之祝
鳳曆萬年臣等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
梁棟材
punctuated:
舞干羽於兩階，茂著文明之化；垂衣裳於五位，彙征俊乂之良。居重馭輕，滄海全歸于禹貢；蓄威昭德，薊門永固于堯封。瞻皇極之尊，鴻圖億世；效華封之祝，鳳曆萬年。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
梁棟材
translation_en:
…May the dance of shields and feathers between the two stairways splendidly manifest the transforming power of civilized virtue; may Your Majesty, with robes hanging down in effortless rule in the sovereign’s fifth position, draw together the finest men of outstanding talent. Holding the central position and governing the outlying regions, may you bring all the seas within the domain described in the Tribute of Yu; storing up might and displaying virtue, may you secure Jimen forever within the bounds of Yao’s realm. Looking up to the majesty of the imperial pivot, we wish your grand enterprise a hundred million generations; following the example of the boundary keeper of Hua in offering blessings, we wish the imperial calendar ten thousand years. We, your servants, look toward Heaven and gaze reverently upon Your Sagely Majesty, overwhelmed with fervent emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Liang Dongcai

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭劉批我
皇上仰體
祖宗仁民至意刋布醫書以全斯民之命
恩至渥矣是以
上天篤愛而錫以
億萬年無疆之壽良有所自此作敷對有條揄颺詳悉而忠誠之意
溢於言外宜錄以傳
考試官敎諭劉批揄揚
聖壽之隆而本于
===
聖學之敬
聖治之神有識之士也
考試官學正楊批敷答有條而贊揚得體
予其沐
聖化之深而忠愛之情見乎詞者歟
聖人之愛民也深是以其衞民之生也切
聖人之體天也至是以其受天之眷也隆
何則莫不欲生者民之情也聖人以民之
情爲情凡可保合性命而納之生全之域
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭劉批：我皇上仰體祖宗仁民至意，刋布醫書，以全斯民之命，恩至渥矣。是以上天篤愛，而錫以億萬年無疆之壽，良有所自。此作敷對有條，揄颺詳悉，而忠誠之意溢於言外，宜錄以傳。

考試官敎諭劉批：揄揚聖壽之隆，而本于聖學之敬、聖治之神，有識之士也。

考試官學正楊批：敷答有條，而贊揚得體，予其沐聖化之深，而忠愛之情見乎詞者歟？

聖人之愛民也深，是以其衞民之生也切；聖人之體天也至，是以其受天之眷也隆。何則？莫不欲生者，民之情也。聖人以民之情爲情，凡可保合性命而納之生全之域
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Our Emperor reverently embodies his ancestors’ deepest intention to show benevolence to the people. He has published and distributed medical books to preserve their lives: his beneficence is most abundant. Thus Heaven’s profound love for him, and its bestowal upon him of boundless longevity for hundreds of millions of years, assuredly have their source. This composition presents its response in an orderly fashion and offers detailed and comprehensive praise; its loyal sincerity overflows beyond the words themselves. It merits inclusion in the record for transmission to posterity.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He extols the abundance of the imperial longevity, tracing its foundation to the reverence of the Emperor’s sagely learning and the wondrous efficacy of his sagely governance. He is a man of discernment.

Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: His response is orderly, and his praise is fitting. May we regard him as one who has benefited deeply from the sage Emperor’s transforming influence, and whose feelings of loyalty and devotion appear in his words [?]?

The sage’s love for the people is profound; hence his solicitude for safeguarding their lives is earnest. The sage’s embodiment of Heaven is consummate; hence the favor he receives from Heaven is abundant. Why is this? The desire to live is a feeling shared by all the people. The sage takes the people’s feelings as his own. Whatever can preserve their nature and life and bring them into a realm where life is kept whole …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
極聖之資撫
重煕累洽之運
盛德
大業之美輝映乎天地
深仁厚澤之布淪洽乎遠邇洋洋哉盛美乎其
不可一二殫述也明問欲諸生效
祝天保以颺言
聖壽乃舉
頒賜醫書為言得非以民命之於
===
國脉所係甚重而醫方之於民命所關最切
者乎善哉宋儒程頤有言曰仁者以天地
萬物為一體夫言天地而必及萬物見天
之於民其理不殊也言天地萬物而必曰
一體見君之敬天恤民其機不二也故奉
天而惠民則元后父母之責盡因民而得
天則祈天永命之慶衍此相因之理而泰
隆之治也盡此道者神農黃帝其選乎神
農氏之王也五穀熟而人民育矣乃為之
punctuated: 極聖之資，撫重煕累洽之運，盛德大業之美，輝映乎天地；深仁厚澤之布，淪洽乎遠邇。洋洋哉，盛美乎！其不可一二殫述也。明問欲諸生效祝天保，以颺言聖壽，乃舉頒賜醫書為言，得非以民命之於國脉所係甚重，而醫方之於民命所關最切者乎？善哉！宋儒程頤有言曰：「仁者以天地萬物為一體。」夫言天地而必及萬物，見天之於民，其理不殊也；言天地萬物而必曰一體，見君之敬天恤民，其機不二也。故奉天而惠民，則元后父母之責盡；因民而得天，則祈天永命之慶衍。此相因之理，而泰隆之治也。盡此道者，神農、黃帝其選乎？神農氏之王也，五穀熟而人民育矣，乃為之
translation_en:
…with the endowments of supreme sageliness, presiding over an age of successive prosperity and accumulated harmony. The splendor of his abundant virtue and great achievements shines throughout Heaven and Earth; his profound benevolence and generous bounty spread far and near, permeating all. How vast! How magnificent! These things cannot be exhaustively recounted one by one. Your illuminating question asks the students to emulate the blessings of the ode Heaven Protects You (Tianbao) and proclaim wishes for His Majesty’s longevity. In doing so, it raises the imperially bestowed medical books. Is this not because the lives of the people are of utmost consequence to the lifeblood of the state, and medical prescriptions bear most directly upon the lives of the people? Excellent indeed!

The Song Confucian Cheng Yi said: “The benevolent person regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body.” To speak of Heaven and Earth and necessarily include the myriad things shows that the principle linking Heaven and the people is the same. To speak of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things and necessarily call them one body shows that the ruler’s reverence for Heaven and solicitude for the people spring from a single impulse. Thus, by serving Heaven and benefiting the people, the sovereign fulfills his responsibility as their father and mother. By winning Heaven’s favor through the people, he extends the blessings sought in praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. Such is the principle of their mutual dependence, and the governance of supreme prosperity. Among those who fully realized this Way, surely Shennong and the Yellow Emperor stand foremost? When Shennong ruled, the five grains ripened and the people were nourished. Then, for their sake, he…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
味草木之滋妙神化之術察寒溫平熱之
性辯君臣佐使之義而醫藥傳焉黃帝之
興也衣裳垂而天下治矣又從而探天下
之賾原性命之理明榮衛之清濁究順逆
之盈虛而內經著焉二聖人體天愛民開
物成務其所以仁天下之法甚精且詳也
故其民旣享龐皓之福而二君亦躋遐永
之年明效大驗豈不章章較著哉周禮周
公致太平之書也今觀醫師掌醫之政令
===
率官分治而統之於天官歲終則稽其失
全之多寡而上下之焉藏冰出冰出火納
火皆所以助陰陽之運而療民疾于未然
也食醫疾醫瘍醫皆所以扶血氣之和而
療民疾于已然也法制纖悉莫備於兹是
以疾苦不貽於黎庶太和洋溢於宇宙卜
世三十卜年八百厥有繇哉嗣是而後漢
文帝赦太倉令而春和賑貸唐太宗見鍼
灸圖而特禁鞭背太平聖惠方頒於宋太
punctuated: 味草木之滋，妙神化之術，察寒溫平熱之性，辯君臣佐使之義，而醫藥傳焉。黃帝之興也，衣裳垂而天下治矣，又從而探天下之賾，原性命之理，明榮衛之清濁，究順逆之盈虛，而《內經》著焉。二聖人體天愛民，開物成務，其所以仁天下之法甚精且詳也。故其民旣享龐皓之福，而二君亦躋遐永之年，明效大驗，豈不章章較著哉？《周禮》，周公致太平之書也。今觀醫師掌醫之政令，率官分治而統之於天官，歲終則稽其失全之多寡而上下之焉。藏冰出冰，出火納火，皆所以助陰陽之運而療民疾于未然也。食醫、疾醫、瘍醫，皆所以扶血氣之和而療民疾于已然也。法制纖悉，莫備於兹。是以疾苦不貽於黎庶，太和洋溢於宇宙。卜世三十，卜年八百，厥有繇哉！嗣是而後，漢文帝赦太倉令而春和賑貸，唐太宗見鍼灸圖而特禁鞭背，《太平聖惠方》頒於宋太
translation_en:
…he tasted the flavors of plants and trees, perfected the arts of wondrous transformation, examined their cold, warm, neutral, and hot properties, and distinguished the functions of sovereign, minister, assistant, and envoy ingredients; thus medicine was handed down. When Huangdi arose, he let his robes hang down and all under Heaven was well governed. He then further explored the hidden mysteries of the world, traced the principles of human nature and life, clarified the purity and turbidity of nutritive and defensive qi, and investigated fullness and depletion in their proper and contrary courses. Thus the Inner Canon (Neijing) was composed. These two sages embodied Heaven in their love for the people, disclosed the properties of things, and brought undertakings to completion. Their methods of extending benevolence throughout the world were exceedingly refined and detailed. Thus their people enjoyed blessings of abundant peace [?], while the two rulers themselves attained great longevity. Were these clear results and great proofs not abundantly manifest?

The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace. Looking now at its provisions, we see that the Chief Physician administered medical regulations and commands, directing the officials in their separate duties under the Ministry of Heaven. At the end of each year, he assessed the number of their failures and complete cures, raising or lowering their standing accordingly. Storing ice and bringing it out, bringing forth fire and taking it in—all served to assist the workings of yin and yang and to treat the people's illnesses before they arose. Dietetic Physicians, Physicians, and Surgeons all served to sustain harmony in blood and qi and to treat the people's illnesses after they arose. Nowhere were regulations more minute or comprehensive. Consequently, illness and suffering did not afflict the common people, and supreme harmony overflowed throughout the cosmos. That divination foretold thirty generations and eight hundred years of rule surely had its reasons!

Thereafter, Emperor Wen of the Han pardoned the Director of the Grand Granary and, in the mild spring weather, provided relief and loans. Emperor Taizong of the Tang saw an acupuncture and moxibustion chart and expressly prohibited flogging the back. The Formulas of Sagely Benevolence for the Era of Great Peace (Taiping Shenghui Fang) was promulgated under the Song emperor Tai…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗焉簡要濟眾方頒於宋仁宗焉雖其有
限之仁未足以媲美於帝王之盛而卽其
愛民之念皆不失爲一時之賢君也已洪
惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
寶籙再開渾淪乃於
開基之五年
詔天下郡縣凡民之疲癃不能自全者官爲養
贍督醫治療而醫學之設徧于郡邑且又
申
===
諭曰仁政所先常加存恤焉
成祖文皇帝光造
丕基聿垂
洪緒乃於
嗣服之四年
命太醫院凡民之疾苦不能得醫者出
內府藥劑隨宜散施而
惠民藥局之
punctuated:
宗焉，《簡要濟眾方》頒於宋仁宗焉。雖其有限之仁未足以媲美於帝王之盛，而卽其愛民之念，皆不失爲一時之賢君也已。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝誕膺寶籙，再開渾淪。乃於開基之五年，詔天下郡縣：凡民之疲癃不能自全者，官爲養贍，督醫治療。而醫學之設徧于郡邑，且又申諭曰：「仁政所先，常加存恤焉。」
成祖文皇帝光造丕基，聿垂洪緒。乃於嗣服之四年，命太醫院：凡民之疾苦不能得醫者，出內府藥劑，隨宜散施。而惠民藥局之
translation_en:
…Taizong of the Song; the Concise Prescriptions for Bringing Relief to the Multitude (Jianyao jizhong fang) was promulgated under Renzong of the Song. Although their limited benevolence could not match the flourishing achievements of the ancient emperors and kings, their concern for the people nevertheless qualified them as worthy rulers of their respective times.
We reverently reflect that our Taizu, the Gao Emperor, received the precious celestial mandate and opened the primordial universe anew. In the fifth year after founding the dynasty, he issued an edict to the prefectures and counties throughout the realm: wherever people were infirm or disabled and unable to support themselves, officials were to provide for their sustenance and oversee their medical treatment. Medical schools were established throughout the prefectures and counties. He further reiterated his instruction: “This takes precedence in benevolent government; constantly extend care and relief to them.”
Chengzu, the Wen Emperor, gloriously established the great foundation and transmitted the grand imperial legacy. In the fourth year after succeeding to the throne, he commanded the Imperial Medical Office to dispense medicines from the palace stores, as circumstances required, to sick and suffering people unable to obtain medical care. And the provisions concerning the Pharmacy for Benefiting the People…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
令申在禮部且又加
勅曰必有實惠勿為文具焉是
心也固天地萬物一體之心也其所以下濟乎
民上承乎
天登斯世萬年生成之域綿
國家萬年靈長之祚蓋已肇於兹矣迨我
睿宗獻皇帝仁敷江漢德合
蒼旻爰集醫方選要之篇實為濟民利物之寳
惟
===
天陰隲下民則是書之懿能不呵護流行使四
海九州之眾咸緣是以登於並育不害之
天哉肆我
皇上以
聖人居
君師之位以
孝思盡繼述之責特
命刊刻普錫中外天下臣民咸莊誦稽首曰我
皇上純孝體
punctuated:
令申在禮部，且又加勅曰：「必有實惠，勿為文具焉。」是心也，固天地萬物一體之心也。其所以下濟乎民，上承乎天，登斯世萬年生成之域，綿國家萬年靈長之祚，蓋已肇於兹矣。迨我睿宗獻皇帝仁敷江漢，德合蒼旻，爰集《醫方選要》之篇，實為濟民利物之寳。
惟天陰隲下民，則是書之懿，能不呵護流行，使四海九州之眾咸緣是以登於並育不害之天哉？肆我皇上以聖人居君師之位，以孝思盡繼述之責，特命刊刻，普錫中外。天下臣民咸莊誦稽首曰：「我皇上純孝體
translation_en:
…the regulations were reaffirmed through the Ministry of Rites, and he further issued an injunction: “There must be tangible benefits; do not let this become mere paperwork.” Such a heart is indeed one that regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as a single body. The means of bringing aid below to the people and answering above to Heaven, of raising this world into a realm of life and growth for ten thousand years, and of perpetuating the dynasty’s enduring blessings for ten thousand years, surely had their beginnings here. When our Emperor Ruizong Xian spread his benevolence throughout the Jiang and Han region, his virtue accorded with azure Heaven. He thereupon compiled the chapters of Selected Essentials of Medical Prescriptions (Yifang xuanyao), truly a treasure for aiding the people and benefiting all living things.
Since Heaven silently sustains the people below, could it fail to protect and promote the circulation of so excellent a book, enabling the multitudes within the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, through it, to enter a world where all flourish together without harming one another? Thus our present Emperor, occupying the position of ruler and teacher as a sage, and fulfilling through filial devotion his responsibility to carry on his forebears’ work, specially commanded that it be cut on printing blocks and bestowed widely within and beyond the court. All officials and people throughout the realm solemnly recite it and bow their heads to the ground, saying: “Our Emperor, in his pure filial devotion, embodies …

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
保合太和而撫綏之念無一時之少疎允
矣其
仁卽
天地之仁
心卽
祖
考之心也是以
好生洽于民心而
國家之元氣厚
===
太和通于
上帝而
天地之和氣應其愛戴所輸則四海之廣億兆
之衆莫不歡欣鼓舞以祝
聖壽於無極如江漢所謂天子萬年令聞不已
殷武所謂壽考且寧以保我後生焉其
眷命之所篤則思或啓之行或翼之莫不單厚
多益以增
聖壽於無窮如天保所謂受天百禄降爾遐福
punctuated: 保合太和，而撫綏之念無一時之少疎。允矣，其仁卽天地之仁，心卽祖考之心也。是以好生洽于民心，而國家之元氣厚；太和通于上帝，而天地之和氣應。其愛戴所輸，則四海之廣、億兆之衆，莫不歡欣鼓舞，以祝聖壽於無極，如《江漢》所謂「天子萬年，令聞不已」、《殷武》所謂「壽考且寧，以保我後生」焉。其眷命之所篤，則思或啓之，行或翼之，莫不單厚多益，以增聖壽於無窮，如《天保》所謂「受天百禄，降爾遐福」，
translation_en: …preserving Supreme Harmony, with never a moment’s slackening in his concern to comfort and pacify the people. Truly, his benevolence is the benevolence of Heaven and Earth, and his heart is the heart of his ancestors. Thus his love of life permeates the people’s hearts, strengthening the vital energy of the state; Supreme Harmony reaches the Lord on High, and the harmonious energies of Heaven and Earth respond. In expressing their love and allegiance, throughout the vast lands within the Four Seas, the countless multitudes all rejoice and exult, praying that His Majesty’s life may be boundless. As “The Jiang and Han Rivers” (Jiang Han) says, “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years, his good repute never ceasing”; and as “The Martial Might of Yin” (Yin Wu) says, “May he enjoy longevity and peace, to protect us who come after.” Through the abundance of Heaven’s favor and mandate, his thoughts receive illumination and his actions assistance, all bringing generous support and manifold benefits to prolong His Majesty’s life without end. As “Heaven Protects” (Tian Bao) says, “Receive Heaven’s hundred blessings; may it send down lasting good fortune upon you”…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉樂所謂保佑命之自天申之焉
聖躬之日以康寧
聖壽之日以綿衍蓋將與
天同運應地無疆而詩所稱萬有千歲豈足以
擬之哉方今普天之下民物熙熙華夏以
奠蠻夷以服山川以寧海宇以謐草木以
蕃鳥獸以若何者非
皇上萬壽之所錫乎頻年以來
瑞應穰穰
===
壽星現焉卿雲爛焉甘露零焉芝草挺焉瑞兎
毓焉白鹿出焉何者非
皇上萬壽之所徵乎此無他民有欲生之情而
聖人者維持調護錫以生全之慶則
德洽於無外而維祺之吉以集
天有好生之心而
聖人者敷教錫類代厥生育之工則
仁周於不息而滋至之祥以享我
皇上所以紹
punctuated: 《嘉樂》所謂「保佑命之，自天申之」焉。聖躬之日以康寧，聖壽之日以綿衍，蓋將與天同運，應地無疆，而詩所稱「萬有千歲」，豈足以擬之哉？方今普天之下，民物熙熙，華夏以奠，蠻夷以服，山川以寧，海宇以謐，草木以蕃，鳥獸以若，何者非皇上萬壽之所錫乎？頻年以來，瑞應穰穰：壽星現焉，卿雲爛焉，甘露零焉，芝草挺焉，瑞兎毓焉，白鹿出焉。何者非皇上萬壽之所徵乎？此無他，民有欲生之情，而聖人者維持調護，錫以生全之慶，則德洽於無外，而維祺之吉以集；天有好生之心，而聖人者敷教錫類，代厥生育之工，則仁周於不息，而滋至之祥以享。我皇上所以紹
translation_en:
…and as “Admirable Joy” (Jia le) says, “He protects, assists, and commissions him; from Heaven he repeatedly confirms him.” As Your Majesty’s sacred person grows daily more hale and tranquil, and your sacred lifespan daily lengthens, you shall surely revolve in time with Heaven and match Earth in boundlessness. How could the “ten thousand and a thousand years” celebrated in the Odes suffice to describe this?

Now, throughout all under Heaven, the people and all creatures flourish in harmony. The Chinese realm is secure; the peoples beyond it submit; mountains and rivers are at peace; the lands within the seas are tranquil; plants and trees thrive; birds and beasts live in accord. Which of these is not a blessing bestowed through Your Majesty’s myriad years of life? In recent years, auspicious responses have abounded: the Star of Longevity has appeared, auspicious clouds have shone, sweet dew has fallen, numinous mushrooms have sprung up, auspicious rabbits have bred, and white deer have emerged. Which of these is not a portent of Your Majesty’s myriad years of life?

There is no other reason for this: the people desire to live, and the sage sustains and tenderly protects them, bestowing the blessing of life preserved intact. Thus his virtue reaches everywhere without exception, and auspicious blessings gather upon him. Heaven has a heart that cherishes life, and the sage spreads instruction and extends blessings to all, carrying out on Heaven’s behalf its work of engendering and nurturing. Thus his benevolence extends everywhere without ceasing, and he enjoys auspicious signs arriving in abundance. The means by which our August Sovereign continues…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
祖宗億萬年之統膺
天地億萬年之曆者孰非大哉
皇心一念至仁之所致哉執事乃欲以颺言之
雅望庠序之士則愚也亦竊嘗推本而揄
揚之矣伏覩我
皇上至德淵微
聖學之緝熈者亹亹也其
宣布而為臣民所服膺則
敬一有箴
===
四箴有註
欽天有紀微詞奥旨上接唐虞精一之訓而萬
世心學之傳胥此發焉不有以壽道統之
脉乎
聖德廣運治功之昭揭者炳炳也其注措而為
民物所快覩者則
明倫有典
秩祀有儀
耕桑有制宏綱大紀上繼唐虞昭明之治而
punctuated:
祖宗億萬年之統，膺天地億萬年之曆者，孰非大哉皇心一念至仁之所致哉？執事乃欲以颺言之雅望庠序之士，則愚也亦竊嘗推本而揄揚之矣。
伏覩我皇上至德淵微，聖學之緝熈者亹亹也。其宣布而為臣民所服膺，則敬一有箴，四箴有註，欽天有紀。微詞奥旨，上接唐虞精一之訓，而萬世心學之傳胥此發焉，不有以壽道統之脉乎？
聖德廣運，治功之昭揭者炳炳也。其注措而為民物所快覩者，則明倫有典，秩祀有儀，耕桑有制。宏綱大紀，上繼唐虞昭明之治，而
translation_en:
…the ancestors’ succession for countless ages, and receiving Heaven and Earth’s allotted span for countless ages—what part of this does not arise from the utmost benevolence of a single thought in the Emperor’s great heart? You, honored officials, look to the scholars of the schools with the gracious expectation that they will proclaim this praise. Thus I, ignorant though I am, have ventured to trace its source and extol it.
I humbly observe that our Emperor’s consummate virtue is profound and subtle, and that he works tirelessly to sustain and illuminate his sagely learning. What he promulgates, and his officials and people take to heart, includes an admonition on reverent unity, annotations to the Four Admonitions, and a record of revering Heaven. Their subtle words and profound meanings reach back to the teaching of refinement and singleness of mind under Tang and Yu—the sage rulers Yao and Shun. From these writings issues the transmission of the learning of the mind for all ages. Do they not thereby prolong the lineage of the Way?
His sagely virtue extends far and wide, and the manifest achievements of his government shine brilliantly. Among the measures he puts into practice, which the people and all living things behold with delight, are a canon elucidating human relationships, rituals regulating sacrifices, and regulations for plowing and sericulture. These grand guiding principles and comprehensive rules carry forward the illustrious government of Tang and Yu, and…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
萬世太平之澤皆此開焉不有以壽治統
之脉乎道統明則所以合
天地之德者愈久而愈昌治化宣則所以和
天地之氣者愈厚而愈長斯世斯民相與永賴
于
皇仁覆載之內而
皇上之壽自宜與
天地相為悠久矣愚跧伏嶺嶠游于
久道之化
===
仁壽之域也非一日矣雖模寫天地難於形
容然華封之祝則豈敢後於康衢擊壤之
歌哉謹對
第二問
劉寧元
同考試官教諭韓批諸儒發明道器之言其
異同各有攸當子能考據詳明辨析精確末段又
恐多言之晦道而欲求之於心是可以觀所養矣
考試官教諭劉批蘊藉深富而敷答詳盡
punctuated:
萬世太平之澤皆此開焉，不有以壽治統之脉乎？道統明，則所以合天地之德者愈久而愈昌；治化宣，則所以和天地之氣者愈厚而愈長。斯世斯民，相與永賴于皇仁覆載之內，而皇上之壽自宜與天地相為悠久矣。愚跧伏嶺嶠，游于久道之化、仁壽之域也，非一日矣。雖模寫天地難於形容，然華封之祝，則豈敢後於康衢擊壤之歌哉？謹對。
第二問
劉寧元
同考試官教諭韓批：諸儒發明道器之言，其異同各有攸當。子能考據詳明，辨析精確，末段又恐多言之晦道，而欲求之於心，是可以觀所養矣。
考試官教諭劉批：蘊藉深富，而敷答詳盡。
translation_en:
…and the blessings of peace for ten thousand generations all begin here. Does this not serve to prolong the lineage of governance? When the transmission of the Way is clear, that which accords with the virtue of Heaven and Earth flourishes ever more with time; when transforming governance spreads, that which harmonizes the vital energies of Heaven and Earth grows ever deeper and more enduring. This age and its people will together rely forever upon imperial benevolence, which shelters and sustains them, and His Majesty’s longevity should naturally be as enduring as Heaven and Earth. Dwelling humbly in seclusion among the mountains of Lingjiao, I have long lived amid the transforming influence of the enduring Way, in a realm of benevolence and longevity. Though Heaven and Earth are difficult to portray in words, how could I dare let my wishes, like those of the border keeper of Hua, fall behind the songs of the broad thoroughfare and of striking the clods? Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Liu Ningyuan
Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: The various scholars’ statements elucidating the Way and concrete things each have their proper grounds, whether they agree or differ. You have examined the evidence thoroughly and clearly, and your distinctions and analyses are precise. In the final section, moreover, you fear that excessive words may obscure the Way and seek instead to find it within the heart. This reveals the quality of your self-cultivation.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Rich in depth and substance, with a thorough and detailed exposition in reply.

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
必如是而後心性情之論無餘蘊矣孔子
之論仁智也曰知者動仁者靜矣而朱子
之解易則有仁陽智陰之說疑於異也殊
不知以本體言則知動而仁靜以生稟言
則仁陽而智陰義固各有所屬耳况明通
足以公溥則動而未嘗無靜也無私足以
有覺則靜而未嘗無動也動靜無端陰陽
無始觀仁知者合而一之斯可矣子思之
論仁智也曰成己仁成物智矣而朱子之
===
釋聖則有自明及物之說疑於殊也殊不
知成己成物者思誠一貫之功不厭不倦
者成德合一之妙意固各有所指耳况存
神妙於應物則成己固成物之本也達順
由於體信則成物固成己之推也體用一
原人己無間論仁智者一以貫之而已矣
盡己爲忠盡物爲信程子嘗示人以立誠
之要矣而乃謂有天道人道之別者則似
以內外人己分之也要之存於內而無不
punctuated:
必如是而後心性情之論無餘蘊矣。孔子之論仁智也，曰：「知者動，仁者靜。」矣。而朱子之解易，則有仁陽智陰之說，疑於異也。殊不知，以本體言，則知動而仁靜；以生稟言，則仁陽而智陰，義固各有所屬耳。况明通足以公溥，則動而未嘗無靜也；無私足以有覺，則靜而未嘗無動也。動靜無端，陰陽無始，觀仁知者合而一之，斯可矣。
子思之論仁智也，曰：「成己，仁；成物，智。」矣。而朱子之釋聖，則有自明及物之說，疑於殊也。殊不知，成己成物者，思誠一貫之功；不厭不倦者，成德合一之妙，意固各有所指耳。况存神妙於應物，則成己固成物之本也；達順由於體信，則成物固成己之推也。體用一原，人己無間，論仁智者一以貫之而已矣。
盡己爲忠，盡物爲信，程子嘗示人以立誠之要矣。而乃謂有天道人道之別者，則似以內外人己分之也。要之，存於內而無不
translation_en:
…Only in this way can a discussion of the mind, nature, and feelings leave nothing unexplored. In discussing benevolence and wisdom, Confucius said: “The wise are active; the benevolent are still.” Yet Zhu Xi, in explaining the Book of Changes, speaks of benevolence as yang and wisdom as yin. These statements seem to differ. What this overlooks is that, in terms of their fundamental substance, wisdom is active and benevolence still; in terms of the endowment received at birth, benevolence is yang and wisdom yin. Each formulation has its own proper reference. Moreover, luminous understanding suffices for impartial inclusiveness, so activity is never without stillness; freedom from selfishness suffices for awareness, so stillness is never without activity. Activity and stillness have no endpoint; yin and yang have no beginning. Those who consider benevolence and wisdom need only unite them as one.
In discussing benevolence and wisdom, Zisi said: “Perfecting oneself is benevolence; perfecting things is wisdom.” Yet Zhu Xi, in explaining sagehood, speaks of illuminating oneself and extending this to things. These statements seem to diverge. What this overlooks is that perfecting oneself and perfecting things constitute the work of seeking sincerity, with one principle running throughout; being neither surfeited nor weary constitutes the subtle unity of perfected virtue. Each formulation has its own intended reference. Moreover, preserving the spiritual achieves its subtle efficacy in responding to things, so perfecting oneself is indeed the basis for perfecting things. Extending harmonious accord proceeds from embodying trustworthiness, so perfecting things is indeed the extension of perfecting oneself. Substance and function have a single source; there is no separation between others and oneself. Discussions of benevolence and wisdom need only be threaded together by one principle.
Fully exerting oneself is loyalty; fully realizing things is trustworthiness. Master Cheng once showed people through these words the essentials of establishing sincerity. Yet to speak of a distinction here between the Way of Heaven and the human Way seems to divide them into inner and outer, others and oneself. In essence, what is preserved within leaves nothing…

text:
以下皆所當取法也而况古之才乎觀才
於天下古今之遠則古之諸子自張崔而
外猶不能無遺論焉而况今之才也此愚
所以有感於人才之難也非才之難也而
立志之難也志苟立焉而復充之以義理
之學使天下之道融會貫通於吾心由是
明之為經術而經術皆道也發之為文章
而文章皆道也措之為行誼施之為政事
而行誼政事皆道也則近而為陳為丘可
===
也遠而為張為崔可也等而上之則周程
也張朱也韓范也富歐也吾從而竝駕焉
可也又進而上之則孔孟也伊傅也周召
也吾從而效軌焉可也此正士君子終身
之所誦法而不以一善成名者也若曰徒
友一鄉之善士而足焉則豈愚生所安哉
第五問
梁棟隆
同考試官教諭林 批 兵食之計今日粵中最
punctuated:
以下皆所當取法也，而况古之才乎？觀才於天下古今之遠，則古之諸子，自張崔而外，猶不能無遺論焉，而况今之才也！此愚所以有感於人才之難也。非才之難也，而立志之難也。志苟立焉，而復充之以義理之學，使天下之道融會貫通於吾心，由是明之為經術，而經術皆道也；發之為文章，而文章皆道也；措之為行誼，施之為政事，而行誼政事皆道也。則近而為陳為丘可也，遠而為張為崔可也。等而上之，則周程也，張朱也，韓范也，富歐也，吾從而竝駕焉可也。又進而上之，則孔孟也，伊傅也，周召也，吾從而效軌焉可也。此正士君子終身之所誦法，而不以一善成名者也。若曰徒友一鄉之善士而足焉，則豈愚生所安哉？

第五問
梁棟隆
同考試官教諭林批：「兵食之計，今日粵中最
translation_en:
…and all those below them should be taken as models—how much more so the talented men of antiquity! Surveying talent throughout the realm and across the vast span of past and present, even among the men of antiquity, beyond Zhang and Cui, there are still others left to discuss; how much more so among the talented men of today! This is why I feel so deeply the difficulty of finding men of talent. Yet the difficulty lies not in talent, but in establishing one's resolve. Once that resolve is established, one must further nourish it through the study of moral principles, so that the Way of all under Heaven becomes integrated and thoroughly understood within one's mind. Elucidated as classical learning, that learning will embody the Way; expressed in literary composition, that writing will embody the Way; put into practice as personal conduct and applied to government, both conduct and government will embody the Way. Then one may become a Chen or a Qiu among men of more recent times, or a Zhang or a Cui among those of the distant past. Ascending a degree higher, there are Zhou and Cheng, Zhang and Zhu, Han and Fan, and Fu and Ou: I too may follow them and keep pace with them. Advancing still higher, there are Kong and Meng, Yi and Fu, and Zhou and Shao: I too may follow their paths. These are precisely the models that a gentleman studies and emulates throughout his life, rather than making his name through a single virtue. If one were to say that merely befriending the worthy men of a single district sufficed, how could I, an unworthy student, rest content with that?

Fifth Question
Liang Donglong

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太平熈皞之化有年矣顧承平日久姦宄漸
生頻年以來海倭山寇迭相為難賴藉
天威遠布文武重臣下及將校咸殫心宣力不
崇朝而嶺海肅清百姓鼓舞更生矣此其
故豈無以致之哉夫廣東嶺海隩區土地
聯絡接荆吳帶閩越南控交桂地方數千
里而島夷時出入邊陲張帆倏至山林洞
壑雜以猺獞姦民往往依險為盜有司急
不能制往時寇至然後調兵比兵至則寇
===
已去兵行然後給食比食至則兵已疲今
皆先期而集之兵先事而備之食故成功
最速以此言之理兵足食之策即此可以
占端倪矣請因明問而悉陳之夫廣之兵
衞所額戍其來舊矣此外有民壯有打手
又益之以召募增之以調集兵非不多也
然名籍空存而技擊非素練之卒白徒應
募而不戢有自焚之虞是數者果可恃乎
議者欲立團保以集鄉兵集之誠是也然
punctuated:
太平熈皞之化有年矣。顧承平日久，姦宄漸生。頻年以來，海倭山寇迭相為難，賴藉天威遠布，文武重臣下及將校，咸殫心宣力，不崇朝而嶺海肅清，百姓鼓舞更生矣。此其故，豈無以致之哉？夫廣東嶺海隩區，土地聯絡，接荆吳，帶閩越，南控交桂，地方數千里。而島夷時出入邊陲，張帆倏至；山林洞壑，雜以猺獞，姦民往往依險為盜，有司急不能制。往時寇至然後調兵，比兵至則寇已去；兵行然後給食，比食至則兵已疲。今皆先期而集之兵，先事而備之食，故成功最速。以此言之，理兵足食之策，即此可以占端倪矣。
請因明問而悉陳之。夫廣之兵，衞所額戍，其來舊矣。此外有民壯，有打手，又益之以召募，增之以調集，兵非不多也。然名籍空存，而技擊非素練之卒；白徒應募而不戢，有自焚之虞。是數者果可恃乎？議者欲立團保以集鄉兵，集之誠是也，然
translation_en:
The transforming influence of peaceful and harmonious rule has prevailed for years. Yet, as peace has endured, evildoers have gradually emerged. In recent years, Japanese pirates at sea and bandits in the mountains have taken turns causing trouble. Thanks to the far-reaching spread of imperial might, senior civil and military officials, down to commanders and subordinate officers, have all devoted their utmost thought and effort. Before a single morning had passed, the region of the southern ranges and sea was pacified, and the people rejoiced at their renewed lives. Surely there were reasons that brought this about?
Guangdong is a secluded region among the southern ranges and sea. Its territory forms a connected expanse, adjoining Jing and Wu, bordering Min and Yue, and commanding the approaches to Jiao and Gui to the south; it extends for several thousand li. Island barbarians periodically enter and leave its borderlands, arriving suddenly under sail. Yao and Tong peoples live interspersed among its mountain forests, caves, and ravines, where lawless inhabitants often exploit the difficult terrain to engage in banditry. The responsible officials cannot bring them under control in an emergency. Formerly, troops were dispatched only after the bandits arrived; by the time the troops reached the scene, the bandits had already gone. Provisions were supplied only after the troops set out; by the time the provisions arrived, the troops were already exhausted. Now troops are assembled ahead of time, and provisions are prepared before action is needed. Success therefore comes with the greatest speed. Viewed in this light, these measures already reveal the outlines of a policy for managing troops and ensuring adequate provisions.
Allow me to respond to your discerning question by setting this out fully. As for Guangdong’s troops, the prescribed garrison forces of its guards and battalions have long been established. In addition, there are local militiamen and fighting men, supplemented by recruited volunteers and augmented by troops transferred and assembled from elsewhere. Troops are certainly not few. Yet their names merely remain on the rolls, and they are not soldiers regularly trained in combat skills. Untrained men answer recruitment calls but are not kept under discipline, creating the danger of burning oneself with one’s own fire. Can these several kinds of troops truly be relied upon? text:
書生耳曩固樷林葦澤之產
繩樞甕牖之儔也一旦薦錄
賢書與縉紳大人揖讓堂階
之上不爲踰越及撤讌而歸
則里中父老子弟咸羣然歆
艷之亦不以爲侈大者則以
諸士負俶儻異常之才別於
===
凡民足以當之也今取諸其
三試之文而讀之雖文質殊
尚輕重異調長短各裁不相
爲侔然率皆言引詩書動合
矩度美哉洋洋文其盛矣然
劔遇割則知利事遇辦則知
才所貴於士者謂其才之足
punctuated:
書生耳，曩固樷林葦澤之產，繩樞甕牖之儔也。一旦薦錄賢書，與縉紳大人揖讓堂階之上，不爲踰越；及撤讌而歸，則里中父老子弟咸羣然歆艷之，亦不以爲侈大者，則以諸士負俶儻異常之才，別於凡民，足以當之也。
今取諸其三試之文而讀之，雖文質殊尚，輕重異調，長短各裁，不相爲侔，然率皆言引詩書，動合矩度。美哉，洋洋！文其盛矣！然劔遇割則知利，事遇辦則知才。所貴於士者，謂其才之足
translation_en:
…merely students. Formerly, they were people of the wooded thickets and reed marshes, men whose doors had rope hinges and whose windows were made from broken jars. Once recommended and entered on the roll of worthy men, they exchange bows and courtesies with eminent officials upon the hall steps, and this is not considered an overstepping of their station. When the banquet is cleared away and they return home, the elders and younger men of their villages gather to admire and envy them, yet do not regard their honors as excessive. This is because these scholars possess outstanding and extraordinary talents that distinguish them from ordinary people and make them worthy of such treatment.
Now, taking up and reading their compositions from the three examination sessions, I find that, although their preferences for ornament or substance differ, their tones vary in weight, and each shapes his work at a different length, so that none is quite like another, nearly all draw upon the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents in their statements and conform at every turn to established standards. How splendid, how abundant! What a flourishing of literary accomplishment! Yet a sword’s sharpness is known when it is put to cutting, and a man’s ability is known when he is put to handling affairs. What we prize in scholars is that their ability should suffice…

title: 嘉靖四十三年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以辦天下事也非徒以其文
焉已也玆所錄士之文信美
矣使異時宅揆亮采寅工錯
事以其所行者質諸所言之
文如投左券然一一符合人
將按錄而求之曰是科所選
士殆彬彬篤行君子也其永
===
聞于世矣倘或侈言無當實
行不揜則如木騮不駕鉛刀
不割卽飾以金鑣櫜以玉鞞
外雖燁然華美其實無所用
已抑又聞之仲尼曰國有道
不變塞焉而訓者謂不變其
未達之所守云夫士窮居在
punctuated:
以辦天下事也，非徒以其文焉已也。玆所錄士之文信美矣！使異時宅揆亮采，寅工錯事，以其所行者質諸所言之文，如投左券然，一一符合，人將按錄而求之，曰：「是科所選士，殆彬彬篤行君子也，其永聞于世矣！」倘或侈言無當，實行不揜，則如木騮不駕，鉛刀不割，卽飾以金鑣，櫜以玉鞞，外雖燁然華美，其實無所用已。

抑又聞之，仲尼曰：「國有道，不變塞焉。」而訓者謂不變其未達之所守云。夫士窮居在
translation_en:
…to manage the affairs of the realm, not merely to compose fine prose. The writings of the scholars recorded here are indeed excellent! If, in days to come, they occupy the chief minister’s post or assist in administration, work together reverently and conduct affairs, and their deeds, when checked against the words of their essays, match them point for point like the left half of a contract matching its counterpart, people will consult this record to seek them out and say: “The scholars selected in this examination are surely gentlemen of cultivated refinement and steadfast conduct. Their renown will endure in the world!” If, however, their extravagant words prove groundless and their actual conduct fails to measure up, they will resemble wooden steeds that cannot draw a carriage or leaden knives that cannot cut. Even adorned with golden bridles or sheathed in jade scabbards, they may appear dazzlingly splendid, yet in substance they are of no use.
